Flawless check-in: Front desk staff greeted me promptly, told me my room was ready and I was given vouchers for breakfast, welcome letters from the manager, and directions with a little map on how to navigate the grounds. I had also forgotten my phone charger at home, so I got directions to the closest Verizon store (but not before the concierge checked to see if he had an extra charger in the stash of chargers people left behind in their hotel rooms). The common courtyardgarden is spectacular- there are tables chairs that surround one side, fire pits at night, adirondack chairs on the edges, all overlooking a showcase water fountain, grass, palm trees flowers. Great landscaping! There are also little nooks between hotel villacottage buildings- I stumbled across a giant lawn chess set as I was trying to get to the parking lot one day- very cool. Room service rides around the property on big tricycles- very cool. When I was here, there were lots of families and older folks- there was a golf tournament Passover event so I'm guessing those are the drivers of the weekend demographics. Hotel room was very standard and almost a disappointment if I didn't read it already in the other Yelp reviews. I got a good deal too so I wasn't too bummed...just know that the rooms are a little dated and don't really match the Wright style of design that dominates the exterior and the common areas. The AC is also very loud- I ran it during the day while I wasn't in the room and turned it off at night so I could sleep in peace. Bed is alright- mattress is a little too springy for me, has a cushy feather bed on top and a good amount of pillows- but Westin bed it ain't. On my last night, there was a giant and bright full moon, which I enjoyed by opening my curtains and letting the moonlight shine into my room. There are quite a few options in different price ranges- the cottages look fun and have patios where you can sit outside...I'm guessing those cost quite a bit more. Huge con- parking. Valet costs 20 a night, and Self Parking is 12...there's definitely not enough space for self parking so you're left to stalk guests who are leaving, or suck it up and park in the valet. It's also quite a trek if you end up parking at the far end of the lot...I didn't mind since I could use the exercise, but if you have luggage or can't walk that far, be prepared to valet or be dropped off at the front entrance. Another con that I ended up being happy about- their spa was completely booked for Spa Week and they couldn't possibly fit in another treatment, even for a paying guest like myself. It ended up OK, bc I spent the day at another resort and spa, which I liked even better. I took a stroll though the spa area- it was attached to the main pool area which was very loud, and didn't seem as lush or pleasant as the spa I ended up going to. The pool areas get very full- try checking out the multiple pools they have on property to see which best fits your style. Cheap thin small pool towels too- you'll need at least 2 to cover your chair. Really convenient- near Biltmore Fashion Park for shopping restaurants, and not far from the highway and airport. All in all, it was a nice place to stay with beautiful ground and great service- I'll probably go check out another hotel the next time I'm in town, but if I find an incredible deal to the AZ Biltmore, I wouldn't hesitate to take advantage.

I so wish I would have sent it back, but our server was so nice. This place is over priced and could take a lesson from Cheesecake Factory where everything is consistently GOOD. Thank God we had a birthday coupon and got a break on the bill. Free chocolate cake that was not moist except for the frosting. Will never go back. We don't care about the beer.

I came to this place originally to get an emissions test earlier this week, it was quick and cheap, the receptionist was great. So I decided to bring my car in on Wednesday, April 2nd. I was going to have a synthetic oil change along with my front breaks done. You get a free tire rotation when you purchase an oil change which I thought was great since I had just purchased mine November of last year. The receptionist was great as usual, she stated I would receive a call when the work was done and everything would be done in two hours, Juan who was one of the people I spoke with said the same thing, two hours and we will contact you. I dropped my car off at 10:30 AM, I never received a call from either of them. I called at 3:00 PM (the time I was off work) and they said my car was ready. I paid 399.99 which I thought was a good deal for my two front brakes, rotors, and oil change. It beat the dealership by about 100 dollars. As I drove off my steering wheel started to violently shake, because of this my car turned into the next lane and almost caused me to be in an accident with a public bus. I immediately called and spoke to Juan, he stated nothing could be wrong with the car because they test drove it and everything was fine. I told him I would bring the car back, at this point I was upset because I was already off work and was trying to beat traffic along with the pouring rain that was coming in. I got to the shop, I test drove it with a really nice individual who actually had great customer service. He noticed the steering wheel was shaking violently and he said they were going to see what was wrong. One of the weights had fell off one of the wheels and they failed to put it back on. They were able to place the weight back on, but how do you miss this? What upset me the most is that Juan had told me they had test drove the car and it was fine, obviously they never test drove it because if they had they would've definitely noticed the steering wheel had a mind of its own. This could've caused an accident to anyone. Another thing, there was no accountability, no one ever admitted fault on their end, no one apologized, I was never compensated for having to stay there an extra hour of my time. Use this place for an emissions test but refrain from anything else, they have decent customer service but if someone is going to be this absent minded when dealing with your car, it's like driving around in a death trap.

One of the things I noticed about Avondale Arizona is the abundance of chain restaurant establishments, especially north of I-10 off of Dysart Road. But if you venture on the south side of the 10, you will come across TJ's. TJ's Homestyle Restaurant is about as un-chain as you will find in these parts. A true mom-and-pop diner that serves up meals that scream comfort. My experience here came on the morning I made my way back to California after nearly a week on the road in Arizona visiting family. I can thank my brother and sister-in-law for taking me here on this morning visit. Arrived to a near empty restaurant and sat down and ordered up their Ham and Mushroom omelet which came with four golden pancakes. The omelet was simple and fresh and the pancakes were fluffy and reminded me of my grandmother's pancakes (just a little beyond golden brown...but not burnt). The Hot Chocolate was out of this world good...super chocolatey and smooth with the dollop of whipped cream on top. The service is friendly but real cut and dry about things...like tell me what you want and make it fast. I kind of like that about this place as it's a real locals spot (witnessed locals talking about family and life with the waitress and each other). I also found it amusing that the cook came out and observed our order being taken...I guess he wants to make sure there's no mistake or screw ups in between us and him. Avondale is lucky to have a place like this...seriously...with a town full of chain restaurants, TJ's gives Avondale some much needed character when it comes to dining options.

All is not well in the Emerald City of Las Vegas. It seems that the nickel and dime mentality has settled in here leaving guests wondering what other unforeseen charges or overlooked amenities will be discovered. I DO NOT recommend staying here. My friend and I have had too many unpleasant surprises in just two days. It is a shame really that a prominent hotel like this has sunk to cheapness and frankly, some dishonesty thrown in. We are here attending a convention and the convention center itself has been wonderful. It is sparkling clean, with great meeting rooms and halls. Our time at the convention is enjoyable without a doubt. But then..... Something is incredibly amiss at the hotel. The MGM is undergoing construction and that is part of the problem This is a BIG reason to avoid this place for now. Their website attempts to gloss over this fact. It says that the MGM is getting a grand renovation and then proceeds to tell you to check out what is new. Oh how exciting! However, it isn't the kind of excitement you want; a letter placed on your bed, informing you to expect construction noise as well as the water supply being shut off on certain days. Why are guests paying 200 a night and being checked onto a floor where the water is being shut off? This is truly a first for me. For this incredible inconvenience (which you pay for) you receive a letter thanking you in advance for understanding the difficulties of renovating this hotel. They offer you a 15 discount on a future stay....WHAT! After checking in and being encouraged to spend an additional 15 per day to experience the grand renovation' experience, you get your water shut off and construction noise during the day! When I called guest services to ask for my 15 discount today, I was lectured on how unemployment is a problem and I should be glad that the hotel did not close to renovate. Can it get any more bizarre? Is there a Wizard behind a curtain spinning politically correct excuses in this Emerald City? Is this mega-million dollar corporation so greedy that it cannot absorb a few empty rooms? How about closing one wing? How about honestly updating future guests on your website like other hotels do that there is construction going on and it may be noisy, and for this inconvenience we are offering a sale? Is it because there is deeply planted nickel and dime antics going on? The strict mini fridge touch it and you own it rule, charging 50 per day if any personal items are found in this fridge (I guess rental fee added to 200?), 10 fee for 80 ATM withdrawal, lack of in-room coffee maker, and mandatory resort fee of 25 per day, even though the resort pools and grounds are closed for the season, are all signs of a grand hotel where the customer comes last. Any good things about my stay? The hotel is clean and the staff is exceptionally pleasant, but one can hardly notice these things when one is staying in a hell of a renovation resort. We have 4 more days here. We will update you on whether the MGM Grand is Grand enough to discount our stay for this inconvenience of renovation, or instead, will be passing out complimentary construction hats. Stay tuned, and stay away!

Bright, huge, friendly, cheap! I have to admit I have a bias because any bar with a ping-pong table in it would have to work hard not to get 55 in my book. 80 of the space is the bar, which is heaving on a Friday night with the after-work crowd. To the right of the bar are booths and tables for eating. To the left is an open area for drinking and playing. The ping-pong tables are against the back wall and there are two full-size pool tables at the very end of the room. The beer selection is pretty standard for a chain bar, but if you want to play pool, ping-pong or just eat well, this is a great choice. I gave this place a miss because I was put off by the 10 euro cover charge (non-refundable). It sounds like a lot, but it's refunded against food and drink bills. It sounds like a great place and if I was after a night of drinking and ping pong I'd go in a heartbeat. I think I might just have to give it a go on a weekday night instead. Btw, I know this isn't in the city centre but there are two more here: St. Stephen's Green and Christchurch. For those of you who love bar food, Mulligan's is the place for you. There is a fantastic selection of pub grub on offer, ranging from a large number of hot and cold sandwiches to a wide variety of appetizers and mains. I had a lovely plate of nachos (10.50), which were topped with melted cheese and served with sour cream and guacamole. There were also chicken wings, beef chilli, sausage and mash and fish and chips on offer as starters and mains. The beer menu isn't the best I've seen in Dublin, but it's not too shabby. They have a good selection of bottled beers, which included Guinness, Kronenbourg, Harp and a lot of stuff you won't be familiar with. I also saw they had a "mega pint" of beer on the menu which costs 10.95. I'm not sure I've ever seen that in Dublin before. I found the atmosphere really good. There was a nice buzz to the place and the staff were friendly. I'm not sure it's the place for a quiet pint, but I imagine it gets very lively on a weekend. The place was fairly full when I was there, so I would say it's probably best to book ahead for lunch or dinner. I would definitely recommend Mulligan's, especially if you're in the mood for a big plate of bar food.

This is a bit of a tongue in cheek tour for the tourists. Having seen the vaults on several programs on the TV we thought we would go see. The first thing you notice about this place are all these artifacts and skeletons scattered around, it feels like an archeological dig site as well with some items being taken out to be studied. We eventually found ourselves at one door that led off into another room where they had shutters covering regular windows from what I could tell or else there were really large plants blocking my view.. This was followed by more doors until finally reaching our destination...the vault itself built deep underground through which visitors enter wearing tracked shoes so that no dirt can get inside curling up over time....I guess?? Once we entered the light emanating dimmed quite quickly making us feel slightly claustrophobic.....we waited while staff came along each row revealing secrets locked away years ago under various names such as "The Dark Room." One group saw some wooden panels behind glass showing illustrations related to Egyptian culture giving them ideas relating back home......everyone went quiet then suddenly started laughing!! As someone later explained when asked why everyone has stopped moving, people have been known to start talking aloud together especially if their partnerfriends aren't nearby! Apparently most couples visit separately since its hard whispering quietly whilst trying not bumping elbows!! After 10 minutes (which felt almost eons) our guide returned saying...that's enough for today folks but come again soon! We couldn't wait!!!! So many mysteries still unanswered!!

I said, "I'm going to have a beer because I'm going to pass on this food and I'm about to get a really bad headache." While I was drinking my beer, I was asking around about the menu items and it turns out that the "quesadillas" were just vegetarian "tacos" - only with melted cheese and sour cream on top. I started chuckling to myself and I was wondering if they really thought that these things were quesadillas. There were two other vegetarians at the bar who had the same experience and we were having a good laugh. The waitress came back with more food and told us that we had to eat the "quesadillas" before the quesadillas were done. We told her that we were not going to eat the "quesadillas" and she left in a huff. After a while, the guy who was talking to me before, said, "That's how you know we're in Mexico - you can't trust the menu. And the food isn't going to be great, but you know you're going to like it." I said, "I can't believe I thought this was a quesadilla." He said, "It's a taco." I said, "Yeah, it's a taco with melted cheese and sour cream on it." He said, "Yeah, but it's a quesadilla." I said, "Haha! Okay, I get it. Whatever, I don't even like cheese. I only wanted it to see if it tasted better than the steamed vegetables." We both laughed and I said, "If I had known that it was going to be a taco, I would have ordered one of those because at least those tacos are made of corn tortillas and vegetables." I ate my "quesadillas" and we all decided that we wouldn't eat at this restaurant again because the food just wasn't very good and it didn't make sense that they didn't have a vegetarian menu. I think they only have vegetarian options if you are a vegetarian who wants to eat tacos with melted cheese and sour cream. If you want a quesadilla, then you're just out of luck. You'd think, wouldn't you, that with a name like Hillside Spot this restaurant in Ahwatukee would be nestled in a pastoral setting with lovely views? Not so, it's in a relatively new plaza at 48th Street and Warner Road, a busy spot where you can drive up and sit on the patio and have a great view of the parking lot. Ahwatukee is definitely a funky area, and the food at Hillside Spot is of the funky variety. It's a wide-ranging menu, with a section of "Southwestern Grill" which seems to mean burgers and chicken sandwiches then a section of "Euro-American" which means, well, eggs, quiche, omelettes, and breakfast burritos. The "Mediterranean" section features pastas and pizzas, and the "Latin" section includes specialty items like ceviche, tacos, and enchiladas. In the spirit of funky, I went for a bit of everything: a Caesar salad, a chicken Caesar wrap, and a spicy black bean burger. The Caesar salad was fine, but I've had better at most restaurants I got the feeling that this was a "house recipe" but it just didn't work. The Caesar wrap, however, was quite good. The chicken breast was coated with a tasty Caesar dressing and wrapped with the greens and lettuce, along with a small plastic cup of white sauce. The spicy black bean burger had a nice crust on the outside and a moist, flavorful interior. I would go back to Hillside Spot again, because it's a nice, casual spot with lots of variety. You can't go wrong with the pizza and pastas, and there are quite a few salads to choose from.

This is a bit of a tongue in cheek tour for the tourists. Having seen the vaults on several programs on the TV we thought we would go see. The beach itself was spectacular and we had been meaning to come back, but there were quite a few people out that day that didn't want to leave or there wasn't enough time for us to get into the place. So I guess it just sort of died down after the sun came up at sunset. We got there around 8pm and went along the coast where all the local beaches are as well, on top of getting a nice view over the crescent - it's a pretty spectacular view. We walked along the beach walking towards the museum next to the large, huge, old church which we have been looking through since October 2008 when I first moved here with my husband and his wife, who were very good friends before we decided to move here. While they weren't really interested in going back home they needed to see something else because so many tourists enjoyed taking pictures of them while staying here. It was amazing how easy it has become now, even though our main goal isn't to visit every single one of the local museums anymore! The only things left behind are the countless souvenirs from the tours we took. It might be nice if you could get some extra cash for these souvenir boxes but that wouldn't be worth the hassle. And no, this was not an expensive thing to do, it was just a great trip by itself. If you plan on visiting any more than once then you should consider having your own private tour to take your interest elsewhere.

My family and I dined here in Nov and ordered an array of dishes. I forgot our waiter's name but he was a tall slender gentleman w. a beautiful smile. We had the sea bass appetizer which is like fresh fish basted with sweet soy sauce, get it while you can! We also had foie gras hot dog (with onion rings) my husband did not care for that one at all so we shared his portion. For dinner we both enjoyed the lamb shank; my wife thinks her dry aged burger made from beef short ribs should be called lady meat because she liked what she ate much better than any other food on their menu. The macaroni cheese were yummy although I think they could use more bacon and less cheeze sauce. My son loved his spinach-artichoke dip as well. Next time we will go back again to try some wine or dessert items since dining out isn't always perfect even if you are doing excellent your meal. Cathy E - October 21 2015 15:34 Atlanta GA USA

Beautiful dining room hidden in Old Town Scottsdale. We made a reservation and scored an outdoor table on a lovely May evening. It was the perfect night to sit outside , cuddle up under a fire with our favorite friends, enjoy sunset views, and get cozy and cozy back at the hotel. We booked the most comfortable room for my family of four and it is located just minutes from Pinnacle Park Mall, charming city center (about 100 block away) and historic downtown Scottsdale. The location provides spectacular indoor and outdoor lighting for a beautiful relaxing night out that also includes a grill, hot tub, pool, poolside grill and fireplace throughout the room. There are great restaurants near by including Pizza Hut, Blackstone more. So much to see and do close by! A short walk from the airport, you can take a train or bus to Pinnacle right down to Union Square at about 9 AM. It's not too far, but the convenience of a metro station makes this a good choice. My mom likes shopping in the mall area but actually chose going to Scotty's instead as she's always found to be really helpful during all her shopping trips. One thing we didn't expect to find in the lot is a patio with a barrestaurant nearby. I'm sure there will be plenty of fun things to bring home and would love to come back to stay again someday! So happy to have been able to make the trip to Scottsdale and spend some quality time with one of the best places on earth!! 3 stars A very nice 3 star resort hotel with both indoor and outdoor shower rooms. The place consists of a master suite that has a bathroom furnished like a hotel but it still has a bed inside so you don't need to clean everything out daily. The hotel offers views of Mt. Rainier, the surrounding forests and even the mountains. You'll probably want to request a lift to meet your own wishes because it doesn't have cable TV, which is a plus since they don't have cable. The hotel comes equipped with a radio, microwaves, air conditioners, mirrorless cameras and coolers. Restaurant staff were very friendly and very knowledgeable and helped me and my husband out quite a bit. They had the hospitality to help us plan our meals around the sun every night. Highly recommended if you're looking for something to eat and drink at a very reasonable price.

My friend and I both ordered combo meals which included a cheese quesadilla, a chicken enchilada, and something that was supposed to be refried beans. The entire meal was very small for the cost. The quesadilla was just a tortilla made with shredded mozzarella cheese, not even Mexican cheese and no spices or anything. Extremely bland. The enchilada was quite bad as well. No flavor whatsoever. The refried beans were extremely watery and as weird as it sounds, they had a coffee taste and my friend agrees. I'm not one to write reviews, and am usually very happy with meals at restaurants but this was not good. My other friend ordered a taco salad and said it was okay but nothing special. The service wasn't wonderful either. Our waiter didn't seem all that friendly, never asked of we needed more chips or water, and forgot a side of sour cream we had ordered. I would not recommend this restaurant. It's a waste of money.

The menu contains CantoneseHunan cuisine. My boyfriend and I noticed how meticulous their staff was- they were ery well organized and paid close attention to detail. The ambiance is beautiful and their dinner menu (s) are enough to get any foodie excited. Be prepared to spend a good amount of money here (this is Vegas, after all). If you're in town and want to treat someone special to a wonderful dinner, or if you just to bask in luxury at this fine upscale restaurant, then check it out. You won't be disappointed.

The Cupcakery is amazing!!! I was in Las Vegas with my family recently and we were on the hunt for cupcakes on Christmas Eve. Thanks to my handy dandy yelp app, we found The Cupcakery, and it was definitely a lucky find! First of all the shop is adorable, it's bright and full of character. The staff was awesome and extremely helpful. They were really patient with us as they explained their menu. They have a box of fresh samples and they give a generous sample size. They have lots of different cupcake flavors, many of which were decorated in the holiday spirit. Some were so pretty that I didn't want to eat them....but of course my family and I did. I tried the Red Velvet, Brown Derby, and Cucumber Chocolate Chip and I thought I hit the cupcake jackpot. They were moist, delicious, just the right frosting to cupcake ratio. The frosting complimented the cupcakes perfectly with the right amount of sweetness. Great cupcake place! We will definitely keep this place in mind.

The Veggie Italian sandwich was the real winner - roasted summer squash, marinated buffalo mozzarella, baby arugula, tomato giardiniera on ciabatta. The drinks (pineapple lemonade!) were good as well, and top notch service (the guy at the counter patiently answered all our questions and didn't miss a beat when we continued to add things to our order). Almost makes me wish I lived closer to Madison, just so I could get breakfastlunch here!

I had to use the tamarind sauce to tone down the heat a bit. Very filling. 45 Aloo Tikki: You get 2 patties for 4. Crispy deep-fried mashed potatoes. Very filling as well. Great flavor. 55 Palak Paneer: I was looking for the cheese on top since that's what I'm used to. 45 Garlic Naan: I love this stuff. We had 2 orders. They're like hot cheese dougnuts in simple syrup. 55 I honestly wasn't expecting the food to be that good. This is my new favorite in Vegas! They also have a lunch buffet from 11am-3pm for 10-11. I'd come back here for that!

A shi-shi sports bar with an appetizing menu executed in a very average manner. The current tenants of this space (previously Daddy Macs, and Blue Wave before that) have stuck with the existing deep red on black decor and subdued lighting. Very Victorian. It harkens back to the supper clubs of the olden days. I half expect to find gentlemen in top hats when I entered the door. Instead I only found a few mid-day drinkers playing video poker. Being a sports bar, of course there are wide-screens all over the shop, which seem a bit anachronistic given that the place is swathed in late 19th-century red velvet drapery. Interestingly, the owners have placed a few old-fashioned items on the menu, such as baked brie, which are juxtaposed with more modern tasters, such as the deep-fried mashed potato bites. The menu is fairly enticing. Sadly the food falls short. It feels like everything here is made to sound impressive, but, looks and tastes like it was cooked at Wendy's. I would have assumed it was all fresh-made, but it all tastes to me like it originated in the freezer. Today, I tried the Chicken Florentine Soup. It definitely came from a can. No doubt about it. Then I got a California Turkey Burger. The lettuce was limp, the avocado was almost non-existent, and the turkey patty was too salty. However, there was a nice char on the patty, and I do love grill marks. My main complaint is that this swanky restaurant has tremendous potential and no one here seems to know how to reach it. The menu was promising. The descriptions of each item got me salivating. Unfortunately, my dining experience turned out to be like a bad blind date: your friend tells you how great this hamburger is, and then you finally meet it.... and it is nothing compared to the burger you tasted in your dreams. My advice to Elixir: if you're going to do gourmet pub food, actually do gourmet pub food. It's just not right to titillate a person's tongue without bringing the taste buds to climax; wink, wink.

I don't think they can get away with these things anymore since their customer base is predominantly Latino families. The menu would benefit from more choices of appetizers and soups but there are plenty of them on offer including traditional Mexican favorites as well as some delectable appetizer combinations (french fries, fajitas) to start the meal or entree. Very few vegetarian options exist but this should be remedied soon if not already. There isn't much else worthwhile in terms of desserts such as cakes or cookies which makes me wonder what happened to the former Tia Maria's Cafe. The atmosphere and ambiance of 1947 was quite good and there is no question that they have an outstanding selection of bourbon. I was also greeted very quickly and cordially by the bar staff. The owner, Justin from Kentucky Bourbon Distillery, was very accommodating to my needs as a customer seeking the best bourbons for aging in oak barrels (50 plus). He presented me with samples of his products which included a great variety of different expressions, including bourbon barrels aged in wine casks, whiskey barrels matured in whiskey barrels and others. My selection process took about 45 minutes and when they were all gone he returned with a bag full of additional bottles. I always enjoy a pleasant experience at a local distillery where one can learn more about their products and learn how they are made. Following this visit we decided it would be fun to attend the bourbon tasting but wanted to make sure we had the right equipment, so I bought assorted food items like chips, popcorn, hot dogs, lollipops and other foods. Our spirits shopping adventure began after lunch by spending some time looking through the gift store. There were many fantastic gifts available ranging from handbags, wallets, socks and shoes to key chains, t-shirts and Barbie dolls. When you purchase merchandise from distilleries it's important to choose what you want based on your tastes and preferences. I chose to purchase a nice wallet as well as a new laptop sleeve. We ate our snacks and enjoyed some bourbon cocktail mixers during the tasting while listening to several speakers talk about various products. One speaker talked about the history of bourbon and another discussed the potential uses of ethanol alcohol for medicine. After each speaker finished up he or she came over to us and asked if we liked the product. This gave everyone a chance to ask questions regarding our purchases. It was interesting discussion especially since all the vendors sell fine goods! Each vendor has built a strong reputation among connoisseurs and even casual drinker alike and it was really neat to see how much people care about the quality as well as prices. Overall we left with a lot of ideas about future purchases and a few additional bottles to try out. We plan on returning next year to sample everything offered and hopefully hear some entertaining stories from the event. If you're ever in Lexington Ohio stop by and take advantage of the great selection of products provided by a highly regarded company such as Kentucky Bourbon Distillery.

Overall I would 100 go get a slice and a PBR, but really don't expect much as far as service.

I went to the Brazilian Bull Steakhouse a couple of years ago for a friend's birthday party and we had a great time. Food was good, the atmosphere was great and we all had a fun time eating, laughing and spending time together. So, when a couple of friends suggested going to the Brazilian Bull for dinner, we all said sure and off we went. Big mistake. When we first sat down, our server rolled over a big cart with different bottles of wine. OK. We look and decide on a bottle of wine - 50. OK. Typical for a good bottle of wine when you're at a restaurant. Next, each person was 35 each to eat. That included my friend's daughter who was only 10. Yup, they charged us 35 for a 10 year old. There was an open salad bar seafood hot food buffet area. Total disappointment. Pasta salad was dry. The crab salad was just shredded crab. The ceviche was terrible. The different salad dressing that they had out looked as if it's been sitting out for hours. It was warm and gooey. Next came the varieties of different meat. The restaurant wasn't very full (it was a Thursday night and only 3 other tables). I expected more variety.... but only had sausages, roasted chicken, ham and sirloin (I think. it was beef I was told). The ham was too salty.... the sirloin was dry and the roasted chicken.... it was OK.... So, we're sitting here eating and we're all wondering what we're getting for 35 each plus 50 for a bottle of wine. I really expected better... Now, for the'if you don't ask, we won't tell' upsell. My friend's 10 year old sees the dessert cart and of course is drawn to every sugary item on the cart. The server cuts a HUGE piece of chocolate cake.... even though we said, just give her a little so she doesn't overdose on chocolate. When we get the check we see why. They charged us 10 for the chocolate cake. So, for the 10 year old, we pay 35 for the dinner, 10 for dessert. All the adults had to be 35 for dinner, spilt a 50 bottle of wine. I feel cheated. We like to eat at nice restauarants and don't mind paying for quality. In this case, I feel as if we were ripped off. Stay away from this place and save your money.

Our group decided to go to Surrender since we were able to get on the guest list. We came here just before they closed the guest list, so we were really lucky to get in. I made sure to bring my ID since I have heard so many horror stories about people not getting in because they didn't bring their ID. It took us about 5-10 minutes to walk from the Mirage to Surrender. It was a little bit hard to find at first but the line helped us find our way. When we got in, we got free water and some free drink tickets. We were able to get a table for free since we were part of the guest list. After a while, the waitress came and we ordered a round of drinks. The drinks were really expensive but they were strong. Overall, I think this was a great place to go out. We were able to meet a lot of people and dance. I definitely would go here again and I would recommend this club to anyone who is looking for a place to go out.

After a quick dinner trip, I think I might be against coming here again. The chips and salsa were quick to come to the table, but after a few bites I knew not to really look forward to dinner. The salsa was not very fresh tasting, and neither were the chips. I ordered an enchilada plate. I got some beef enchiladas with rice and beans. My enchilada was very bland and the beef was grey and unappealing. The rice was dry, there were a few crispy pieces I had to spit out. The sauce was thin and had color but I couldn't taste anything. Welcome home new (drastically discounted) designer handbag. Thank you Marshall's! As others have said, this is a smaller store with less variety than the Cotswold location. I have to add that with a little bit of patience and persistence, you can find a great deal at this Marshall's as well. I've come to this store if the Cotswold location is out of my size in a particular shoe - it's great to have two stores within a short drive of each other. Ladies, if you're looking for spring or summer dresses, this store JUST stocked up. There are lots of bright Calvin Klein or Nine West dresses in a variety of sizes. It's much less picked over than the Cotswold location. Stop by quick before this one is picked over as well! As for parking - if you must park in the attached deck, enter by the Trader Joe's (and not by the Best Buy). Alternately, park on the bottom floor of the Target deck. In all reality, it all comes down to which direction you take to leave the parking deck and head home - turning left at the intersection of Best Buy Target Wendy's is near impossible any day or time. I would love for the city to put a traffic light here! A girl can dream, right?

My favorite place in Vegas in terms of getting away from tourist and uber-marketing. This place is a classic, and the food is excellent. If they have the King Salmon 5 stars

Bocci, strip, and bar, are all better places to rock, but if you need some grease lube because you have trouble using the bathroom, or you want to have a massive food baby, then go here

If you are looking for a great place to eat off the strip this is not it. The place is overpriced, the server we had spent the entire time telling us how bad it was to work their. I can almost imagine how bad it must be if the radio commercial focus on his nephew or son being able to fix your computer almost while you eat. I think the true character of the owner is obvious in his public ads. However, we still went to check it out, and we are still sorry that we wasted out money. I'm not your typical Vegas-goer as I don't do the club scene and am usually here for conferences. HRH has a reputation for being pretty crazy with their Rehab party - from the looks of it, I think it certainly lived up to that reputation. Here's a review from someone who was sober the entire time: Pools: I think that they have the best pools in Vegas. If you're like me, then Sunday morning is probably not the best time to go...but anytime during the week, when it's fairly empty, the pools are like a glimmering oasis of blue. I think there's 10 or more. I know that they close early, but I was able to walk in and dip my toes in.... I saw some people swimming so as long as you're discreet, maybe it's possible to do some pm swimming:) Food: I only ate at Pink Taco. Their happy hour was ridiculously cheap. We sat at the bar and ordered one of everything (giant fatties). They seem to do chicken the best (skewers). I also recommend the tamales. Room: We stayed in the Paradise Tower. It's set further back from the hotel. The room is very rock'n roll - dark wall paper (very gothic) and I think the most comfortable bed...ever? I've slept in some nice beds, but wow...after a long (make that 5 LONG days at a conference) this was a total treat. Bathroom: The shower was pretty big and I like that it was separate from the sinks. Products were great - some brand, Prickly Pear (?). Gym: I really wanted to go...it looked very clean, small, but had a lot of equipment. I took a star off because the resort fee does suck - especially since I didn't get to use any of the amenities.

Rented space here for a couple years. Clean and convenient central Phx location. Great staff. Would highly recommend. They are located on the corner of East 18th Street and North Hudson Avenue, near McDonalds. The office also offers lots of free parking spots.
Love them the girls are so nice. They have energy to get you hyped up. They appeal both to females and males also. They way they dress is sexy but not trashy like other casinos.

This is probably the worst hotelresort I have stayed at... The only reason I gave them a star was because the front staff was friendly. First off the rooms are WAY smaller then they look in the pictures, the furniture is chipped and cheap looking. I was excited to stay here because I love the decor of boutique hotels. This one Looks like a fancy motel 6, definitely not a resort. No clocks, No fridge (extra cost) and no blankets. The waitress at Addiction was nice until we had a question about the check then she quickly had turned into a btch. Needless to say I will not be returning here nor would I recommend it to anyone.

What a great little hidden gem! Jimbo, the bartender, was super sweet and very attentive! I went on a Thursday, but WILL be back on a Wednesday because word around the campfire is there is a GREAT ladies' night deal! I had the Rodeo Burger. DE-LISH! The BBQ sauce was tangy and fresh and the BEER BATTERED FRIES were to DIE for! I am a fan of beer battered anything. Another bonus was the beers on tap. Alaskan amber (my fave) AND Alaskan White. Also Magic Hat!! Which is a little hard to find on the west coast. I highly recommend coming and sitting at the bar on a weeknight when it's nice and quiet. Next time I am trying the fish tacos!

Pay the extra for the VIP seats. We sat in the fourth row and had that up close experience. You also get the programs for free with the VIP. The drinks are expensive but good and they come in a PT cup. The show is not for those wanting cheap and cheesy Las Vegas magic. The show is intelligent with a touch of politics and social commentary added in. Getting photos and autographs after is amazing.

When this place first opened, my husband, friends, and I really enjoyed it. The food was great, especially the macaroni and cheese. The atmosphere was what you'd expect when going to a nice dinner out. However, I am not sure what has happened in the last few months. Apparently due to a change in management they have cut their menu down drastically taking away some of the better options, including the macaroni and cheese and salmon BLT. Big mistake. We ordered the 2 for 20, which is a little misleading on menu. You're thinking you get two pizzas plus two salads but you only get one pizza, which in some cases is not even getting as better dealthan just ordering individually. Definitely not worth the money. We spent 29 with tip for a tiny pizza, two very small salads, and my husband's iced tea. I wouldn't have necessarily minded that if the pizza was really good, but it was not. It was just average. We were left unsatisfied and very disappointed. Also, we went on a Wednesday expecting to find a nice quiet place to eat. Instead, they had half of the restaurant closed off with a DJ playing loud music for what I'm assuming was to be some sort of private party eventually. However, there were only the DJ and a couple people over there during the time we were having dinner. Seems like a waste to have someone preparing so early, playing music so loud that we couldn't even hear each other speak. This place had more of a sports bar feel with Italian food. If you're drinking then you'll probably be ok with the mediocre food. However, if you want a nice dinner, we suggest you go somewhere else. We had thought that this place was going to become one of our new favorites until new management came in and changed it for the worse. The food is not as good, the options are few, and the atmosphere has gone downhill. We definitely won't be going back and we will make sure to warn our friends and family as well.

STAY AWAY They are slum lords and could care less about the tenant. I had to wait about a week in 110 degree temps to get my AC fixed. It was dead... "You will have more success if you change your attitude toward others." -Ward Cleaver, "Leave it To Beav,"

Let me preface this review with a couple of things: 1. I went on a Monday at 3pm, so probably not the most ideal time to see the freshest foods in town; 2) This is my first visit here and perhaps it's worth another trip back later when all tulips are out or more items have been added (I'll definitely be coming again since everything was amazing). The restaurant has several seating areas you can choose from - very cozy for datescouples but if your party exceeds 4 people then might want go somewhere else because tables may feel cramped together depending where they decide put them around inside especially during peak times due being popular among locals as well tourists alike....one thing about Pai that will really catch strangers attention even though we're used seeing foreigners having their families there...is how young everyone looks- like babies! Even through kids aren't allowed until past 6 years old yet tiny ones run amok everywhere which actually makes an interesting picture capturing moment:)

Yes it carries a 59 price tag but it's definitely an experience worth partaking once in Las Vegas. This is not your typical brunch buffet. You can get those at the World of Buffets for unlimited breakfast, lunch and dinner. This is an experience. It really breaks down to what do you value for your money. Is it food alone or can ambiance be a deciding factor. For me, it's the whole experience. I enjoy buffets. I enjoy making a reservation. I enjoy being seated on time for my reservation. I enjoy the extra attention from the wait staff. I enjoy the option of ordering off a menu during my buffet. I enjoy live music and great customer service. And finally, I enjoy scrumptious food. So why only 4 stars? Not much variety for the buffet. Just Prawns. Large large prawns.
Tried the oreo concrete this time. it was so good I had it for dinner! Must try if you love deserts..

J'ai decouvert ce resto par une amie. Delicieux, meilleur restaurant que j'ai pu gouter a date.... A essayer l'entree de homard, plat de medagloni de foie gras et comme dessert un truc qui n'a pas ete nomme mais c'etait de la pates d'amandes aux petites feuilles bien moindrement soigneuse avec bonne sauce a peine vinaigrette. Une epicerie a proposer plus ou moins le gout des traditionnels du coin, superbe place pour se calmer sur les terres dorures. Je suis parti vers le bas aussi quelques minutes apres avoir decouvert le Japon. Ca est assez exceptionnel tout en restant simple (les plats sont pratiques). Les desserts, quant a elles, sont Petit Fours. Pour quemener l'effervescence je me ferais remarquer au Dragon Sushi - si tu te demandez pourquoi on ne te donnera pas la connaissance des meilleurs menus veut dire "le menu du week-end." L'enjeu, c'est justement de trouver ton vrai cheval de Troie... On arrive a la creperie The Crumpet's Tale offrant la chasse a l'argento: une crepe accompagnee de 3 morceaux de saucisson a la remiere, une camembertaise complet dont le montage commence a l'interpretation de la batterie et terminates au style francais. Le reste du repas offert dans ce petit etablissement matinale est accompagne d'une grande variete d'un autre genre: beaucoup de cones de pain et patisseries sans fin! Il y a plein de restaurants et brasseries en France (et dans le monde) de seconde zone, il existe souvent rapprochements entre differents "restos locales ." On voit ici ce que ca signifie vivre dans un village ou desormais non seule la paix sociale est impregnee d'une conciliation commerciale plus ou moins implacable. Cette idylle moribonde revient, au final, toujours a peser sur l'habitude d'un rythme vivrier, la spontaneite humaine. Quelle consolation pour nos familles perdues entre Paris et le bassin de Seine?

First Hooters experience. Sure were a lot of boobs around the building, but sorry girls, your sets do not compare one of the girls in my party of 3.:) All boobs aside, since I was a first timer, my girlfriends gave me a brief crash course of the menu and some recommendations. We started off with fried pickles for appetizers and 20 piece boneless chicken. Not knowing what kind of seasoning we want for our chicken, our Hooters girl was chill enough to allow us to do half and half on certain flavors to explore around. She recommended the Honey Thai seasoning and we chose the Cajun to seal the deal. Our fried pickles came out, fresh out of the fryer, and we dove right in. Too bad they only gave out one dinky cup of dipping sauce, which completely ran out halfway into our appetizer. They charge extra for extra sauce (oh come on, really?), but we still went ahead and requested some more. Our boneless chicken finally came and I like how each flavors were served in separate plates. The Cajun was spicy, yet tolerable, and indeed SALTY! I suppose that's how Cajun seasoning is supposed to be, but it was alright. The Honey Thai, recommended by our Hooters girl, was probably my favorite. It's sweet, with a hint of spiciness. I would like it if the spiciness was kicked up another notch, but our Cajun wings already covered that department, so it was all good. They were also a bit salty. Overall, it was a nice and SALTY experience. I think I chugged down 3 cups of water throughout the meal. Our Hooters girl was also nice enough to split our check three ways. She definitely got a nice tip from all of us. I want to give it 3.5, but had to round up because of the accommodating staff and clean atmosphere. Warning for those at risk for high blood pressure, this is where sodium dwells.

What a great experience located in the South end of uptown. With any new experience, I will ask what is either most popular or recommended. I ended up with a group that had just been to one place and all agreed on this restaurant but didn't know what it was called. Upon arrival we were greeted by a very friendly waitress who brought us menus as well as our drinks without asking (we ordered their specialty cocktails which are amazing!). This was such an unexpected treat since in many places nowadays they seem so concerned about making sure you order before your drink comes out! The food arrived quickly and hot off the grill after ordering at the bar. We started with some appetizers - small crayfish piccata and crab bisque and then moved onto a bowls of lobster ravioli for dinner when the pasta came out. Everything here was delicious. My husband loved his lamb chop while my daughter enjoyed her soup. Both kids' dishes included different types of mushrooms the best type of mushroom around IMO!! They did make me wish I could have gotten there earlier though because not only does no-mushroom lunch mean no cheese fries BUT also they apparently serve the BEST mashed cauliflower EVER!!! After my kids ate everything else they wanted to try so we shared some desserts including the chocolate souffle and my favorite cheesecake ever called "Grandma's Cookies" made from scratch using dark chocolate sauce caramel whipped cream topping the top instead of chocolate buttercream. For dessert, we opted to share a slice of the really moist cake from the menu named "Almond Joy." It wasn't too sweet but perfect for sharing...Enjoying dessert? Yes?? NO???!! Have a seat anywhere....not necessarily towards the front of the restaurant if you're trying to eat on time like myself:) Overall can highly recommend. Highly suggest skipping breakfast because everyone says brunch is better anyways but would love recommendations for something similar nearby. Lots of options available for both Asian AND American fare. Was happy to find this hidden gem tucked away down town. Rustic decor in addition to inside dining makes it feel cozy and homey. Don't miss their "pies au chocolat" bread pudding. Chef has created another masterpiece bringing together ingredients from all over Europe creating tasty combinations. Decorations add warmth and comfort to the space. They offer special events catering services to fit every occasion. Great atmosphere with great service and beautiful surroundings. We recently celebrated our 10th anniversary in Park City and decided to check out the local restaurants where we used to hangout years ago. We thankfully found La Cucina, a charming Italian resturant in historic downtown SLC. The outside looks great; however upon entering through the door, we felt immediately uncomfortable that it looked more like a coffee shop than a fine dining establishment. In fact, we thought it might be a little challenging going into a quaint and stylish setting wearing tuxedos and gowns and expecting anything other than socializing amongst ourselves! Many times do couples want to go somewhere quiet or classy and relaxing, yet still enjoy themselves during an evening mealdrink. However LAC met these expectations exactly: the seating area was intimate enough for us to sit comfortably side by side throughout the entire meal despite our dress code and excellent wine selection. Our server was absolutely delightful and attentive along with the owner who owned his business directly across the street made things even sweeter, knowing he knew the people sitting next to him. We truly appreciated how much effort went into immersing each dish into the ambiance of the room and accentuating the flavors. Be prepared to dress appropriately and expect a long wait line especially on Friday night when locals come in for happy hour specials. Overall, however, it was worth the wait and we plan on returning again soon!

I can't believe the pool closes at 8pm during summer time. We have to get the mini bar refrigerator unlocked and I understand that it has a sensor and that we have to pay for whatever we take from the mini bar but they should at least provide a small refrigerator for the guests. Oh wait! They do have refrigerators to offer the guests but they will charge 25night. I can smell the chlorine coming out of the shower heads also and its way too strong. Delicious food, knowledgeable staff, and a modern-chic setting. I loved the Vogue Martini and my husband enjoyed his Vogue Manhattan. The Vogue Burger was nothing short of perfection. It was juicy with just enough bacon on it to make me happy! They were both delicious but that had been eating all day so there wasn't much room left in our stomachs!! You can also order alcoholic beverages by the glass including wines from California vineyards like Chateau Montelena and Crescent Ridge Vineyard as well as other fine liquors such as Crown Royal Canadian Whisky. We definitely plan on going back here soon!!!

They also left the door open a bit to let some of that cold air out during dinner and my husband noticed it too as he came up with his jacket at the end! We will definitely go back, especially if you are looking for something new or unique where your choices aren't limited by what is available right now!" "We have been going here every Thursday night since the beginning of this year... really enjoy their food, atmosphere service!! The people that work there make everything so enjoyable. I highly recommend coming down on Thursdays!!"

Awesome place for lunch in the area. These people know good Mexican cuisine. I had the carnitas burrito with red sauce. Chili sauce wet is the way to go, trust me. Carnitas were tender and juicy. Also, it's family ownedoperated. Nothing commercial about this place at all. Just real, flavorful food.

Fantastic steakhouse. It has everything Flemings has with the same quality but within a five minute drive of my doorstep and at least 15-20 less expensive. We usually eat here once or twice per week for lunch, right next to our apartment building in the heart of the city centre. It is really nice to have such an inexpensive feast on your table when you are visiting Brussels! The food was cooked very well. We had two different entrees: a lovely steak (pork shoulder) with some fine cheese sauce, and a delicious piece of beef tenderloin which we ate whole. All this for under 10 from the main bar menu! I should add that it wasn't served raw; we'd already eaten about half of the meat before it arrived safe and sound in its plate. Unfortunately, as both my daughter and myself were full, we didn't finish all of our meals there - so by the time we did eat the rest later after work we were still hungry, since we hadn't had breakfast yet (hmmmm). However, this restaurant will definitely be one of our go-to places for anything steaks related! I would recommend this restaurant if you like to spend less than 10 and enjoy good quality food and service. For example - they have a bar area where you can get drinks, wine, beer, smoked salmon and desserts. But the real reason to visit here is the great atmosphere and friendly staff! We came over to Belgium having heard nothing but fantastic things about Bruges Steakhouse and decided to give it a try. The pictures don't do justice to how beautiful the place is inside and out. It seems every inch of space is filled with amazing decor and, unlike many other restaurants in Brugge, it's not too crowded. Our waitress was amazing - she and her entire team made our night so special while also giving us plenty of information on Belgian culture and history along the way! Our starter was quite large and was accompanied by salmon and catfish salads. While these weren't particularly fresh, the salad itself was perfectly acceptable and pretty tasty. My husband ordered a nice ribeye steak with fries and side dish of potatoes. This portion was huge and was probably the best steak dinner I've ever eaten in Europe...and yes, I did order black truffle fries! Both my kids loved their portions too and thoroughly enjoyed the dessert buffet and the appetizer platter. Overall, this was the perfect evening for sharing stories about Belgium and enjoying each others company. There isn't a bad seat in the house! And no matter what you choose to drink, even the most fussy eater won't complain! They serve excellent beers and wines alongside the main course and for something extra, ask for a glass of local champagne. I highly recommend making a reservation ahead of time online because you may need it given the amount of people who come into the restaurant daily. That being said, keep in mind that reservations only last 5 minutes and thus are typically booked through the phone system. If you want to avoid booking a reservation and just get comfy on the couch, I suggest asking to sit up front near the bar and you can easily watch the action! Overall, I think this is one of the must-visit places in Bruges. It's absolutely amazing to see how much Belgium cares about it's heritage and culture! With prices like this, you better start planning now...or make sure you bring Euros!

We had to be near downtown today, and when scrolling through nearby restaurants on my phone I saw this one. On Google it's rated 5 stars. Here it's 4 stars. And only a single dollar sign! So we drove over. The place looks like something you might find in Mexico. No hostess. Walk up to the counter, order your food, wait for your number to be called, walk into the dining area (ducking under a low arch if you over 6' tall) where you are greeted with basic tables and chairs. Seriously...if you didn't know you were in Phoenix you'd swear you were in an eatery in Mexico. They also have a bakery and a market attached to the food counter. On to the actual food. As this was my first time here I ordered the chimi. I usually do that so I have a basis for comparison to other places. My wife had the albondigas soup. We both liked our dishes. The chimi was done perfectly. A light crunch of the shell. Not overcooked, not greasy. The chicken was moist and tender. And it was a pretty big chimi. I think one does need to add some pico to it because the chicken's seasoning was very mild. The pico added just a bit of flavor that really made the difference. And the Mexican rice was very nice. I wish it wasn't so far from home (Gilbert) because I'd love to make this my regular spot for Mexican food. I would say it blows away just about every place else I've found in the Valley, and is neck-and-neck with Guerrero's (in Tempe). I can't choose between the two at this moment. I hope to return here, and will be trying something different. Their menu is pretty extensive with several traditional dishes (including menudo, lengua, and albondigas).

Came here this past weekend to pick up some donuts before heading back to the OC. Got there about an hour before they closed so we knew we would be having a great time and then figured out that it was pretty much day 1. The drive from Los Angeles to Arlington, Texas took about 90 minutes and was short of everything we wanted in Arlington (and for good reason). Here's my plan: 1) Make a trip through Arlington on I-35 from downtown LA (after you've already done your morning thing for dinner), then head south east on I-35 for three hours, stopping at the Arlington Zoo to see that one exhibit about birds, and finally take our car around and get all of the goodies we need (the only problem is that no food wasn't available as of yet). We decided to stop by the zoo tomorrow since we had been there a few times but couldn't seem to find anything for us. I think I might have even made the long walk to the exhibit if not for the fact that there were some crappy wifi connections everywhere we looked. It was nice to just go home and watch movies on a small screen and listen to podcasts! 2) Go to the Oak Creek Zoo in Arlington where they are known for their magnificent animals like tigers, lions, and rhinos. In 2004, we went to the Oak Creek Zoo because some folks thought they couldn't do the zoo without seeing them live. They actually got very close to the animals in a wild animal exhibit (which, when you look hard enough, can turn into a massive circus event).On Sunday morning the kids and I went to see the zoo. There are no animals to be seen except for a couple that you may have heard about - but that doesn't matter! When we got to the first place, the entrance was open and the children forked out 20 each for admission but unfortunately, there weren't any people able to show us what they had for us to browse while waiting in line for some animal exhibits.Unfortunately, everyone who showed us something else did not make the zoo experience any easier or more enjoyable. My daughter and I tried to talk the whole way through the exhibit but she refused. She told me that there was nothing wrong with getting out of the car and walking in front of the big dog, which was kind of funny because I am a little worried that they will eat her and bite her nose off...I just hope it won't happen again. So we walked across the street to the elephant room, where there were lots of cute elephants that were hidden away until it was time to move on to another exhibit! Every once in awhile, I ran into one of the guys there who brought his son with him and he said he wanted to see them come down to look at other elephants and at least one giant turtle lady! We also saw one of the elephant drivers and it seemed like he was going crazy making sure nobody saw his stupid elephant.Finally, we headed over to Arlington National Cemetery. Arlington has a beautiful cemetery but we could almost feel the special love being felt by the people below us at such an old cemetery. They observed some graves in the early 1900's and many of the figures were decorated with Easter eggs (some of which are still left inside). This cemetery gives the most perfect view of the city and the grounds where the worshipers grew up in, so you definitely want to check them out. I found a really cool fountain in the center of the museum and the tricolored flag of the Republic of Ireland topped it with flowers. Let's hope that those flowers continue to float above the gravesites of these fallen soldiers-Howard Stern of "The Voice" fame reported that this fountain is set on fire after the war ended and the soldiers reportedly died there. Food: Ginza offers traditional Japanese cuisine ranging from hibachi to sushi to noodles, with plenty of appetizers and deserts as well. We started with the miso soup, which was just right for me! Ginza is also offering a variety of rice dishes such as mango and tomato soup alongside a sweet potato shake paired with chicken and shrimp cocktails, lemon cake with rice cereal with rice pudding and a snack food called fish taco. The foodie hotspot offers exquisite Japanese spices like strawberry shortcake with peppers and paneer creamer roasted soups paired with steamed cucumber salad in a sweet tea beverage named after the Japanese word for "samurai," and a variety of desserts including a chocolate cake that includes chocolate or desserts made from rice cakes dipped in chocolate sauce topped with whipped cream and bananas. Ginza connects the dots between Japan's diverse culture and cuisines by combining Japanese traditions while still maintaining the traditional flavors of each country with tips on Japanese food styles you've never tasted before. Ginza features an extensive menu featuring locally sourced seafood, vegetables, herbs and meats such as burrata fried rice balls, grilled salmon with onions and cucumbers baked with soy sauce and creme fraiche, along with spicy chicken wings served with rice cake and peanuts. Ginza has been welcomed back into the family fold since opening, allowing guests to enjoy their favorite meals not only at home but over time too. Ginza also serves up Japanese Breakfast foods like Filipino fried tofu pancakes with chili sauce, rice cakes stuffed with gyoza flan and honey mustard, and rice krispy treats like egg rolls with eggplant parmigiano reggiano and rice cake. Ginza serves up breakfast items like Japanese pancakes with hazelnut bread filled with rice cake, Japanese rice toast stuffed with peanut butter jam, and rice cakes topped with yogurt and hot sauce. Ginza taps into the Japanese tradition of eating fresh ingredients instead of relying solely upon processed products when it comes to their fresh-cut orange juice bottles, and their Japanese breakfast bowls are packed full of delicious homemade almond milk shakes and rice cakes. Ginza also showcases Japanese snacks like superfast sweets like Korean bunny nuts and jumbo Thai popcorn. Ginza has also introduced new seasonal menus each month ranging from seasonal Japanese fried oysters to seasonal seafood plates using a variety of meats, vegetables and fruits like seaweed jellyfish and mango juice filled with mango smoothies and rice cakes. Ginza serves up appetizer offerings such as chewy lemon chicken sandwiches and sushi rice based salads mixed with other kinds of vegetables like mangoes and Japanese broccoli. Ginza's menus have always been fun and unique so guests can choose what they want from each meal category whether it be sushi or a vegetarian dish. Ginza also encourages guests to send in food suggestions via email or social media if anyone wants more options. At the second hostess station, I was greeted by name and escorted to my table which was windowside. I sat down, and seconds later my waiter introduced homself (Chas, prnounced Chaz), gave me the menu and specials, and took my drink order. A bread basket was immediately delivered with butter in a cup which had been piped through a pastry bag unlike the night before where I recieved butter in gold foil in the other fine dining place. I ordered French Onion soup (8), a Caesar Salad (8), and a NY Strip Bone-In (42) for my entree. The soup was delivered hot and served in a huge cored-out onion. The Caesar Salad dressing was absolutely one of the best I have ever had and anchovies were delivered on the salad as ordered. The steak was absolutely cooked perfect and was butter soft. Having had three perfect courses with such great service, I decided to try one of their desserts. I am not a sweets person, but I had 3 choices from 12 on the menu. I asked if I could just get the vanilla and was told that many customers had that request, and the chef prepares larger portions of just vanilla, although that option was not on the menu, but available. From that point on, I have to say that the Creme Brulee was THE BEST I have ever tasted from Paris, New Orleans, Montreal or anywhere! The meal, restaurant, and service were so impeccable, that I did something I have never done in 25 years of travellingI repeated the restaurant a second time the next night with a different menu! Now for the good news. If you stop at any of the 11 Tix4Tonight locations in Las Vegas, you can buy a coupon for 50 off an Entree for The Range for 3.00. So for 2, you spend 6.00 up front for a savings of about 45 for a couple. Be sure to make reservations in advanceeven on a weeknight, and be sure to ask for a window table.

Il Mulino Staple of NYC and My Hometown comesto Las Vegas in the new section of the forum shops on the North End of the Strip. Everything is pretty much spot on with the NYC location, with a few exceptions. The bread is not as good, but still tasty. I think this location has a bigger menu and more of an Italian wine list, but I'm not positive about that. They have a similar menu to the NYC location, with some differences. There are more meatfishpoultry options here, while the menu at Mulino's in New York seems to favor a more vegetarian fare. I had a very enjoyable dining experience. I started with the Carpaccio di Tonno, which was a simple dish, but one I could tell was executed perfectly. It came with frisee lettuce, lemon, olive oil, and slices of tuna (not sure what kind) on top of a toasted slice of bread. This was a great dish and it reminded me a lot of a dish I had at Del Posto (which I loved), though this was much simpler and less expensive. For my main course, I ordered the tagliatelle al ragu bianco. This was a very hearty dish and quite filling. The pasta was prepared perfectly and the sauce was creamy and very flavorful. As with the other dishes, the portions were quite large, so I would say the portion sizes at Mulino's are quite generous. My dessert was a chocolate mousse with raspberry sauce. The raspberry sauce was very light and refreshing and the chocolate mousse was just the right sweetness without being too rich. All in all, I thought this was a great meal. The service was exceptional and the wait staff was very attentive. I would definitely recommend Mulino's if you're looking for a nice Italian meal in Las Vegas.

RA sushi is so-so for sushi. It's not spectacular, but usually not terrible either. A group of us (7) came on a Saturday night and while we expected a wait 2 stars

This was our first time here. The happy hour prices are very attractive. We got the Edamame app which was brought to the table in a cute little covered bowl that held the steam and flavor. Better yet, we use our check-in deal on Yelp mobile to get it for free. The beer selection is good and happy hour prices make it even better. We also ordered the Chicken Catsu which was one of the best versions of this dish we've had. The portion size is enough to split if you get a couple of appetizers too. The manager was fantastic, ensuring we got the happy hour prices even though we ordered just a few minutes before 6pm. He was very attentive and made sure the place was running smoothly. Stayed here this past weekend and was not impressed at all. The Studio was very small and I needed to upgrade to a 1 bedroom. When I called the front desk, I was told that a Casino Host could sign-off on the upgrade. I went downstairs and verified with the front desk that a Host could sign off on the upgrade. All through the weekend I gambled at Planet Hollywood, and when I checked out, I was told that there was no affiliation with the actual casino. This was a total bait switch from what I was told. At checkout, the clerk told me she would hold the upgraded room charge on the side until a manager called me, since I was leaving town. NO phone call and they put the charge through after I left. Came here this past weekend to pick up some donuts before heading back to the OC. Got there about an hour before they closed so we knew we would be We had to drive an hour. Would not recommend it.

We've been to Bacon Bar several times, and the food has always been very good and very consistent. Great Sushi! Very fresh but a little pricey. The place has an excellent ambiance...great for celebrations! Location at the Epicenter is great, especially if you are planning to go out for drinks afterwards.

Went to this bar last night since it was close to my apt. and rec'd decent reviews from Yelpers.......NOT!! I have never been so obviously ignored since my days in the service industry! The bartender had a "look" that screamed of disinterest, she didn't ask about drinks or what anyone wanted, let alone new customers......ouch!!! I guess this is why the place wasn't busy when we got there (probably only 5-6 people).....but come on?!? The waitress was friendly enough but seemed pretty apathetic too...didn't even remember our order once! The service here is incredible. The good is always fast and delicious. Even better is the conversation and the culture. To my boyfriend, who is from Detroit, it's like going home. My favorite is the hot fries, but they have an excellent menu with something for everyone. The owner always remembers us and even sat down with is to talk about Detroit. Love the food and most of all, the people.
Drinks were served in filthy glasses the flatware had food stuck on it! Complained to the waitress- who nicely apologized but the manager never came out! Still got charged for the undrinkable drinks.

This place is only awesome if you are one of three things: 1. an Ohio State fan, 2. a metrosexual, or 3. someone trying to hook up with an Ohio State fan. If you don't fall into one of those three categories, then this place might not be the best fit for you!

Bring a sweater! They keep it coooold in here. I think all Starbucks are cold in order to get you to buy some hot coffee. This Starbucks was clean, had plenty of seating, and a good variety of drinks.

I eat here all the time with my girlfriend and we can't say enough about this place! Amazing decor, service, and cuisine! She loves the Thai ice tea and veggie pad Thai and I always get the chicken pad Thai or duck basil. Amazing quality and variety.

Gross, what happened?! It has been a while since I have been to PF Chang's. It used to be one of my favorites...I remember going to a conference and I ate at the PF Chang's across the street from my hotel every day. This last time there was pure disappointment. From the quality of the food, to the service, to the taste it was as if I was at some cheap fast food joint. Each dish tasted like it had the same sauce as a base. It was way too salty! Since when did they start rationing out their rice? We got a very tiny portion of rice and we had to keep asking for more to soak up the salty sauce on the dish. Blah. The service was super slow to greet us at the table and to bring us what we needed. Made for a very unenjoyable experience. Blah...and I'm sad that it wasn't better.

I've eaten at probably all the fine places Las Vegas has to offer and I have to say I didn't expect a bad experience with this one (especially after reading the reviews). Pros: Nice staff Cons: Nice staff but my particular waiter lacked menu knowledge Pros: Nicely decorated restaurant;) Cons: Sushi overfilled with rice and has no special taste. By the time we had our third roll I figured might as well just load up on drinks because I was getting no excitement with the food. Drinks were mediocre. In conclusion, more cons then pros. Not recommended. Go to Social House instead, way better in all aspects!

We stayed here for two nights in July. Here's the break down: The good: 1) Super helpful staff, every person we came in contact with was fantastic. 2) Awesome innkeeper. Great breakfasts and she made us feel like we were in her home. 3) Friendly staff, it's a small place, but they were great. 4) Bathrooms are nice. 5) Beautiful grounds and gardens. 6) Nice location. 7) Well appointed rooms. 8) Complimentary internet. 9) Lots of freebies. 10) Lots of free parking. The bad: 1) They were closed at 4:30, so if you are going to come to WV and want to get to the CO Canal, you're out of luck. 2) You can't rent bikes there. 3) You can't rent kayaks there. 4) No outdoor pool. 5) You can't rent canoes or rowboats there. 6) No onsite restaurant. 7) You can't get shuttle service there. The Ugly: 1) The restaurant has the same menu every day, but they had some things on it we didn't see on the previous days. 2) The service was poor, and we didn't see any of the staff in the dining room the entire time we were there. 3) We weren't shown to our room until 10:30pm. 4) Our room wasn't ready until 10:30pm. 5) There was no air conditioning in the room. 6) No windows in the bathroom. 7) No safe in the room. 8) No hangers in the closet. 9) No fan in the closet. 10) No towels in the bathroom. Overall we were very pleased with the hotel. We would stay there again, and recommend it to others. Great place to stay, and it's in a great location. We didn't want to leave. I'm so glad we stayed at the Point Breeze Inn. We have stayed at many other bed and breakfasts and inns in our travels. This one is a winner. I'm glad we found it and I'm glad we had the chance to stay there. It was in a great location. The rooms were beautiful and clean. The staff was friendly and helpful. The restaurant was great, and we ate there every night we were there. The breakfasts were wonderful, and the food was very good.

The pearls in the bubble tea weren't made right. For some reason, they weren't serving sushi (it was 3pm so I don't know if there was a time limit). So I ordered the Thai red curry. It was served in a huge bowl with a small bowl of rice. A few chunks of chicken and some vegetables.
This rating is only for the Karaoke room. Karaoke system is soo outdated, I don't know where to begin. Also, very limited of options to adjust the system.

I've been to Rumbi probably a few dozen times. Worked near the (now closed) Rumbi on Frank Lloyd Wright in Scottsdale and ate there several times. Have gone to this I've been to Rumbi and been to Rumbi several times. And it's not the same place as the other location in Scottsdale.

Very disappointed in this place. It's looks clean and nice on the outside so I thought I might have found a great spot for a good breakfast burrito. Unfortunately the employees seemed like they were out of their element and didn't know what they were doing. I will not be back. I stopped in today for lunch and was very happy with the food. The waitress was very friendly and quick. I ordered the cheeseburger with fries and was very pleased with how it was prepared. I am looking forward to going back and trying the breakfast. Ordered the smothered burrito and it was decent for a small town burrito shop. I am from Dallas and I have ate at many many Mexican restaurants. I can honestly say, this one is right up there with the best. I have been eating here for 2 years now, every time I visit my family in Weatherford. They have great food, and the best Mexican drinks I have ever had. The green drink is delish! I ordered a cheeseburger and a chicken sandwich. The chicken sandwich was very dry and the cheeseburger was ok. They had no chips and no onion rings. We also had to ask for our drink refills.

Sin City Wings really is a one-of-a kind wing experience. I've never experienced food that's as hot, yet bursting with flavor. I was also unfamiliar with the concept of a naked wing, meaning there isn't any breading - absolutely delicious. Being from out of town, I also got to learn more about some of Vegas' locals. The wings are named after several iconic figures, including the Oscar Goodman, which was my favorite wing and extremely hot, yet flavorful. I also have to mention the pot stickers because they are awesome and rolled in the same spicy sauce as the wings. If you're cruising around the strip and happen to see the yellow wing truck, I would definitely recommend giving it a try!
