I love Paradise Bakery, just not this one. On too many occasions have they messed up my order or not had key ingredients for main sandwhiches. I keep returning based on a general disdain of the place as it sucks and is plagued with a very bad reputation from their customers (which was to me). Funny how it's reputation has nothing to do with quality. Sure there are some things that don't work but you never know if people will like something or not because they're trying to make money off of the food.

Yes, their pastries are amazing. I love their vanilla bean iced coffee, which is a major diet splurge.The egg sandwich is good (though way overpriced). But their other food is hit and miss. Granted, I've only had their veggie options so I'm a bit biased. Overall, the portions are tiny and way overpriced, and the service is often slow and rude. The owner is nice, as are a couple of the employees, but there are several cashiers who don't even have the manners to say please or thank you!! Usually I call ahead and pick it up, and when I get there they scramble to put everything together. Today I dropped in without calling, which I will never do again. I ordered, and the cashier said, 9.75. No please. No thank you for payment. So rude! I sat down and I watched about 5 people who ordered after me get served their meals. When I asked the cashier after 20 minutes, then again after 35 minutes for her to check on my order, she coldly said, we're backed up, without even checking, without a single apology! Finally I flagged down a polite cook to check on my food, who brought it right out to me at room temperature. Yes, they were slammed, and I can empathize. But why on earth didn't they give me a heads-up when I ordered, or give me an update after 15 minutes, or at the very least, APOLOGIZE? It's extremely upsetting to spend so much time and money at their establishment and be treated like this. Today I got the 9 veg special and they gave me a small salad, a yummy round croissant thing, and a soup the size of a cappuccino. The 3 spoonfuls were delicious, but come ON!! Would it kill them to be a tad more generous? Also, they don't have decent vegetarian options, which is insane considering how proud they are of their organic food. Now they have Vegetarian Tuesdays, which is the only day I eat here because I've tried every veg option and nothing is satisfying: Their meal salads are ok, but lack protein (adding nuts, beans, tofu, or even cheese would make it a meal). The side salad is a joke: a few leaves of lettuce and vinaigrette that's it no tomato, no onion, no crouton, no cheese, no dressing options just lettuce with oil and vinegar. The grilled veggie sandwich is slimy. The Mediterranean platter is greasy. And their grilled cheese sucks the mozzarella is like melted plastic (see below). Their hummus plate is served with ample crusty oil-drenched bread but only 2 tablespoons of hummus! I have a small appetite and eat healthily and I still feel gypped andor grease-sodden every time. What bothers me more than anything is their holier-than-thou elitist attitude. A few times I've made suggestions and they clearly have zero interest in making improvements. My helpful attitude is always met with an insolent dismissal. Among them: have cheese options for the grilled cheese (they refused), and sell the mini macarons as singles, for those of us who don't like to blow our entire meal calorie count on dessert (they claimed that's too labor intensive.... yet, if they sold 3 of them an hour it would pay the hourly wage for an additional employee). That they're closed evenings and on Sundays, and sometimes for a week or more at a time, is a major negative too. As is their too tiny location and horrific parking situation. I only eat here because there are no other options for organic, locally-farmed food options in the area. If they were in a larger city, or even if they were in a hipper part of this city, they may not survive.

I got to stay here for free, as one of my travel companion's parents had timeshare points we used. I have 2 cats, and I love this place. I buy them things like Innova Evo (dry and canned) and Nature's Variety frozen raw meat medallions, which are difficult to find in other stores. I also buy their canned Evo and freeze it in individual daily portions to save money, because I have a picky kitty who won't eat any dry food. If you are going to be buying this brand of canned food, I would recommend buying the largest size, and freezing what you don't use. They also sell all kinds of raw meat, some packaged, some not. You can get chicken wings, ground beef, turkey necks, and more. They also sell all kinds of frozen raw meat patties (beef, chicken, turkey, lamb) which are so convenient for feeding large numbers of cats. I have never had an issue with prices - they seem to be very competitive with places like PetCo, etc.

I went for dinner with a Client last week while in town for business. We sat at the bar and I immediately noticed the most impressive whiskey wall, (predominantly Bourbon) I have even seen outside of The Library in NYC. They have it all. THE STAFF: The female bartender Maggie was fantastic. She was attentive, engaging and knowledgeable. She spoke to us just enough to make us feel more than welcome without interrupting our business dinner. The other bartender. THE FOOD: My Client had the hanger steak and I had the wagu beef steak. Both we amazing! Also very reasonably priced at 22 and 28. Cooked to perfection, portion was perfect. Absolutely spot on! THE BOOZE: They have every whiskey known to mankind, and a very up to date prohibition style cocktail menu. They have a great signature list as well. Here is the issue. The pricing was beyond sky high! It was as, if not more expensive than Manhattan. Actually it was like Dubai not Pittsburgh. EXAMPLE: The Woodford Reserve Sonoma Cutrer Bourbon which is one of my favorites that Chris Morris of Woodford makes. It's something I look for and generally, (from low end to high) around 18-35. This is across the country, from LA to Denver to Houston and Boston. I travel a lot for business and I can stand firm on this pricing model. Well, here it was 90 for a two ounce pour. OUCH!! And most of the cool whiskeys like this were outrageous. I won't dwell on the negative pricing anymore. IN CLOSING: I certainly don't want this to be a negative at all because I loved the place and will definitely visit again when I'm back in PBGH. However their booze pricing needs to be examined. It was the difference between a 5 star review and 4 starts for me. If they get the pricing to just industry standard, it will be a grand slam. I also want to try their other restaurant Meat Potatoes. I heard it was spectacular as well.

Wenn man die Architektur des Weinbrenner kannte und schatzte ist man schockiert, wenn man ins Besitos kommt und fragt sich, wie man solch schonen Raume derart mit pseudo-spanischem Dekor wie "El Puerto" und "El Barrio" gestalten kann. Vielleicht kann man das mit der meisten Blick auf den Weinbrenner machen, da die Gebaude in den letzten Jahren mit wenigen europaischen Bauten (oder anderen Stutzen) geteilt wurden, die man am besten mit den in den Blick halten kann. Allerdings lassen die Leute die Architektur so zusammenbauen, dass man diese direkt aus der Hand kann und dann nur die Dingen noch mal so anpassen muss, dass sie am besten passen. Wie lange noch wird es so gehen? Obwohl die Kunst und die Bibliothek der Bruder des Weinbrenners in den letzten Jahren einen breiten Umstieg und die Raumaufteilung fur eine breitere Blicke und Anspruche gemacht hat, scheint es in den letzten Jahren wieder alles von vorn zu kommen. Dabei gibt es hier einen Grund, warum das so ist. Die Bruder stellten bei der Besetzung 1973 den Blick auf den Weinbrenner zwischen 1973 und 1976 erstmals auf eine breitere Blicke in den Raum und deren Anspruche, d.h. eine groere Bucherwohnung und eine neue Kulturzentrale, ein. Nachdem sie diese beiden Wohnungen in den Raum und die neuen Anspruche 1976 aufgehoben hatten, stellten sie die Blicke und Anspruche auf eine bessere Umgebung im Besitos. Diese neuen Anspruche und die neuen Raumaufteilung in den Blicken, die sie in den letzten Jahren erneut aufgehoben haben, verdanken ihrem wirklichen, sichtbaren Eindruck allerdings nicht ihren Brudern. Es ist die "Mutter" des Besitos, die dieses Bild hinterlassen hat. Sie hat die Aufstellung der Bucherzimmer fur eine breitere Blicke in den Raum, die Durchfuhrung der Einrichtung der Musikkammer, die Reparatur der Sanatoriumkammer und die Anpassung der Kulturzentrale zum Besitos in den Blick gebracht. Es ist die "Mutter" der Besitos, die diese Aufstellung der Bucherzimmer und die Sanatoriumkammer und die Anpassung der Kulturzentrale zum Besitos in den Blick gebracht hat. Es ist sie, die fur die Weinbrenner-Bruder und das besagte Besitos zustandig war. Als das Besitos 1976 auf diese neue Anspruche, auf diese neuen Anspruche, auf diese neuen Anspruche, auf diese neuen Anspruche auf eine bessere Umgebung im Besitos und auf diese neue Anspruche auf eine bessere Umgebung im Besitos kam, war sie die "Mutter" des Besitos und das Weinbrenner-Bruder-Projekt. Und als sie diese neuen Anspruche auf eine bessere Umgebung im Besitos und auf diese neue Anspruche auf eine bessere Umgebung im Besitos erneut aufgehoben hat, hat sie die Weinbrenner-Bruder erneut in die Bruder-Besitos-Familie einfuhrt. Sie hat die Aufstellung der Bucherzimmer und die Sanatoriumkammer und die Anpassung der Kulturzentrale zum Besitos in den Blick gebracht. Es ist die "Mutter" der Besitos, die diese Aufstellung der Bucherzimmer und die Sanatoriumkammer und die Anpassung der Kulturzentrale zum Besitos in den Blick gebracht hat.

Thursday, May 13, 2007 My aunt and I were out to dinner at a restaurant in River Oaks (a restaurant chain that has several locations around Houston). The restaurant is called FG Restaurants, and they have a location at 4500 Eastheimer Road. We had just finished our dinner, and I had one glass of wine. As I was walking out, the waiter said, "You're not supposed to drink that." He said it was a rule. I said, "I'm a doctor, and I know better than that." The waiter then took my plate and said, "We'll put it in the kitchen." So I took my plate back to the kitchen, and they put it back on the table. The waiter then took the plate, and I asked him, "How long is this going to take?" He said, "Well, it's a pretty big table." So I said, "Well, just put it back on the table, and I'll just eat it." So he put it back on the table, and I ate my meal. We left, and as we were walking out, the waiter said, "We'll put your glass back on the table when you get home." I said, "I'm a doctor, and I know better than that." And he said, "Okay." The funny thing is, I'm not even sure what the rule is. It doesn't appear to be on their website. I'm not sure if I can prove this, but it does seem like the waiter was just making up the rule to get rid of me. I've had plenty of conversations with other waiter's who are just trying to get rid of me, too. It's really quite annoying. I have to wonder why a restaurant would make up a rule just to get rid of a customer. Do you know of any other restaurants that do that? What do you think of it? As fans of small business in general, and as a local business owner myself, my wife and I could not wait for Va Da Vie to open. The fact that they were setting up inside the Park Road Shopping Center, a favorite area of ours since we are only 1 mile up the road, was just a huge plus. For the past 8 weeks I have made it my mission to introduce everyone in my office to VaDaVie and even have made sure to make a stop for gelato a must when relatives have been in town. Usually I can count on the smiling face and warm greeting from the male owner which has more than made up for the cold shoulder you get from the female owner who is always there. Tonights experience turned the usual cold shoulder and kicked it up a few notches as my wife walked in past 8:00pm (8:12pm to be exact) as the door was still open and there were still people in line ordering and two women sitting enjoying their gelato inside; just what a new small business would like right?! Instead she received a very snarky I better lock the door or else people will just keep coming in from the female owner followed by the comment well I'm not going to turn you away now after my wife asked if she should leave. Well, my faith in Claim Jumpers has restored! We had a group function today, serving our local support team. Our appetizers came out before our meal and we were given the option of choosing additional sides to have with our meals (like stir fry vegetables or fries). Two party goers chose the side of broccoli cheddar soup, which I did not notice until after they left when the server said "oh sorry, that's all there is." They returned shortly thereafter and asked for more... They asked how much it was and the manager told them it would be 3 each. She didn't see anything wrong with charging her husband and herself an extra 6 since she saw no other options on the menu. That person promptly went back up front and got us another order of the broccoli cheese soup along with a copy of their receipt so we could dispute this charge. They also gave me her name and email address so if you are reading this please contact her directly at Nutrition: 810- The chef used the leanest meat possible from grass fed animals resulting in very few calories but high protein content. One of our entrees was made using ground turkey which added some fat as well, however, two of the three entree 'side items' were baked potatoes which will provide potassium and fiber without any saturated fats. Despite these positives, our portion sizes were quite large allowing a single person to consume over 1000 calories per day while two people can easily exceed 2000 calories. Our lunch entree consisted entirely of grains which provided good amounts of protein and B vitamins, the most important being thiamine, however, whole grain bread tends to lack iron, calcium and zinc. The one exception was the potato salad served with our sandwich. It contained as little as 1 oil AND had been prepped ahead of time by a different kitchen staff member making it virtually free of preservatives. Even though we ate our weight in carbs, we still managed to get nine servings of fruits and veggies between the three main dishes and the accompanying vegetable side. All in all, a very healthy meal except for the quantity served. Service Cleanliness: 910 - There wasn't a lot of interaction with the servers during the course of the event, however, everyone seemed pleasant enough and there were plenty of people around to take care of things. At one point we even noticed someone handling one of the tables doing something strange like wiping down the table top completely with sanitizer. While there was no visible evidence of food on the table surface, we figured better safe than sorry. My wife actually mentioned he might want to check his hands for grease afterwards. Other tables had tableside service where both parties received complimentary condiments such as ketchup, mustard and melted butter along with napkins. Thankfully, no one spilled anything on themselves. After the first round of food arrived, people started cramming into the dining room causing some guests to spill drinks and put pressure on the beverage stations (which are far too close together) resulting in a pretty significant mess. Some guests decided just throwing plates onto the floor was ok because they weren't going to eat them anyway. Old business cards and other paper products littered many tables and chairs throughout the restaurant. This kind of behavior really makes you wonder why they bother paying for such nice linens, glassware and furniture... Overall, cleanliness isn't usually my primary concern about an eatery but considering the price tag of this place it should be.

OK, already! After running across this restaurant several times in smartphone apps we decided to find Times Square and chow down on what was described as unbelievably good Italian food. Reviewers have got it right, this place is fantastic. Shea, our server was great and she knew the menu which is pretty extensive. Before I begin, be warned that the place gets crowded quickly around dinner time so an early arrival is suggested. Now for the food. First, the anti pasta is wonderful. It has all the ingredients an anti pasta is supposed to have. Most Italian restaurants nowadays just put some iceberg lettuce, a sliced tomato and if you are lucky, a pepperoncini. Times Square's dressing with the anti pasta was just right, not overpowering the decilicious vegetables and meats. The meats, wrapped around cheese or olives, were deliciousyou may read delicious once or twice in this review. The entrees are varied, substantial and, againdelicious with a capital D. We both had pasta dishes and the sauces were thick and yummy. Bread was served with the main dish, my only suggestion would have been for the bread to have been served with the anti pasta. Could not eat all of the food so take-home boxes were gladly volunteered. You will be slightly incredulous that this restaurant located where it is would be so great. It will be great. Times Square also serves breakfast, kind of unusual for an Italian eatery but no problem as far as I am concernedkeep serving incredible Italian meals and I am completely satisfied. (I hear the breakfasts are great by the way.) All in all, we will be back and can't wait to do so. Thank God there are great places like Times Square to move the chain Italian restaurants aside.

While I'm starting low because my experience hasn't been that great, I'm still willing to come back and try it again. Walking in the decor is modern hip diner with a play on the classic feel of an old fashioned lunch counter. It's very pretty - bright colors, even flowers all over. The drink menu has some interesting options: I really like the '60s Fizz.' The PBR is also good. But if you're going for something completely different, they have one called "Disco Sucks." And finally there are two specials every day (I was at their brunch), which include McCafe coffee drinks, special house wines, Bloody Marys, mimosas...also fun! They were super nice when we were seated outside; we got a bottomless cup of water before our food arrived. They brought us complimentary bread as soon as it came out from the kitchen too. Everything was delicious - what more can you ask? My wife had the chicken parm sandwich (14) served open-faced with lettuce and tomato, so she could layer cheese over the top herself. She said it was perfectly seasoned, but nothing especially noteworthy about texture or taste. There wasn't much meat either; this may be why her sandwich ended up only being covered by 2 slices of mozzarella. Maybe next time...she liked how fresh everything looked though. My friend ordered the corned beef hash melt (12). He says that both he and his girlfriend thought it tasted bland, not knowing that they might want a little saltiness to balance out its sweetness. Too bad, according to him, since it looks beautiful - browned bits of potatoes, onions, and mushrooms sitting inside a grilled bun. Unfortunately he didn't enjoy eating it straight out of the container, saying "it's cool looking...but way too sweet." Regardless, I think it would definitely make a solid addition to your breakfast plate without a problem. That crusty French toast egg casserole thing sounds tasty! Our waitress says they use cinnamon rolls and other stuff in them sometimes, although today she couldn't remember what exactly. We did get the crispy crab po' boy (15) poutinefried oystersshrimp cocktail combo appetizer (served hot!) that sounded really yummy during our meal. One reviewer suggested trying the O.J., 22.50, which is basically fried shrimp with spicy remoulade sauce on brioche buns. At least three bites should do it justice. Also available: steak fries, fryer basket, ramen burger, corn dogs, etc.

I was pleasantly surprised to see this small display featuring a substantial range of outdoor power tools and accessories. The same quality is still evident with all the products: great value for money on many items; some are marked VERY low by comparison! The large selection of power lawnmowers (including those from brands such as Deere, Makita, Husqvarna) have also been well received - the duct tape cutter looks like a good buy when you can get it for under 40. A few months back we purchased two of these machines at a very competitive price and were extremely happy with them. Both of our children had some time off school recently so sat down to have a look around. Their big attraction appears to be that they both cost under 400!!! They would certainly make an excellent addition to any garden or paddock. DON'T DO IT! Let me save you the wasted time and dinning dollars Every Sunday our family has what we call hot wings Sunday. World's smallest bar! I kept seeing Hef's and was excited to finally go there. Total let down. The staff was friendly but the drinks just weren't good. The couple next door were having a hard time finishing their pints of Guinness, so we thought it would be nice if we could help them finish up too. They ordered some more food as well because they knew what that meant in our world: another 10 bill for us. This place has been on my list forever; how cute is this? We went with friends from work who have never been anywhere before (we are all 18 years old). It wasn't very crowded when we got there, even though it started at 7pm. All in all it turned out great! I had heard about this restaurant through social media. When arriving around 5:30 pm on Friday night after several cups of coffee, we received an amazing surprise - two people outside waiting patiently in line for our table. We arrived 15 minutes early and found an empty booth right away. After ordering the starter platter, which included three different salads, one pasta dish, one seafood mushroom soup, seven mini pies (including pancakes waffles), four breadsticks, brownie sliders and bacon cheeseburgers cooked perfectly medium rare followed by smoked ham burgers and crispy French fries. My husband opted for a chicken Caesar salad while I enjoyed braised short rib lasagna with homemade baby back ribs. The waiter brought every single item to our table within five minutes and also told me not to worry if any dishes didn't arrive quickly since he will pass the items along to others faster than anyone else can get it done himself. Even though the prices aren't cheap, you should definitely try these foods especially during your first visit. Try everything you see here, it's worth it!!! From what I've read online, everyone says this restaurant is delicious, however I am still undecided whether or not its really worthy of being rated as one of the best restaurants in NYC. We decided to take advantage of our free Monday lunch offer and headed over afterwards to check it out ourselves. When entering the building you immediately notice the custom-made mural painted across the front window which features a large photo of a man wearing sunglasses holding a glass of beer looking into his camera phone. Inside you'll find lots of vintage artwork hanging on walls as well as tables decorated with bright red flowers. Our server Tom came by a few times throughout the meal asking us about various aspects of our orders such as where we wanted our wine served etc... During later portions of the meal he offered suggestions based off the seasonality of certain ingredients like pumpkin pie spice cookies and vegetables. Overall, we felt comfortable enough discussing things with him without fearing he might skip something important.

RA sushi is so-so for sushi. It's not spectacular, but usually not terrible either. A group of us (7) came on a Saturday night and while we expected a wait, it was over an hour and a half! I've had the Veggie Lover's Roll before and it's good. The Mango Crab Salad is a good starter.

The Spice Market buffet was really disappointing. The shrimp, wild mushroom stew, strawberry cream cake and bread pudding were the only redeeming dishes. The crab legs had the frozen seawater The rest of me did enjoy the desserts. I ordered a chocolate mousse with raspberry Macchiatos for dessert.I think the cocktail wine with the red fruits was a bit sweet.

Perfect place. Designed to a T. Edgy and classy. Service is excellent. Drinks are tasty. Food is creative and delish. Coffee is the best- but beware is espresso. Patio seating I had the apple fritter and the egg sandwich. Great combination.

I booked Paris because I received comp room and I couldn't resist, so I booked it right away. The entrance is always full of people crossing but so is Bellagio and Mirage, the valet area was taking forever to park my car but that was no biggie. Checking in took 20 minutes but the front desk woman was very friendly checking me in and told me the pool was open 24 7 but I should be cautious because of no lifeguards being on duty. That was a plus for the pool being open 24 7 but the weather was too cold to go night swimming. Casino wasn't as stuffy and was pretty clean to me. My room was very clean and updated with the flat screen TV and the mini fridge was a huge plus, so no need to bring coolers to Paris unless you have lots of food and drink to bring. It beats going back and forth for ice. The room was clean and has a French contemporary design and is not to shabby for a basic comp room and your hardly in your room unless you're here for work and no play.:o I request a non smoking king bed with a strip view but they they only had 2 queen so I opted for that. I do like looking at the view from my room to relax and enjoy the scenery but it was nice to get what I requested despite checking in late. I would come back and stay here again if it was comp and a deep discount. Even though they don't have wifi, the internet on my smart phone still works so yay for me.)
The food is great, and the staff are so nice and friendly. I will definitely be back.

Wow, first of all, I'm from Socal and I didn't expect to find a gem of a sushi joint like this in vegas. Didn't feel like paying big bucks for overrated pricey sushi joints on the strip, so we decided to hit this place up as a recommendation from a friend. I was blown away by how many items they had on their AYCE menu. Suppppper thrilled to order every single item possible to try. Their nigiri was superb because the fish was really fresh and sweet. The best has to be the white tuna! The sweet shrimp and uni definitely had to be my favorite, and it sucked that you can only order it once. All their rolls were very unique and each one satisfied my tastebuds. The best part was that they allowed half orders on the rolls, so you can try more! The icing on the cake was the selection of ice cream at the end. From tempura, to mochi, to red bean.... It was heaven Can't wait to come back to Vegas in 2 weeks and hit up this spot again. BEST AYCE sushi I've ever had, and that's coming a lot from someone who's had multiple hot spots in socal. THUMBS WAY UP

Food Is good. Service is slow. Large salads and sandwiches with plentiful sides. Burger was cook ed as ordered. Their special sauce is killer good. Peppery spicy alone but on the burger is fantastic. Cuban sandwich is large and filling and delicious. Brownie Ala mode is enough for two, maybe three. Order dessert only if you are not pressed for time. Took over 30 min to get dessert menu, order and stated eating. It will take 1 hour for entree and another for dessert. Hard to get into a lunch hour.

Sadly, Snottsdale denied the light rail a home, so I have to drive to work (or take my bike on the rail and then ride my bike for another 20 minutes uphill)....I may as just well bike the whole way. Great value, 5 for a day pass, ride it all you want. Don't understand the crabby attitudes of some of these reviewers. Drive your gas guzzler all you want and stay off the light rail if you hate it so much.

Got the Mango smoothie w pearls. For some reason, it wasn't that flavorful. I don't just mean it wasn't sweet enough (it wasn't). I mean it was hard to tell if there were any good, but not too bad at all. I've been looking for a smoothie recipe and you have brought me one!

Delicious, but expensive. Dined here a few weeks ago and I just remembered right now how awesome the dinner rolls were. They looked sweet from the glaze on top, but tasted like cinnamon sugar (which is my preferred flavor of side.) Those little savory bread sticks are pretty good too
Horrible service! Overpriced and dirty! I wouldn't go back to this place and don't recommend it to anyone!

Another great Groupon find. Teakwoods is kind of tough to describe - it is like 34 sports bar and 14 lounge. On one side they have big, burly tables with lots of TVs up on the wall, showing every available example of athletic competition. And golf, too. On the other side, they have pub-style tables and an area for local music to come in and play. The place - even though it borders on Snotsdale - was unpretentious and populated with an eclectic crowd of folks. I saw cowboy boots, jauntily-cocked bowler hats, and a tatted up chick stuffing sugar packets in her purse. I was charmed. The boyo and I have been back several times since. The wings, as noted by others, are really good. In our case, we go for boneless as neither the boy nor I particularly enjoy sucking hot sauce from under our nails. The wings are always tender, and have great flavor. Service is usually pretty good - sometimes a little slow, but.... whatevs. Throwing peanut shells all over the place is enough to keep me entertaining while I wait for my beer. (To the person who complained about the dusty, dirty nuts in the buckets.... don't suck on the shells. Duh! The nuts are well sealed inside their safe, dirt-proof casings and are totally tasty when you crack'em open. With your hands.) I wouldn't recommend Teakwoods for folks who aren't into meat. Not a lot of variety for someone who doesn't want beef or bacon on some form of bread. But the Chicken Philly is muy yummy (I eat it every time we go there). The boyo has worked his way through a number of interesting varietys of ground cow with toppings, and has enjoyed them all (except the sliders - he found them dry). Ultimately, we would definitely (and have already) go back. I think we've been 3 times so far - twice with groupons (and we have another one to use), and once at full price. Always a nice, relaxing night out.

Crazy busy airport with long wait times at security. Plan ahead! That said however, this is a pretty decent airport. There are plenty of food options with both local and national chains, there are cute stores to buy Southwest themed treats, toys and take-homes, and the walkways (once you're through security) are pretty wide. I also found the bathrooms to be tidy as well as the carpets in the gate areas. I know that's odd to mention but dirty carpets really gross me out and this airport seems to be nicer than many I've been to recently. Go PHX!

I have loved this place for a long time. It troubles me that people write such negative things in their reviews. Hi, it costs money to have a credit card on my account and they do not care about the customer service or customer support. I am very annoyed because after spending so much money in online shopping, I am now going back to other websites when the cost of credit cards are high too! Hope you can find something better!! Ahead of a new year, I decided to purchase some books from Amazon and read them before bedtime. On Tuesday morning at 7:30am, my husband and I went into the kitchen to check out the books we had purchased. We were both wanting to get some books that were supposed to be an active read in our house. So, we left our children alone (this is why the kids liked reading) and walked through the kitchen into the living room. The book was called "Nothing But an Earthly Read" by Chris T. Burns. It contains everything one would expect from a book. They didn't like it but they wanted to read it anyway. We gave it a good review and got it put together. It has been so nice to see that there is still more to learn!!!! After getting all the books set up, the first thing we did was unload the books. This happened around 11pm. My son was waiting patiently outside the door until I answered his call. His name was Chase and he wanted to know if any of us knew anything about this book. He told me that when we found out we had requested free copies of this book, we could go ahead and order them until he arrived. So, we spent a lot of time making them available provided that anyone who wanted them would email us their names. As soon as we received our orders, we went inside to talk with the seller. During this conversation, she started asking us questions. She said that when she bought our two books, she saw that we already had a few copies of this book and asked what we should select (If we choose to buy this book, please tell her where it comes from!) Chase then followed him to another location. When we finished our search, she asked if we wanted to take this book with us. After she told us yes, she asked if we wanted another copy, which we replied in the affirmative. When she finally said no, we continued our search. Then, she sent us a picture of our second copy of this book, she also said that this book will make a great gift. Chase also informed us that he planned on buying our current copies. He even ordered two copies. For those who have two copies of this book, we thank you. We want to help others find their own ways to enjoy reading these books. You can ask your friends or family members to give us these books either via our website or Facebook page. If you don't mind having a friend bring your books to your home, create a personal blog or post something related to this topic here. Or just approach someone that lives close to you and say "Hi, I'm Chase" and meet up at their house. Sometimes such conversations usually involve an informal group chat. Please let me know what's behind his comments, please let me know how to feel whenever I hear them. Thank you again and sorry if this sounds like it isn't clear enough for you!

I tried their pizza on different occasions, different toppings but..... I just don't like it. It's tasteless and somewhat expensive. I always have to add either Parmesan cheese or garlic salt to make it taste like pizza. We have other better choices in town. I can't recommend it. We stopped in last weekend to eat on our way to Knoxville. The food was good. They have a nice variety of sandwiches and desserts. We got a slice of pizza to go and it was delicious. If you are in the area and hungry give them a try. Honestly one of the best pizza's I've had in a while. Not a huge place but you can tell they take pride in their food. The pizza had great flavor and a nice crisp on the bottom. I will definitely eat here again when I'm in the area. We stopped here on our way home from the beach for lunch. The pizza was good but I had the Italian Sub which was really good! The bread was crunchy but not hard. Food was good. Nothing special. Price is high for what you get. The staff was friendly and place was clean. Not a bad place to eat. There are few really good pizza places left. This one is the best. There are other items on the menu, but we love the pizza. There's a great atmosphere with some TVs, but not a bar. Really good pizza, and family friendly! Our favorite pizza place! Service is always great and the pizza is amazing! Went to Isabekka's tonight. Got poor service and excuse of communication error as to who was our server. Not acceptable. I tried the "Ice Cream" which is a special for 4.00 (so, not cheap!) It tasted like it had chunks in it but she brought me another one so no ill will there. The food was good though! I went with my mom on Tuesday night before going out for dinner at Giovanni's. We got the place mostly taken care of since we were early diners so they didn't have all their reservations filled yet...that meant that when we walked into the restaurant, the hostess was still behind the desk asking people what table they wanted. So, we asked her to get us an outside booth because we needed some privacy from other tables since this floor plan has a lot of walkways between tables. She took us back to where the manager told her about us being meal trays and didn't think we'd be able to sit together. Both meals came with salad, sweet tea, chocolate chip cookies and to top off our order we both opted for coffee drinks instead of water or soda. (all prices per person) Before leaving, we remembered we forgot to leave change and offered to pay later. They declined and even put the money down on the tab because we are regulars here. Overall we were very impressed with everything except the bill came totally unexpected and just as we finished eating. Before paying the bill, the waiter called up the hostess again to explain for why things turned around on the bill. When the owner saw the extra charges he immediately paid us through his personal credit card. He assured us they would take better care of us next time. All bad feelings aside, we can say without question that Isabella's Mexican Cafe is now 1 stop when taking family outings because we love the family atmosphere and wonderful staff. If only every business followed suit!!:) Mikey Gourdough's Pizza Pub.A new addition to town by the owners of Calhouns Bar-B-Q.This is the first pizza pub located anywhere near mid Georgia, although many cities have been experimenting with this concept lately. Mikey Gourdogh's Pizza pub offers pizza made right in front of you using 100 organic flour. The pizzas are big enough to share if desired. There is great beer selection and sports events shown on a large screen TV. Open air dining with lots of seating inside and out. Live music often featured. Good quality bar fare available too. Very popular during football season. A quick trip across town will land you within walking distance of Downtown Atlanta. Just returned from lunch today. Great ambiance and friendly folks working there. Service was excellent. My son did point out the possibility of getting two entrees rather than sharing, particularly if you're ordering soup. The price seemed high given it was Thursday and the location doesn't look busy. Other than that visit seems fine. The mahi tacos are fantastic. Try the pollo de calamares taco...you won't regret it!!! Also try the crispy fish tacos with avocado crema. Awesome snack items include cornbread muffins and churrasco sandwich wraps....great value and tasty!

One of my favorite places in Pittsburgh! You cannot go wrong here. Very extensive beer menu, great sandwiches, and wings. Could be my favorite wings of all time with a great variety if flavors. Sandwiches are fantastic as well. Many many beers to choose from. What more could you want?

Typical old-style casino and hotel. My first impression was good. It's nicely taken care of on the outside with lots of parking. 2nd impression: Really smelly. It wreaks of smoke and just oldness. I hated that, but I'm not a smoker. 3rd impression: great customer service! The employees must be well-taken care of and well-trained. They were smiling, happy and a joy to be around. 4th impression: Room is older, but remodeled. It's comfortable. I had a nice view of the mountains and part of the strip. It wasn't as clean as I like. The granite table top in the room is beautiful but the de sign was so busy it made it difficult to see all of the residue left from prior meals. It was really sticky, the bathroom door had finger prints all over it, the baseboards of the bed were muddied, and a beer can was forgotten under the armoire. The bathroom was spotless though!! And nicely remodeled with a neutral marble and tile. This is not a classy hotel but it is cheap, close to Chinatown, has a reportedly killer dim sum restaurant and has really great customer service.

Used to be a regular at bazix. But now the servers here are disgusting. It's even empty here now on the weekends (when it used to be packed). It's EMPTY HERE NOW. Only old folks come and eat and talk. That's telling you something. And waited. And waited..... After about 40 minutes and three diet cokes, I overheard a conversation between the manager and my waitress. Mind you the place is open, which means the grill is in view, the shake maker, etc. I wasn't even near the center and was able to hear. My waitress told the manager that one of her customers wanted a soda instead of a shake. The manager told her too bad, the deal comes with a shake, so they needed to pay for the soda. Were they talking about me? I always expected to pay for my soda, since it was an extra item. Mind you, I still didn't get my shake, but the manager who was making the shakes was VERY concentrated on making shakes. I mean 5 minutes to make per shake concentrating. That's all he did was make shakes, rather slooowly. I saw maybe 6 made in a 40 minute window. A few minutes later, my food arrived. I reminded the waitress I ordered a chocolate shake, to which she said ok, and walked away. She scooted to her manager, and said problem solved, he wants a chocolate shake, to which the manager replied too bad. I was really hoping he had a dry, sarcastic personality like me. So on to the food. The burger was delicious. It had a little too much mayo, but I guess that's why they wrap it in paper. The bun was rather large and a little cold, like it just came out of the fridge, but it was good. The pickles were thick, the burger had a few crispy, overcooked spots, but flavorful. For some reason I expected a tiny patty, but it was a good size. It was worth buying. The fries on the other hand, cold. I like salt on my fries, so nothing irks me more than getting cold, unsalted fries. Yuck. After eating extra leisurely, in hopes of eventually getting my milkshake, it never came. I waited about 10 minutes after I ate, and got my check, but no shake. At least I didn't have to argue about the bill, since I was charged only 3.99 for the deal of the day. I gave the waitress a 20. bill and got back 5. and change. What??? After I walked over to my waitress, and explained I only got 5, she apologized and gave me back 10. As this occurred, the disgruntled manager making milkshakes gave a dirty glare and snicker to the waitress and I. I got the hell out of there as quick as I could. Would I return? No. I may be willing to pay 2.99 for a burger a la carte, if they offered it. Instead, you have to order a burger and all-you-can eat fries for 5.99. I asked if someone can get the burger alone to go or to eat in, and was told no. A soda cost 2.50, and a shake 4.29, definitely not worth the price. Everything was slow motion, like my time machine back to the 1950's broke and I was stuck in slow motion. It took almost an hour to get a burger and fries. I'm sure it would have been an hour and a half if I ever got the milkshake. The service was horrible, but when you look at the manager it's no wonder. These poor miserable kids are a slave to the 1950's with a manager who is rude and disrespectful not only to the staff, but also to the customers. I would also have a hard time enjoying my job and going to work under those conditions. I know these restaurants are franchised, so hopefully the manager was not the owner. Either way, good luck trying to stay in business with him schlepping around.

The place has a warm and inviting bistro feel, although a bit sparse as you move away from the bar area to more intimate tables further back in the room. A sojourn into the drinks menu would suggest an attention to detail goes far beyond just your standard dry martinis or margaritas here: there was a very long list of unique cocktails with names like "The Devil's Own," "Not Quite As Bad As Bourbon" and my personal favorite "Live Dangerously." Overall, it felt pricey compared to some other local bars where 10 gets me two mixed drinks. I can't say enough good things about this small eatery near Metro State University! It is clean, organized, well decorated, brightened up by lots of light wood accents and natural sunlight coming through huge windows. When dining alone it might be impossible to avoid having conversation interrupted unless you order one of the booth seats at the rear of the restaurant - great if you're going out to eat with friends. The food was delicious - my husband ordered Chicken Pot Pie and loved it plus he tried something new called 'Curry Nachos' - yummy!! Prices were reasonable for the quality of food served. This is definitely somewhere I will return again soon once I get over my craving for curry nachos:)

I used to have one of those Gourmet Society cards and their website told me I could get a 25 discount at Chop Chop. Excellent. I had friends coming to stay and they had all heard of the place and wanted to try it. So I rang and booked a table and told them on the phone that I had the card. They said it would be fine to use it. You've got to love a discount! There were four of us and we are not good decision makers so we ended up opting for the unlimited banquet for four. Lots of variety and you can have seconds (and thirds, fourths and probably fifths if you could fit them in - it's unlimited after all) at no extra cost. Hurrah! The food arrived in a higgledy piggledy kind of way in no particular order but that was fine as there were so many different dishes it was rather nice to be able to sample them a couple at a time. It was all delicious and we had second helpings of several different things. I was tempted by third helpings but was pretty full at that point so exercised some restraint. And then we asked for the bill. And this is where it all went wrong. When I got out my Gourmet Society card I was abruptly told that they no longer accepted them and we couldn't have our discount. I protested saying that I had been told on the phone that it would be ok. The waiter went to get the manager who came out and spent some time angrily grilling me on who I had spoken to when I booked the table (what day did I call, what time, did I speak to a man or woman, what accent did they have...?). I tried to be as vague as possible because, clearly, someone was going to be in a lot of trouble and I didn't want to be responsible for that. Eventually he grudgingly let us have the discount but by then the damage had been done. I had high hopes for Chop Chop but now have the impression that, though they serve lovely food, they treat their staff really really badly. Never say never.... but I'd certainly be reluctant to spend my money there again.

We had 100 tip set aside for the DJ. We chose not to give it to him.

I know, I know. It's Red Lobster. It's been at least 10 years since I set foot in one. But Hubby and I watch the Food Network, and on Sunday we saw Kelsey win the Fresh Fish Challenge on the Next Food Network Star. It was an odd sounding dish- Macadamia Tilapia with White Chocolate Beurre Blanc- and Hubby decided he had to try it. So I got a couple of gift cards using my AmEx points (so if it was awful, at least we weren't paying for it). Hubby's Advice to Yelpers: Get over your disdain for chains and do not miss this dish. Kelsey is some kind of bizarre genius. And I have to agree. I never would have thought this would be good, but it totally works. The tilapia was perfectly cooked, crusted with a generous amount of toasted macadamia nuts, and sitting in a pool of beurre blanc with a light taste of white chocolate. For Top Chef fans, this was NOT anything like Dale's butterscotch scallops. It was subtle and unexpectedly amazing. My dinner was fine. I had the honey and citrus glazed grilled skewers of shrimp and scallops. The scallops were overdone, but the shrimp were cooked well and the glaze was a really nice complement to them. Conclusion: Go for the Kelsey special. It's the real deal.

We had broken down at around 7am somewhere along the highway between Phoenix and Palm Springs. At least we were able to get some food before continuing our journey. We finally made it to San Francisco by 10pm, exhausted but happy to be together once again. It took us about three hours just driving through the night because everyone wanted to stop off for dinner or some sightseeing. The next morning after having breakfast together, we went straight back to work. My boss said we could only leave early so long as I finished everything on time. And when he came over to check if there was anything else I needed, I told him not really since I was done already. He then asked me if there is anyone left and I replied yes, two others. He then apologized and informed me that he would have to let them go as well and that they wouldn't make it home until 11pm. He also mentioned how many days we still had left and I started counting: 14 more days...I didn't want to think about what that meant. How much money would I lose every single day that happened? By the end of the week, we lost 500 dollars per person. I thought about going home but then decided against it. What good would it do for me to come home? No one would help me anyway; everything would fall back to where it stood originally messed up customer service, missing supplies, etcetera. So I stayed behind; worked even harder than usual and figured all this misery will eventually pass and put things right. That is until one afternoon when I arrived late into the office and noticed something different about the place. Things were being rearranged and equipment was moved around which meant that I might be gone soon. I had never heard of something like that happening in my entire life. I sat at my desk reading a newspaper while trying to focus on other tasks. After the paper became too boring, I pulled out my calculator and started adding up numbers. This is serious business, you know! The next day I received an official letter stating that my position would now become a part-time employee. They did say they'd keep paying though, but I wasn't sure whether or not I should accept their offer. After thinking about it some more, I called the Payroll lady who helped me during the hiring process. She sounded very apologetic and promised her best effort in ensuring I receive paychecks every month. All she could tell me is that due to budget cuts, they'll have to let most people go including myself. I felt sick hearing those words from her and changed the subject immediately. I quickly began searching online for new jobs hoping I can find a permanent solution. Then again why would I expect anything different when companies are always laying people off and downsizing branches? That's when I remembered this trip I've been planning ever since last year. I knew I couldn't leave the children alone in such dire circumstances especially now that school had begun. Plus I don't mind teaching either, so why should getting paid back be such a big deal? In fact, it would be the perfect opportunity for me to practice my English skills lol My plan was simple actually: Leave my hometown once again and try to teach in America. All I need is some experience working at least 3 months under my belt and I'm set. Maybe it won't turn out to be completely bad. Right now it sounds like the best option available. So far my plans haven't changed. I'm moving forward slowly yet steadily gathering necessary documents for my move. Hopefully I'll start our journey sooner rather than later. If all goes according to plan, I am expecting to arrive in August and arrive safely here in America.

Oh Caps. I used to love you! You upgraded your TV's and downgraded your service. Last year I loved going there for early football games with my family. We'd eat hot dogs and listen to the game on the big screen. Now the food is awful, the concession prices are outrageous and the service is so slow. Plus, I can watch the game anywhere else on the Internet. The only reason I go there anymore is for the gameday atmosphere. I have no other place to watch the game. Can I help it if I want to see the game on the big screen and hear the crowd? I guess I'm just not cut out for the corporate culture of the NHL. In my opinion, the NHL should be about the fans. I love going to the games and spending money on food and beer. The players should take note of what is happening and try to keep their fans happy. The Caps have a great fan base. It's time to take a look at what is going on. There's no excuse for the poor service and bad food. The cost of the tickets and concessions is also outrageous. If the Caps are going to stay in DC, they need to be more in tune with the fans. I am so disappointed in the way the Caps treat their fans. This isn't a good example for the NHL. Maybe they should consider moving the team. That way they can start fresh. The new team could start with the name of the current team, but call it the Washington Capitals. They could make the uniforms and the logos exactly the same. The only difference would be the team name. Fans would be loyal to the new team because of the name. It would be like getting a new team. There would be no need to buy new tickets or concessions. Maybe the new team would be a big hit in the market. I just hope that the NHL does not move the team to another city. I'd rather see them go somewhere like Chicago or Detroit. Those are two big markets and the NHL needs to expand to them. Let's face it, Washington DC is not the NHL's market.

This is a bit of a tongue in cheek tour for the tourists. Having seen the vaults on several programs on the TV we thought we would go see. The first thing that struck us was how different it looked from what I had expected, and how big it was! We all went up to the top floor and climbed up through these little passageways with a seemingly endless staircase. While we were there we took pictures at every turn looking down into the tunnels below. This really gave me an idea about just how many people lived underground. It's amazing how much life can fill up a small area like this. After our walk around we decided to try out some other things they have here called "Museum Chairs." These are chairs you sit in while you're watching a show or museum exhibit. They allow you to take in the atmosphere without having to leave your seat. If you want to make sure you don't miss anything you can always look ahead to the next screen or wall to see if something else is going on. We sat for quite a few hours as they played their shows while we watched. This museum was great because it allows its visitors to interact with the exhibits so easily instead of sitting back and taking everything in. The best part about this place though was seeing Dan's face light up when he saw the mural on one of the walls "The Great Wall of China." He said that he would love to visit China someday soon. After walking around that area we headed over to where Dan had his bike parked before the trip started. There were numerous information boards detailing various places within China you could visit and stay for free. Our favorite was definitely the National Palace Museum which had displays on fire fighting, military history etc. You wouldn't even need to sign up to get in since you could simply walk right in. As we were leaving we noticed a couple of older Chinese men chipping away at the side of a building behind bars. We asked them why in the world they were doing work there and found out that they'd been arrested for breaking and entering. It turns out that it takes a lot less money than it does to build a building nowadays to break someone's foot. Although it did bring a smile to my face to think about!

Hang with me here...... I had a vertebrate paleontology class in college. Our professor often discussed the lack of evolutionary changes in crocodilian species over the course of millions of years while other species have evolved all sorts of other features. He basically said it's not possible to do what they do any better. A bigger brain means they'd probably lose jaw muscle. Larger body size means they'd probably lose some of their ability to sneak up on prey. Over the course of millions of years, these things would be a big deal. But I'm not happy about the 777X, the newest product to come out of the 787 line, and which uses the same batteries. When the 787 gets fixed, that fix will go to the 777X program. But the 777X program is already behind schedule. And I expect that, because of the battery issue, 777X deliveries will be delayed further. This place is only awesome if you are one of three things: 1. an Ohio State fan, 2. a metrosexual, or 3. someone trying to hook up with an Ohio State fan. The first thing you notice is that the place is dark and the second thing you notice is that the beer is expensive. The food is mediocre at best, with most people coming here to get a bite to eat after the bars close at 2 am. The menu does offer a variety of choices for the vegetarians and vegans in the crowd, which is nice. The service is friendly, but sometimes slow. Most of the time I have been there has been at least one television turned to Ohio State football, so you have to be a fan of the Buckeyes to really enjoy the place. I really hate Ohio State, so the whole atmosphere of the place is kind of annoying. The crowd here seems to be a mix of college students and young professionals, so there is a good chance that you might be able to meet someone. The big problem is that the place is dark and cramped, so if you have a problem with bumping into people, this is not the place for you. I think that the food is mediocre, with it being nothing special, but not bad either. The beer prices are definitely on the high end, so you are definitely paying for the atmosphere when you come here. In my opinion, this place is worth a shot, but I would not go out of my way to go here. It does not really have a neighborhood pub feel to it, and the food is nothing special. I do not understand why there is no live music on the weekends, as that would be a huge draw. That being said, this place is more about the people than the food, so if you are looking for a place with a variety of people, this is the place. Review by: Katie on 2182014

I take my family here (a bunch of picky-eating-indian-oldies) and they LOVE IT. With a good amount of spice in their dishes, this place is a go to if you like Thai. This is a must go place! I have been a regular at the Deer Valley location, and this lactation is just as good. Same great food, and same great people! The atmosphere is nice and upscale. My only regret is that I do not live closer!

Was stoked to see this little coffee shop while wandering PHX during a long layover. The menu boards in the back showed Aeropress, Hario V60, Clever, and Chemex at MKT price points with pricing available through their website. I've tried some of these machines at home but have held off on purchasing one because they were too expensive for my budget. So excited that I finally caved and picked up an Aeropress! So what did we get? A classic espresso blend, fresh mocha frappucino and light passion tea lattes! Can you say perfection?! In addition to those offerings there are several other espresso drinks listed such as espressos, shots, cappuccinos, and lattes (which is exactly what it sounds like). For me personally, an aeropress isn't about how much milk or water gets used per shot; its more about using a larger cup than regular cups so that the shots stay fresher longer. I don't usually drink caffeine ... You know what I mean right?! But after trying the AeroPress and seeing all the mouthwatering photos online I decided to give it a try. It was super easy to use without any tools needed: simply place the basket into the juice section and pour your favorite liquid of choice into the percolator. After putting it together with my Aeropress stirrer it took about 10 seconds to get ready. After steeping for 5 minutes both my latte and frappe tasted amazing! As soon as the brew process started, I noticed a bigger difference in taste between the two blends than other types of coffees I had before. They didn't taste sweet because of the more acidity found in the drink, also not over-sweetened which is something I often find happens when my coffee has a lot of sugar added. The flavor of the drink itself was smooth and not bitter. Of course I could tell immediately if I drank too much by feeling nauseous the next day. This is definitely one of those "don't eat anything within 6 hours" things that comes from caffeine intake and doesn't go away unless you stop drinking it altogether. Not sure why I would want to do that out of curiosity... The only gripe I have with this machine is (and this might be only me) but sometimes the bottom language of the screen can look scratched up or faded - just like mine looks. Other than that though I think this thing is absolutely worth every penny. No matter where you live, shopping around for the best deal shouldn't cost you a fortune. If you're willing to pay a bit extra for it then you'll definitely enjoy the results because you're getting amazing quality for the money.

He also really knows how to work an audience: there was one point where he asked everyone who had someone die recently to raise their hand...and no-one did. What?! So he made some lame joke about people dying like "all the time." Then after asking again later during another part of the show, half the room raised both hands. Another example of him working the crowd was when he told one story from his childhood involving his mother calling out for help while she lay drowning. At first he played it off as if he wasn't serious, pretending that he saw her laying there in distress and called for help with nobody coming. However once you realized what was going on, it became absolutely hilarious. It got funnier still after he explained to the whole audience exactly why his mom died in such tragic fashion. And believe me, his explanation is quite graphic! But to see a comedian say something totally outrageous without any hesitation or holding anything back is kind of refreshing. He was performing at 3 pm Saturday afternoon and tickets cost 25 each (plus tax) which included free drinks and appetizers before the show started. If only he could have stayed through dinner!

We were in Las Vegas one week ago, We purchased a one day ticket for 12 each because we were wanting to get from the Wynn area down to the airport and then take off. That seems to be changing with the influx of visitors coming in and out of Australia. As far as I am aware, most touristy places have not been reopening yet. Next door to us they closed their doors and started booking meals online only and sold anything they could find while they were open. In fact, we ordered a buffet lunch to enjoy. So I decided that we would order some ice cream to drink to help keep us happy. Since the store was pretty small, everyone got their own chairs and tables to sit on. Are you ready to hear about the East Valley's best kept secret? Once you experience Superstition Ranch Market, you'll be a fan for life! Here's the story: They've been around since the 60s. The building looks like it. They do no advertising. There's no Muzak playing in the store. And because of all that, and because they own their own trucks, and because they have many deals grandfathered in with regional growers, their prices can't be beat for fresh produce! Whenever I make pepper steak, I could go to WalMart or another grocery store and pay 2.99 for a red bell pepper.... or I could go to Superstition Ranch Market and pay 25 cents, as I did yesterday. Yesterday I paid 5.75 for two large bags of produce, and when I went to WalMart, I figured out if would have cost me 11.84 for the exact same items! Here's how the comparison stacks up from yesterday, WalMart Neighborhood Grocery Store vs. Superstition Ranch Market: Baking potatoes - WM 85 centslb, SRM 35 centslb Green bell pepper - WM 94 centsea, CRM 59 centsea Red bell pepper - WM 1.50 each (on big-time sale), SRM 25 cents each Red potatoes - WM 99 centslb, SRM 20 centslb Yellow onions - WM 48 centslb, SRM 39 centslb Need I say more? You won't be sorry.

Just walk away. While my specific waitress was doing her job everyone else was clearly slacking. The food was bad even for a chain, and the worst part might have been the wine. We got a bottle of chianti for about 22, and it was completely undrinkable. We were given a special menu because we had a coupon, and so I was a little hesitant to order anything that wasn't on that menu, but most of the things I wanted did not come in under our coupon limit. We ordered a couple appetizers and the chicken alfredo. The chicken alfredo was decent enough, though it was a bit salty for my taste. It was pretty much what I expected from an Olive Garden dish. It was a good size portion and would be filling for someone who didn't eat an appetizer. The appetizers are why I wouldn't recommend this Olive Garden to anyone. The breadsticks were way too sweet, in my opinion. They were ridiculous. But I have a problem with all breadsticks that they aren't nearly as crisp as they should be. The calamari was fried perfectly and very tasty, but the sauce was bland. Overall, I wouldn't bother getting either appetizer again. I was very disappointed with the service at Olive Garden. Drove into Pittsburgh really late at night. So late the city had pretty much shut up shop. Walked around Station Square for literally an hour passing this place three times before finally having lost all sense of reason and succumbed to the kitsch seafood decor, flying shark with mardi-gras beads in its mouth and party lights. I am allergic to crab but thought hey you only live once right?! and ordered the lobster and king crab steam pot from the extra super buff teenage waiter whose shirt was so tight I could not understand how he could carry around a tray full of food. He was pleasant enough and although the place was practically empty he was never around when I wanted him and always around asking if I needed anything while I was stuffing my face full of sea creatures. The steampot was fine but the whole box of spices they add to it completely ruin the dish and I shudder to think they try to do that to hide how not-so-fresh the seafood is..ugh..Well I didn't have my face in a toilet or have exploding diarrhoea after or die from sea creature poisoning so there's a plus. The prices are really high for what they serve but Pittsburgh is pretty far from the ocean. On the plus side I love trains and you can sit right next to the train line and not even hear them pass every 20mins. Also the view across to the city is amazing across the river framed by the monumental massive amount of bridges and you are literally steps from the funicular to walk off your dinner. So whats the lesser of two evils this place or the Hard Rock Crappe next door?

I must say it is tough to get a 5 out of me. This place however does it. Starting off, the outside and inside of the burger restaurant was carefully crafted. Colors are done right. Has a style if it's own. Ordering is straight forward. Burger - Drink and sides. Cost though I just think was a bit high, but in the end so worth it. My first time here so I went basic with a little chip crunch on top. Solid Dark Chocolate Milk Shake and the mix of sweet potato fries and regular fries. I will start with he fries. Delectable dish and I had the dijon and horseradish sauce. Spectacular! The dark chocolate milkshake was a proverbial happy punch to the stomach that was so good, I wanted more... Smooth and not overly chocolate. Just the right amount. Now the burger, I do love burgers and I have to shout out that the best one I have ever had is at the El Corral in Bogata Colombia. The beef standards there are so much different and better. However, BBP does a stellar job of setting the Angus beef standard there and giving us good quality beef.

I had the beginning stages of my bi-annual physical this morning...after the good doctor (and he is a good doctor...some of the best doctor jokes I've ever heard:) was finished prodding, poking and invasively examining me, I set my Yelp for'droid on healthy eating...the app thought I said hot doggies and took me to Famous Uncle Al's (hey, when a computer (no matter how small that computer is) tells you do something, you had better do it:) I am trying now to figure how to rate it...3 Stars?...4 Stars?...Pi Stars? (with apologies to Brian S for the blatant theft of Pi Stars: I don't know...this is a hot dog joint and there are rules...and Famous Uncle Al (not his real name, BTW) breaks nearly all of the rules! Lets take a look at the Rules of Hot Dog Joints, shall we:) - Crappy linoleum floors and counters, accompanied by a kitchen in severe need of a degreasing - Not available at FUA:) I swear, I have never seen a cleaner, brighter hot dog joint in my life...you could eat off the floor (or really, pretty much any horizontal surface) in here...the place is just kept in pristine condition:) - A cook who's seen better days and a little bit of attitude from the help - Also, sadly, unavailable at FUA:) The little family that owns and operates this franchise greeted me at the door, asked me to sit at one of their lovely clean tables, anywhere I wanted to sit and then waited on me at that table...what a novel concept...service with a smile:) - Crappy, wobbly little tables and a dingy, torn wallpaper motif (with the optional, but ever so popular, No Pest Strip dangling from the ceiling)? - Nothing remotely like that going on here:) FUA is open and bright, airy and nicely decorated...they have a nice big LCD TV set on ESPN, or the news or something like that...so I don't have to watch Lost reruns on my phone while lunching solo:) - Hot Dogs and buns from the what we didn't sell last week bin, served for your pleasure from a grease and water bath - Again, just not how they do things at FUA:) These dogs are alright...certainly on a par with any other decent hot dog joint and better than most:) They serve their variety of dogs in a variety of ways...if you don't see it on the menu as one of their standards, just ask:)...want a brat with mustard, celery salt, relish, red onion sauce and shredded (not melted) cheese?...they are only too happy to accommodate (and for not a lot of cash, either:) - The last rule they break is a doozy, though...hot dog joints are always little and underfunded...a hand to mouth existence for all but a fortunate few - not FUA...a public company traded under the symbol FDOG.OB...fdog?...really?...OK:) 2 dogs, wshredded cheese, and a large beverage set me back a cool 9.10 today...for a couple of very good dogs...hey, my physical was arduous...I needed the boost at lunch:) I didn't even have to stand in line for it:)

I didn't really need to add my review because there are so many and most agree that is place is great. This review is strictly for the pharmacy. IF YOU HAVE A CHOICE, GO ELSEWHERE! I've been here a few times and I always left a little irritated. This is the closest 24 hour pharmacy by me but I try to avoid it if I can. I usually wait until the next day to go to my usual CVS. Unfortunately, my mom needed her prescriptions right away. I drop off the prescriptions for my mom. The guy said it would take about 30-35 minutes. Okay cool! Since my mom had to take food with her medication, we decided to stay close by and order some food to go. We got back to CVS after about 45 minutes. It turns out that they haven't even started the prescription. They were extremely backed up and it would take 2 hours!! UMMM WHAT?! NO. I was quoted 30-35 minutes and the guy who was helping me earlier was no longer there. Then they told me it would be ready for me in 1 hour. Apparently, they couldn't do anything better than that. I don't understand why they couldn't fill it right then and there. If they had originally quoted me 2 hours, I wouldn't have made it a big deal. It's understandable that they are backed up and I would've gone home and went back. Oh the nightmare doesn't end there. When I go back to the pharmacy, it turns out that the insurance they had on file was expired. So the lady is trying to update it and whatnot. My mom's insurance company's system was down for a routine update. Now I can't pick up the prescriptions until the morning!! I understand that they have no control of that but WHY didn't someone check the insurance when I dropped off the prescription and when I tried to pick it up the first time?? UGHH.. AT LEAST the lady was nice enough to give my mom one pill from each bottle to tie her over until the morning! TL;DR I went to the pharmacy a total of FOUR times in a span of 12 hours just to get a prescription for my mom. What an ordeal!! Wasted gas and valuable time!

After weaving through the labyrinth that is the MGM Grand we finally stumbled on Emeril's just in time for our reservation. The view from outside in unimpressive and looks more like an indoor strip mall or, dare I say, a Food Court. The hostess was friendly and guided us to our table without issue. We were seated near the rear of place toward the kitchen. They have a really cool light fixture above the expo window and a see through glass to the kitchen. The waiter comes directly to the table and laughs at me for looking toward the kitchen and says no he is not here assuming that I was looking for Emeril. But then he adds in fact he is never here. This is not my first trip to a restaurant run by a famous chef, and I was not looking for Emeril, but I am sure that this would be lost on this arrogant jerk, so I said oh, I was just looking at the kitchen to which his response was you can do whatever you want. My wife adds cool, can we go back and cook and he replied I am sure you wouldn't be any worse than those guys. I thought this was an odd statement but after the meal I realized it was an honest account of how bad the food really is here. My wife got the baby spinach and blackberry salad. The dish came out and was she just ate the berries and nectarines. The dressing had absolutely no flavor so the spinach was ruined, The dish just didn't seem to come together; however, it was miles better than the heirloom tomato and avocado salad that was placed in front of me. This flop of a dish was nothing more than a poor way for the kitchen to reuse yesterday's stale cornbread, I picked through the tomatoes and avocado and left 85 of the dish in tact. The waiter cleared the plate away without asking any questions. For the next course, I decided to take a chance and try the trio of chilled summer soups. I am usually not a fan of cold soup, but with Emeril's reputation of nailing flavors, I thought this might be an interesting way for the kitchen to show off some cajun flavor. I was wrong. The tangy tomato soup was gross. The avocado lime was palatable but boring. The roasted pepper soup (that had Emeril's initial on it) tasted like sink water after soaking red bell peppers. My main course arrived and the meat was cold, all four little strips of meat on the plate. Of course this was no surprise because of the odd service style of this place. The food runners take food only as far as the servers area then your food just sits and waits for you. So we sat ten feet from our food and basically watched it get cold. The meat sat atop a small mountain of oddly fried potatoes that were rubbery as though they had been fried yesterday and reheated. The bread pudding was more like a bowl of day old Quaker oats that had congealed. I took some of the chocolate shavings from the banana cream pie topping and rescued this disaster of dessert. For a chef that is known for kicking flavors up a notch this place was several notches below acceptable.

Woohoo! Best Cirque show I've been to yet! Some might say I am biased because I have this love for Beatles music, but I think that the content of the show and the performers themselves were incredible. We went with Aunt Jill, Uncle Bob, and Aunt Kathy. I think the show was so good that it will be the first I ever buy on DVD. The show was really intense and kept us on the edge of our seats. There were the expected acrobatics, aerial acts, and clowns, but the show also had a little bit of a storyline. They would take a song and make a sort of skit out of it. For example, when they did "I Want to Hold Your Hand," they had people holding hands on the sides of the stage, and the "Rose" character (Rose is the girl who is telling the story of her life and how it has been affected by the Beatles music) would hold someone's hand and then they would do some cool acrobatics, and then she would move to the next person, and the next. It was very interesting to see a storyline in a Cirque show, and it made it even better than usual. The music was, as you might guess, wonderful. I've never been to a show where I knew all the songs they were singing. And the music was performed with a great band. They had some really cool instruments, like a harp, and a sitar. The costumes were really cool, too. They were sort of a mix between the 60s and today. And they weren't crazy and over-the-top, which is what you might expect from Cirque. They were just really cool, not so outlandish. The characters in the show were also really interesting and well done. Each had a personality and a storyline that went along with it. There were some characters we really liked, like the Blackbird character. She was really cool. She had this great voice and she was sort of a diva. There was also a character that we dubbed "Gandalf the White." He was the main guy in the show and he sort of directed everything. We thought he looked like Gandalf. One of the best parts of the show was the Ringo character, who was named Eggman. He was a clown who sort of did funny things on the side, while other things were going on. He was really funny and had us all laughing. The other thing that really made this show cool was the way it ended. The cast all came out for a grand finale, and we were told that we were part of the show, and we should all sing along to the last song. The last song was "All You Need is Love," and it was so fun to sing along and just be part of the show. Then, when the song ended, there were huge confetti cannons that shot confetti over the whole crowd. It was really cool, and definitely a good way to end the show. I would definitely recommend this show to anyone who likes the Beatles music, and even if you don't. It's a really great show, and a nice change from some of the others. Labels: Cirque du Soleil, Las Vegas

It was nice not having to deal with any bullshit trying to get onto the crowded dancefloor like you would have to do in, say, the Liquid Lounge.
