So yeah, kind of disappointed in the music selection-there are tons of hip hop songs that were played earlier in the evening; though I suppose none of them were worth paying 5 cover charge for anyway. Another disappointment came later in the night when the DJ started spinning nothing but rap tunes instead of his usual music mix between RB, soul, pop, house, etc. That just seemed really lazy overall and showed very little effort on behalf of whoever runs the playlist for Wild Knights weekly events. Anyways... Anyway....a few minutes after arriving in Bob Evans we ordered another round of beers and hung out with Scott while he continued nagging Chris about how lucky he feels whenever he gets free food at restaurants. Then Jennie arrived and pretty soon after Robert joined us too. Then Erin greeted everyone she possibly could...it seems she literally knows everybody in Columbus so it made sense why everything worked out perfectly and there were more than enough tickets sold to fill every table in both locations. Also thanks go out Jenna, the person responsible for getting the event together, making sure things ran smoothly and keeping track of money owed and all that fun stuff. As always our waitress Jennifer was excellent as well...she keeps becoming better and better at her job and makes going to restaurants feel almost like being home again! She definitely deserves extra credit points. As far as the meal itself goes - oh man, what can I tell you? This place is fantastic!! And yes, once again Jim got exactly what he asked for.....nothing short of perfection!! Starting off the meal with a glass of Chardonnay was perfect timing actually and went great with my starter dish called Chicken Marsala (9). For the small price tag attached to this dish I definitely received plenty of value - big chunks of chicken breast cooked medium rare topped with sauteed onions, bell peppers and mushrooms served atop a bed of pasta tossed with marinara sauce. Though it may sound overly simple sounding, let me assure you that this was absolutely amazing!!! Definitely among my top ten dishes ever eaten anywhere in Ohio. Scott, probably due to his allergy to tomatoes, loved his entree equally - the Garlic Steak Fries (12), also a special of the day. Very tasty indeed. My next plate contained two items from the daily specials section: Crab Cake Sandwich (10) and Seafood Nachos (13), both quite good although I felt the breading on the crab cake needed to be baked longer or something like that, perhaps tenderizing them slightly. Overall very enjoyable, however. Finally, Jim finished off dinner with a slice of Meatloaf Sundae (!), which sounds weird the way he phrased it doesn't it? Anyway, this dessert was tasty AND impressive to look at. At least 4 slices of meatloaf layered generously atop vanilla ice cream drizzled liberally with caramel syrup plus chopped nuts sprinkled overtop. What else needs to be said?! All in all, a successful outing with many laughs shared amongst family members.

I sat at the bar which was mostly regulars enjoying pleasant conversation and unwinding after the work day. Not being a regular, the bartender definitely addressed me much different and in a very sterile manner. We went to Mix with a party of eight to celebrate my friend's 30th birthday. While the views and the interior of the restaurant were amazing, the food and service was not what we had expected. The only thing I liked about our meal was a salad that came served with an egg on top! The waiters were very nice but they didn't seem like they cared much about us or knew much about their menu offerings. We asked for some recommendations on appetizer because nothing really jumped out at us from the menu as something we wanted to try. We did end up ordering two appetizers which turned out to be quite tasty: grilled shrimp cocktail and bacon wrapped dates stuffed with goat cheese. Our entrees also seemed heavy; we ordered the jumbo lump crab cake and filet mignon both of which lacked flavor in my opinion. Although it wasn't terrible, it just couldn't compete with other restaurants around town. Our server was very attentive throughout the night so we decided to stick around and have dessert. The chocolate fondue combination made by them looked delicious but the warm chocolates were cold when they arrived. My friends and I wanted to dig into them immediately since we thought the hot ones would melt quickly, however the desserts were too cold to eat. When our server brought out fresh hot bread pudding she said "I guess you can heat these" and pointed to the ice cubes inside. If these weren't supposed to be heated why put them inside? She never even checked if they got warmed enough before bringing them back to the table. Needless to say none of us finished any of our courses. Overall, I think the price point is pretty high compared to others around downtown so if you are looking for great seafood then this isn't the place for you. And although its probably due to the fact that we live here, but it doesn't look like there is anything'mix' about the atmosphere either.

Most sushi places end up with a bill with around 15-30person depending on how much you order or where you go. Unless you are going to be planning on eating a second dinner or drinking a lot, usually you need more food afterwards to settle your stomach. Mido sushi has all you can eat 20 sushi. I have been to places like this, such as Todai. The significant difference between Mido and Todai is that they ask you what you want to order and it is freshly made. The all you can eat also comes with a soup, salad, tempura, edamame, hot tea, and ice cream (get the mango, has a few chunks of real mango). I didn't waste too much space other than the sushi, and that is what I recommend if you want to get a bang for your buck. I think between the 4 of us, we ordered around 25 rolls of sushi. As much as the sushi was excellent, the service is a hit or miss depending on the mood of the servers. I think last night was a good night, but I have heard they can be crabs. I also heard they actually ask you why you don't tip at least 15. In my opinion, even though tip is very standardized, I still feel you have to earn your tip. My standard is 20 for far exceeding service, 15 for great service, and 12 for average service, 10 or sometimes less for poor service. When we entered, they had a disco ball and some music playing for someone's birthday. They should have had the Celebration theme song after the amount of sushi we chowed down!

NOCA is the epitome of a strip mall gem. From the outside, it looks like a bonafide hole in the wall. Nothing flashy, just another storefront next to the Safeway. However, once you walk inside, you are immediately whisked away to a world of culinary delightfulness. My husband and I ate here a few weeks ago when his parents were in town to provide free babysitting for the little one. Eager to venture out on our own, we decided to try NOCA. While there, we chose the tasting menu. We began with a mis which consisted of a balsamic cured strawberry with a marcona almond. Yum. Hubby started off with the Reuben and I had the avocado soup. Both were delicious. The pasta course was tasty. For the main course, hubby had the veal and I had the sturgeon. Both were perfectly cooked and perfectly paired. Desert included complimentary cotton candy along with a peanut butter smores dish which may have been the crown jewel of the evening, and a peach shortbread which was also very delicious. It is not often that I eat out and feel that desserts are on par with the general menu, but NOCA was an adventure from the mis all the way to the after-dinner cordials!

Where do you go when your washer and dryer break down? How about Starcrest, which can boast it's own little study room with two desks, four chairs, and free wi-fi? Downtown Ithaca is a great place to hang out during the day. It's close enough that you don't have to worry too much about traffic; for example, even if you live on campus, there are plenty of parking options nearby where you can get some exercise while still getting to class or work on time. Being able to walk around town as well means that you're not stuck in one area either - you could walk from one end of town to another and see lots of beautiful scenery along the way. Ithaca has great nightlife at all hours because so many people live downtown. You can find yourself walking through busy streets late into the evening enjoying local music performed by students of all ages, especially those who've come home early after an exhausting day at school. Not only that, but the city also offers an awesome number of restaurants ranging from upscale dining halls like Dining Hall 21 to more casual places like the Greek Street Food Truck or the Ithaca Brewing Company. The best part about living here is how clean everything is: our toilets and sinks look brand new, central air conditioning works perfectly, and we never once had a litter problem this year! At first, it seemed like everyone else in our dorm shared these luxuries, but soon enough people realized they were just being spoiled. After moving back into my girlfriend's house in upstate New York after freshman year, I discovered that she lived in a single bedroom and her parents kept their bathroom very neat and tidy. While it wasn't quite as clean, it was definitely better than mine, thanks to my roommate's diligent cleaning habits throughout the week. The same goes for any other apartment complexes located near downtown. Almost every college student lives somewhere close to campus so their apartments are always spotless. This makes us feel like we actually earned them instead of just having them handed to us. Being an easy commute away from downtown and not needing a car, students have the option to take public transportation to and from the city easily. Being able to visit places like the Ithaca History Museum or the Cornell Bookstore or simply walking around downtown only takes 20 minutes instead of 45 minutes by car. Take advantage of this fact! If you want to explore Ithaca without taking over your entire trip, walking to the nearby bars and clubs won't be hard at all. Sounds fun right?

I've been to a few other places for dim sum, so my opinion is somewhat biased. For the record, I'm also your standard adventure-seeking gringo, inspired by Andrew Zimmern. So, I'll try anything once, but I'm not the best judge of authenticity, though I can give you a feel for the experience. The hostess is a little shy and unassuming, but she's very friendly. There are two main dining rooms, one on each floor. I started on the upper floor, where I found most of the tables and almost all of the other diners were asian, which is a good sign. There were also several large groups of young asian women, so it's a good place for a ladies night out. I was seated at a booth, and I asked for dim sum. I had a choice of having the waitress roll the cart to me, or having her come up to take my order. I opted for her to come over, and she was right there with pen and paper. She was also very personable, and I got the feeling that she was genuinely interested in helping me. She was very polite, and the whole transaction felt like a casual conversation rather than a business transaction. After I ordered, she thanked me and said she'd be back with my tea. I'd expected to wait a while for the tea, but she was right back. I was impressed. As we waited for the food, the waitress checked on us a couple of times, and made sure that my water was full and that I was enjoying the tea. My tea arrived before the food did, and it was very good. Not too hot, and plenty of flavor. The tea was served in a traditional handleless cup, and the saucer is the large round plate on which the food is served. The tea service was very attractive. The food arrived quickly, and was hot. We had barbecue pork buns, steamed pork dumplings, steamed chicken dumplings, shrimp pork dumplings, and steamed shrimp dumplings. All of the food was excellent. The buns and dumplings were steamed rather than fried, which I prefer. The pork dumplings had a nice sweet flavor, the chicken dumplings were excellent, and the shrimp dumplings were good. I'd call the experience great, not just good. In the lower dining room, I saw the same friendly hostess. She was attending to the whole room, taking orders, and checking on people's tea. The lower dining room was slightly more formal, with table cloths, but the service was the same. All in all, I give this place a thumbs up. The staff was very attentive, and the food was excellent. It's a very clean place, and the decor is pleasant. It's also a very busy place, which speaks for itself. If you're looking for authentic Chinese food, you can't go wrong here. Our family loves the food, and also the service. They do have the best shrimp pork dumplings.

Sadly, I have to give Gordon Ramsay's Pub and Grill at Caesars Palace, Las Vegas, a less than stellar review. I can only muster the kindness to give this restaurant two stars. I must admit, that were my rating based solely on my latest dining experience there, I would give the restaurant three stars, and, had I based my review solely on my first dining experience there, I would have given four stars. I'm sure that you will ask, How does the average of 3 and 4 equal two? The answer: disappointment. This will sound silly, but bear with me. The reason I returned to PG after my first visit is also the reason I will not return: potatoes. Specifically, two potato dishes: the Potato Puree and the Pub Fries. These were not ordinary mashed potatoes and French fries. These were a demonstration of what a potato can taste like if a fine-dining approach is taken when preparing ordinary dishes. Every now and again you taste a dish and experience it for the first time all over again. Such was my experience with the fries and mashed potatoes at PG. They made me feel that, as a foodstuff, potatoes have much more potential that I had previously imagined. The key to their french fries was the cooking technique: thick-cut potato planks, steamed, then lightly coated in seasoned flour, then deep-fried, then baked. The result: a hearty potato plank with a crispy outer crust that created the perfect seal to keep steam inside. When you cut into them, you discovered a steamy, flaky potato meat. These fries did not need any condiments whatsoever, and highlighted how good a potato can taste if treated properly The mashed potatoes had a beautiful flavor. The fluffy peaks of this dish were topped off with a drizzle of a chive infused olive oil that exploded in your mouth, filling your entire palette with the aroma of garden-fresh chives. The key to this explosion was temperature of the potatoes: served piping hot. On my second visit, I ordered these two side dishes again. This time, the Pub Fries were plain, old french fries, and slightly soggy at that. The mashed potatoes were a salty, gluey concoction that someone had tried to repair by thinning it out with copious amounts of cream and butter. They were served cold. Other highlights of the evening: arrived at 7:15pm and checked in for my 7:15pm reservation. The hostess forgot to check me in, and when I made eye-contact with her every time she seated a walk-in customer before me, she quickly looked away and left the podium. I approached a different hostess and was seated right away. I ordered the seared scallops: scallops were seared on one side only. They were served in a bland seafood broth, with carrots, and artichoke hearts. Not flavorful at all. I ordered an espresso with dessert and it arrived cold. The chocolate mousse trifle was sensational, though. At any rate, I believe that what happened to this restaurant is not so much carelessness on the part of its founder or staff. It is a reaction to the caliber of the customer. I spoke to the manager about the food, and he admitted that they had to change some recipes because their customers did not see the value in waiting extra time for french fries to be cooked three ways or for mashed potatoes to be prepared to order. So, they have turned from their fine-dining philosophy to a food-mill philosophy: crank out orders. And that is where the disappointment lies. PG once provided a fine-dining take on British pub fare. It now caters to the lowest common denominator and provides tourists a place to grab a quick bite and gain some bragging rights: I went to Vegas and ate at Gordon Ramsay's. You know? That guy from TV? Sadly, the Gordon Ramsay on TV is no longer anywhere to be found at PG. The Gordon Ramsay on TV preaches fine ingredients, food prepared to perfection, good seasoning, good service, consistency, and, above all, passion and pride. Where is the pride to be found when you don't stand by your food, and, instead, you cut corners to ramp up production. Sorry, that's not fine-dining. That's a factory. I'll gladly drop 20 at Applebee's for factory food. Not 200 at Gordon Ramsay's.

Visited on 82313 for a retirement party in the back room where 1 server was assigned to serve a toastie with family and friends, eating what turned out to be a tasty dessert. Before getting into the booth, the server proceeded to pour him some wine from the fountain which he had poured down the sink when his grandson called him "Queen." He asked if his grandson could drink from the fountain while he stood there drinking his own wine due to his grandmother's lack of any interest whatsoever, but alas that didn't stop him from pouring himself another bottle of wine onto the table before returning his favor by drinking it all up. Afterwards, the server returned to return his order of cake which was served at the table over the two tables beside him. The server left the restaurant without saying goodbye or making sure everyone was satisfied, but his father survived because he refused to leave the table after the tables were set so it wasn't very likely that other guests would have eaten anything else until the server went home alone. After dinner, the server changed again to serve drinks to the living room audience who enjoyed a glass of red wine. He then explained why he decided to go into the house instead of heading back to his car while wishing his grandson well; "I know the house has enough furniture already," he said. Finally, the server summoned his son and daughter-in-law to join the table as they ate their dinners together (which included a few sandwiches). The server tried desperately not to look so young next time around since his granddaughters would only listen to his grandson talk about his grandfather and his wife. When the dining room came roaring back up, the server thanked the guests for coming along. The server mentioned that he wanted to tell his granddaughter how proud he felt knowing that it really helped her grow up to help her learn about God. This pleased his granddaughter immensely considering she hadn't heard the conversation yet. If you're looking for motivation, the server showed off his dining room decorations: a large board, a picture frame depicting the history of the church, a pile of books about the church, a large box containing a VCR tape recorder, a small bookcase filled with DVDs, a small stuffed animal, and a large box full of books about God among others. He also pointed out that his grandson, who swore he couldn't wait to see his grandchildren watch their movies, loves books more than he does movies now. When the server left the restaurant, his grandson questioned why his grandfather kept telling his grandson everything. The server responded by pointing out that it doesn't matter whether it helps your grandson study religion, because he keeps telling him good things about God. Since we've discussed the server's personal life, you can bet your ass that his relationship with his grandmother will end soon. It seems like he hasn't been able to convince his granddaughter that he realizes the importance of God anymore although he still talks about God highly often every day despite being married and having children. At the end of the meal, the server told his grandson he'll never forgive him ever for letting his grandma die, leaving the grandparents confused and shaking throughout dinner. After asking his granddaughter to come decorate his attic cabinets with colors reminiscent of her favorite house furnishings, the server let his granddaughter take them apart using her imagination. The server also confessed that he missed having grandchildren visit as he forgot about them once his grandson showed up unexpectedly one night. Now when you think about it, it might seem strange that the server wouldn't tell his grandson why he thought a man shouldn't touch women unless they are pregnant. Had he realized his grandmother was dying upon hearing her voice say something so profound and insulting? And why did he assume that neither grandmother nor siblings existed when he followed her footsteps? After all, we saw the server saving his grandson's life earlier today helping him make his wish come true... just remember the server talking about God in front of everyone?! Also On 97.9 The Beat:

Tucked away on Broadway is The Hungry Cat Restaurant - we had heard good reviews about it so decided to check it out during our visit to Denver. Maybe it's because of its location or maybe it just hasn't found an audience yet...but if you like pan-Asian cuisine then you will love these dishes. We started off with Fried Green Tomatoes, which were amazing - not too greasy and they had plenty of flavor. They came topped w peanuts sesame seeds making them even better! Next up was their special house fried rice, which has some "secret" ingredients that give it extra crunchiness. This dish also comes with shrimp chicken sausage added into it as well - definitely above average fried rice! For mains, we tried their Crab Rangoon which are served deep-fried inside pastry shells. These weren't your ordinary crab rangoons either; instead, each one holds a piece of juicy crab meat mixed w veggies such as carrots celery. Sounds weird? Trust me, try it once and you'll be hooked! Our last main course from here was Spicy Szechuan Beef over Rice Noodles. Not only did it taste great but it gave us enough leftovers to make 2 more meals!! It really doesn't get any tastier than this - tender beef cubes soaked in spicy red sauce mixed w noodles vegetables. What makes it all happen though is how Chef Artemiyev uses his secret blend of chilies spices to spice things up while maintaining a perfect balance of flavors. If you're ever in Denver, don't miss this place!

There are also some bistro items on offer like pastas and pizzas. The large panini selection will be sure to please any hungry diner, although we did take full advantage of the daily specials. Sides or entrees are served with your choice of chips or fresh baked garlic fries accompanied by cole slaw and a side of ranch dressing for dipping. We tried their duck breast panino and the chicken parmigiana panini featuring marinara sauce, mozzarella and basil pesto, lettuce and tomato. We enjoyed the crispy bacon strips, smoky sausage, and fresh veggies on our sandwiches quite a bit. I highly recommend stopping in at Mama's Kitchen, especially if you're craving something tasty for lunch after shopping at Downtown Disney Marketplace!

I could imagine that getting a healthy case of the shingles might be an altogether more pleasant experience than staying at The Palms. I can easily imagine being gunned down in the lobby. It's that ghetto. Not that I feared for my life, there are just a lot nicer places tostay in Vegas with a lot more atmosphere and less people trapsing around looking like cheap hookers. My stay started out with a bad valet experience. I'm used to extremely helpful valets who offer directions in advance of your asking. The valet at The Palms have a unique approach- they ignore you or are absent from the stand altogether. On three separate occasions the valet stand was unattended. The room, while nice fora second- rate discount motel in Shanksville, Pennsylvania, oh wait, I am reviewing a four star Maloof property in Las Vegas. You get the picture: broken light fixtures, a tube TV, dated, worn furniture (which seemed to mimic the look of the clientele). If you like eating at the Cracker Barrel, you're going to love the Palms. If that's not your thing, save yourself a lot of heartache and go somewhere nice to sleep.

Many airports these days are attempting to become more upscale; there are sculptures and musicians and art and fancy food. In theory this is great! If I'm going to pay more for a plane ticket I expect a bit more. But I also have a big problem with this. First of all, the airport staff has no idea how to handle this kind of event. Airport staff should not be forced to handle a situation that they have no experience with, especially when they are completely unfamiliar with the surroundings. A good rule of thumb is that the staff that handles the situation should be able to explain the situation and their role in it. This is not the case here. A helpful customer service representative from Delta was very helpful in the beginning, but when she found out that there were only two Delta employees working the whole day, she could not assist with anything. She had no idea how to help us. This was especially frustrating as we had already been through a TSA screening. TSA employees know what to do and how to handle an explosive situation. When you have someone who is unfamiliar with your surroundings and doesn't know how to handle the situation, you are essentially sending them on a wild goose chase. This is why I am glad that the employees of American were the ones that took charge and handled the situation. They had more experience with the situation, and handled it much better. The second problem with the airport staff is that they have no idea what to do when they do have to handle a situation like this. We were only there for about 20 minutes, but we did get a pretty good idea of what to do when the situation arises. You should call the police. The police have a plan for every possible situation that they can handle. You can always ask for help from the police, and they will always be more than willing to help. In this case, the police arrived on the scene within 5 minutes of the explosion. They took over and ran the whole situation. All the staff did was follow their instructions. I feel like this would have been a more efficient way to handle the situation, especially when you are only dealing with two employees. It would have been nice to see a TSA employee in the background, but the police were still there, and they had a plan. If the police are the only ones who know what to do, you will have a much better chance of handling a situation like this. Airports need to be more aware of this, and train their staff to handle a situation like this. We were in the security line, so I had no idea what was going on. I was expecting the usual waiting and screening process. Instead, I was told to get off the line and go to the other side. The security line was being used as an emergency exit. It was not until I got to the other side that I saw the bomb squad and ambulances. I was told to go to the side of the airport where the security staff were. I didn't really know what to expect. I was expecting some sort of inspection, but I was not prepared for the bomb squad. I don't think that the security staff knew what to do either. I saw one security guard that seemed to know what was going on, but he didn't seem to know what to do. He kept asking people what was going on, but no one knew. The bomb squad was stationed at the gate. They kept asking everyone if they had any liquids or food. This is the kind of situation that you really want to know how to handle. I felt like this was the most important part of the airport experience. It would have been nice if the airport staff could have known what to do. I don't think they had any idea, and they weren't prepared. I was there for less than 20 minutes, but I got the impression that this situation could have been handled much better. When a bomb is detected, you want the police to take over the situation. It was very obvious that the airport staff did not know what to do. You want to have an organization that can handle a situation like this, and it would have been nice if the airport staff had a plan for this. In my opinion, the airport staff did not have a plan, and they did not know what to do. This could have been handled much better, and I feel like the airport staff could have handled it better. This is not the first time that an airport has had a situation like this. When an explosive device is found in a plane, the airport staff should be able to handle it. It would be nice if the airport staff had a plan for a situation like this. 3. You will have a TSA screener inspect your bag. This was the most important part of the whole airport experience. The TSA screener did not know what to do. I had never had this experience before, and I didn't really know what to expect. The screener told me to go through the metal detector.

I was really excited to check this place out. The menu looked pretty awesome when I checked it out online. Reviews here, to sum up, seemed to be pretty mixed, with one's experience tied pretty closely to ordering the right things on the menu. Armed with knowledge gleaned from other reviews, the lady and I rolled over there on a Friday night at 7:00pm. The parking lot was a ghost town. There were two tables being served. Not a good sign, but hey, let's give it a shot. We were immediately greeted by a friendly young guy who took us to a table of our choosing. We were also immediately greeted by a NASTY smell in the air. It smelled like someone dropped a deuce under a table. Five days earlier. This eau de outhouse permeated the entire restaurant. I'm not the kind of guy who is up for making a big deal out of things. I was fully prepared to try and ignore it and have some dinner. The lady? Not so much. Ummmm..... excuse me. Do you smell that? Our hostserver sheepishly replied, Haha.... yeah, I guess I'm just kind of used to it. It comes and goes around here. It's the whole area. Now, I'm not a huge fan of the East Side in general, but come on. The parking lot smelled fresh as a daisy by comparison. There is clearly something horribly wrong with this building, and I hope that the young owners of Nosh and Swig have an attorney to help them get out of whatever ugly lease they are tied up in. After he said he'd be back to take our drink orders, we held our breath, and made a beeline for the front door. I feel awful for them - and I hope they can get into another location. One that doesn't smell like the parking garage of the Four Queens. Two tables at prime time on a Friday night? How many more Fridays can they possibly have in that space?

We drive into Vegas from the CA side several times a year. We always make one of our stops Green Valley. I know that they are now part of the station casinos but this is one of our favorite ones. Pretty good restaurant. I think I liked the root beer there the most. Got the sour dough sandwich and added some thousand island on it and it was pretty amazing. A little heavy on the grease though. My friends sandwich was a lot greasier though. Fries are nothing to write home about. Just basic crinkle cut fries and the onion rings were lack luster too. Good for large crowds and kids and you are able to really make anything unique and to your liking.

I received a ten dollar gift card to Best Buy recently (as much as I am thankful to receive a gift, 10 won't get you much at an electronics store!). In any case, I figured I might be able to pick up at least one little item for that price. When I arrived at the store today (121212) around 1:00 PM, I looked around and found a female employee (whom I cannot describe other than she was wearing a tan cardigan on top of her store uniform). When I explained the little predicament I was in (looking for ANYTHING under ten bucks that I might buy), she looked a bit annoyed, and suggested I buy candy (perhaps she thought I had been given a ten dollar Visa or American Express gift card and I should take the card elsewhere to buy said candy...but then, why would I be so foolish as to go to an electronics store with a 10 gift card that I could take anywhere? Or maybe Best Buy actually does sell candy...I don't know). In any case, after I awkwardly laughed at her suggestion to buy candy, I reiterated my problem, and she walked me over to the DVD section, where there are at least a few cheap DVDs. She indicated that some were 9.99. I stated, That's good, except with tax, it will be over ten dollars, to which she responded: Well, yeah. Apart from the fact that I wasn't asking for something I could buy with the gift card PLUS additional money, her sarcasm was, yet again, off-putting. She kept stating that most stuff in the store falls above the ten dollar threshold, and because of the I'm so done with this customer, get me out of here! vibe that radiated from her being, I thanked her with a smile, and indicated I could take things from there. I found an area for DVDs on clearance for a price of 3.99, that she did not even bother to bring me to for some reason, but frankly, I either had most of the movies, or they didn't appeal to me, so I didn't end up buying anything today. But the employee at the door, a young man, said Thanks for coming in today, to the elderly gentleman about fifteen feet ahead of me leaving the store. When I got to the door, however, the aforementioned door attendant gave me a hollow, almost annoyed glance, and looked back into the store, not uttering one word of thanks to me. Now, I don't normally care that much whether an employee says goodbye to me or not...but when I witness it occurring to another customer right ahead of me, of course I'm going to note the lack of politeness when no such kindness is extended to me....what am I, chopped liver?!?! And the annoyed look was certainly unnecessary. As an investor, I have seen the financial trouble that Best Buy is having in a world where internet retailers such as Amazon are totally undercutting them. It is for this reason that I have to wonder....where is the customer service?! What makes a tangible, real-life store different than an online retailer? Two things: getting to test the equipment, and the PEOPLE! The customer service, getting help, and answers to questions. I have already written another less-than-complimentary review of different Best Buy location (I promise, I don't have any ill will for the company...I'd actually prefer them to garner my highest praise), and it all hinges around the same issue...customer service. It always seems to be that the store is either like a middle school dance, with the employees awkwardly huddled with their friends talking, looking out at the customers but too timid to ask them if they need anything....or it is like today where the employees just seem to act as if they have better things to do. NOTE TO ALL BEST BUY STORES: If you want to stand even the slimmest chance of surviving the fierce competition that online retailers are giving you, then fix your customer service. I believe that there is a large group of people that still, and will continue to want a real-life shopping experience. Give them a good experience, or I am almost sure that your company will go the way of Circuit City...out of business.

I went to Big Earl's this week with my co-workers and the BBQ is amazing! I don't know how good the ribs were but I got the pulled pork and mac n' cheese (my favorite BBQ dish) and it was probably some of the best I've ever had. (I'll say it. Better than Joe's Real BBQ!) The portions were huge and reheated wonderfully - I'm eating them now as I write this review! Parking isn't easy in old town but they have their own parking lot. Also, the chef even came out and talked to us while we ate. It was an all around great atmosphere. I'm only sad I didn't get to stay for happy hour - 3 sangria! I need to clarify that. I'm so sad I didn't get to partake in happy hour since I had to go back to work. I can say for sure, I'll be back for HH and some more mac n' cheese!

It was our last meal in Montreal and probably the best. Service was excellent. Very friendly and helpful. Especially helpful when describing the different kinds of beer and wine they had available. Started with the venison carpaccio which we enjoyed. I had the rabbit leg which was served with farro, carrots and cauliflower. The rabbit was very juicy and the broth it was in was so delicious. I could have just had the broth and some bread. Btw- the bread is also very good. My husband had the venison steak which was also delicious. Everything about this place was great. We had dinner at Au Pied de Cochon a few nights before, and while we really enjoyed our meal there, I think this place is better. I wish we had gone here earlier during our trip so we could have gone multiple times!

In 15 years of going to Las Vegas, this is about the worst meal I've ever had. Here's my experience, in convenient list format 1) 9pm reservation - we sat at 10:15pm. Seriously. They blamed OpenTable, whatever. At the end of the day, if they knew there were problems, how come nobody contacted us? RIDICULOUS. 2) Prices - 44 for a piece of fish or chicken? Really? I've been to top restaurants in LV, NYC, SF, etc, and while I've seen expensive food, it comes along with.... amazing service, uber-fresh ingredients, creative menus, etc. This was just ripoff central. 3) Food quality - my seabass was bland, as in had less flavor than microwaveable fish sticks. One person in our party sent their food back! Chicken was dried out, sides were meh. The bright spot was the appetizers, which I cannot recall even a few days later, so probably not too bright. 4) Ambiance - eh, it was fine. Nothing special, no great decor, nothing revolutionary. 5) Service was decent, they kept glasses full, etc. Again, not amazing (no synchronized food delivery for example), just average. Nothing to justify the cost of the meal. The entire group walked out very disappointed. Wouldn't go back, wouldn't recommend, wouldn't do anything ever again. Maybe they call it Fix because it still needs to be fixed?

I have always had an amazing meal at Dinette. I've only tried their pizzas, which their menus change periodically. But everyone I've tried have been very good! Parking is very easy because it is in a large lot that is shared with Chipotle, T-Mobile, a bike place, and others. Overall, definitely high quality pizza and one of my go-to places!

Woohoo! Best Cirque show I've been to yet! Some might say I am biased because I have this love for Beatles music, but I think that the content of the show is wonderful. I really like Old Chicago (OC) for a few different reasons. If you're a fan of beer like me, they've got a decent line up and rotation of beers (draft and bottle) from all over the world. Also they have this program called world beer tour where you get some free goodies if you drink a certain amount (can we say promoting alcoholism? I'm down). This kinda reminds me of the old program they had going at rock bottom where they would put your name on the placard if you drank like over 100 beers (and you get like tshirts, free food, etc along the way) Secondly, the pizza is darn delicious there. I know it's a chain, but still great tasting pizzas with variety of toppings. I haven't got a chance to try anything other than the pizzas there, but hey isn't this supposed to be a pizza place? Mama mia. Lastly, it's super close to my school and I have gotten take out a few times so another star for convenience.

Comme Ca brunch rocks!! They have a 20 pre fixe menu with multiple selections for app, entree, and dessert. I ordered the duck confit cinnamon bun, quiche, and creme brulee. The duck cinnamon bun sounded so different, I had to try it. I like that balanced mixing of sweet and savory. It was really good and it was a large portion. My two guests had a bite and I still saved half of it. Next, the quiche was delicious. The homemade crust on the quiche was oh so buttery. Again, a really large portion and another half saved. The creme brulee was just as expected and nothing stand out. I wish it was flavored with earl grey or lavender or another kid of floral. Even though you can't really taste it, the smell of it would have been nice. Some notes about service. They are a little casual but it's cool. They are not over the top and you can actually carry a conversation with them. I think it's funny that they all wear these red plaid shirts. I think it looks american country but I guess it could also be like French country. So with my leftover bun and quiche I saved it for lunch the next day. Both items held up and tastes almost better. I've been for dinner on a previous occasion and loved the dinner menu too. I drool over the bone marrow dish and the beef tartare. I would totally recommend this place for lunch and dinner. It's not crazy busy and I hope it stays open. I would hate for this gem to leave Vegas. Oh yes, next time I will sit at the bar and people watch. I've sat at the window and it's nothing special for me. It might be better at night.

I've been coming to El Burrito since I was in Middle School and it's still one of my favorite homegrown Mexican restaurants in Las Vegas. I've never really had a bad experience or bad food at this place because I pretty much stick to three things on the menu because each of those items are so good that I just never decided to branch out and try anything else. The complimentary chips and salsa are always an awesome start to the meal. I usually follow that up with the Noodle Soup. It's pretty salty, but it'll warm you up on a cool night and it tastes great. I usually get one of three entree plates every time I go, which comes with the aforementioned soup. 1) Two Chicken Burritos w Red Sauce 2) Two Tamales 3) Carne Asada Each of the items comes with the typical fixings, rice and beans and whatnot. Each of the items are equally tasty, and if you get the two burrito plate you will DEFINITELY have leftovers! I usually cap the meal off with the sopapillas, which are cinnamon-sugar covered pieces of dough that are absolutely delicious.:) I highly recommend this place, as a loyal customer for most of my life.

We ate here a number of times over the summer as it is located near our house and has good menu offerings and reasonable prices. I haven't been back since October so things may be different now (it looks like they've moved their coffee stand down to the bar). Service is pretty slow - often all you see behind the counter are two workers who will run your order through the kitchen while you wait, however my last visit they had just one worker running the register who would place your food orders on separate paper tickets that you brought up later, presumably to take them home. The other thing is that the food doesn't arrive quickly enough - takeout time is about 30 minutes whereas eating inside it takes closer to 45 - possibly longer depending on how many parties you're seated with. I can say this: if you plan on dining alone or with one friend, don't bother because you'll probably spend 40-60 minutes waiting for your meal. However if more than 2 people are coming over, expect longer waits and there isn't anything nearby to eat except Subway where the wait is no better (30 mins) and it costs 6 per person plus tax. The only reason why anyone eats here is if heshe lives within walking distance and wants something quick before heading off somewhere else. While this may sound harsh, remember these are tourist dollars going towards local businesses that hopefully aren't suffering economically due to COVID restrictions. If you live closeby and still choose to dine here, please tip generously (5) even though that definitely won't change anything!

Yelp 100 Challenge 14' 7100 Got wonderful rear orchestra seats for my mom's advance birthday to Shania Twain's'Still the One' thanks to Erica Y. The Colosseum had a very intimate setting with not a bad seat in the house, a giant screen and tech that allowed for all the right details to make a concert worth the price...and in my case, worth the run. Since school started, I've slowly reverted back to a planned schedule and the spontaneity of getting the tickets for my parents on the day of meant hopping on a couple of buses and running straight for the theater after my last class ended. And when I say racing two city blocks was worth it, I would do it all over again if it means seeing a concert as great as that. Before I get into details about the venue, my family - who's been a fan of Shania since the late 90s - got our fill. Although my efforts to get there on time didn't quite work out (15 minutes late), we were told that we only missed a couple of songs. Gracious and beautiful as ever, Shania delivered an incredible show with theatrical props I've grown accustomed to seeing only in Broadway shows. Transitions made use of the big screen with music filled in continuously by the band, strings, back-up vocals and did anyone else actually smell actual burning wood during that campfire number? Shania would come up to the audience, give them a hug, allowed pictures to be taken with her, even had a handful of people join her up on stage as they sang around the campfire - funny how the security guards were going pretty ballistic over how much of us were snapping our cameras. Beautiful beautiful woman, inside and out. We adore her just as much as we did way back when and I guess we got even more respect for her with how she's handled herself over the years. Now I understand why people get figgety about the sound quality at the Smith Center. Comparatively, the way the Colosseum was designed and sound was engineered amplified a balance to the ears, almost as if we were listening to a recorded version of a song. You could make out every instrument in the background and the voices blended in perfectly while at the Smith, words tended to get muffled. The use of projectors also provided more room for creativity with lighting; painting sceneries, atmospheres; producing colors; triggering certain emotions. Stage was huge. Number of times, I felt like we were at an IMAX theatre. There's a snack bar right outside for audience members to get some food or drinks to enjoy. Staff was very friendly and we were escorted by one then relayed to another smoothly till we arrived at our seats. Ultimately, the concert was very accommodating and we felt right at home to the rockpopcountry beats. To those who may have second thoughts about the concert, I promise you won't regret.

I looked at the bathroom door again, and that is when I saw the ladies going back into the bathroom. I thought that was very rude of them to be talking so loudly in the bathroom, and I was actually a little irritated. I just wanted to eat my dinner and enjoy my husband's company, and I just wanted to forget about the conversation that I had overheard. I decided that I just needed to go back to the table and enjoy my food, and I would find out later what was going on. I sat back down and tried to eat my dinner, but I couldn't help but to think about the conversation that I had overheard. I know that I am probably being very mean, but

I had a good idea of what to expect, having had Laotian cuisine maybe once or twice in the past. I can't comment on the restaurant itself because my friend was driving so we were in the parking lot. I remember when we ordered the pho, I was expecting it to be more spicy than it was. The usual flavors were there but not the heat. I guess that's a good thing for me, a hot and spicy food lover. I do remember that the broth was amazing. But I think I liked the flavor of the dish more than the meat. I liked the texture of the noodles and the broth but the meat was pretty much tofu to me. The banh mi was fine. Nothing out of the ordinary but it was good. I would have liked it better with the usual pate. The meat was too fine but it wasn't bad. The bun cha was ok. I didn't really like the spice here either. It was a bit too sweet for me. The sweet sauce went well with the sweet bun but the meat wasn't as flavorful as it should have been. I expected it to be spicier and more flavorful. I'm not sure why because I thought the lemongrass was supposed to be spicy? I think I liked the fish sauce better than the sweet sauce. Overall, it wasn't the best Laotian food I've had but it was close. I think the pho was better than the other dishes. But it wasn't bad at all. I would give it a 7.5 out of 10. I love the pho, but have never had the bun cha. I will try it next time I see it. The bun cha is pretty sweet, so if you're not into that you might not like it.

I came here during the Mtl a table festival, a festival that allows foodies to try out new restaurants at a fraction of the price. I was looking forward to trying out Le Chien Fumant, as I've heard great reviews about it, and I was also looking forward to try their food. They have a small kitchen and their main dining area is also small, with not many seats, so come early to make sure you get a seat! I had a three course meal here, and I'll post them in this order. The apple and cheddar soup was very tasty, it was creamy and had a nice apple flavour. It had a nice hint of cheddar in it, not too strong, but just right to compliment the apple flavours. I had the duck breast here, and it was very tender and tasty. The skin was nice and crispy and it had a good amount of fat on it to add to the taste. The duck was very tender and juicy, and it was complimented well by the corn sauce. The corn sauce was nice and sweet, and it was a nice contrast to the duck, as it was more on the salty side. This dish had a lot of flavour, it was very tasty. It had a good portion of meat, and I was able to get three slices of duck out of it, which was a lot of meat. The corn sauce was a nice touch, as it was sweet and contrasted well with the duck. The chocolate cake was nice and rich and it was topped with a small amount of cayenne pepper, which gave it a nice kick. The chocolate cake was moist and rich, and it was a great ending to the meal. The dish was very well presented, and it was a nice size for an appetizer. Overall, I had a great experience here. It was nice to try out new food, and I had a nice time here. The food was delicious, and it was well presented. The service was also great, they were fast and efficient. The food was also a good value for the price, as I was able to get a lot of food for the price.

Doohan's is a bar located within a boutique nightclub called the Cathouse. Once you manage to figure that out, be forewarned that this establishment has a serious identity crisis. There are tvs everywhere broadcasting sports games, drinks named after athletes and pub-style grub. The print, tv and web marketing conveys a casual, atmosphere - a good place to pop in for a beer and a bite before heading out for the night. Meanwhile, you arrive and feel like you're sitting in the middle of the Moulin Rouge, surrounded by black vinyl, tufted wall coverings, velvet booths, granite tables, black chandeliers for mood lighting.... it's like drinking in a hooker's boudoir. The place was dead when we arrived; just two other tables were occupied, and we all shared one waitress. I thought, okay, maybe it's just early? At least we'll have good service since the waitress isn't busy.... We told the manager and the waitress up front that four people in the group had purchased a deal for food and beverage credit online and intended to use them that night, two at each table. Sure, no problem! from the manager. The waitress had no idea what we were talking about and excused herself to speak with the manager about it. She came back and told us that the credit could only be used by the person who purchased it (which was not indicated on the deal - in fact, it said that up to two vouchers could be used for one table, as long as food was ordered). The rest of the table would pay for their own food and drinks. Since we all planned to pitch in, the group decides that it will all come out in the wash and why make a huff? Service started off okay and then quickly went downhill. We order a round of drinks that came out in a timely fashion, then ordered some apps - mostly chicken and fries, since they ran out of what I wanted. The apps were nothing special. In fact, they looked like they came from Friendly's, and were even served in the typical plastic basket and wax paper you'd get. A few of us order tobacco for the hookah and another round of drinks. It's taking forever so we tell her to cancel the order and that we want to settle up to go somewhere else, and she says she will try but they might not be able to cancel since they may have already mixed the tobacco for us. Next thing you know, the order comes out so we smoke, finish our drinks and we're still waiting for the bill. The tables that were there when we arrived had left and a few more had come in, but there was no rush. Our waitress just disappeared. When we finally see her, I reminded her that we wanted to settle up and she says she needs to process our vouchers with the manager. Isn't that why we gave her the voucher numbers when we first arrived? Apparently, she misplaced them. So we wait...and wait.... and continue to wait. Members of our group are standing up to signal we are ready to go and clearly annoyed. She finally comes back with 8 separate bills! Everyone paid in cash except me - another mistake. I tell my friends to go on without me while I wait for her to run my credit card. I physically walked it over to her while she was standing at the computer. And my wait continued. She finally returns my credit card, explaining that it didn't go through when she ran it (I had no problems at any other location I used it that weekend). You can bet that no one in the group left additional gratuity over what was included on the bill. In total, our visit to Doohan's for 2 rounds of drinks, some apps and hookah took about 2.5 hours. Note the the management: If you're running a deal online, make sure that you and your staff are educated about the fine print, and that you are prepared to actually process the deals when people want to redeem them. Don't get me wrong, if my friends and I had gone with the intention of going to an intimate nightclub, I might have enjoyed the Cathouse. I really loved the decor and could totally could have seen myself going back to check out the nightclub. But after our experience at Doohan's, I wouldn't consider going back. There are so many other clubs and bars in Las Vegas that will give you prompt service. While our group can usually make the best out of any situation, the service was simply unacceptable. Our visit to Doohan's put a complete damper on our last night in Las Vegas and I really regret that we ever stepped foot in the place.

I was a bit creeped out the first time I ate here. I took my wife's younger brothers because they had seen it on the Travel Channel, so I thought I'd try it out. Being a large man, I got to eat for free (score!), but only had one single and some fries, but enjoyed watching my teenage brother-in-laws try to finish their doubles (haha). I've been back several times with mixed experiences. It really depends on your nurse: sometimes you get a nurse who is very talkative and makes sure your order comes out real fast and hot, and sometimes you get a nurse who is watching the clock. It's not the best hamburger I've ever had, but I enjoy the do-it-yourself condiments (jalapeno and mustard for me), and the fact that you know you are going to get CHEESE and BEEF, and in good portions. You get 10 discount just for checking into any Caesars Hotel, Palace or Palace Jumeirah Resort between April 15th to May 31st 2012. So if you're planning to spend your summer holiday in Emirates Towers, enjoy a staycation or maybe take a family vacation to the Maldives then make sure you order those tickets ASAP otherwise you'll soon run out of time to book anything else. This Cheesecake Factory has 3 entries on Yelp. It was Happy National Cheesecake Day on July 30 July 31st, 2014 so I went over to a Cheesecake Factory (not this branch) to have a slice of cheesecake at 12 price!! Anyways the following is my review for this location written back in February 2014: I must confess that I am a diehard Cheesecake Factory fan! Unless the service is very bad, I will not give them less than 4 stars. This specific location inside Caesars Palace holds a special place in my heart, but I will not go into specifics. Suffice it to say that I love this place! Normally, I get here before it gets too crowded. Sometimes I will have to wait, but it is worth the wait. Will just wait and people watch or browse around some of the Forum shops til it is our turn. The menu reads like a small book. It can get confusing at times cause everything sounds so good. Every appetizer and entree that I have had has not disappointed. All are above average, and the portions are huge so come hungry. Of course, a meal here is not complete without dessert. I will always save room for a slice of cheesecake. If it means that I cannot finish my entree, then I will just take home the leftovers and enjoy it the next day. I have tried over a dozen of their cheesecake flavors. My current favorites are Dutch Apple Caramel Streusel cheesecake, White Chocolate Caramel Macadamia Nut cheesecake, and White Chocolate Raspberry Truffle cheesecake. I only have one complaint. Stop discontinuing my favotite sandwiches. They used to make a three cheese Grilled Cheese sandwich which was awesome. They also used to make a Monterey Cheeseburger which was the bomb. I truly miss those two items. With that being said, every time we return to Caesars Palace, going to this Cheesecake Factory is a must. Many good memories here.

There's a very good reason that the Dane County Farmers' Market routinely appears on many top ten lists of best markets in the countryit's tops in every category. The market is open year-round and features a huge variety of organic and sustainably grown produce from asparagus to zucchini. The Winter Market, held every Saturday from November to April, is one of the few farmers markets in the country that does not allow crafts or other non-food items. I love this place. Great breakfasts, lunches and dinners. Their pastrami is the best in the state, and their turkey that is used in sandwiches tastes real (as in NOT the watery deli stuff you find in most places). We were seated right away (occasionally there is a wait, but they usually move through it pretty quickly) and taken to a table outside, as requested. The patio seating is nice if the weather is right and you enjoy the fresh air while dining. Had the hummus appetizer, which is tasty and only around 4-5 with several slices of pita bread. I'm not sure about the prices of the dishes because we had a very pleasant dinner w. our waiter and we did not pay much attention to the prices. I'll start with the good. Their coleslaw is fantastic, crisp and sweet and light with little bits of broccoli in it. Now for the rest. I went with two friends and my two children, one of which uses a high chair. We walked in on a Monday afternoon and the place was about half full. A waitress motioned from the back for us to sit at a round table so we did, picking up our own menus on the way. And then we sat. And sat. My son squirmed around on my lap but I had nowhere to put him. I watched two different waitresses walk by us repeatedly, even cleaning tables but not making eye contact. I finally flagged one down and she came over and said, You've been helped right? We said no and she turned around and left. A few minutes later a different waitress comes up, tells us we want coffee and seems put out when we ask for something else and sighs when I say I need a high chair. 5 more minutes go by and we get half the drinks. I hope that this was just an off day but really the second star is only because of the coleslaw. I will probably try it again if someone else wants to go, but overall not a winner in my book.

The Attic is the new name for Cave Ives. It's been taken over by new owner (who happens to be very familiar with Cave Ives), but all the elements we loved about Cave Ives are still intact. The official grand opening for The Attic is in August, but they are in fact open now! We were so bummed when Cave Ives closed in April. It was our favorite restaurant in the valley. We used to drive 40 minute to get there at least once a week. When we heard that Cave Ives was reopening under a new concept and new name, we were hesitant to go back. We didn't want to ruin the fond memories we had of Cave Ives. Now we kick ourselves and say, Why have we not been back sooner! As soon as we walk through the door, we were greeted with familiar faces and some very pleasant surprises. Ryan, the bartender that we loved for his great service and beer knowledge, was still there. In fact, they added more taps and now serve even more varieties of beers than before. They no longer have the large selection of bottled beers, but their draft beer selection was, and is still, very impressive. If you don't know what to drink, ask Ryan. He will not steer you wrong. In fact, we often choose to sit at the bar because Ryan is there. We were ecstatic to see that the menu hasn't changed too much either. The burger is still being served and all the pizzas are still the same. If you go to The Attic for the first time, YOU MUST ORDER THE BURGER!!! Ryan just informed us tonight that their burger was named one of the top 10 burgers in the United States! The Burger is a grill 12 lb. patty topped with grilled onions, chipotle mayo, spring greens, on a pretzel bun with your choice of cheese, and a side of French fries. If you can, order the bacon, sauteed mushrooms, and blue cheese. You can also order The Hangover Burger, which is the burger with a fried egg and bacon strips. If you're into spice, ask the server for Da Bomb. They keep it behind the bar. Our second favorite item on the menu (by a very close second) is the steak salad. They didn't have it this time, but Ryan assures us that the steak salad will also be coming back soon. We were so happy that the experience of going to The Attic has not diminished our memories of Cave Ives. The new decor with darker walls and pops colorful art is a plus. The music choices and more relaxed atmosphere made the place better. We also discovered that they added a burger challenge to the menu. Each challenger will need to each more than the last challenger (1 more patty, 1 more egg, 2 more strips of bacon). The winner gets to rename the burger and get their picture up on the wall. My husband is psyching himself up to doing the challenge on Tuesday! The Attic might be a different name, but same location, great service, delicious food, and excellent beer selection.

With Marche Bacchus, one of the best'off the Strip' restaurants literally a few steps away, Garfields has formidable competition. This place was absolutely outrageously delicious! We got there early (a few minutes before 5pm) so we beat the dinner rush and were seated immediately. There were 4 adults and 1 child in our party. For appetizers we ordered: Fried Clams and Hush Puppies. For dinner we ordered: Dungeness Crab (it was 2.5 pounds!), Blue Crab, Clams and Shrimp and put it all in the middle of the table and shared. Since it was our first time we just went with the house seasoning on everything and ordered it mild. Absolutely everything was out of this world tasty and beyond our highest hopes! Super fresh! We had a hard time cracking our dungeness open and one of the servers came by and helped us with that. This is a messy, butcher paper on the table, noisy, family friendly, plastic bib provided, eating at a picnic table, throw your shells in a bucket, fresh-off-the-airplane-fresh-seafood restaurant. The food just shows up at your table once it is cooked; a server will come by with a plastic bag filled with your order and plunk it down. And for those of you parents out there - yes, they have chicken strips and fries and they were tasty according to our very picky 5 year old. We spent 147 with tax and a 20 tip, which we thought was very reasonable for all of the food that we stuffed ourselves on and the beer, wine and tea. There are a couple of sinks to use to hose yourself off when you are done which was very handy too! I am from the west coast and the other 3 adults were from the east coast, so we definitely are aware of what good seafood is (hence the blue crab vs. dungeness order) and we all place our seal of approval on this place!

As a new Las Vegas resident, it's been my task to find decent pizza and Rosati's brings the flavor and quality of those small Chicagoland pizzarias to the Las Vegas area. Delivery service usually takes an hour, but the hour is well worth it as pizzas are delivered hot and well-made. The buffalo wings are delicious and mozzarella sticks are good. Rosati's thin-crust pizza is delicious and exactly as it's made in Chicago. The cheese is delicious and the italian sausage is flavorful and slightly spicy. Rosati's deep-dish is great with chunks of tomato in the sauce. Their pan pizza is very similar to Chicago-style pans. My only complaint is that the crust could use some additional flavor, maybe a more buttery consistency. Overall, I've used this Rosati's for delivery 32 times since I discovered it in March 2011. Excellent food quality and fair delivery times.

Let me start by saying that I would have given the casino alone a 3.... but unfortunately the casino gets rated with a hotel that I won't stay in again. The hotel is ok, it's just not great quality and the service was lacking greatly on both ends. I'm going to assume this is because they don't get a lot of people staying there at all, so you can imagine how much effort goes into making them happy. We arrived at 8: 00pm (didn't leave until 6: 30am) after an hour drive, checked into our room then went down for dinner. Once we got to the restaurant area we were surprised to find out that we had been seated next to two other guys from Florida who also had just booked their trip. So as soon as we sat down we decided to ask if anyone wanted to share a bottle of wine or beer... which turned out to be a really good idea! (That way we could split one bottle between us instead of four!) When we finished dinner we headed back up to our room and immediately started drinking our beers wines while watching TV in front of the fireplace. Again, very relaxing, but in my opinion the perfect thing to do before bed when your tired and ready to take off your shoes! Now, let me explain this part about the casino. If you haven't heard yet, the casino floor doesn't open until 11: 00pm!!! This means that the 7 bars don't even serve alcohol till midnight!!! And since there are no slot machines anywhere near where you check in, you must first go downstairs and give money to some random guy in order to play any games!! It took like 20 minutes just to get through security and get upstairs! Then we walked around a bit before heading over to the bar. There are only 4 bartender stations at this place, and you want to be sure to get there early enough to snag one because once it fills up everyone pretty much has to stand outside for drinks until another station opens. Since this wasn't happening at 9: 15 pm we quickly made our way across the street to the Atlantis Casino. You walk right up to the door and pay 10. 50 for parking (if you're lucky, otherwise 20). After paying and walking inside, you enter another hallway filled with slots and video poker machines. Although there aren't many choices here, they usually have something decent going on, especially during football season. The best part is that every machine has free wifi so you never need to worry about getting drugged! Just make sure to bring plenty of quarters, since these things cost a buck each. 1 - The food at Atlantis is absolutely appalling!!!! 2 - You will spend more time waiting in line than actually gambling. Even worse? They'll send you to the cashier without letting you know what wait time you're looking at! Most people think that Atlantis will guarantee you a quick game if you show up within 30minutes of opening, but that isn't true either..... they lie!!!!! For example, when we showed up at 10: 15, we waited 45 minutes to get onto a table. But when we left at 12: 05 am the same night, we barely saw a line. You literally have to figure it out yourself. Plus, sometimes the tables fill up fast when only three seats remain and you might not notice that they emptied the table for a new group coming in. At least we didn't lose too much playing Blackjack and Roulette, but still.... it certainly wasn't worth the hassle. Next stop: Caesars Palace in Las Vegas.

We had breakfast there both mornings and it was delicious. 3) Location is great, it's in the heart of the city and very convenient to walk to many attractions. The not-so-good: 1) The room was a bit small, and the air conditioning wasn't very strong, so it got a bit stuffy. 2) The bed was too soft for our liking, which made it difficult to get a good night's sleep. 3) The bathroom could use some updating, it was a bit outdated and there was some mold in the shower. Salty Senorita in Scottsdale.... mexican food, football on flat screens, outdoor seating, margaritas! Kinda sounds like a little piece of heaven to me? What's not to like, right? The horrible staff and the overpriced food? The location is cute, but not worth it. We had a reservation for 5:00pm (on time) and our table was ready when we arrived. The hostess sat us at a table in the back of the restaurant, which was fine, because we were with another couple. The waitress was fine and took our drink order right away. From there on out, things just went downhill. It took forever to get our drinks. I ordered a frozen margarita, which sounds amazing, right? No....it was so watered down it was terrible! My husband's beer came out, finally, and then my margarita followed shortly after. We placed an order for chips and queso and waited...and waited....and waited....for that to come. When it finally came, it was just awful. The chips were cold, hard and tasteless. The queso was bland and contained no spice whatsoever. We told the waitress about the queso and she brought us some jalapenos, which helped a little. We ordered the shrimp tacos and enchiladas verdes. The tacos were alright. The shrimp were a little overcooked, but they had a nice spicy taste to them. The enchiladas were very good. They were filled with chicken, cheese and topped with a tasty green sauce. We also ordered the house speciality, the "Salty Senorita," which is a grilled chicken breast served on top of a bed of rice, beans and covered in a yellow sauce and cheese. This dish wasn't too bad, but could have used more flavor. It didn't taste bad, but it wasn't really anything to write home about either. After 2 hours of waiting (yes, we were still sitting at our table), we finally left without ordering dessert. The waitress never asked if we wanted to see a dessert menu. The check came and was way more than it should have been. We had 3 beers, 1 margarita, 1 queso appetizer, 4 tacos, 2 enchiladas and 1 house speciality. This meal should have cost us around 60, but our check came out to be 95. I am never one to argue prices, but this was outrageous. At first, I thought maybe we were being charged an additional 20 gratuity, but there was nothing listed on our bill. If you are looking for a fun place to watch football and eat some decent Mexican food, don't waste your time with Salty Senorita. There are plenty of other places to go in Scottsdale.

This is the main branch for the Carnegie Library and it is needless to say, HUGE. The place holds more books than you can imagine, and even if they don't have the book you want, you can special order it, and they will bring it in. It is also a major attraction for the kids because of the huge kids section. It has a stage, a puppet theater, a kids reading nook, a craft corner, computers, and more. I was surprised to see how they have been able to keep this a "library" and not a "digital center" like so many other libraries have become. They have a lot of digital devices, but they still have a lot of the traditional stuff as well. They have magazines, cassette tapes, DVDs, and even VHS tapes. They have tons of computers, but they also have a traditional card catalog. They also have a lot of "social" stuff going on. While I was there, there were two different kids programs going on, a movie night, a musical performer, and a computer class. The only thing I really disliked is that the bathrooms are on the top floor. While it is nice that they are located next to the kids section, if you have to change a diaper, it is a really long way to get to the bathroom. Overall, the Carnegie Library is a great place to visit, and it is FREE!

Let me preface this review with a couple of things: 1. I went on a Monday at 3pm, so probably not the most ideal time to see the freshest foods on tap in L.A., but we didn't have any issues. 2. We were all supposed to be eating at the same place (see below) and that was fine. Next day was full of foodies, so I just ate my salad and chorizo sandwich. I'm going to say no because it's perfect for when your family isn't there - but that probably sounds like a bad idea, too? It's not! That said, I love grilled cheese sandwiches. They're yummy, they taste great, and if anything, they are healthier than salmon, which is the only fish-focused thing about pizza. And while you can make an exception for what really tastes golden - they also taste good. If you do go to a restaurant on a weekday since the city has its own outdoor dining area, you might even regret having an hour between meals at a patio restaurant instead of at a bar. But if you want to experience a piece of food more consistently from the kitchen, here are some places to try them out: The Friesie Fried potato chips Ground meat tacos, or beef brisket Baked potatoes, or mashed potatoes, or salami If you aren't feeling hostessly, try grilled cheese sandwiches. You'll find these items on Amazon, or across the street at Red Lobster. Go to their website, and get yourself some sandwich-like fries. It gets better with lime juice liberally sprinkled throughout. The bacon and tomato slices are light enough to really compliment the spicy bites and the homemade cheddar cheese sauce. Over the years (and I even gave them away to friends), I've tried several cheeses, including white and black, cherry tomatoes, pinto beans, and alfalfa bell pepper. While I haven't yet picked up anything new, I thought it would be fun to experiment with one I'd never tasted before. So I did. Since then, I've been learning how to enjoy grilled cheese sandwiches, and I don't know why I keep doing it... well, except for this recipe that I found as a cookbook. Note: This is a classic recipe I used on my own (no extra ingredients). To test it out, I made margaritas without a stir-fried pan. I left the pan covered overnight, until the chips came apart in about 6 hours. So far, I've had nothing to eat, so I am now wondering if I should continue using the same method if the chips are still forming after a few minutes. My favorite flavor, though, is chicken broth. For a traditional sandwich, the dip in olive oil and garlic powder, or with ground almonds, gives them a unique flavor as opposed to other flavors, such as shoving them into the boneless breasts. For a grilled cheese sandwich, use a layer of chopped avocado, thinly sliced, in a skillet over medium heat, reduce the heat, add the tahini and salt, and simmer for 10 minutes. You may need to let it cool slightly, but not significantly. Then, the chipotle seasoning will start melting and become sticky, making the same combo delicious again. As for the toppings, I couldn't give two fucks where food was concerned. I kept putting the hot peppers in water until the chips started to smell like home. But when I poured the chili spread on top of the airbrushed mock pit of shredded naan, I knew something was wrong. After letting it dry completely, I added some sliced onions, chopped parsley, and shaved sour cream. I think that the texture helped matters a lot less than keeping the chips in the pan long enough to allow the pressure to take hold in the middle. The last thing I wanted to do was throw in another bite of bread, because every time I do, I end up with a wicked chilli paste. Instead, I put the hot peppers in my like-for-like ham sandwich with plenty of water and salt. The leftover salsa was done in a blender and mixed with the cold cream, and was ready when the melted onions came together. I topped the shredded chicken in a glassy bowl with the ham and tomatoes, and then pulled the salad out to serve. And finally... it gets darker. Do you remember how beautiful the fall colors looked as I poured myself a drink? That's when the sun began shining. Did you notice the redness when you finished your glasses? Yeah, you do.
