Had dinner here the other night for my birthday. I've been to teppanyaki restaurants before and have had a good time as the chef always told jokes while he was cooking. This place was a bit different. The chef didn't tell any jokes. In fact, he was a bit of a grump. He did not acknowledge any of the customers until it was time to cook their meal. The food, though, was very good. My steak was cooked perfectly, and the shrimp was very good too. I ordered the chicken fried rice, which was excellent. The prices were about what you would expect for a Japanese steakhouse, maybe a little less expensive. It's located in the old Golden China building on Fruitville Rd. When scoping around online for a good NYE dinner destination for my husband and me, Casbah's prix fixe menu really jumped off the page! Since the Big Burrito group is so popular, I was happy to get reservations, especially since a lot of times were already booked. The hubby and I arrived a few minutes early for dinner. I had planned additional time to park and was delightfully reminded that Big Burrito restaurants have free valet parking so great, especially with slushy snow on the ground! Even though we were a few minutes early, the hostess took our coats and seated us immediately. Service was extremely attentive from start to finish. Waters were re-filled quickly. Bread was brought to the table almost immediately and we were offered another basket as soon as we finished the first. The bread came with a delicious spread - was it goat cheese? - that I just couldn't stop eating. Silverware whisked away with each course was promptly replaced. We ordered both the land and sea courses to share so we could try the entire NYE prix fixe menu. None of the eight dishes disappointed! The first courses were Sea Scallops Octopus and Duck Confit. The sea scallop was perfectly cooked, the octopus - thought not my cup of tea! - was also well cooked, and the balsamic flavor in the dish was very tasty. I absolutely loved the duck confit dish. It was served with mustard greens and fruit with a to-die-for dressing - a delicious combination! The second courses were Potato Gnocchi and Mushroom Tortelloni. The gnocchi was served with lobster, which was a unique but nice paring. Though a strongly flavored dish, the tortelloni was delicious, and I enjoyed another unique paring, tortelloni with chunks of beef short rib. Lake Ontario Walleye and Roasted Veal Strip Loin were the third courses. Both were cooked to perfection. The walleye's skin was perfectly crispy, and the veal strip loin was cooked medium well but was still deliciously juicy and tender. However, a component of each dish was disappointing a mustard flavor in the walleye and pickled mustard seeds covering the veal. I really can't hold this against Casbah though. I'm just not a fan of mustard! Finally, the desserts was fantastic! The Chocolate Ganache Tart was the ending of the sea courses. The chocolate was strong, even a little bitter, and was served with a little champagne strawberry compote. I grew more accustomed to the bitterness with each bite, and it was the perfect ending to three courses filled with fish. A Caramel Macaroon completed the land courses. The macaroon was delicious and served with a little apple sorbet and caramel sauce. Our experience at Casbah was spectacular! Based on this experience, I debated giving the restaurant five stars.... but decided to wait until I returned a second time. And I can't wait to return!

I was planning on taking the valet parking since it was raining, but he said the valet parking was full and to use the self parking. Then he asked me if I wanted to check in before I parked. That was a first. I said no, so he gave me the key to the room and off I went. I parked my car in the 4th floor of the garage and took the elevator to the 6th floor. I went to my room and was in for a bit of a shock. The room was small and very dark. I turned on the lights and nothing happened. I was planning on watching some TV, but again, no luck. The TV wasn't working. I called the front desk and they sent a maintenance guy up. He fixed the lights and told me the TV was broken and to call the front desk. I did, and they said to call back in a few minutes and they would send someone up. After an hour I called again and they told me to call back in a few minutes. I called back an hour later and they told me the same thing. I gave up on that. The next morning I checked out and went to my car. I got a 10 parking voucher, but the parking was 12. Whatever. I put the voucher in the machine and the machine said the voucher wasn't valid. I went back to the front desk and explained to them that the voucher was no good. The girl behind the counter said that she would talk to the garage people. I said thanks and went back to my car. She called me as I was walking out of the garage and told me that the garage people said there was nothing they could do, and that I would have to pay the 2. I told her I would not, and left. After I got home I called the hotel to speak to the manager. I explained the whole situation to him and he told me he would call me back. I'm still waiting for that call. In conclusion, the casino is great but the hotel is terrible. If you stay here make sure you get a voucher from the hotel, not the casino. Also make sure the TV works. Not the best but not the worst. Good value for the money, and great customer service.

First to state I was really disappointed with my experience at circus circus in general. But me and my brother were so tired by the time we got to the hotel we weren't going to spend all day there. My brother had a 3 day package but I only got a one day. So we got a room with 2 queen beds. After checking in my brother and I found that our room keys weren't working. We went down to the front desk to get new keys. We were told we were on the wrong floor and needed to go up. So we went up and it was still the same room. My brother tried to get on the wifi and it didn't work. Then it said on the computer that our room key was a 2 day pass. So we went back down to the front desk to get a new key. We were then told to go up and try again. So we went back up and it still wasn't working. We waited about 20 minutes for someone to come get us. We were told we were on the wrong floor again. So we went back down to the front desk to get a new key. They were still telling us to go up. We waited about 30 minutes before we told them we wanted to cancel our rooms. The lady told us we could do that but we couldn't get our money back. We had to go out the front door and then go back in through security to do that. So we did that and they did give us our money back. After we got our money back we went to the front desk and we were told that we were still on the wrong floor and needed to go up. So we went back up and it still wasn't working. We waited another 15-20 minutes before we decided to call security. They came and got us again. So we were there for about an hour waiting for someone to come get us. Then we were told that the wifi wasn't working in our rooms. We called security and they told us we could go up to the rooms but the wifi was only working in the casino and then you had to go back down to your room to get back on. So we went up to our rooms and the wifi still didn't work. Then we had to go down to get on again. The rooms were very small and they had no place to put our bags. So the room felt very cramped. It was very dirty. The bed had a lot of hairs and the bathroom was very dirty. The toilet was broken and the water didn't work. The shower had no hot water and the shower head didn't work. The tv was so small. The pillows were very uncomfortable. The air conditioning didn't work. I didn't like that we were on the 3rd floor but they gave us rooms on the 1st floor and our door was still on the 3rd floor. It was very hot. We couldn't use the microwave in the room but it was very close. The wifi was free and it was very slow. There was no chairs at the table. It was very uncomfortable. I don't think I would go back there. There were many better places to stay at.

We arrived in St Thomas after having dinner with friends and had no problems getting into town due to port authority working overtime so we did some shopping while waiting. Once inside the terminal there are several restaurants close together on one level as well as shops right outside where people will line up trying to get through them quickly when going from ship to shore since those are all open 24 hours. The inner harbor area gets crowded also around 8am-11AM (when bus tours arrive). Also note that the island shuts down completely at midnight. For example on the Thursday night we went ashore their were NO scheduled activities anywhere except the 2 local bars which closed mid afternoon. If you need more time ashore there's usually taxi service available like Uber or cab services. To be safe though I recommend staying onboard until 11-12 PM every day. In summary the marinaharbor area feels crowded during certain times depending upon whether there is activity happening or not, but most importantly make sure you enjoy yourself and do NOT rush around taking pictures looking for something great to capture each moment of your vacation. After returning back its best to book another excursion early morning such as snorkeling first light tour. Or sometimes even better to catch the sunset walk safari the following evening. It's been open for approximately 2 months and they have a bit more to do to impress me. Upon entering it took a few minutes of us waiting at the front to finally be acknowledged and greeted. There's a hostess area, but no hostess. We wanted something light, easy, and fast. We ordered a pizza special that included a drink, slice of pizza, and a salad. The pizza came out re-warmed and dry. I was not happy about them passing off fresh, gourmet pizza with a re-warm in the toaster oven appeal (I've re-warmed enough pizzas in my time that I know it when I see it). I asked the server about it and he admitted that it was not fresh and that they would make us fresh slices. The new pizza came out 10-15 minutes later and it was a stark difference compared to the initial slice. The pizza was freshly baked (not freshly made by hand) and the cheese was delicious. Some helpful tips: 1. Do us both a favor and get it right the first time. You only have one chance to make a good first impression. Unfortunately, the initial impression I have of this establishment is disappointment. If you know you were giving out old pizza, why do it? Especially when you are a new business and you are building your reputation. 2. If you advertise gourmet be it. The quality of the pizza was ordinary. If you were to advertise as a regular pizza joint, I would think you were great. However, since you say you are gourmet you have missed the mark entirely. Gourmet to me is handmade and extraordinary with toppings and spices and I didn't see that. 3. Same line of thought...if you advertise organic wheat crust use it. My crust was an ordinary white flour crust. The two main reasons (gourmet and organic wheat crust) I picked this restaurant instead of the one next door were the very things that I didn't end up experiencing. The service was okay. The restaurant itself is in a great location and is decorated very nice! I think this place has great potential, it's just getting the form and function to align (be consistent in your advertising message with the product you give to your consumer).

Roses are red, Popeye juice is green, Hula Juice Bar, J'adore The most fruit-filled, colourful cafe I've seen On Valentine's Day, I am dedicating a review to one of my favourite places in Edinburgh. My previous reviews tell a long-lasting love affair with Hula, and even after two years, I have something new to include in my review. When I first moved to Edinburgh, two years ago, it was the winter the Snow hit. You remember that snow? That covered the whole city in frozen, trampled down, thick snow. I had researched Yelp for nice cafes in my area, and being something of a health-conscious person, I was delighted and intrigued by a smoothie and juice cafe that promised to fill me up with vitamins. So along I came and had a coffee with chocolate caramel shortcake, and orange juice. Back then, the cafe looked different. I can't even remember how it looked really. Flash forward two years and in that time, Hula has had a makeover and is now one of the most colourful cafes in the city. Some new juices have appeared on the menu - the aforementioned Popeye which is filled with Spinach being one of my favourites. For a day when I'm feeling super hungry, the mexican tuna wrap provides a feast with the excellent, spicy guacamole a bonus. For a morning when my yoga practice was particularly hard, and I'm at once thirsty and hungry, Sunshine in a Cup smoothie with a slice of banana cake (gluten free) does the trick. For an afternoon when I'm tired and run down, I could skip coffee and have a Ginger Jack juice with extra fresh ginger, and an Energy Booster. There are salads, wraps, bagels, fresh soups, porridge and fruit salad for breakfast, juices and smoothies all day long, and cakes that are supplied from several local Edinburgh cake-bakers (Mrs C, Love Pure Cakes, Peppers to name a few). And the new, wonderful addition to Hula? I believe they are now running Juice Detox programmes, whre you can pay a set fee and Hula will provide you with literes upon litres of juice each morning, which you drink all day. So I want to premise this by stating that I am not someone that goes to a restaurant trying to hate the food, especially Mexican food which has always been my favorite type of cuisine. The restaurant itself is called "La Villa de la Reina" and it was located in San Juan del Rio Verde Mexico on one of those high tops tables with bar stools right underneath an open air ceiling fan at most times you have people hanging out there drinking beer or margarita's etc... so naturally when we came in he immediately sat us down at their table next to the open door where all the flies were flying around getting into everything including our food but then again who are they going to complain about? The waiter tried his best to prevent any more bugs from entering the premises whatsoever. He did bring out water no less than four different occasions throughout dinner as opposed to just bringing it once like other restaurants would do but he kept doing something else wrong too... oh well.... Now back to what we ordered: My wife and myself had Enchiladas Suizas which are basically deep fried spicy pork enchilada's topped with shredded cheese rolled up in corn tortillas served with avocado sauce, pico de gallo and guacamole......my son opted for Choco-Taco (elaborate name aside) which consisted of two churros dipped in chocolate syrup drizzled with hot fudge and peanuts.... my daughter had Papa's Pancakes which consisted of green chili pancakes served with avocado sauce. We also received 2 orders of chipssalsa bean dip per person. So, needless to say lunch ended up being quite caloric even though none of us ate much afterwards because we were full after having breakfast before coming here...lol.. so needless to say we didn't eat anything else until almost 10pm that night! As far as prices go during the week you can get three items off the menu plus beans and rice for 9 pesos (0.48 USD). During weekends it becomes 12 pesos (0.63USD) and includes refried beans, rice AND meat such as pastrami, chicken breast, grilled steak,...etc. That is pretty reasonable if your midwesterner standards hold true. Although it seems cheaper when compared to American prices its actually slightly more expensive since Mexico receives a huge amount of U.S. dollars daily.......but still worth every penny considering how great these dishes turned out to be!! For reference here is a link to a website that explains exactly why mexican food isn't healthy.....you may need a translator however if you don't speak spanish!

And then there were desserts! There was soooooooo much dessert variety here that I'm still trying to decide what I liked best. Italy has great wine, chocolate and pretty much every other type of sweet treats you can imagine: gelato, cheesecakes... In Italy also some amazing vegetarian options exist such flavoursome pastas stuffed with cheese and vegetables, very nice soups and stews made from beans and legumes, lots of nuts and berries etc Spain has wonderful fresh local produce and olive oil but unfortunately few people know how to cook properly using this product because olive oil doesn't come cheap!! Here in Spain most dishes need to be cooked slowly over low heat; slow cooking takes time and patience therefore making Spanish often require long preparation time. (Of course both sides work) But apart from these two main differences between places I've stayedvisited, I don't remember anything special about them..

Being a member of the Edinburgh University Scandinavian Society, this Swedish cafe has been the venue for a couple of our events, and it's definitely appropriate, even down to it's decor of minimalist scandinavian design. I lived in Sweden for two years, so was increasingly surprised as I spotted one swedish speciality after another on the menu and at the counter! It's primarily a bakery, so all the delicious pastries and desserts I'd only found in Sweden were here, and in abundance as well; cinnamon buns and all sorts of muffins! They also sell a selection of sandwiches, and for those homesick Swedes, hand made crisp bread and jams imported from the land of the Vikings! On the occasions I've been there for society get-togethers, there have been free for all waffles, served with ice cream, jam and cream.... extremely messy but equally satisfying! And ofcourse a Swedish cafe wouldn't be complete without an endless supply of coffee; seeing as I'm not particularly a fan, I'll give it a pass and say I've definitely had worse. Peter's yard is just off George Square, so a student favourite, and with outdoor seating, it's a glorious place to be when the Scottish weather decides to be generous!

I really like what The Huxley have done to this space, and especially on their menus: both food, and cocktail. Previously the Rutland Bar, which had been around for a fair while, a makeover and change of name can do the world of good. I always liked the Rutland, but it felt very much like a bar to have meetings in, or a subdued drink. The Huxley has a great vibe midweek. I've yet to visit at the weekend. But yknow what? As far as a bar for a mid-week after-work drink and munchies goes, it's pretty good. I've heard amazing things about their burgers and hot dogs. I will be back to try these (the burgers come with two patties per bun?!) When I came, I tried a Grapefruit Mojito and it was really fresh and delicious. When a bar isn't specifically a'cocktail bar' I can be very suspicious. So many times a cocktail can come unmuddled, or with chunky ice instead of crushed, and it can just taste like watery, alcohol with a sprinkling of fruit. Not at The Huxley. I happened to meet the mixologist at the bar, who was very proud of all his creations (he has made all the recipes) and was really keen to make some cocktails for me. I love this kind of energy and passion. There were some delicious looking numbers there too. The food menu is also really unusual, inspired and different. Hot dogs are, well, so hot right now. But there were also nibbles like Poached Duck Egg with black pudding and chorizo. Or a Scotch Dug Egg with HP sauce. Or Mini Chipolatas with dip, which I had. And the Battered Sole, with a side of seaweed salad. Note: do not put half the seaweed salad in your mouth at once. It tastes like the sea. Like the sea and fish. Its 4 A.M. You've been out partying in Vegas all night and staring you in the face is a huge Denny's sign. It's easy to understand why though. If you're in Vegas and looking for some Hawaiian food, Island Flavor is definitely worth checking out.

This is an outdoor seating only Starbucks. There is a walk-up window for drinks, but no visable snacks. There is also a drive thru window for cars. There are 4 small round tables with 2-3 chairs a peice, and 1 larger rectangular table for disabled access with 2-3 chairs also. Prices are normal for a starbucks. Pros: Outdoors in late fall and early spring will be nice here, and it definately can't get crowded here. Cons: Only 2 umbrellas outside keep you shady from the sun or dry from the rain, there doesn't appear to be snacks here. No indoor seating, Midsummer here is going to be bad, also Semi-trucks are constantly shifting on the freeway here so it is very noisy, and there are no power outlets. There are several other open wifi spots here like the days inn and dennys, so you might be better suited to moving to one of those locations, but if you must sit here, then the attt free wifi hotspot speed is 1.4 Mbit download speed, and 1.2 Mbit upload speed. (divide Mbit by 8 to get actual MB speeds). Overall I give this spot a 2 thumbs up out of 5.

This is unadulterated pinball nirvana. When I assume room temperature, just spread my ashes over this place.... Located a couple of miles off the strip, Pinball Hall Of Fame offers you a trip back to your youth, provided you grew up being a pinball geek like me. I played games that I haven't touched in 35 years. I was so happy I seeked this out and can't wait to return. In addition, you can play the latest pinball machines available. I F! love this place!

I cannot say this clearly enough, DO NOT GO! We wasted 86 on this place. Took over 20 minutes to just get our chips and salsa. Chicken Fajitas and Pork Carnitas were bland and tasteless. We ordered a pitcher of margaritas, I am a lightweight, I had almost 3 glasses and never felt a thing. My husband used to bartend and seriously doubted ANY tequila was in there, the overwhelming flavor was sweet and sour. No dissing the waitress as she attempted her best with no help from front door staff or bus staff. Yes it was a busy Saturday night but did they not expect that? C'mon already it's the strip! The only part that made us feel any better was the view of the Bellagio water show. Come sit at the bar overlooking it and have water!

ehh overrated!! price was ok, but the food was not. Our steak was really thin and dry. We requested medium-rare but what they gave us was overcooked.. other plates didn't have that problem so I'm still left confused about why ours did... Overall, our dining experience at this restaurant has been great! The staff is very friendly and helpful to make sure we get exactly what we want or need when eating here. And their service is actually better than many of the others in town were well worth it:)

Reserved a car for noon. Showed up late (my fault) to find they rented my car to someone else; didn't bother to call me (their fault). Both employees were on the phone when we got there and didn't bother to acknowledge us for at least 5 minutes. They said they could get me another car from another location if I was willing to wait 45 min. So Make sure you call or show up on time because their inventory is like 2 cars.
Best black bean burger ever in life, get the onion sticks instead of fries. Always crowded but really delicious. There salads topped with a burger are pretty good!

Monte Carlo, why did I choose to stay here? Must be that it is located right in the middle of the strip, next to Aria and the City Center. This is the closest I will ever get to stay in a Las Vegas resort, that's for sure! I have always been a fan of the Monte Carlo, after seeing it in countless TV shows and movies. It's a resort that I always wanted to see for myself. My parents stayed here once, in 2010, but the only photos they took were of the inside of the hotel. I had to see the outside for myself. We arrived in Vegas around 2 am. We checked in and then went to our room on the 30th floor. It is a nice room. Big TV, comfy bed, and a nice bathroom. What to do at 3 am? I had no idea, but I wanted to go to the pool. The pool was closed, as expected, but we could see it through the windows. We ordered some pizza and then went to bed. The next morning, we went for a walk in the City Center. We then had some breakfast at the Cafe, at Monte Carlo. I had the Monte Carlo breakfast, which was 2 eggs, bacon and toast, plus a mimosa. I was kinda bored with the food, but it was alright. In the afternoon, we went to the pool. The pool was awesome! I love the big chairs, the water fountain and the big pool! The pool area is called the Rivea Pool and Lounge, and it's for ages 21. After lounging in the sun, we walked over to the Aria casino. It was a pretty nice casino, but we didn't stay there for very long. We then went to our room to get ready for dinner. We were going to the brand new restaurant at Monte Carlo, Yusho. This was one of the main reasons I wanted to stay here. I had to eat at this restaurant. Yusho is located on the casino level, and it is a Japanese restaurant. I've never had Japanese food, so I wanted to try it out. I ordered the Beef Tataki and the Beef Ramen. I didn't like the ramen, but the tataki was good. It was beef with rice, and it was really good. After dinner, we went to the Aria again, and then to the Mirage. The Mirage had some cool aquariums and a cool volcano. We then went back to the Aria. The next day was our last day in Vegas. We went to the pool in the morning. I went down the waterslide, and it was fun. I didn't really get to see the whole resort. It was really big. I wish I could've explored more, but I guess I will just have to come back. What did I think of Monte Carlo? I loved it! It was definitely my favorite resort in Las Vegas. I hope to come back here one day!

I've been going to cafe rio for a few years. Tonight I went and ordered a pork quesadilla with extra meat for a first time. I had ordered it to go and when I got home to open it I was very disappointed. They put meat inside, but seemed to have no cheese so the tortillas didn't stick together and meat fell out everywhere. They never cut it into pieces so I had to use a knife and fork to cut the whole thing apart. It looked so unappetizing and looked like an open face taco, not a quesadilla. Very disappointed they would serve this.

What can I say about this place that hasn't already been said?? Easily the best food I've had in Montreal. I had the mac cheese, which was perfect. The mushrooms were cooked to perfection. I've never had mushrooms taste so delicious. The pesto was amazing. The cheese was so good, I want to marry it and have its babies. I don't know what they did with the macaroni, but it was light and fluffy and I don't know what to do with my life now that I've had it. My boyfriend had the poutine, and I was able to have a bite or two of that as well. It was the best poutine I've ever had. The fries were so fresh. He said it was the best poutine he's ever had. I just stared at him, trying to figure out why I wasn't having his poutine, and he just told me to get my own. I wish I could have had half of that. Their fries are seriously the best thing I've ever had. I'm starting to feel like I'm getting repetitive, but I can't help it. They just make the best food I've ever had. We even had a dessert, the strawberry cake. I'm not sure what it's made of, but it's definitely some kind of cake, but I swear it was so good, it didn't taste like cake. I wish I could make something like that. It was strawberry flavored, and so delicious. I seriously need to start getting my butt over there and learning how to make some of this food. We had a white wine that was delicious as well. I don't know what it was, but it was a white wine. The food is so great and unique, that I think I just have to learn how to make it, and then I'm set for life.

I was extremely disappointed when ordering pizza from this place. The girl that rang up our order said it would be 20-25 minutes for our pizza and garlic knots to arrive so we just went to another nearby restaurant instead, probably the best decision of my life! The food is not good but I would never go back there again!

The pizza was ok..... Dinner salad was still defrosting and came after our pizza deep fried mushrooms.... They seemed to be overstaffed with romper room rejects! The mgr should cut staff maybe pay a dollar or two more an hour to hire people who have reached puberty.

I came here during the Mtl a table festival, a festival that allows foodies to try out new restaurants at a fraction of the price. I was looking forward to trying some dishes from Aka but couldn't find any on their menu.
At one point while at Bacchanal, sometime after eating a plate overflowing with at least a pound of crab legs and before taking on a final slice of cheesecake (one rink).

First time here recently. Great place! Friendly bartender with good recommendations for beer. Terrific happy hour as well. I had the Prosciutto and Peach Flatbread which was easily one of the best flatbreads I've ever had. It was on special, but still a great price. Service was fantastic. Really enjoyed the two beers I tried as well. Will be back! Best beer in town! Bartender was great!

Love this place. Food is always great and ready fast. The employes are all american and speak English and the restaurant is clean and bright, a lot different from the teriyaki joints I'm used to. I usually call in my order and it it always ready by the time I arrive to pick it up. Wish they had a bigger beverage selection.

I love taking my friends from out of town to Bistro Fruits Folie. It is much better than Chez Cora and rivals Eggspectations in my opinion. The servers are always fresh and the service is always good.

The cream Italian ice is amazing. I love the chocolate chip cookie dough and mint chocolate chip. It tastes like ice cream but lighter, seriously amazing. I normally get the small size which is plenty of ice cream-like texture. Highly recommend!

Round Two! ding-doh?! I recently was at an event that featured the Rusty Pickle Truck. They were giving out samples of their pickles and a Pulled Pork BBQ Slider. The Pickles were better, but still not crunchy or all that special. The Slider however was really good. It had a good flavor, and was well made. While I may not like the pickles, I would order this again.

Creative Nails is still the best! I've never seen a nail salon that cares as much about customer service as this one. They really take the time to give you an amazing manicure and pedicure, they are very clean and have everything from acrylic nails in all colors of your dreams (which look gorgeous!) to gel polish overlay which lasts longer then any other product on the market today!! You can't go wrong here:)

Centurylink is the WORST company I have ever had to deal with. My internet and landline have been knocked out now off and on for over 2 months. When I call them to resolve this problem, they transfer me around until they eventually hang up on me. I want to disconnect ALL their services forever, and tell EVERYONE what a worthless company they truly are!!!!
It might be my first check in but I've been here three times already. This time I brought my boyfriend with me. They have a wide range of flavors when it comes to weed too, gotta love them!

I was so excited to see a Pink Box Donuts coming to this location, as it is close to where I work. I'd seen them on some food show, and I decided to bring my kids along for this event! Pink Box Donut Shop has always been my favorite kind of donut shop!!! It's huge! There are no better place than Pink Box Donuts!! Here they serve delicious chocolate chip ice cream cheesecake without cheese! This store also houses a huge selection of candy bars but have you ever considered adding a smorgasbord of other treats such as chocolate milk drink, juice box or candy wrapper? They're only 5 and if your kids want more than one then you can get like 20 pieces in a day (or something similar). Their cheeseburger recipe ideas are great too!

I celebrated my boyfriends 30th in Vegas so we came here for small bites. I found out they have a Happy Hour on Oysters- 1.75 each instead of 2.75. Boy , that sounds like a great deal! What restaurant are you at? If you're looking for some other small bites, I can recommend a few dishes that go well with oysters. Some good options include shrimp cocktail, ceviche, crab cakes, and calamari. If you feel like something a little more substantial, perhaps you could try some fish tacos or sliders. Don't forget to pair your food with a refreshing drink - a crisp white wine or a cold beer would be perfect with oysters. Enjoy your meal!

Really good place for lunch or fast food better than your average burger joint! Culvers offer more of a deluxe burger. They are good size and offer many tasty sides the cheese curds are pretty tasty as well. Also, they have seasonal combos for food and concrete mixer which I highly recommend. I mainly go to culvers for their amazing concrete mixers. Their flavor of the day always changes plus you get two free mix ins for the concrete mixers! I am a huge fan of their cheesecake options you can get just about any berry and cheesecake combo! Friendly staff and they usually have coupons available. try their- Butter burger with or without bacon Sweet potato fries Concrete mixers- Ask about their seasonal specialties

Not a buffet that I'd recommend in Vegas! The lay out and design is poor. I know that doesn't seem important, but it is. When you have people going in a million different directions with plates piled high, small children darting all around and very little space to move in - It's a disaster waiting to happen! The actual counter space is pretty expansive, but they only use half of it and cram it all together. This is what creates the CLUSTER! The offerings on the buffet are fairly dull. Not a lot of flavor to any of the dishes. The only items worth checking out are shrimp crab legs. The crab legs are sliced right down the middle which makes easy retrieval of the meat without little effort - perfect! The seafood is only offered at certain times of the day so make sure you've timed it right before throwing down the cash.
New restaurant, the food was not bad. There was no one there but our table when we went, I believe that is because they are located in a business district 3 stars
Took this firm four tries to fix my air conditioner last July. Wouldn't have cared except for the 115 degree temperatures at that time. Would recommend avoiding this firm at all costs.

I'm giving this location 1 star because the service is horrible!! The yogurt is yummy, but every time I have gone the lady working at the register has been very rude. First time I was there she was talking on her phone when I walked up, I waited about 30 seconds for her to look up and say hi. She never smiled or said a word. Second time I was there she screamed my name, I never heard my name being screamed in my life, I walked up to her and asked her to repeat herself and she did. Third time I was there she wasn't even in the store when I walked up, it took about 2-3 minutes for her to walk over to the register and ask me what I wanted. I would not recommend this location! I love this location because they have the best yogurt! I have tried other locations and the yogurt is not as good as this one. The lady working is always nice to me and I get to know her more every time I go there. I am glad that I found this place. The yogurt is the best! I have tried all the yogurt places and hands down this one is the best.

This was the second of two buffets we visited while in Vegas (the first being Wicked Spoon). Of the two, this was far more hyped up, but that only led to a bigger let down. There isn't a whole lot to say about the environment here: it's beige, really abundantly lit up, and loud. If you need an idea of who you'll be eating with, just comb the line before you head in, or people watch as you wait well over 30 minutes in some cases to get a table. Oh, and expect plenty of families. The service was solid, albeit busy. I don't remember our servers name because she never physically stopped moving as she said it. She was either dropping of drinks, checking up on us as she walked by, or grabbing plates off the table when the busing staff was busy else where. She certainly smiled the whole time though. I was trying to put together a list of highlights and misses like my other buffet review, but to tell you the truth, a lot of the food here was a let down. I really don't remember much of it. I did like the first cut of lamb I had, but when I went back for another serving it seemed like they had prepped it completely different and all the flavors I liked the first time around were completely missing. The sushi was abysmal. The rice was dry and had a styrofoam taste to it. The ribs were pretty good, but no one seemed to be stationed to cut them, so I had to make two trips before I could try them. There were two things that stood out now that I'm concentrating on our meal: the strawberry and cream desert shooter, and the salmon poke. The poke had a great fresh taste to it, and a really nice and subtle heat that reared its face after a couple bites. The desert shooter was also really refreshing, light, and had a great tang to it from the slightly sour strawberry. All in all, I don't think I'll be coming back to the Bellagio for their buffet. It really shows it's age, both in the food and in its looks. Plus, the wait was pretty awful, and we stepped up to the line as it ended at the restroom entrance. By the time we left, it had wrapped itself even further down the casino, easily another thirty to forty people deep.

I decided to try this place after reading all the reviews, boy was I wrong!! I live in Orange County, was in town decided go out the way to this place instead of eating the overpriced food in the hotel. Low and behold it's definitely overpriced for not so great food. I'm not a food snob, but I'd like to think I know what great food tastes like. Oxtail chili fries (what oxtail??) - can't taste the Oxtail and the chili itself is somewhat odd tasting left like a sour after taste. 2 stars Duck Steamed buns - nice presentation, but duck was cooked a bit rare and so tough that you can't even take a bite without pulling all the meats off. I've had better...I told the server and he was nice enough to it take off the bill. 1 star Miso Burger - I thought it tasted pretty good, flavors all work together. 3.5 stars Shogun Burger - Of course the server recommended this burger, it's the most expensive burger on the menu 25. First off all if you don't know what Unagi is it's (eel) not everyone is familiar with the term. My son who I think is a food snob wanted to try it, I only noticed it had Foie Gras. Since it's illegal to eat Foie Gras in California, I thought we're in for a treat. Let me tell you this burger combination is terrible...It has eel, Foie Gras, Pear, and beef, how does all this come together???!! Fish, beef, duck and pear in a bite is so weird and it left a fishy after taste, totally not what we expected. At the end the meal for 3 people cost 70 that's we 3 drinks and with the steamed duck buns taken off the bill. I'll take the all you can eat buffet at the hotels anytime...sorry Bachi Burger you're overrated!

I hate this center it would so hard to get in and out of; especially on weekends and during the holidays. I have almost been hit a handful of times at both ends. The police force has had no real presence there, its just some people who are trying to be funny with their loud music blaring from their car windows which is not very safe when you don't know if they will stop or not. People that do stupid things can always spot each other on camera because everyone else drives like they're invisible.

I had the Beet salad and it was delicious! My girlfriend had the Kale Ceaser and that was even better! Something about the honey-dijon dressing had me at hello. The salad came with a side of crispy kale chips, which were tasty as well; but I'm glad they weren't offered in place of some bread or something because those things are like crack for someone who doesn't eat glutengrain products (ahem). The staff here is always very friendly too - this is one New York City restaurant where there seems to be more "soul" than commercialism going on. It definitely feels less corporate (and thus sterile) compared to other spots around town that seem just obsessed with hoarding diners into their establishments so they can slap them all over Instagram (notcomplaining), while also trying not make any waves whatsoever by being overtly political anywhere near you or your meal. As long as we have places like Little Sister, our society will remain totally chill in terms of politics dinner conversation topics...okay maybe not 100 chill, haha..but still pretty sweet overall
What is there to love about Toby Keith's Bar Grill? Not a whole lot. My family and I had dinner at TK's last night as an alternative to Guy Fieri's Diners, Drive-ins ... More "

Worst run restaurant ever. Seriously. I know this is a tourist trap, but I'm from NYC and thought I could handle it. I came here because they have a pretty descent beer menu. My boyfriend and I were seated right away by a polite hostess right outside. We received menus and that's it. That is where the service stopped. There were 3 waitresses running a total of maybe 12 tables outside and not a single person even brought us water, looked at us - nothing. We waited and waited. I stared the hostess down and tried to get her attention from 4 feet away but she didn't care. Only one waitress was manning a few tables well but apparently we weren't in her section. I tried to get someone's attention, as did my boyfriend. A couple who looked like had been sitting there for 5 minutes longer than us finally received their beverage 20 minutes after we were there. So after 25 minutes, we got up and left. We couldn't take it anymore. There were about 4 or 5 tables in the same position as us. Didn't get to order, with menus on hand trying to hail down waitresses that were busying chatting it up and looking busy inside but actually doing nothing. Believe me, I was watching. The food looked crappy and overpriced and the beers weren't worth the effort. If I could go up to the bartenders that were clearly under worked, I would have. Steer clear or spend the end of days waiting to be served.
Freshest seafood in AZ! Everything made fresh. Great menu. Great atmosphere. You need to make this a regular spot if you haven't already!!! Great burgers. Great atmosphere. Always a treat.

This is an outstanding place. From the menu to the exceptional customer service, you will not be disappointed. I am a local to the area and have been here on many occasions for dinner and drinks. The food is consistently great and the service is always exceptional. Yes, the prices are slightly on the high side, but the quality of the food and drinks is well worth it. On a recent visit, the women's restroom had a gorilla hanging out of it. I will definitely be back.

Had a bug in my sake and they did not even care! Saryah was our waitress and although attentive not friendly nor apologetic about the visitor in my drink..... will I go back probably not....2 stars cause the food was good...too bad the service was NOT

Absolutely a beautiful place to hike! Whether you're A. A beginner B. Out of practice C. Out of shape or D. All of the above (like me) Pinnacle Peak can still be conquered! I love that there are multiple sitting areas at the bottom, and along the hike for resting and taking pictures. The paths are clearly marked and easy to follow and are wide enough to move over for the faster more experienced hikers, again while you rest and enjoy the view!; There are also signs dedicated to letting you know what types of plants are there, a great distraction for the younger hikers aka good excuse to stop, read, photo ops and catch your breath! A wonderful way to enjoy the outdoors and get a decent work out too. I survived, my 8 year old princess did too! If we can do it so can you!

I think it is a bit pricey for a super casual family restaurant. The kids meals are like 6 each! Also, as a vegetarian that doesn't care much for pizza the choice was EXTREMELY limited. I had a dinner salad and a cheese hoagie. Would much rather eat somewhere else.
Had a couple mix ups when I moved in but sunshine was great and helped get it settled! Way better staff and much more professional than the last apt I stayed... (talus ranch north phnx)

I have been a regular at Copper Star for the past 3 years. I love the uniqueness of this place - the drive thru with cheerful baristas (os) and the variety of specialty drinks that are constantly changing. If you like coffee, grab one on your way to work or home after a long day! The staff is very friendly and professional! The Growler Grabber was my favorite part about being here. It allows patrons to instantly fill their own growlers from any keg in stock without having to wait days until they get filled again. Copper Star has always been second to none when it comes to quality coffee. This year, however, it's even better than before as they've implemented some new features including: - The awesome gulp counter which lets customers see how many shots they're drinking while waiting for watercoffee to be made. It's easy to experience an entire city when you're staying right next door to Michigan Avenue Mall. Whether you want to shop or enjoy great dining options, our hotel is conveniently located near downtown's most popular attractions such as:

This is the best Thai I have found in Mesa. We had a variety of things off the menu, from appetizers to curry to stir-fry. All were excellent and portions were generous! Good water (not that awful tasting city water) was a nice bonus. Friendly service, too. Will definitely be a repeat customer. Probably tomorrow.

Four of us went there to watch football. The games were on, but music was playing, so watching the game was not much fun. I had a 3 Sunday special bloody mary. Meh. Weak on the vodka, and the bloody mary mix just didn't taste right. Food: I had the fall off the bone pork ribs. Fall off the bone they did, but the reason why was that they were boiled to death, then browned in an oven and dunked in sauce. Was more like eating pot roast with bones in it. Awful. The onion rings were just so so, same for the chili mac cheese. I guess the warning was evident when we walked in and the place was not very busy. Sorry...this is a one and done for me.

I'm continually unimpressed by the Amber Rose. I've not eaten there, and if I do I'll gladly update my review if it proves me wrong. But on the visits I've made to drink there, I've been put off by the way they've treated me. I've been to the Amber Rose several times over the years. In 2008 it was a tiny pub with no outside area, as you can see in the photo at the top of the page. It was known for its range of real ales, and had a good reputation as a community pub. The locals in the area loved it. Then the pub was bought and refurbished, with a new outdoor area. This sounds great, but the outside area is mostly concrete with an uncomfortable few picnic tables. The place also lost its regulars and became a drinking place for tourists, stag and hen parties, and sports fans. As a result, it's become a generic pub, rather than a great pub. The place is also known for its expensive drinks. In 2008, a pint was 3.50, now it's 4.50. If you think that's expensive, the Amber Rose has the cheek to charge 17.50 for a cocktail. (I do agree with them that some cocktails are worth that price. But the Amber Rose isn't a cocktail bar). The Amber Rose is also known for charging over the odds for a pint of Carling (4.00), and over the top prices for food. For example, their special of 'handmade' burgers and chips is 12.50. The burger is good, but it's nothing special, and this price is ridiculous. (In the Beefeater in Liverpool One, you can get two handmade burgers, chips and drinks for 20). The atmosphere in the pub is terrible. When I've been there, the music is too loud and the bar staff are snooty. The Amber Rose is also known for being one of the worst places in Liverpool to go for a game of pool, due to the quality of the tables. (If you go to the Liverpool Echo website, you can see that the Amber Rose has had a few complaints over the years). I know this review is a little on the negative side, but I'm trying to be honest. The Amber Rose is a fairly standard pub that's let down by its high prices and pretentious attitude. If you're in Liverpool on a budget, or you're a tourist looking for a pub with character, I wouldn't recommend the Amber Rose. The Amber Rose is at 203 Smithdown Road, Liverpool L15 3JR. Phone: . I'd give it 5 stars, except for the following few reasons: 1. it is slightly on the noisy side (being on the busy 10-lane Las Vegas Blvd S) 2. It takes more than an hour to get seated outside, due to the popularity. 3. Some of the waiters are not very friendly or personable. Especially this one guy called Kareem: he is too moody for a waiter at a French restaurant. And unpredictable.... He snapped at me in a very unkind way for simply telling him we're ready to order why- are you in a hurry? No, I am not in a hurry, but we waited over 80 minutes to sit here! Well I have so many customers before you. I guess you must be overworked, Kareem- but it is none of my business. As far as I am concerned, you still need to treat me as a valued customer! I don't deserve to be given attitude in front of my lady. At a restaurant that costs 60 or more per person... Other than that.... highly recommended! Our favorites here are: - Escargots Bernaise - Warm baguette bread - Delicious Market Salad with fresh tomatoes - Belgian Endive Salad (with blue cheese and pears). - Steak au Poivre (peppercorn wine sauce) - prepared medium - Red wine from Burgundy (around 7.50 per glass) sorry cannot recall the name:) - goes so well with the meat! - Creme Brulee - amazing - Tarte Tatin - apple cinnamon- but ummm, so yummy, so warm, so sensual. Not your average apple cobbler!

Ok this review is about 7 months late, but I still remember it like it was yesterday. The Boy had taken me to Mont Tremblant for a skiing trip for my belated Graduation present and Christmas present. On our trip, we stayed in Montreal our first night across the border. I had read many times over on websites that this place was the place to go for great Canadian-French cuisine so I thought this was the perfect place to try my first authentic French meal. Boy, they were not lying! I'll admit I did not know really anything about French food prior to this trip so I asked the waitress for her recommendations which she gladly gave in her thick French accent. We started off with the cromesquis with foie gras appetizer which is basically this tiny pastry thingy filled with hot, liquid foie gras that explodes in your mouth. It exploded so well that I think some of it came out of my boyfriends mouth, oh! We also ordered an appetizer of marinated smoked sausages that Boy just had to try. Next, for our main course we split the infamous Duck in a Can entree as well as the Beef tartar with a side of fries cooked in duck fat! The tartar was great but the duck was PHENOMENAL. Even though I am pretty sure I contributed heavily to my LDL count in this one meal, I must say that it is one of the most delicious and mind blowing food experiences I've ever had! It has opened me up to the world of French cuisine! I can't wait to eat here again when I come back for another skiing trip. It was my favorite meal the entire time I was in Canada. If you're ever in Montreal, do not miss the opportunity to have a food revelation like I did at this neighborhood gem!

They didn't seem to believe in miracles. It still haunts me to this day. And if anyone has any ideas, please let me know. Also, if anything ever changes at a hospital or clinic, feel free to reach out and tell me what happened right here! (For more info on how to help people, visit www. rwmlsdc. org).

Went for a 2lb. lunch yesterday just to'check in' on the classic. I went in with an open mind, but my suspicions were right: The most inconsistently-sized shrimp and crawfish of it's kind in Vegas. If you order a bag of shrimp here you WILL get some tiny runts, and over half of my shrimp's heads had fallen off by themselves in the bag, a telltale sign of non-freshness. And, this place serves up consistently stingy portions - I'm convinced that they weigh the sauce when they weigh your 1lb. bag of food. The sauce is not as good as I remember, and though I have fond memories of this chain from years past, I feel like Hot N Juicy has become the Pho Kim Long Lotus Of Siam of seafood-in-a-bag joints. Popular because of public relations, not because the food is great. Hot N Juicy's food is no longer made with love. You get a sense that the bottom line is king here. More profits more PR budget more TV exposure more first-time customers more profits. Sad. One day Robin Leach will be Hot N Juicy's only customer, and he'll expect to eat for free, because that's how he rolls. So, where to go for cajun seafood-in-a-bag? Cravin' Cajun is SO much more consistent, the crawfish are huge and the shrimp are ALL 10-15 count (and you get 16-20 in a 1lb. bag!). All of your shrimp heads will be intact, and the sauce at Cravin' Cajun is straight-up tastier. Please, if you only have time for one of these joints, try Cravin' Cajun. If you have time for two, try Hot N Juicy so you can make your own judgement. If you can't already tell, I am passionate about this subject.

This is by far the best Margarita deal I have ever come across in this town or any other en los Estados Unidos. No, I didn't drive home. Any serverbusser coming within 3 tables of us checked our table to see if we needed anything, every single time. La Fiesta is not fine dining. However, it is a superlative casual dining Mexican restaurant and delivers incredible value and I can't wait to go back.

What a great experience located in the South end of uptown. With any new experience, I will ask what is either most popular or recommended. The place was clean and nicely decorated (all modern except for a few walls painted black which were covered by thick curtains). It has two elevators that go to the top floor and an escalator going down as well as stairs to walk up one side of the building if you want to get off at the other entrance on S. Streets. The staff are friendly and helpful, if not overly enthusiastic. They did mention that their staff were mostly young students but they seemed fine with it. Nice looking carpeting and quite comfortable furniture and well appointed bathrooms along with a small kitchenette area. Interesting addition to East Blvd! Hopefully it helps bring back some life to the area. The atmosphere is great, super casual but packed and lively. Everyone is here to have a good time. The bar tables are ridiculous. The concrete top is only inches larger than the barrel base, so you cannot sit under the table at all. You have to sit sideways at the table. If I had waited an hour and a half to get that table, I would be pissed. Fortunately, we were sat at a hightop near the bar with regular seats. Other than the grotesquely under-estimated wait time, the service was really good. The tacos were interesting, but out of the four we tried I'm not sure I would eat any of them again. For me the food to go back for is the baked cheese dip and the tostadas. The cheese dip is not your standard Mexican fare. It has an awesomely bruleed top but eat quickly or it will get stringy and hard and cold. The potato tostada was fantastic! Served in a cold iron skillet, with a bottom layer of dressed romaine salad, it has two layers of fresh made crispy tostada shells. Separated by beans and crispy potato cubes, it has a great balance of flavor and texture. The green sauce on the table adds a lot to it. Definitely a good addition to the restaurantbar scene.

The chef's, Franco and Paolo, have a garden in the back, in which they grow some of the ingredients they use. They also recycle, and use eco-friendly cleaning products. In addition, they are one of the few restaurants I've been to in which a full vegan menu is available. While I didn't try any of the vegan items (I was too busy drooling over the mozzarella), I did get to sample the ravioli and the homemade gnocchi, and it was some of the best I've had in my life. I was also lucky enough to sample a delicious vegan dessert - tiramisu. Not only is this a delicious meal, but you can feel good about supporting a restaurant that cares about the environment. It was also fantastic. The dough was perfect, and the Nutella was ooey-gooey and warm. It was hard to stop eating it. I'm still thinking about it. I can't wait to come back and try the rest of the menu. There were so many things I wanted to try. This was my second time going to Bella Serra. I was here for a business dinner and I have to say that it was great. I had the pasta with the ragu sauce, which was perfect. The pasta was al dente, and the sauce was fresh and flavorful. My colleague had the pizza, which was also great. We had a great conversation with the waiter, who was very nice and accommodating. When we got the bill, he had taken off the tip, so we had to add it back. I didn't even have a chance to ask him to do that. The service was great, and the food was fantastic. I can't wait to go back. I've been to Bella Serra twice now, and I'm in love. This is my new go-to restaurant. It's small, which is one of the reasons I love it so much. The ambience is very cozy and homey, and the service is great. They really seem to care about their patrons. I can't wait to come back and try the rest of the menu. Having already visited the Home Hardware store in Morningside, I was expecting to find more of the same at their sister store in Portobello. I was pleasantly surprised to see an abundance of proper quality hardware and home decor items on display as well as a few lesser known specialties that you might not normally come across there such as a large glass sculpture made from marble. At this point I am now going into my second day of regular visits to Home Hardware stores and have been quite impressed with how they are taking care of their employees. We've spoken to several of them after our visit today and learned that while this is likely just a one-time occurrence it has become something of "standard practice" for these stores where many other businesses seem to ignore or even ridicule them. One employee even talked about how his store was actually closed during the last inspection because he couldn't afford to repair any damaged windows due to the immense amount of damage caused by all the broken glass. He said that customers were coming back weeks later asking if the store would be open yet again! From what we can tell, he should probably change his business model since nobody seems to want to shop there anymore! He also explained that this situation isn't unique to him but apparently happens frequently all around the city so he hopes that residents will speak out against it publicly when they hear about it first hand next time they go shopping: I think they really need some kind of public shaming campaign done throughout the city, especially with the way things have been going lately... A lot of people don't know that these places still exist and what goes through their minds when they walk into a place like this? They expect to be treated with respect and decency which clearly they're not getting here. It's really sad that this kind of thing is happening to these businesses and hopefully these guys will get help soon so they can stay in business and keep providing us with high quality products that we deserve. We aren't just talking about some random picture either... These pictures are highly recognizable throughout Vancouver - no matter where your family comes from or who you are. In addition to dealing mostly with local business owners, Elizabeth Brian also talk to other employees about their experiences working there. Here is an excerpt from an email exchange between Liz and another worker which she sent along with her interview requests: A lot of people say "oh you work at Home Depot?" And we always laugh and say "no" but we both know deep down inside that we do indeed work at Home Depot. If everyone started doing this they could make big changes. Especially if we all told our friendsfamily members to avoid Home depot whenever possible until things change. Finally, they ask anyone else reading this blog that might feel inclined to contact Home Depot about the issue (or themselves) whether they'd like to send an email calling attention to it. Not sure why in particular Home Depot needs to pay attention to this case specifically though since they have plenty of other similar complaints to deal with each month already.
