What a great way to end a night spent celebrating life:) My first attempt at making my own salsa (from fresh tomatoes) turned out pretty yucky! Not only did it turn brownish around the edges by the next morning, it tasted horrible as well. So I've been trying again ever since. Turns out, if you make enough jars [like my mom does] you don't really need to cook anything other than peel, seed, and slice them. Just dump 'em in a pot, cover' em and wait for them to end up tasting good, haha. When I tried this batch last weekend, I used a different recipe. I love the variety. Mine has refried beans which gives it a little bit of extra flavor. You should try adding olives green onions peppers etc., depending on who you are cooking for. Oddly enough, the people I usually share it with prefer mine without those things. I think they tend to overwhelm the tomato taste. I happen to disagree though; I guess everyone likes what he she likes! Kinda wish I could find tomatillos locally but until then, I'll use any kind of store bought ones. Anyway, here's how you make it!:) Tomatoes (or whatever fruit works best for your family) sliced thin. Rinse off the shells and throw them away. Place in a medium sized pot, fill halfway with water, add salt pepper, cover, bring almost to a boil, let simmer for 20 minutes. Strain through a colander, rinse, repeat process 2nd time to catch as many seeds as possible. Return mixture to pot and heat toward boiling point once more, letting simmer for another 15 - 30 minutes. Now take your lovely roasted tomatillo salsa and let cool completely. Store in airtight containers for up to 1 week:). Posted by

The Nile Cafe is very, very small. Very. I mean, really, the place is teeny-tiny...but it doesn't matter much. It's also usually empty. When I first started working downtown, I didn't know where anything was. I had no idea where to head for lunch, with the exception of the Jack in the Box across the street from my building...and that was just not going to do. Driving around on 7th St., one of the first beacons of possible culinary delight winked at me from the corner of Roosevelt - The Nile Cafe. I love Mediterranean cuisine, so I made time to stop. I've actually visited the Nile Cafe several times, and the experiences are always so different from one another. The food is consistently okay, with two marked exceptions - the delicious artichoke hummus, and the absolutely terrible falafel. The service is where the big gap resides. There is one man who works there, (I perceive him as being the owner, although I have no actual reason to think this), who is very kind and courteous. He is patient, attentive, and soft-spoken but also friendly. Everyone else who works there is disinterested to the point of rudeness. Blank stares, no verbal acknowledgement...it is very uncomfortable to dine in, and, honestly, a little uncomfortable to order out. I go back occasionally to fulfill my desire for artichoke hummus. Other places make this, but none are as full of chunky goodness as their variety. Some of their soups are tasty, and almost everything else on the menu is typical Mediterranean fare - not bad, not great, and capable of hitting the spot if you're in the right mood. The falafel is baked, not fried - being moderately health conscious, I thought I would enjoy this change in preparation. I didn't. Falafel just needs to crunch, man! If you're going to try the Nile Cafe, order out. It is so rarely busy - you can be in and out in less than 15 minutes, unless you neglect to fill up your meter's belly and your car gets towed.

At one point while at Bacchanal, sometime after eating a plate overflowing with at least a pound of crab legs and before taking on a final slice of cheesecake (one of my fave dishes of all time), my friend Karen turned to me and said, "You have a lot of treats in your life." That's true. I do. And I am very, very grateful for them. One such treat came into my life a little over two years ago. It was the result of a chance meeting between a guy named Bill Linder and a woman named Alex Blankenstein. I met Bill when I was working at the IndyStar. He was a regular guest on my radio show and a longtime friend of the newspaper. He was also a very well-known and well-respected businessman. Alex was a 23-year-old former Notre Dame cheerleader who had recently moved to Indianapolis to take a job with a nonprofit organization. Bill's daughter, Julia, was one of Alex's good friends in college. Bill and Alex had met a few times before, but it was never a friendship that I thought would blossom. I always assumed that Alex was a little too young for Bill. But then again, I didn't really know Bill. A few months before his death, Bill called me and said he wanted to introduce me to someone. When I asked who, he said, "My girlfriend, Alex." I was totally shocked. Not because he was dating someone half his age. He had been single for a while and I was just so happy he had found someone. It was just that I didn't know how deep their relationship had become. Bill and Alex were the perfect couple. She was outgoing, vivacious and one of the most positive people I had ever met. Bill was quiet and reserved and easily intimidated by younger people. They were absolutely crazy about each other, and it was evident in everything they said and did. Sadly, Bill died in December of 2007. The outpouring of love and support for Bill and Alex at his funeral was incredible. And while I knew Bill was loved, I had no idea that he loved so many people. It was obvious how much he meant to Alex. She was a mess. And she had the support of her Notre Dame friends and family. I felt helpless, watching this young woman so full of life deal with such a devastating loss. But I was wrong. Alex is incredibly strong. She has matured so much in the last year and a half, and she's developed a grace that is totally beyond her years. She has also become a true friend. She is smart, kind and thoughtful. And she is always there for me. We talk or text almost every day, and I am so grateful for her friendship. I hope she knows that I will be there for her, always. I know that Bill is watching over her, and I'm sure he's proud of her. I know I am. I have been blessed with so many incredible people in my life. And they are all treats.

Not to even mention the stellar and unique cocktails that are offered here - from unique twists on classic drinks like Alexander's Revenge (a twist of apple pie liqueur with brandy) or the Dirty South Mule (vodka with peach-infused simple syrup in a copper mug), there is something for everyone! Forgot to review this place before. Been here multiple times (including just now to see Skyfall) with the never ending 5 Groupon. Basically you get a soda or iced tea a ticket for 5. Also, like other reviews have noted, the office chairs suck, and the LED service lights can be annoying. tl;dr Buy a few Groupons, sit in the love seats.

This is a fine steakhouse with great service which is well worth the short drive off the strip to come to. They did a great job with such a large group of rowdy guys.
I grab a slice here whenever I'm up for a basic east-coast style pizza. It's a small place it's good for take out or for a quick dinner.

I'm not a huge ice cream fan. However, mix it up with some booze, and you're talking a totally different game! I was first introduced to Lee and her liquor-ific confections at the Phoenix New Time Gala Event (or whatever it was called) a few months back. It was a huge hit, and the ladies I was with couldn't get enough! Fast forward to this weekend, and one of those ladies (who looks very much like my mother) came back to down with three friends in tow. They asked about Lee's and I found that she had just opened her shop. Were I not a devout skeptic, I'd claim divine intervention! Through the course of the weekend, we took two different trips, for the gals couldn't get enough! And truth be told, I was mighty impressed myself. As other reviewers have said this is ice CREAM. Very creamy. The booze isn't overpowering, either. It's a nice addition, so you don't have to worry about an open flame. And yes, Lee even serves up non-alcoholic flavors for those who don't partake. I assume those are good. Not like I tried any. We'll be back. Lots. It's hot out there! Adult ice cream, FTW!

Just got back from Vegas in which we stayed the last night at Aria, so thought we would hit their breakfast buffet, thinking it would be on par with Belligo and Wynn. Boy, were we wrong. OK, know it's only their second day in operation, but how can you screw up bacon and eggs? My wife and I were shown our table, and immediately went to get our food. The food area was quite long, but not a great selection. Usually I walk and look at the food and figure out the few things that look best so I can fit them onto my plate, but here, it was a struggle to find enough things appealing enough to eat. Their eggs benedict looked very weird; the eggs were freakishly white. Hard to find just regular breakfast fare. There were two omelet stations with many people waiting at each (you know a buffet is bad when people opt for the'ol standby omelet) I got in line behind Mr. Picky who had to have a special egg white only omelet with veeeery light Cheddar cheese and was also behind some punk kid who was eating off his plate in line. Idiot. The chef manning the station seemed overwhelmed by the special order so I moved on. A huge slice of ham (not bad), some Chinese egg concoction and a slice of pizza later I went back to eat. Started eating and no server yet. Half way through and still no server. Finally when I was almost done, a server asked if I wanted anything to drink. I barely chocked out, orange juice. Finally, when I was on my second to last bite, my drink came, all six ounces of it. I asked for two more. For 15 bucks, this should have been much better. I have gotten just a good breakfast at Terribles for half the price. Also, since this place should be one of the elite, what I found totally tacky was at each of the foods, instead of having a nice plaque with what the food is, it was written on the sneeze windows with grease pencil. Totally lame. Not sure if we would go back to eat here even if comped. Perhaps their lunch and dinners are better.

Soooo ono! Its like chipotle had a hawaiian baby, but better! Great food service:) Every time I've gone in, I have never been disappointed. Very convenient location to go on my lunch break I love the seaweed rice coconut bark! Must try this place out.

I loved your Hummus... I loved your Pita Bread I somewhat liked my Spinach Casserole But your service needs a lot of help. 1. My Greyhound was served in a glass with dirt. 2. There were 4 of us at a table. 2 of my companions got their shish kebab 10 minutes before my friend and I got our meals. 3. Our server actually said Is there anything else you need before I go on my break? 9pm on a Saturday night no less, you get breaks? I guess there was also supposed to be a tarot card reader that they advertise, but she hasn't shown up in three-four weeks. Think she is still coming? At least I was with awesome and intelligent people that made my time there a lot of fun...so I wasn't bitter last night. (even if I was seated hunched over. The seating is not good for the back.) Wished I was in the room with the belly dancing (she could have least came into the other room where most people were dining). My friend was a little upset over that.

Wonderful Thai food - best I've had in Pittsburgh! Watch out the food is HOT and the portions are big. Some friends ordered two fried apps - the calamari and the wonton. They were OK, I don't like fried food though, so you should probably take that with a grain of salt. My entree, the Panang curry, tasted wonderful, but was too hot for me (it was set at a 3, don't let that deter you though my taste buds are weak!) so they replaced it with the Massan curry, which was also awesome. I also tried a little Pad Thai and then a meat and vegetable dish that I can't remember the name of - both were great! The only downside was the lack of ambiance, but if you get a table up the stairs in the back of the restaurant it's OK. I'll be going back!

Bella Serra is an Italian gem in downtown. They have some of the best, most delicious wine options - including organic. What really impressed me was their effort at sustainability: they are 100 juice-based and offer a zero-waste program that makes use of all recyclable waste from your glass (as well as compostable containers for bottles). If you want to get decent takeout sushi these guys were recommended by our neighbors who live across the street in South Park. The Smoky Mountain Cafe near Asheville also has one of my favorite burgers. Plus it's got great coffee!

I recently moved down the street from Havana and I had heard great things. I've dined here a few times now and the food is amazing! My favorites are the Havana, the food is amazing! The service is the best and the staff are amazing! I had heard great things about Havana and I love it more than ever!

The food was outstanding, the service was good, the price was high. I was in no way disappointed by the quality, presentation or ANYTHING about India Oven, but the price for entrees here is shocking, particularly when rice or breads are not included in it. The decor is nice generic white tablecloth, the building unremarkable and the location not upscale, so these can't be the cost basis. Maybe the buffet is cheaper, but I ordered from the menu so I could get the amazing onion bagee and a standard, but non-buffet entree, which was 17. FYI, the little strip mall it's in is a pitwithout having reached graffiti and boarded-up window statusbut the food was stunning! If you likeeat Indian food as much as I do, you'll want to visit India Oven. If it weren't for the entree prices, I'd have given it 5 stars.

Meh. I was really excited to try this place out. I saw that they had ballpark pretzels so I was psyched! When we arrived there were no parking spots, so we had to go across the street to Safeway and walk over. Not that big of a deal. We were seated right away. I liked that they had big booths and the picnic tables were fun. Our waitress couldn't have cared less that we were there. We even told her it was our first time there and she didn't even welcome us or tell us anything about the place. We ordered the ballpark pretzel to start. I wasn't impressed with it at all. He said the sandwich was just ok, not terrible but not memorable either. The onion rings were a joke. They had zero taste and honestly tasted like the onion rings that you buy in the freezer section of the grocery store. We each ate one and then he took the rings off his plate and set them off to the side. No one wanted to eat them. I actually asked the waitress if the onion rings were made FRESH, she said yes, I said really because they taste like they came out of the freezer, she said, welllll ummmmm ya I think they are frozen. NOT cool to lie to customers. My mother in law got the fish and chips. The fish was actually pretty decent, I stole a bite. However, once again frozen run of the mil french fries and the coleslaw was not edible. When the bill came I noticed they charged us 1 for the horrible onion rings. I told my husband and when the waitress came back he asked her why. As I had said previously, we had told her it was our first time, when she asked him what side he wanted he said he didn't know what they were so she listed them off for him and did not tell us that the onion rings were a premium side dish and were extra. Seriously it is only a 1 and we wouldn't have even made a deal out of it if they would have actually been edible. So we asked her if she could take the 1 off as they were terrible and we didnt eat them and we weren't even told they were extra. She sends the manager over, seriously. To take a 1 off. He told us he could take the 1 off or give us a free dessert. We went with the 1 off as we were all ready to get out of this place. He didnt even ask why. So there you have it. Its a cool looking place, looks like they have a nice patio. The food is underwhelming. For 3 dinners, 2 beers and an app our bill was about 64. Would I go back here on my own? No. Would I go back here if some one asked me to join them? No.

I don't eat at Mcdonalds after finding out the food is filled with GMO genetically modified organisms. Look up how dangerous this is. It's in most all food that is processed. Genetically modified organisms (GMOs) are organisms that have had their genetic material altered in ways that do not occur naturally, often with the aim of introducing a new trait or modifying an existing one. GMOs have been used to produce food since the 1990s, but their safety and potential health effects have been hotly debated ever since. There is still much research to be done on the potential long-term effects of consuming GMOs, but some studies suggest that they may cause health problems such as allergies, inflammation, and changes in gut bacteria. They may also lead to antibiotic resistance and decrease biodiversity. Additionally, some people are concerned about the potential for GMOs to increase the use of pesticides and herbicides. It is important to note that there is no scientific consensus on the safety of GMOs.

When I want to go out but not spend 100 on entertainment and also get some exercise in at the same time and see some beautiful Arizona landscape, the Desert Botanical Gardens is the best place I can go. I enjoy walking around the Garden looking at all of the flowers in bloom and all of the different kinds of cactus. I also enjoy when they have different exhibits that you can see as you are wandering the garden. I really enjoyed the Chihuly Glass artwork that was displayed a few years back. Probably my favorite time of the year to come here is when they have the butterflies. They are so pretty and this year there were so many of them! We went this last weekend on my day off and the weather was perfect and we just had a great time. I also get to brush up on my photography skills here the best because I can take some amazing pictures of flowers and butterflies. If you want to see what the Arizona desert is all about, you need to come here to experience it first hand. Its not only about dirt and cacti. There are flowers galore as well.

After moving from NYC, I was in search of a good dancing club. Don't get me wrong, I love Charlotte, but there aren't a lot of going out places besides Epicenter, which is the go to place for when you have out of towners with you and you want to show them a good time. The Oak Room, located in upcoming South End is trendy and posh. Everyone is dressed to impressed, the music is upbeat, and you can barely hear yourself think. The Oak Room consists of two rooms, and it's connected to the All American Pub. However, these two venues are COMPLETELY different. The Oak Room is filled with mid 20s-40s looking to dance the night away. The place gets packed after midnight, so be sure to get there beforehand, or you'll be waiting behind the velvet rope. There is a dress code, which alot of people complain about...but guys if you don't like it, head next door! The dress code is strictly enforced, so don't be surprised if you're not allowed in. The Oak Room is for those that want to dress up, have a girl's night, sexy date night, and want to dance. The DJ is awesome and the music makes you want to move!

For a place open just a matter of weeks The Spot seems to be off to a great start. We arrived to a full house on Saturday evening and settled at the bar for a few drinks and a look at the menu. We were quickly seated and I'll tell you right now this is the best restaurant in Manila, no doubt about it. The food is incredible, the service is spot on and the ambience is perfect. I would rank it up there with the best restaurants I've been to in Australia, Singapore and the US. I was a bit worried when I read the menu and found that the entrees were priced at P750 each. I thought we were going to be broke before the main course arrived. The good news is that the portions are huge, especially the Mushroom, Parmesan and Truffle Fries which we ordered to share. I had the Steak Tartare which was sublime, plenty of capers, a perfect amount of anchovies and a great fresh tasting salad to accompany it. We both had the Duck Breast and Fois Gras for our main courses and again the portions were more than enough. The duck was beautifully cooked and the sauce that accompanied it was light and very tasty. The Fois Gras was beautifully prepared and served on top of a potato puree that was delightfully flavoured and just the right consistency. We were both quite full at this stage but still managed to share a serve of the Chocolate Cake for dessert. The cake was very rich and the ice-cream was the perfect accompaniment. This was a great end to the meal. I understand that the prices will be dropping a little in a few weeks which will be good news for the locals who will want to dine here more often than I can afford. We'll be back for sure. For more info on The Spot you can check out the website here.

Ingredients 14 cup plus 2 tablespoons unsalted butter (divided) 12 cup all-purpose flour 3 large eggs 4 tablespoons granulated sugar 1 tablespoon ground cinnamon 5 large fresh or frozen coconut halves, cut into 16 wedges 8 oz canned sweetened condensed milk (15 fl oz total; use less if you prefer your pie thinner) 3 Tbsp light corn syrup 10 coarsely chopped pecans 13 tsp salt 14 teaspoon nutmeg 14 cup finely grated lime rind Directions Preheat oven to 350F. For crusts, combine butter, flour, and remaining 1 tbsp ground cinnamon in small bowl until well combined; set aside. Beat egg whites with electric mixer on medium-high speed until foamy. Gradually add sugar and beat until creamy. Add flour mixture and beat at low speed just until blended. Place half of dough in bottom of 9-inch springform pan lined with parchment paper. Arrange coconut wedges over top. Fold sides up to meet center, pressing edges together firmly. Repeat process with second layer of dough, filling and topping with coconut. Bake for 20 minutes. Remove from oven and cool completely before covering and chilling. Combine condensed milk and corn syrup in small saucepan; bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce heat to low; stir in nutmeg, ginger, and lime zest until smooth. Cook over very low heat, stirring occasionally, until thickened, about 30 minutes. Pour filling over chilled crusts. Sprinkle tops with pecans and bake 15-25 minutes more, until golden brown. Let stand for 15 minutes before serving. Yield: 6 servings. Summer time is supposed to be healthy time, so I am trying to watch what I eat. Now, I will always be a big guy (not two fat twins on their matching motorcycles big, but you know, not little) but I definitely am eating more appropriately. However, I work in an office, and around 11:30, people start to double-think their lunch choices. Yes, the night before, a breakfast bowl from Jimmy Dean sounds like an excellent lunch selection, but all that pushing of buttons and watching your meal spin in the microwave? Forget it; one What are you doing for lunch from a buddy and I was out of there. Athenian was a prime lunch spot for me for awhile, and just fell out of favor. No time like the present to return, plus SB had never been there before today. We took the 2 minute drive to Central and rolled in to a 13 filled Athenian Express. Happy to have missed the rush, I immediately ordered my favorite dish, the gyro feta (no tomatoesonions, add lettuce) with fries, and SB got a chicken sub and potato salad. First issue, no fountain soda? If I can't destroy myself with aspartame in my free refills, it's not a great lunch. Plus, I don't like drinking out of cans unless its a more adult beverage. Fix yo machine, Athenian! Outside of the 1.50 soda, the meal was as good as always. It was a bit lighter on the feta than usual (and LOVE me some feta goodness), but still had quite a pile. The meat was thick and cooked through, definitely filled up the pita to an overflowing Greek party. The french fries weren't overcooked, which is good because burned fries suck fully. Add in a side of tzatziki sauce to poor over everything, and times were well spent. It's a ton of food for what you pay, and one of the best deals downtown. My coworker didn't fair quite as well, but it was more his preferences than issues with the meal. His chicken sub came with a huge breast, which I would think is a good thing, but for him caused the sandwich to be overstuffed (like I said, weird preferences). He demolished the entire thing, so it must have not been too bad, along with the potato salad, which he was a fan of as well. All in all, very good lunch experience. I usually get take-out, but the Greek team had their World Cup game, so it seemed appropriate to hang out and watch the exciting 0-0 match-up. If we can get some fountain sodas up in there, Athenian will likely jump back on my radar (and I may even get a salad.....maybe).

Malmaison (bad house) is about right, but MerdeMaison is much more fitting. I was really looking forward to spending NYE in Edinburgh and thought this hotel would round out a fun holiday. How wrong I was. At first glance, the place looks impressive with quirky, fun decor. But it's all about the details, isn't it? While the room was well furnished and large, the phone didn't work at all through the entire stay (and nobody came to fix it after maintenance made an appearance on day 1). So every time we needed anything, we had to go down to the front desk (see detail on staff attitude later in this review). In addition, the beds were like wooden planks. And the breakfast was AWFUL. Food two of the days was only partially cooked and inedible. I'd upgraded our initial rate to include a full breakfast as part of a NYE package the upgrade cost about 100 US for two guests for three days. But when we got to the cafe we were told our package only included the continental choice and we'd have to pay extra for additional items. Seriously.... that is expensive bread and pastry (which I don't even eat). So the desk manager (I assume that was his title), after a discussion, told me he was only upgrading our breakfast package to include meat to keep me happy (delivered in a very snide tone and smirk complete with eye roll). Which brings us to the hotel staff. Most importantly to me, about 50 percent of staff was extremely rude beyond the norm of European travel. I can tolerate a little bit of sassy attitude, but this was shockingly insulting. Lastly, I'd paid in full two months in advance of the stay only to be presented a bill for 10 percent more at checkout. The girl at the desk could not explain it, only point to line items and shrug. I'm still not sure why I was charged the additional fee (probably a malicious mark-up for the inedible breakfast).... I'll probably never know. I should have followed my instincts initially and booked the Balmoral. Much more spendy, but worth every single penny. I will NEVER again stay at a MerdeMaison property. But as I don't think the Malmaison brand can possibly last with this type of service, hopefully nobody will have to.

Another Mexican place that makes Americanized Mexican food that reliance a on lots of cheese and salsa. Nearly everything looks and tastes the same. If you want American Mexican, flowing chips and salsa and sweet margaritas, there is always a crowd.

Ive returned to get my own suit taken in. OMG, excellent. My suite looks made for me . The room is a nice size and very clean with everything you need. The bed was comfortable as well! The location couldn't be better, near the train station but also walking distance from downtown. Also within easy reach of all restaurants and shops in this area! My stay at Hotel Continental Paris Gare Du Nord has been one of absolute luxury experience. It's located seconds away from the famous Notre Dame cathedral which I visited twice during that week alone (not counting countless other times throughout my life). At first glance, it might seem intimidating because there are few signs if you don't know where to look. But once we found our way around it really didn't take long before feeling right at home.

Didn't understand I wanted the lunch special and not the lunch plate. Mostly vegetables in the Kungpow chicken. Place is run down. Large portions. Simply Amazing!!!! So clean and the food is delicious. I live on the other side of town and I will drive to eat here. My family is very picky and they loved it. The staff is always so friendly and the food is always good. Best Asian food in town!! The food is always fresh and hot! The price is right! The staff is friendly and the service is quick. China 1 is my favorite restaurant! I love all of the variety they offer on their menu. The service is always outstanding and the staff is always friendly and very helpful. They always have my food ready in a timely manner. We're going to miss them. They were so friendly and nice. Friendly service, fresh and tasty food, and great prices! What more could you ask for? Love this place. Food is awesome and the staff is so nice. Love this place! They have great food! They are the best in town! Food is always fresh and hot! And the service is always excellent! This place is amazing! The food is always hot and fresh. The service is always great! I love this place! The food is always hot and fresh. The service is always amazing!

This review is for breakfast only. Unbelievably bad breakfast. Wobbly table, bad service, had to ask for salt, pepper, napkin and silverware. Cream for coffee was old and curdled, sausage waffle was constantly running out of batter so you could not flip the waffle without it falling apart. Don't waste your money on this one!

Food is good, still their service lacks, took an hour to get food, no apology, no explanation and there was maybe 4 other tables of people. I was excited to hear about a new Mexican restaurant in town. My expectations were high. It was a good experience. The food was delicious. But they still need to work on their service. The service and the food was good. I enjoyed the food. I had a lot of food left over. It was plenty of food. The waitress was very helpful and friendly. My husband and I enjoyed our meal at this restaurant. The service was excellent and they were fast with getting our order in. We will definitely be going back. I've been going to El Buen Amigo for over 30 years. The food is always fresh and delicious. The price is very reasonable. The service is excellent. I've been there with a group of 14 and the service has always been excellent. Delicious! Very clean and the food is always good and very good portions! A little cramped but good food and good service. Food was awesome! Service was a little slow. Would definitely go back! I really enjoyed the food, but the waitress was a little rough. She was in the middle of a phone conversation with a friend while serving our table. The food was good but service was poor. Great food, fast service, a little loud. The food was good. However, I would not recommend the Mexican Salad, it was very small and not worth the price. Great food! And the staff was so friendly. Would definitely go back! The best Mexican food in town! I'm in love with this place. We usually eat here on special occasions because of the price, but it's so good we can't help ourselves! The food is always great and the atmosphere is so fun! We went on a Sunday evening and the restaurant was busy. The waitress was a bit rude when we asked for more chips and salsa. The food was good. We love this place. We always get the same thing and it's always good. The service is always great. I highly recommend it.

Almost great service! Burgers are perfectly done and cooked your way. Kobe beefawesomeness! Bartenders always great in helping you pair it up with the right beer. Always crowded...so get in early or sit at the bar. You can thank the hostess for not making this a 5 star.....this is a restaurant not a club.:)

I hate writing bad reviews but this seriously warrants it. Maybe other Lowes are better but this particular store just fails. Management hides behind their employees and don't own up to the fact that they're terrible customers, which is why they have a lot of problems. Lowe's doesn't do anything wrong. They aren't selling beer because they sell stuff you can buy at Ryerson? That makes no sense too

I love Paradise Bakery and have always had a great experience at this location, but not today. The employee that helped us was clueless (later found out it was her first day...and believe me, it showed)...it took her entirely too long to locate the sandwiches on her order form that we were trying to order. She served me chicken noodle soup that was broth only...sorry, we paid 10 for 2 soups and would like more than broth. I discussed the situation with the employee that delivered our new soup and he only gave me the excuse of her being new fail! Make sure your employees are fully trained and representative of your brand even on your first day...it will go a long way!

I have had too many negative experiences with the staff in this store. Today I tried going back after a year, and again the staff is so unhelpful, unknowledgeable and downright rude. I called to talk with the Manager, and her attitude is just as bad. Which I guess explains the attitudes of the staff. There are plenty of other places to shop that actually appreciate and help customers.

This rental community does not offer its residences a recycling drop facility! If you're looking for an eco-friendly housing option, I recommend considering this property. 22 new homes are currently available in the area and they all feature very good energy ratings (average of 60). My family has been attending or performing in shows at the Tuscany Theatre in conjunction with AYT since January 2014. We have been cast in two, helped backstage with one show and even appeared on set for a photo shoot! Currently we are planning our third show which will be coming up soon. We love being part of this amazing community and participating in AYT's events. The performances that take place here give us an opportunity to see what other local performers do and offers many fun opportunities like visiting festivals out in town! Thank you so much Tony and Barb! It is always my pleasure when I am asked to share my story about raising children who have Down syndrome. After all none of it would have happened without your help and support during those years as well as sharing ideas from experiences shared by others around me during these same years. Thank you again!! I can't imagine having the journey ahead of your daughter while she was growing up without being given such wonderful information through the down syndrome awareness month blog. I'm glad you were able to attend some of her sessions because they really meant something to you both - perhaps more than anything else? Your experience gave you great insight into how things could work better but also provided a lot of inspiration along the way...

Currently the best buffet in LV. I love how they give you the option of hot or cold crab legs (if hot-they are prepared for you right then and there). There is a wide selection of food ranging from ramen (the broth was actually quite good) to wagyu sliders (overcooked). I do appreciate that everything is portioned out for you so that food doesn't go to waste. Try coming at off hours to avoid waiting for hours. The first time I came to Bacchanal the wait time was 3-4 hours. Hell no. I came back the next day and only waited around 40 minutes.

Great store with a lot of cool clothes! It is true with all the other reviews...the regular price clothing can be a lil steep but you have to check out the clearance racks and even their sale section. Was this review helpful to you?

I can't believe I didn't check the reviews before coming here. This place was disgusting. The price person was ridiculous for such cruddy quality food. Where do I start off? I started with soup, as soon as I saw it from a far being swirled around by the chef standing by, I felt a little skeptical about getting it. You could automatically tell that shit was all starch, because it was soooooo thick. It was soooo bland, blegh. Crab legs? That stuff tasted so old, it was frozen cold too. And there's barely any meat. My boyfriend took advantage of their meat selection. He mentioned the meat was tough and bland. We are a big fan of truffle recipes. And they had macaroni and cheese made with some truffle oil. It was gross, it was all butter and a tiny dash of truffle oil to make it smell like it. The only thing good about this place, in terms of food, was their unlimited crepes. I was able to get a dinner crepe and a dessert crepe after. Both were OKAY. The staff that were working and taking our plates were very sweet. They refilled our drinks as soon as they were empty and they took our plates fast. I was able to converse with one of the chefs making my crepe, she was cool too. But, I thought this place wasn't good. I wouldn't recommend it to anyone. Even one of our taxi drivers said that this place is one of the worst buffets here because we told him how we ate there.

Me 5 other friends were in Las Vegas for a trip in the month of august. After a long day trip to Grand Canyon we were hungry and searched online and decided on Satay for dinner (saw the stars in yelp and decided). The atmosphere was fine and nicely decorated and we requested the waiter for an outdoor seating. They have a quite big menu and we order Roti Canai and Vegetable curry Samosa. Both platters seem to be Indian dishes and they taste excellent. We are tempted and ordered one more order of Roti Canai. Nasi Lamak with curry chicken served with coconut rice. The chicken was delicious and in addition we have half boiled egg and cucumbers. Nasi Goreng - fried rice served with shrimp, squid and half cooked omelet.....it was yummy and shrimp is flavorful. Singapore fried noodles - it's a vegi noodles with no egg was perfectly cooked and tastes excellent. Green Curry - cooked with peppers, coconut milk and egg plant...just tasted and it was fine. i checked the online menu and each dish was self explanatory with most of the images. All the dishes were not so spicy and we asked for extra chili sauce!!! I am not sure about the local crowd, but we were lucky to be there for dinner without knowing much about it. Totally I was impressed with the food and service.

Ah wish this wasn't the case. It is a nice little spot and decently priced for a known chef stop in Vegas. I love him maybe that made my expectations too high. The food was good but nothing special for the price. The coconut rice was tasty. Sorry I didn't like the shrimp. The flavor and texture was too crunchy for my liking. I did like the spicy chili. I think the spice took over the flavor of the shrimp for me. But the shrimp and the chili were my least favorite dishes. The beef was very tender and flavorful. The veggies were a very nice mix of colors, textures and flavors. The "Jamaican Me Hungry" cocktail is a good mix of flavors. It is not too sweet and nice and strong. I like it. But what I really loved was the 2013 Charles Heidsieck champagne. It is very light and fruity and has the right amount of sugar to go with the cocktail. It was a good lunch with friends. I would not go back again. I'm sorry you were disappointed. That's a real bummer. This has been on my to do list forever.

After looking at several reviews about this place I decided to try them out. So I called one day and asked if I could make an appointment for the next day for a specific time. We agreed on a time, and since it was my first time here I told the girl who was booking the appointment it didn't matter who cut my hair but that it is important my hair gets cut at the appointment time that was set because of my extremely busy schedule. She told me it would be no problem and I was set to go. I show up the next day excited to get my haircut. I get there four to five minutes before my appointment and let the receptionist know and I take a seat. She asked me if I wanted a drink and that it would only be a few minutes. I notice there were two hair stylist's working and both were in the middle of cutting another clients hair. About fifteen minutes pass and one of the stylist's finish with their clients haircut. The next thing I know she starts quickly cleaning up and starts packing her things. She completely ignores me and walks out of the salon when she knew I had been waiting now at this point twenty minutes past my original appointment time! I get no status from the receptionist. I continue to stay calm and think ok my time is running out before my next business appointment but I still have some time so I wait for the next hair stylist. At this point it is now thirty five minutes past my appointment time! Finally a few minutes later the only hair stylist left is finishing her clients haircut. I think to myself just in time. THINK AGAIN! The next thing I know someone sitting in the back quickly gets into her chair, and the only stylist left starts cutting this persons hair. I get no acknowledgement from the hair stylist or the receptionist!!! I felt like I was invisible. This was one of the worst experiences of customer service and professionalism ever!!! At this point I was furious. No haircut, a waste of forty five minutes, and a clear view of how this place conducts business. I guess the first girl didn't want to make some extra money? Because I was ready to give a big tip. I was looking for a new person to cut my hair since my old stylist is no longer in the area. If you believe in being punctual, professional, and good customer service this IS NOT the place to go! If you want a drink, and to play a game of pool and maybe get your haircut within a two hour time frame then you found your place. But I can go to a bar for that, minus the two hour waste of time hoping for a haircut. I would never recommend this place to anyone and let everyone know how horrible this place was. I am not the type to complain like this, but this is noway to run a business if your trying to win new clients and possible referrals from that client.

Had great service and food. The calamari app was one of the best I've had. It is worth a visit. My favorite place in town if you like seafood and has big canapes, right on Ocean Drive off Archer Street

This is an interesting museum. It definitely has a great variety of musical instruments from many countries, and mostly of older eras, with musical content you hear by way of headphones. It's extremely educational, and will take most of a day to fully tour. The downside I experienced was that a large group of school children came for a tour - which is great - but they were extremely noisy and one couldn't hear the music content on the headphones. The museum was unusable for the 1.5-2 hours the children were present. My advice is if you are planning to visit this museum, call ahead and see if there will be any groups like this when you may visit. Plan your visit around them and you won't have a major distraction.

Good burger, Good Atmosphere. I had the Western burger, which was pretty good. It was made with buffalo meat. Yum. So it was pretty juicy. It was lacking the BBQ sauce it hoped to promise though. Overall I'd order it again, just ask for more sauce. My BF got the Sam I am, which has a fried egg on it, and normally comes with ham on top, out server suggested replacing it with bacon, and so that's what he did. The egg explodes in your mouth when you bite into this burger. It's gooood. And the pesto on it is simply delicious. The part that disappointed me thought, was that our sides...sweet potatoes fries, and tater tots were overwhelmingly salty. It may have been an accident, but I couldn't eat more than five, and I was done with them. Overall, I'd go back.

First timers in our group and at least 2 or the 3 of us will not be back. We (two of us) arrived to the table our friend had already He had a party going on who was walking into the restaurant. We were so frustrated that we didn't have a table and had room. The waitress was very nice and made our drinks and arrived promptly.

What is with the super high reviews for this place?! The food was SO mediocre and I felt disgusting afterwards. Two stars for the large portions and pretty fast service, but it's not worth the calories. Go to PF Changs instead! Easy parking. Great place to take kids. Good food! Kids loved the fortune cookies! We were there for an evening meal and had a party of 14. The restaurant was very busy but we were seated quickly. They were very accommodating for my gluten-free daughter. The server was very attentive. The food was very good! I will definitely go back. The food was amazing and the service was great! We will definitely be back! The place is so clean and the staff is very helpful and nice. Food is always delicious. We had a party of 12 in a private room. The food was excellent. The room was perfect. The service was outstanding. The manager checked on us several times. The food was served hot and the portions were generous. We will return and would recommend to friends. The food was good but not the best Chinese food I've ever had. Not sure I would go out of my way to go there again.

Been here dozens of times, mainly for their pizza. PIzza: Cheese was on the mild side with some bite, sauce slightly sweet, doughcrust nicely balanced flavor and texture. NY style, got that chewiness and droopiness, made to fold, then consume. Pepperoni, Mushroom, Sausage... Toppings are typical and plentiful any size. One of the better pizzas I've had here in Vegas. Spaghetti: I've ordered it with marinara and sausage meat sauce and meatballs. Both combinations were Delicious and had that Comforting good ol' spaghetti flavor. Came with bread (garlic would be nice). One order could feed 2. Delivery was always on time and prices fair. One of my'go to' pizza joints

Super unique and informative. Educational and not trashy! I love statistics and random facts...this place has a bunch. The artwork collection is diverse and unique. I went with a girl friend and we had a good time. It wasn't weird; we had some good laughs and ah-ha! moments. I would suggest this for a random date night with the girls or your significant other.

Wish I could give them ZERO stars. Cheap flight, sure. I booked through Expedia and paid 650 for round trip dallas to vegas including 3 nights at New York Hotel for 2 people. HOWEVER when I went to check in I had to pay an additional 258 for each of us to have 1 carry on and a crap ton of additional fees. WTH! They suck you in and then sucker punch you. You want a soda, charge. You want coffee, charge. I'm surprised they don't have a pay toilet on board. Save money, fly Southwest. You can even fly American cheaper than these rip off artists. Oh and I would be remiss if I didn't mention. NO LEGROOM on the plane. If you want to pay an additional 25 you can get an exit row.

Good thing this place has a lot of good reviews or I would never go back. Since I worked in the Biz and I am a forgiving person when I enjoy myself, we decided to stay for dinner one night after another really great meal at the restaurant's "Blue Ribbon" Lounge. Our first visit was about 2 years ago (I had my older sister with me) before they added live piano music on Friday nights that were very entertaining. We also ate here during our honeymoon which is always special. We came again last year about 6 weeks later so it was nice to see all of the staff still there but then realized that most everyone appeared happy since the place started receiving very positive reviews around town! This time we only had lunch. The food is excellent as usual and service at their counter area is pretty fast. In fact that day was no exception...we even got our check 30 minutes from ordering..not bad at all considering the popularity of the place. Unlike some places where you get your check right away without any wait, they don't rush us at ALL..even though we blew through like 4 plates of delicious seafood pasta that evening!! The atmosphere is fun whether dining inside or outside....a little noisy if crowded out front during peak hours because of traffictraffic lights etc but otherwise not intrusive. There are tables available near the entrance under umbrellas until 7:00 pm while waiting for your table indoors but definitely bring an umbrella due to heat once dark falls. Bring a flashlight too so you can actually find your way down the aisles when its pitch black.....the lighting isn't bright enough. The people who work at White Water Grill seem genuinely friendly regardless if you're just having breakfast or coming across them getting a drink...they make up for what seems to be quite possibly long drive times from other areas. Plus, despite being more than 10 mins past midnight parking lots do have spaces sometimes and the valet will move your car so you aren't stuck leaving late (which happened to my friend last time). Parking may come at a price depending on how far away the hotel you ultimately decide upon staying is but its worth it for sure compared to taking public transportation. A tip - next time plan ahead as to where you want to be parked as many floors become unavailable after 11pm. If you get lucky, you'll end up by the elevator door on ground floor instead of above it but usually they assign those spots to higher bldgs as well. Overall, its been less expensive than going to a nicer sit-down location within walking distance AND the quality of food rivals anything nearby with prices much lower so a win win situation overall. Now 9 months later, we returned along wmy niece nephew for Valentine's Day weekend; timing our arrival around brunch service 8am. As expected, everything else remained exactly same including 3 course menu and tasty desserts. We love the lobster macaroni n cheese so we ordered that each to share and enjoyed every bite. It wasn't overly spicy either so kids could eat it as well. My brother sis loved the crab cake Benedict which we couldn't try since we already had plenty of meals earlier in the week. The trolley comes by at intervals throughout the morning for refills with coffee and water and all types of yummy drinks anyone orders whatever flavor floats their boat. Also, ask your server for tips on creative combo plate ideas that allow guests to sample several dishes at once such as the Bacon S'mores Tostadas for example or the Lemon Pepper Shrimp Scampi Fries..one large order of fries and half dozen shrimp scampi served over spinach tossed lightly cooked bacon, topped off wtwo halves of grilled sourdough bread stuffed with melted cheddar cheese and marinated lemon pepper potstickers (excellent idea given the high sodium content). Other suggestions include trying something new the second time around using different sides of interest. So why didn't we give white water grill two thumbs UP? Because although the seating indoors and outdoors looked inviting, the ambiance lacks character. Dinner parties seemed to consist mostly of families rather than groups seeking intimate conversation. Two separate events held consecutively lasted approximately 15 minmax from open table to closing....surely not ideal for a romantic setting or couples wanting to celebrate VDay together. One event featured a 40th birthday party consisting of 25 adults dancing till close plus an additional 1 hr private reception room set aside wan audio system and huge screen TV playing the movie 'Avatar'. Every single adult seemed intoxicated drinking alcohol straight from chilled pitchers placed squarely in centerpieces. Only young children seemed to be able to dance to the songs played continuously via speaker throughout event. At least 40 of patrons standing against walls mostly female looking fairly unkempt wcasual attire....no effort made to dress up except for women wearing dresses, lipstick and heels. With regard to service habits since both visits I observed that servers did appear rushed initially but after bringing out appetizers, salads and cheeses ended up doing double duty during the client to report "unbektspeal court

The salads are very good here everything seems fresh.... The prices are a bit high in my opinion and the serving size is way too big even for half a bowl. Worked out to be about 20 more than I would have spent on other restaurants, but still within our budget and we took advantage of their lunch buffet which was delicious!

Excellent! Went here for a last minute nail appointment with Mai and was very happy! Everyone there was very nice. Most the customers were regulars which says a lot about this place!! Was this review helpful to you?

A hidden gem! We never knew this place existed and stumbled into it after lunch at Chino Bandito (next door). They have all sorts of flavors of popcorn and are more than willing to let you sample them. Even some seasonal flavors. We were really excited about the Cake Batter flavor but we sampled it in the store and were a little disappointed in the lack of cake batter flavoring, too much spoiling by Cold Stone's ice cream flavor I guess. We took advantage of the bakers dozen deal on the small snack size bags so we could try lots of flavors, it was 13 bags for 11 (normally 1 each). They were even willing to make us a bag of a flavor if we didn't see it in the small size. They have many more flavors than what's on their website, some of the ones we got were Churro, Bacon Cheese, Cookies Creme, Coconut, PB Chocolate, Cherry Chocolate and Candy Bar. The store had lots of cute tinsgift ideas so next time you are trying to come up with a gift idea for someone, this might just be a great alternative option to the classic gift card.
OMG! I see tall hot Asian guy! Let's follow him! OKKKKK!!! Go talk to him. He looks like he'll dance. No. I'm scared... Out of all the guys there, we get a guy talking.

My job was suppose to provide me a company car from the Las Vegas government agency. But they ran out of their vehicles. So without making any reservations from one month in advance, I had no choice but to get another vehicle for my long journey. I finally managed to find a rented SUV on the Internet. It cost 750 plus gas and maintenance fees - costs about 1200 per day (800 cash 200 prepaid). The process is complicated: you have to fill up the fuel tank at your local filling station with 30 US gallons each time before returning it back to the agency where it will be inspected by an official who has the right to take away the vehicle if he thinks that there are problems such as scratches or dents etc. And even then... failed inspection twice! But that's my story... So we met a woman named Lisa who told us she could arrange all our taxi needs via her friend Tom (we're going to call him Tom because I'm not sure how many times I've heard this name). When our first meeting happened yesterday morning after breakfast, she gave us two options - either hire a cheap minivan truck from his firm's website or pay more expensive rates by taking care of everything herself through direct contact with various transportation companies' websites. We decided to go with option 2 since it's less risky than buying some equipment only to realize that it's far too big or small depending upon where you're going Tom took us to meet Mike, the ownerdriver, and Mark, the mechanic. We found ourselves seated next to three very nice guys having just finished working on a Toyota Camry whose engine needed replacing! After signing documents, paying additional 100 fee, getting our driver's license photos done and waiting until the vehicle repairs were done, we drove off into the desert with Tom driving.

The salads are very good here everything seems fresh.... The prices are a bit high in my opinion and the serving size is way too big even for half a portion. I like the variety of salads they have here though.

You'll likely need more than 3 minutes depending on your mixer speed. Add the eggs slowly mixing well between each addition. Sift in the flour mixture alternating with the cocoa powder. Mix thoroughly. Fold in the vanilla and then stir in salt. Chill dough before scooping 2 tablespoons portions onto ungreased cookie sheets leaving approx. 4 inches between cookies. Bake at 350 degrees F for 10 - 12 minutes, remove, allow to cool slightly, set aside and repeat process twice more. If desired melt remaining chocolate in microwave oven until smooth, drizzle over cooled cookies. Refrigerate again for 15 minutes and cut into pieces once completely chilled. Enjoy immediately or store refrigerated for several days. This recipe came courtesy of Emmaline at A Clean Plate. A Laughably Poor Existence of an Amusement Park for Adults and Children This was my first experience at a Jambo Amusement Park with no knowledge beforehand of what is actually available. As a result of my lack of knowledge I was a bit stunned by the prices. I had an expectation that this would be a fairly reasonably priced amusement park for families, however to my surprise the prices were extortionate. So much so that I thought to myself, if my children were at school I would be walking out of there in a huff. This was my first impression of Jambo and therefore my expectations were quite low, however when I got there I was surprised by how good it was. The area around the park is littered with stalls selling gifts, clothes and various different things. We did stop off for a coffee in one of the cafes which is a nice place to sit out and relax. They offer a range of different coffees and various different cakes. They also have a range of different soft drinks and a few alcoholic drinks available too. It is a well-kept, clean area with a range of different animals available to pet. There is a large open space for children to run around and play with their friends. It is a good way to spend some time whilst the children have fun. There are a few different places available to sit down with a drink and a bit of food. The prices seem to be in line with what you would expect, it is not ridiculously expensive, but it is not cheap either. I would have preferred it if the prices were a little more reasonable, but I was happy enough that I was not ripped off. The prices seemed reasonable when compared to similar places in the UK, but we have a much higher minimum wage. The amusement park itself was huge. I was a little bit overwhelmed by it all and I was not sure where to start. It was quite difficult to work out how the tickets were going to work and where we would go. There is also a range of rides that are in various different sections. I think that this is quite a good idea. I think that it means that it is easier to work out how long you want to stay in the amusement park. For example, you may want to do the rides with the bigger kids and then get the children on some of the other rides. However, the way it works is that you need to buy a ticket for each ride that you want to go on. There are a few different options available. Firstly, you can buy a ticket that will allow you to ride everything in the park. This will cost you 10,000 yen for an adult and 8,000 yen for a child. Next up, you can purchase a ticket that will allow you to ride everything in the park, but you will need to purchase a ticket for the roller coaster at 2,000 yen. If you are a thrill seeker you can purchase a ticket that will allow you to go on every roller coaster in the park. This will cost you 15,000 yen for an adult and 10,000 yen for a child. Lastly, you can purchase a ticket that will allow you to go on every ride in the park. This will cost you 12,000 yen for an adult and 9,000 yen for a child. If you are in Japan then you must try the food. There are a few different options available, but I thought that the ramen was delicious. They have a range of different options available and the prices are not extortionate. It was a pleasant surprise. For example, I had a delicious ramen that was a similar price to what you would expect to pay in the UK, but it was a lot better in quality and was a lot tastier. It is possible to purchase a ticket that will allow you to ride a ride once. This will cost you 500 yen for an adult and 300 yen for a child. I think that this is a great idea and I would be very tempted to buy one of these to do a couple of the rides. There is a playground with a few different slides and a swing. It is a good place to take a small child for a short time and give them something to do. I think that this is a good idea and I think that it will save a lot of people having to purchase a ticket for a small child that they are not going to use. Overall, I really enjoyed my time at the amusement park. I thought that it was really nice and the children really enjoyed themselves too. It was a great way to spend a day. The roll

While I acknowledge I got there at 5:05 am - 5 minutes after they were set to close, the complete lack of compassion of the people I encountered was quite surprising. Here I am, 5 months pregnant with a sick toddler still in his PJs, in an obvious rush to make it in the doors by 5 a.m. The lobby is completely empty and the front door unlocked when I arrive. I hear someone in the back say that's not someone new, is it? and another voice responded no, probably just someone leaving. Next thing I know I see the people who own the voices I heard - one looks like one of the doctors or nurses and the other like the person who runs the front desk area. All I get is sorry, we're closed. With the fact that I didn't make it in time sinking in, near tears (I blame the pregnancy hormones) I explain that I had a difficult time finding them in the strip mall where they are located and got stuck at a light. This time I get one word - sorry. I look up to see faces of stone. Nothing. Neither of the ladies offered any suggestion on where else I might be able to take my sick child to be seen by a doctor, which we were obviously in need of since we'd come to their urgent care for that very reason. I say, you guys don't open again until 9 pm, right? I get a short reply, 5 pm. I then ask if they know when Phoenix Children's urgent care opens. Absolute silence. I know this is technically a competitor, but if you care about kids, wouldn't you want to ensure a sick child gets the care he needs irrespective of whether it comes from your company or another? I was so frustrated when I left that I did start to cry a bit as I buckled my son back into his car seat and made my way home to wait the 7 hours until the next pediatric urgent care opened. On the drive home I tried to see the positive side of my encounter- maybe it was a good thing that we were too late to be seen since I wouldn't want such uncaring people to treat my son anyway.

Takahashi Teppanyaki is not a safe place for children under 4. It appears some kids didn't get the message about this restaurant's reputation because they stayed after school to stand in line. We encountered numerous adults (including parents) who were showing up on their lunch break to sit at the bar area where there are usually only 15 people. They all looked around 18ish. While others waited for a table, some ordered drinks from the soda machine which took forever to refill. I saw several women pull purses off of someone else in front of us. If possible, try to find seats near the entrance window and away from the back of the restaurant. Otherwise, enjoy your meal...it might go fast since there aren't many places open late on Fridays.

I just returned from Vegas for a holiday girls' trip, and the Spa at MOLAS was one of our stops during our vacation. My travel partner works concierge at the spa at Mandarin Oriental's DC location, so she was interested and checking out the facility even though neither of us could spare the cash to splurge on a treatment here. This review is strictly for the facilities, which I simultaneously found both incredibly impressive and disappointing. Disappointing only because the spa lacks some of my favorite standard spa amenities like a jacuzzi (they only had a warm vitality pool which was at least 10 degrees cooler than how I would run my bath) and a sauna. To me, use of the spa facilities are half the draw of visiting a spa even when I do book treatments so the lack of some of my favorite amenities was a bit of a bummer. That aside, this spa has a lot going for it. The spa areas were immaculately clean, attractively modern in their design, offered stellar views of the strip, and had a lot of cool techy features like experience showers with touch screen menus and the ability to turn on the jets for the vitality pool on a stationlounger by stationlounger basis rather than for the whole pool. Their relation room is one of the nicest and most relaxing one I've ever been in, with plenty of beds situated in front of windows overlooking the strip to rest in while waiting for your appointment or just to get some rest. Finally, I can't say enough good things about their staff. The service was top notch, friendly and extremely attentive without being obtrusive. Always there to offer you a towel, a bottle of water or to fetch eye makeup remover for when the experience showers have ruined your eyeliner and you've neglected to bring your own. Really top notch service.

Flying with any airline can be painful, as many reviews indicate. Over the last ten years of nearly weekly travel I have come to know many of the Phoenix employee's who were booked on planes before the flight and they still don't understand why they didn't contact us when we arrived at their hotel. A day after arriving, the flight attendant asked if anyone had left anything for her. She also said that most people would not mind if she made sure to bring a few drinks from home for them. Another traveler reportedly reported that he was confused by what he saw in front of him and kept making up his own excuse for just leaving money. He eventually walked off the plane feeling sick, but didn't return until he discovered that he had bought some bags of food from the local grocery store because he felt like taking his meal back home. The second round of the enforced quarantine has caused widespread suffering across all sectors of our society. Businesses are still struggling to survive even during this time of uncertainty, leading to layoffs of workers and job losses affecting hundreds of thousands of Americans. In response, Congress passed legislation last week requiring airlines to resume flights into and out of the United States and requiring customers returning home with COVID-19 vaccines to self-isolate or receive a test within 72 hours upon arrival. As you can see here, airlines have been hit particularly hard. It is believed that over 10 percent of international travelers returned home since March 12 while others using domestic routes remain stranded overseas due to lack of safety protocols. So it should not surprise me that the US Air Force Air Station in Arizona received several letters from employees of Delta Air Lines about this situation. Of course, the USPS, which operates almost 30 air carriers, doesn't make much money off of these visitors either so they may very well have no idea how bad things are. The USPS has issued statements to passengers saying that the company was "aware" of the issue with Delta's service, adding "We took action against the airlines responsible." However, no one spoke to the employees directly so I am guessing there will be a number of questions raised by the affected pilots' union. It seems that the airlines at least may have figured out - however, the fact that they did it despite having no clue about the actual reason doesn't seem right either. According to an article by The Washington Post on Monday, "Delta apparently decided to send out notices informing its employees of the worst-case scenario as soon as possible after receiving 23 false positive tests prior to the initial letter." So far, no word yet on whether the company is aware of the problem in advance of returning to normal operations.

We sit there in our Vegas hotel (my cousins and me)... It's been over an hour and a half, it's about 2 in the morning and we're not hungry anymore. We're tired, a bit sleepy, and just want to go to bed. Then all of a sudden, we hear a loud crashing noise. It sounds like something heavy has been dropped on the floor. We look out and across the hall, and see the maid's cart. It's been pushed out of her room, the door has been left open. We hear some rustling, a bit of loud talking, and then silence. So then we go back to our room, and it's quiet again. Then after a few minutes, we start hearing talking. We look over, and across the hall, we see the maid's cart. The door has been shut. We hear a few loud, male voices and then it's quiet again. Then, a few minutes later, we hear it again. The voices are getting louder, and then a few minutes later, the door opens again. The next day, we talk to my cousin's husband, and he tells us that he was working out in the gym, and he saw three guys walk by him. Two were white, and one was black. They were wearing suits, and he said that they were "clean cut" and "weird looking." He said that they seemed to be together, but they didn't seem to know each other. "I've never seen any of them before," he said. "And I've never seen them since." We think that they were the maids' pimps. Later that night, my husband and I have a mini-bar key. We're really bored, and we decide to go up to the 27th floor to see if we can sneak into a room. We try about 10 rooms, but we can't get in. The last one that we try, is the one across the hall from the maids. We are about to give up when we decide to try one last time. The door opens, but we can't get in. It won't open all the way, and the light from the hallway is too bright to see if the door is locked. Then, out of nowhere, we hear a really loud voice yell, "Get out of here!" We look across the hall, and see the maid's door open. The maid is standing there, and she is glaring at us. She says it again. "GET OUT OF HERE!" We start to leave, and she looks at us and says, "I know you!" My husband and I are freaked out, so we quickly leave. We run to the elevator, and get out of there as fast as we can. We never went back. I told you that story, because my husband and I have a lot of ghost experiences. A lot of them are personal and more on the emotional side, but this is one that happened to us, and I have never forgotten it. I believe in the paranormal. I believe that we are not alone in this world. I believe that spirits exist, that ghosts are real, and that there are other dimensions in the universe. This is one of the main reasons that I love the show Ghost Whisperer. I watch it every week, and every episode has me glued to the TV. I recently interviewed James C. Swan, who is a ghost investigator, psychic, and author of two books. He also runs Paranormal Investigation and Research Society (PIRS) out of Portland, Oregon. I asked him to talk about his experiences, and to answer some questions. (P.S. I have not done any editing on this interview, so please excuse the spelling and grammatical errors.) 1) What is the most interesting thing that you have learned about ghosts? I think the most interesting thing I have learned about ghosts is that they are very human and act like us in most ways. They have emotions, emotional attachments, desires, pettiness, cruelty, anger, and love. They are simply the human condition without a body. 2) Have you ever had a ghostly encounter? I have had many ghostly encounters, some that were very frightening, and others that were quite peaceful. My most frightening encounter was in a very old haunted house in rural Wisconsin. I was on a ghost investigation with a friend of mine. We went into this very old house that was built in the 1800'

One of the most relaxing places that's within biking distance from my house. I, am indeed, one lucky gal! While it's not huge, the farm can keep me occupied for hours and still have room to play. There are also plenty of other things to do on this land including hiking and 4-wheeler trails (which I'm currently trying to conquer). I grew up with horses so that interest has stayed with me all these years. We recently got a new little horse named Missy who is about six weeks old. She came into our lives when we found her in need of help after she was dropped off at a stable where no one had claimed her. It breaks my heart to see young animals left out like that but I truly believe God sent us her right then and there because it turned out to be just what she needed. Little did I know how much more work caring for four chickens would turn into. Since we've gotten her, Charlie and I have been working hard to get her trained and comfortable around humans - a difficult task considering she never really knew anything except being abandoned by those who should love her best. But when you find yourself surrounded by people who want her as part of their family, your love grows tenfold for them too. They took her home, where she will now live happily ever after. A couple of months ago Charlie brought over this adorable little goat kid he'd raised since it was born. He said "He needs a name." So here he is: El Capitan. A nice little name that fits his personality perfectly. The name actually means "big mountain" which seems fitting enough seeing as how I call him my baby boy. El Capitan is well loved in our household and enjoys having friends over to visit regularly for cuddles and food alike.:)

Let me begin with a quote taken straight from the Caesar's Qua Baths and Spa official website: Playing off its water motif, cooling blue tones, slate and stone set the mood for the spa, and signature mineral water is served. Not bad for a spa that boasts 15 treatment rooms, including two saunas, two steam rooms, two spa tubs and 20 baths. Caesar's Qua Baths and Spa is the newest addition to the famous Caesar's Palace hotel in Las Vegas, and they did not disappoint. Caesar's Qua Baths and Spa, which is the biggest spa in Las Vegas, has everything you would expect in a great Las Vegas spa. My husband and I are two of the biggest fans of the spa, so we were excited when we arrived in Las Vegas and got a chance to try Caesar's Qua Baths and Spa. The spa is located at the top of the hotel, and when you walk in, you are greeted by the staff who are ready to help you with whatever you need. The spa is massive, and we were overwhelmed by the options. There were two spa tubs, two saunas, two steam rooms, and 20 baths. We went to the baths first, because it was something we had never experienced before. There were different rooms for different purposes, and each room was more unique than the last. We had fun in the salt room, the fragrance room, the milk room, and the red wine room. After that, we decided to go to the steam room, which was almost like being in a sauna. We stayed in the steam room for about an hour, and it was a great experience. The steam room was full of people, and there were a few other steam rooms to choose from. After our time in the steam room, we decided to go get a couple's massage. We were both having back problems at the time, so the masseuse massaged the right places. We were so pleased with the results of the massage, we booked another one for the next day. If you are staying at the Caesar's Palace hotel, then you should definitely take advantage of the spa. You can choose from a variety of packages, and the prices are reasonable. Caesar's Qua Baths and Spa is located in the heart of the Caesar's Palace hotel. It is located on the 5th floor, and you will see signs pointing to the spa once you enter the hotel. If you are driving to the spa, you can use valet parking. The spa is open from 9:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. daily. We recommend taking the spa tour before you go to the baths and steam room. There are many rooms to choose from, and the tour is the best way to find out which one is the best. The spa is massive, so if you are interested in going to the baths, the steam room or the sauna, we recommend going early in the morning or late in the evening. If you are going to one of the spa treatments, you can go any time of the day. The Caesar's Qua Baths and Spa is located in the heart of the Caesar's Palace hotel.

For my entree, I went with the Honey Glazed Duck, described as follows: Duck confit and goat cheese puff, wilted arugula, pear, puree of carrot and orange. I ordered it at the suggested temp of medium-rare. I can honestly say it was the worst duck I've ever had at an upscale restaurant (as opposed to duck in a take-out Thai dish). It was not medium-rare. It was rare, if not blue. It lacked the crispy skin that makes duck so wonderful. And it lacked flavor. The puree was hardly edible as it was barely present on the plate. Despite all these missteps, the worst part of the plate was easily the puff. When I think puff, I think light, airy, flaky. This was heavy, dense, compact. I think there was a crumble of goat cheese in it. I will say, though, that my side of Brussels sprouts were good. Now, to be completely fair, my server was attentive and receptive to me when I told her about the problems with the dish, which I usually don't do even when I don't like something in a restaurant. The duck was taken off the bill without any fuss, which was not my goal in pointing out how undercooked it was. I also didn't give them a chance to take another shot at it, which might have changed things. Every kitchen has a bad dish now and then. This was one experience on one night, but I thought it worth sharing.
