Some older men stood nearby, engaged in conversation, smoking cigarettes. One asked me who i worked for and explained that it didn't matter because he knew everyone anyway. Others nodded in agreement and laughed lightly. They seemed friendly enough, though perhaps a little bored even by the end of day...like me. After leaving them, I continued on until I came across the pool area, hoping to find water otherwise unavailable elsewhere within the compound. On top of each low building off to the right side of the courtyard stood several wooden platforms, suspended high above ground level by metal rods attached to the buildings themselves. Peering between the small openings in the walls surrounding the pools revealed a view of mountains shrouded mostly by clouds whose tops appeared closer than what I saw from inside the lodge. Upon seeing this sight, I felt completely content. Even as I walked past, the sun shining directly upwards, I couldn't suppress the feeling of peace that overcame me. My eyes closed briefly, smiling as I recalled moments spent swimming in such conditions. Behind me, someone called out my name and I turned to look. Several younger women waved at me, giggling as they pointed at my camera equipment. A bell rang somewhere further away, letting us know that dinner would begin in less than 20 minutes. Standing alone in front of a small pool filled with clear liquid - the same color as the sky itself - I watched them splash, shouting happily among one another, sharing jokes and laughter. I envied every single person present, especially the children runningabout without carefree abandon, as well as the adults enjoying this brief respite from daily demands. Looking around for the source of my sense of joy, I wondered what path leads to finding happiness. Perhaps it lies hidden beneath the surface of things as opposed to hiding amidst dark shadows. Or maybe it resides almost everywhere, yet all too often goes unnoticed. Is it possible for anyone to attain true happiness without fighting hard battles, struggling patiently alongside thousands of unknowns, as well as enduring countless challenges both big and small? Where does one turn when desiring enlightenment? Can we ever hope to achieve lasting happiness by following the path laid open before us by Buddha himself? These questions may sound odd coming from a man who knew nothing about Buddhism prior to his arrival, but if truth be told, I felt far more comfortable asking myself such things than I did living through a life full of many trials, pain, and suffering. Does only contentment exist, or also passion? When will we fully realize that life should simply be lived...without regard for worldly gains? Are we guaranteed freedom to follow whatever path strikes our fancy? All the answers lie within us, waiting to be discovered, just as much as they already reside deep beneath the layers of soil covering our planet's surface. Maybe someday we shall finally glimpse them...and experience what the word means, literally and figuratively. I wholeheartedly agree with Mike K. - for your money, this is a great deal in Charlotte. The Dowd Y is a very nice gym that offers a bevy of group fitness classes, up to date (and always functioning) equipment and a super clean atmosphere. Why I love this Y in particular...the machines are always in service (and I've head that techs are out fixing them weekly if need be). They also do not allow any children under the age of 16 in the workout areas. Now, don't get me wrong, I love kids, just not when I'm trying to get my sweat on. As mentioned before, this Y offers so many great group classes. I'm a big fan of Total Strength, Pilates Mat and Kickboxing. I've also heard the Spin classes are great. I've tried Athletic Conditioning, and while it certainly is an awesome workout, make sure you're at least in decent shape before you partake in that class! It's a rough one. As other reviewers have noted, this gym can get packed especially after 5 pm during the weekdays. So be patient while parking. Some classes can get a bit crowded too, so keep that in mind when you're sprawling out your mat or equipment. I haven't had any issues with theft in the locker room, but I'm a big proponent of a big papa lock on my locker. For the money and the friendly service, the Dowd YMCA is a great deal for anyone looking to slim down or tone up.

Well, it's worse than I thought. One of the teas ended up being over 100 a pound! And even though I immediately returned everything, the money has not shown back up on my card yet! I emailed the company and they said it will be back in 24 hours, but I doubt it. I guess I should have read the fine print. I will go back to my wool tea. It's very good. The one I bought in the store was 15.99 and it was at the cheapest price they could get it, so I guess I shouldn't complain too much. I also bought a new juicer that's supposed to be very easy to clean. We'll see. I finally got to go to the Hathaway factory in Cambridge, Mass. It's been 35 years since I've been there. The factory is still in existence but the buildings are on the National Register of Historic Places. There was a sign saying not to take photographs. I guess I'm lucky that I found out that was the case just before I went in. I could have been arrested. I did manage to get some good close-up pictures of the looms. They have a very interesting display of looms and threading from the early days of Hathaway, as well as a stunning example of a decorative loom. I'll have some information about the factory for the next blog entry. I've been drinking tons of water lately. I have a water bottle that I can put on a rock next to my sewing machine to keep it cold. But if I don't have a cold drink available, I take a few sips from it. It's not so good to drink it straight from the tap because the water here is a bit hard. However, it does help to drink a lot of water. I am also drinking coffee, which helps a lot to keep me going. I'm still not happy with the way my stitching is looking. I think I'm going to go back to a thicker size, and use the DMC 12 ply. I'm using 2 strands of one ply, and it is so hard to get the stitches nice and tight. So, we'll see how it goes. I have some pictures of the work in progress, but I'm waiting until I'm finished with it to post them. I had a very interesting day today. I went into Cambridge, Mass., to the Hathaway factory. It was quite an experience. I wish I had my camera with me. I got to see the looms, and the water-powered pantographs. They have quite a few machines in the building. I was impressed by the size of the looms, and by the size of the factory. This factory was built in the 1800s. They still manufacture thread. The tour guide was very nice and answered all my questions. I wish I would have had my camera with me. But it was such a small tour that there was no room to take it with me. I'll try to post some pictures when I get them developed. Today, I took the day off from stitching and did laundry. I finally figured out how to wash my bed sheets on my own, so I did that. It was very interesting to see what I had to do to get the sheets to come out clean. It was quite a process. It was mostly just getting the sheets wet and then putting them in the washer. It's a little bit different than the way I wash them at home. Yesterday, I took a class on how to make a wedding ring quilt. The class was very interesting. It was basically a one-hour class with some people coming after the class to finish up their quilt. We made a 6 inch by 6 inch wedding ring quilt. We made the foundation by using some Raffia. Then we put the fabric on the Raffia, and then put the batting on. We sewed the squares together. We only had time to make one quilt. We had to make 50. I think I'll make more than one. I really liked this class. I started stitching on my tapestry again. I started a new part, which is a bit more interesting than what I was doing before. I am using 2 strands of one ply, and it is very difficult to get the stitches tight enough. I'm using the backstitch, which looks better than a satin stitch. I am also doing some satin stitch, but I'm using the DMC

Several families enjoy the nearby restaurants including The Cove restaurant and private dining rooms located just off Main Street. The Harbor Village community brings together many small businesses and organizations offering services ranging from a number of local parks near the beach, arts community events held throughout the year featuring local artists to community groups displaying artworks often featuring local craftsmen, photographers, musicians and dancers showcasing local history and popular exhibits such as the Aquarium Museum. Harbor Village offers events including the annual Thrillist Festival annually hosting live music concerts each Friday night. The community also hosts events such as commercial events hosted at the Harbor Village Farmers Market which attracts numerous artists and vendors selling handmade items for sale outside the Harbor Village Market as well as events every Saturday evening and Sunday afternoon giving residents an opportunity to meet and greet neighbors and make new friends while enjoying their favorite seasonal foods during the month of January and February. Harbor Village has been providing transportation options, meals served by boat tours, attractions such as a pier and picnic facilities, shopping centers, a golf course and restaurants catering to all ages inside and outside the Harbor Village community center. Activities include a Physical Activity Center where residents can visit with family members who may have questions about running water racing boats or biking bicycles. Harbor Village features a fine tennis training facility allowing households to work toward fitness goals daily creating a positive environment for everyone to gather outdoors; community events include a seasonal outdoor theatrical performance series, a monthly craft fair organized by Harbor Village volunteers; a music festival attended by local musicians, performers, artists and entertainers weekly; and a weekly parade highlighting local products featured prominently displayed throughout the Harbor Village community. Harbor Village also features a free library, gym and hot tubs available for activities including yoga classes, a fitness center and small group exercise class classes. Harbor Village citizens are encouraged to explore the community and take advantage of the many opportunities available to them both with visits guided by Harbor Village staff as well as activities offered including a Sea Love program facilitating kayak trips for adults and youth participants on the Harbor Village Aquatics League's own charter boat. Harbor Village also welcomes visitors as they stroll the streets enjoying local street food trucks sponsored by Harbor Village Food Bank sponsored by the Harbor Village Community Association seeking to create new friendships among residents. We had dinner at a place called Tapas and Wine in Portland last week. It's a great little restaurant with a cool bar and a ton of interesting people. My girlfriend ordered a wine called 2007 Sangiovese from "Italy." It was good, but I could tell it was from the US, and I was curious. I asked the bartender if he could point me to a winery in Italy that produces wine like this, and he couldn't. I asked him about the "sangiovese" wine he had just served me, and he told me that Sangiovese was a variety of grape from Italy, but he didn't know the specific winery. I guess that makes sense, because he wasn't a wine expert, and he had no idea what the heck Sangiovese was. So I did a little research, and I was surprised to find that Sangiovese is actually a variety of grape that originated in Sicily. In fact, the region of Sicily produces a large number of wines from the grape. It's a popular variety because it produces high quality, highly aromatic wines. It's also quite hardy, so you can find it growing on the hottest of hillsides in the hottest of countries. In fact, the hot Italian summers make Sangiovese a very cool climate grape. Sangiovese grapes are very rich in volatile aromatic compounds, so the aroma of the wine is very strong. The flavors of Sangiovese can vary from spicy, peppery to spicier, and the flavors can range from slightly bitter to extremely bitter. There are a number of wineries that make wine from Sangiovese, but I think the two most famous are Stag's Leap Winery in Napa Valley and the Tignanello Winery in Piedmont. Historically, Sangiovese was the predominant grape in the "great Italian wine regions" of Tuscany and Piedmont, but it has been pushed aside in favor of the new generation of varietal wines. The grapes are more resistant to the cold, dry winters of those regions, so they can produce a higher quality wine. However, I think it is still the grape of choice in the warmer climates of Sicily and Sardinia, where the weather is hotter and the grapes have a better chance of producing high quality, aromatic wines. I would have never guessed that Sicily and Sardinia would be the two regions that produced the best Sangiovese wines in Italy, but I'm not surprised that the grapes grow well there. They're like the old fashion American "great white north" grapes. Now, if only I could find some of this wine at the end of my long workday... 2011-04-11 I have a great friend who is a very good cook. She's not a professional chef, but she's good enough that people ask her to cook for them. I have eaten at some of her amazing meals, and they are always great. In fact, I had one of her meals for dinner this past weekend, and I was surprised by how good it was. I guess I was expecting her to be cooking the same dishes that I've seen her cook on TV. I was expecting a lot of healthy "Mediterranean" dishes. Instead, she served a very good vegetarian "Sicilian" meal. Now, I'm not sure if she had "Mediterranean" influences in her cooking, or if she just learned to cook a Sicilian style from her mother. Regardless, I was pleasantly surprised by the meal. The first dish was a very tasty eggplant and chickpea stew. The chickpeas were soaked overnight in water and the next day they were added to the stew along with some tomato, onion, garlic, and olive oil. The stew was served with a nice drizzle of olive oil, a couple of good olives, some raisins, and some fresh parsley. I've made this stew before, and I usually add a little bit of diced red pepper and some paprika. This time, she didn't, so it was a little bit different. However, it was still good, and it made a great meal. I was very happy to find this dish on the menu, because it's a very popular dish in Sicily. It's a traditional dish that's often served with some pasta or bread, and it's a great meal for a cold winter day. The second dish was a delicious eggplant parmigiana.

Swung in here on a recent early-summer weeknight and only later realized they'd just opened the place. It had been packed the previous weekend, with a front window that opens up onto the great terrasse on Avenue Mont-Royal. Terrasse was unfortunately closed on this particular night as the permit was in transition, so we sat inside. Our fab serveuse, Emilie, was very quick to serve us and knowledgeable on the beers on tap. Saint-Sacrament has house blonde and rousse brews, the former of which isn't stupendous in terms of taste but is rather good, and one could imagine sinking quite a few over the course of a Saturday night. Other beers on tap include Stella Artois, Hoegaarden, Alexander Keith's, and a couple others nothing out-of-the-ordinary. The bar seemed not quite as well-stocked as it could be, but the place does not profess to be a nightclub or cocktail bar, and Emilie was able to improvise where necessary. It is, quite directly, a tavern. Ambiance was really where Saint-Sacrament has things kicking on all cylinders. Amazing long wooden tables made from reclaimed wood are at bar-stool height, and are great for larger groups. (I anticipate if you show up at a decent hour on a weekend, you won't have to contort to ask for chairs from other tables.) Fantastic tin ceiling. There are about four or five individual and properly-interior-designed washrooms in the back. Place is spotless, and the music is fantastic: good mix of Rolling Stones Bitch! Hadn't heard that in years), Johnny Cash, and other proper pub music blasting over a great sound system. After cranking the music up louder at one point, one of the proprietors actually came over to make sure our table wasn't disturbed by the volume, since we were right under the speaker. Nice touch there, too. (Considering the quality of the music we weren't disturbed at all.) There's at least one TV in there; it was being used for a Euro repeat when we arrived, but as the night wore on it was shut off in favour of the music, which is entirely proper for any reputable establishment. Didn't try any of the food, but everything coming out of the kitchen looked nice. Prices for the beer and liquor are very modest for a watering hole that has a proper sense of design and great service about it. Bottom line: certainly worth spending a few hours in here if you're in the Plateau on a weekend night (or even a weeknight). They're opened until 3am each and every night, too c'est genial!

I was underwhelmed with my experience at Matt's Big Breakfast, although I visited the place prompted by reviews from others. The location is cute and the place delivers wholesome foods for those who are on a health kick or just want to eat clean, but if you're looking for an authentic breakfast in Vancouver this probably isn't your best bet (unless it's been updated since the last time I went). Matt's specialties include his homemade granola served straight out of its large bowl topped off with fresh fruit as well as hot coffee made using beans roasted within hours before serving (you can either get iced cold brew instead when requested), which makes sense given that he also uses them in some items cooked up including one item called "the Mighty Mac," an omelette featuring portabella mushrooms stuffed inside filled with ham cheese avocado covered in house-made guacamole. There were no other offerings during my visit aside from a few different types eggs benedict styles offered - everything else seemed rather simple like baconegg sandwich combos along with first rate pancakes doused liberally with syrup. For me personally nothing really stood apart about what they had here except maybe their hash brown casserole baked dish while another more interesting sounding meal would have been the "five hour breakfast," consisting basically of scrambled egg whites mixed into quinoa then covered in salsa fresca all wrapped up in tortillas. You could go even simpler there though with only a protein option added such as chicken breast over rice pilaf followed by ice cream sundaes. The service wasn't great (though perhaps understandably so) being slow initially yet once we finally got our food the servers worked hard to keep us happy. And yes, be prepared to wait because many people do come in for dinner too. Perhaps not surprisingly, the prices weren't cheap; however considering how delicious much of what's available looked, per person still came below 20 Canadian (14 USD) most likely due to the fact that many meals are better suited for sharing than eating completely alone especially the hearty breakfasts rich enough to make you feel full throughout the morning until lunch comes around again. If you consider yourself healthy minded and occasionally find yourself wanting options outside a typical greasy diner fare, give Matt's Big Breakfast a shot despite having never heard of the man behind it himself:

The jimmy roll was so good that I would recommend it to everyone! My husband had the special, two soft shell crab tacos 14 and he loved them. I ordered three tacos for 15 - the Baja fish, braised beef and cheesesteak. All were good but the cheesesteak was my favorite. I really enjoyed the food and will go back.

I was extremely disappointed when ordering pizza from this place. The girl that rang up our order said it would be 20-25 minutes for our pizza and garlic knots to come out. It was easier to just order garlic knots, because you could eat them right away. So we ordered the garlic knots and waited. And waited. And waited. After 45 minutes went by, we were done waiting and left. We had to stop at a different place for dinner. I will never go back to this place for food.

I took our VW Passat here on Wednesday to get the oil changed. They squeezed me in, and rotated the tires too. Cool. As I was driving to Minneapolis on Friday, however, the plastic bottom covering the engineoil area (or whatever is down there, I don't really know) began to fall off. Eventually, I had to stop at a random dealership right outside of Eau Claire so that they could remove the rest of the plastic, which had been dragging on the highway. I called Goodyear, and Polly basically said oh yeah, we noticed that the bolts were stripped that hold it on, we shouldn't have put it back on. This is a common problem with VWs, and it's really not a big deal - the plastic isn't necessary for the car, it's just a pain when it actually falls off and drags. What I don't understand is why they put it back on when it was obvious to them that it wasn't going to stay on. So now it's back at Goodyear for the day. They are putting a new cover on, for free of course.

World's smallest bar! I kept seeing Hef's and was excited to finally go there. Total let down. The staff was friendly but the drinks just weren't good. The couple next door were very respectful, though, so I decided not to bother with that. For me, it felt like I was in a carnival of tables - mostly french way- instead of a bunch of bars. It felt more like a carnival than a restaurant. I didn't mind the food at all. Their beef stew is always really tasty, especially when you have lots of spiced soup or curry (yum!). They had regular breakfast (which I actually thought looked delicious) although their other options included just plain chicken breast and scrambled egg. The menu was pretty damn weird. There are only two options on tap as well as just "chicken" and "eggs." Some people said this wasn't a great option for them, while others said they liked eggs better... it was definitely interesting. It would be cool if we could order lunch separately from our meal plan. We often get our meals cooked at the same time (like most restaurants).

I love Houston food, yet has any place been able to compare with houston food for me or bigger than that...Texas, but then again I haven't traveled to many states. Finally!!! I made it!!! I went in with Spicy Pastor Tacos on my mind. But when I saw an order of Carne Asada Fries pass by me, I changed course. I got the small order and glad I did because the large would have been way too much. Let me tell you, TEG is some straight up Mexican food goodness! I love this place. The lines were crazy, it was hot in there, families squished in together at the small tables, people hollering across each other - I loved it! And I will be back now that I know where it is. For the past three trips to Vegas, I would make the effort to get to TEG, but could never see it. It is in a sort of strip mall with a small parking lot. This time, I rode around twice before I spotted it. And I was rewarded with some really good eats. (This review was from my July 2013 trip)

There aren't enough adjectives or stars. If you only see one show, this is it. Stunning! I have seen this show three times. What an amazing theatrical experience! A must-see for all ages, even teens. Went here for my honeymoon. The air conditioner was making a loud noise when we got to our room at 2:30pm. I called the front desk and asked if we could switch rooms and was told that they would have maintenance come look at the unit. The guy shows up to our room at 10:35pm. He looks at the unit and says that they needed to replace a motor. Said he would come back the next day at 11:00 (Saturday). He never showed up for the rest of our stay. I may be lactose intolerant but that has not stopped me from binging on gelato. Gelato 64 is located in the Lee Lee's Plaza on the NE corner of Dobson and Main Street. It is a small gelato shop with a seating area. Their gelato is actually quite good. I personally like the peanut butter and chocolate flavor. I've been to gelato 64 numerous times and only once have they run out of the flavors I wanted. So, that's pretty good. The flavor selection is always the same. The seating area can be kind of a bummer. There are 6 or 7 tables and a few chairs. The tables are always sticky and gross. The chairs are uncomfortable. The view out the window is not pleasant. Great italian food, all their pastas are homemade. Nice extensive wine selection, and some nights they have live music. Perfect location right across the street from hard rock.

It's not cheap, but it's the best vanilla yogurt I've ever tasted. I'll definitely be back! My husband and I were a little disappointed with our first visit here. The quiche was a bit rubbery and lacking in flavor. The muffins and cookies were all good.

This place is wonderful! I ordered the Sesame Encrusted Salmon and it was the best thing I've had in a while! I've read about celebrities going to Nobu. My friend talked about Nobu like it was a god of sorts. When we found out we had a table waiting for us at Nobu, I was ready to go and feast myself on its delights. We ordered: The miso black cod, salmon nigiri, a soft shell crab roll, the hamachi and jalapeno appetizer, the mushroom salad, a vegetarian cut roll, and the tiradito. To drink I had the cucumber martini. It was seriously one of the best drinks I have ever had. It tasted like it was made with lychee vodka, and was smooth, refreshing and not too sweet. Unfortunately our positive experience ended there. After waiting an hour for our table, we had ordered about 15 cucumber martinis and was dying for some water. We sat at our table and for 9 people, 2 drink menus were placed on the table and then we were ignored. I glanced at the menus, waited. Our waiter came by and I asked him for waters all around and food menus. 15 minutes go by. We had no water, and no menus. Finally, we're given 5 menus for 9 people, as he handed me the last menu, he left saying We're a little short on menus. We shared our menus and within 3 minutes he was back asking us what we were going to have. We asked him for some suggestions, and he pretty much just brushed us off. We finally ordered the hamachi and jalapenos. Before I could order anything else, he rushes off. The next time we saw him he is dropping of a plate of hamachi and jalapenos. Pretty much the whole night, he just ran off with us halfway through ordering and as a result, we were unable to dine together. I can only speak for the mushroom salad and vegetable cut roll. The vegetable cut roll was pretty good, I mean, steamed vegetables, wrapped in a cucumber wrap, with a little ponzu sauce. The mushroom salad was pretty gross. The mushrooms were varied; trumpets, oysters, shiitake, enoki. The sauce it was cooked in was sour and as a result made the mushrooms taste bad. Everyone else thought the hamachi and jalapenos were pretty good, and they loved the miso black cod. Everything else, however, they said was mediocre. Mediocreness is ok, if it wasn't coupled with poor service and a 400 bill. When the bill came, we inquired about the drinks on the bill as we thought we had taken care of them all at the bar. His response? No you didn't, but you can just take it out of my tip. I secretly think that everybody raves about this place so much because they don't want to admit they spent that much money on a mediocre experience that you can get anywhere in San Francisco for a quarter of the price. Overall verdict: Skip it. The atmosphere is not really that great, the food isn't really that great, and the service should not be called service. The Pros: The cucumber martini was super good.
I went in to purchase overalls and was treated so rudely I had to walk out even though he had the item I wanted. I will never step foot in there again. Lowest prices are definitely not "treatments"

So I wish one of these airports I frequent would have a nice mexican restaurant. But that is impossible. Short and sweet: Good: The steak quesadilla was alright. The tacos were good. The churros were delicious. The hot chocolate was very good. Bad: No refills on soda unless you bought a bottle of water which is weird. Service was not great, it was very slow. I would recommend that if you are going to have a buffet, give people the option of ordering at the counter and getting their food quickly that way. This is a nice airport restaurant. Good food. The food was really good and it was one of the few places open after 8pm. It's hard to find food late at night, so I was happy to see a full menu available. I will definitely come back here next time I'm in the area.

Let's get something quick to eat, yeah? OKAY! Pho is supposed to be fast. Just ladle that soup broth over the noodles and meat and you're fricking done. Right? NO, NOT HERE. My friend ordered spring rolls, which were 2 tiny rolls cut in half. That took a good 40 minutes to make. (BTW, there were barely any other customers, so it's not like they were busy making other food!) The rest of us ordered pho, which took nearly an hour for it to come out. We would've bounced the fuck outta there if we didn't feel so bad for doing so. So we just stayed because we were hungry and waited that long already. When we finally got our food, it wasn't even that good! The broth was piping hot, which was nice...but that's probably what they were doing this whole time...boiling the soup. My friend mentioned that they forgot the flavor. Yup, the broth had little to no flavor. Plus, my rare steak tasted sour, which meant it was probably old and should not be eaten! People who have rated this restaurant anything better than 2 stars have not eaten GOOD pho before. Also, if you were drunkhungover when you ate here, I'll excuse you because of the lack of judgment. Lesson to be learned: Don't eat pho in Vegas!

If you have shit with good food and service, I would definitely try again, but for ALL the buffets I would rather stay at a mediocre buffet.

I'm really pleased with the services that we got at this place. My wife and I are on a specialized meal plan that requires that we weigh and measure all of our food before eating it, so they were kind enough to set up scales for us in their office where you can get weighed after every piece of fruit or vegetable that goes into your mouth... Allergy-friendly dining options: They have a separate kitchen staff who prepare meals using gluten-, dairy- and egg-free ingredients; as well as an allergy specialist on call eighteen hours per day (who will come out to see you no matter when you've made contact). The hotel also has its own 'on demand' chef service which allows guests to order whatever dishes don't contain eggsdairy etc from any other restaurant within walking distance around town without having to worry about cross contamination! We loved being able to eat life without feeling cut off by allergies while here - great to be given such freedom!!The Hotel is part of Wyndham Rewards program which gives members incentives like points redeemable toward free stays gift cards. There's also the option for daily breakfast credits if needed.

Well after a few months since my previous review I did return and things have not changed one bit. The silver age, war and horror (old school subjects, from the 60s70s) drawers are still empty. I collect silver age, but I don't have a specific item that I am looking for, I basically browse the drawers and if a cover appeals to me I buy it. To me not having a structure in my collecting makes it more fun, I don't need to complete a full run and any random book or subject is just fine with me. The cover art is what I am mostly looking for (since 90 of the time the story in the book lets you down in relation to the exciting cover art). I really liked it when they had several drawers full of silver age that I could concentrate on and they were located in one place towards the beginning of the line of drawers. Now you can find silver age, but they are mixed into all the other hundreds of subjects and those drawers are so full you can't even look through them without removing a huge stack so you can take a look. Some drawers are so tight, you can't even remove some to make room, other drawers are packed so loose that the books are falling over damaging other books and folding them. I did manage to find a few items that totalled about 15, but when I checked out, again no mention of the rewards program. Again this is a sticking point with me, since for all the years I was buying there it was at about the 250 in total purchases that I was finally offered a card for the rewards program. Ugh!

Let's start with the positive, which begins about an hour after we sat in the bar area - the Big Ass Burger is big and delicious. Now to the rest: We ordered the Green Chile Pork appetizer after asking our waiter to help us decide between that and the guacamole and queso. We take our time ordering dinner because we have an appetizer coming - except that we don't. When it becomes clear it isn't arriving we start eyeing the kitchen for signs of our dinner. Our meal shows up much later than our leisurely ordering would have dictated and we advise our waiter not to bring the Green Chile Pork. He responds You didn't get that? I was thinking, you helped us order it but you didn't bring it, you didn't arrange for it to be brought, and you certainly didn't clear it from our table prior to serving our entrees and still you seem surprised. But because I am on a sarcasm control regimen I just said, No, we didn't. Two of us ordered fish tacos which were very tasty but 4 of the six tacos across the two plates served were extremely undercooked. We are not afraid of fish a bit under temperature but this was well below that. On the plus side the manager stopped by to apologize. On the minus side he was unaware that both orders were off. Plus - he recovered quickly and graciously said he was buying our drinks. Minus - he comped less than half the drinks. We were a party of 4 and none of us ordered another drink after his offer so our drinks were fully accounted for on our bill at the time and we were not trying to take advantage. Perhaps he comped just the drinks of the two who ordered the tacos but the meal was interrupted for all as we waited for the re-fire. On to dessert. Plus - the good and hot coffee came quickly and the chocolate infused pecan pie was delicious. Minus - the pecan pie was very small and we were again craning our necks toward the kitchen looking for clues to its arrival as it was served well after the coffee. Had the tacos been served correctly the first time the taste and quality of the food would have tipped this over to a 3 star review. The food was really very good but difficult to enjoy when the overall meal was so poorly managed. We are divided about a return visit.

We decided to give brunch a try for our first visit to Casbah. We were surprised by the huge tent covering the outdoor dining area. We opted for an inside table outside, rather than in the street-level dining room. The crowd was mainly families and college students who seemed pretty content with their view of the beach, as opposed to one or two people seated at tables along the sidewalk. The weather was warm - about 75 degrees with a slight breeze - so we took advantage of this seating location while eating. There is no place for small children here; they're welcome only when accompanied by an adult. I recommend starting your meal off with a cold appetizer like the crab cake (8) that came with chips and choice of drink (we chose water). It had a light mayonnaise-like consistency with soft white cheese on top. For the main course, we went back to Casbah's famous chicken wings (11-13), which are served in stacks separated by white paper-covered plates that look like cardboard boxes. They come in two sizes: large and medium. I ordered the medium, but my companion didn't order it because she wanted something less spicy. She got her usual hot wing flavors, including garlic, chili pepper and Thai chile. The wings were dried out fresh, crisp and juicy. I definitely preferred them to Casbah's other hot item, cashew chicken (10). First, the cashews don't always cook through evenly, causing some pieces to be dry while others are still moist. Second, the wings take longer to fry than Casbah's other dish. Third, you can taste a hint of vinegar from each bite compared to our favorite house speciality, the New Orleans Hot Wings (14-15): every bite has a little bit of spice. Casbah's Memphis BBQ ribs (12-16) are even better. This dish features three racks made up of overlapping beef bones surrounded by fried pork ribs, served over a bed of creamy coleslaw and baked beans. My partner added onion rings and hot sauce to finish. These homemade bites were jalapeno-spiced, smoky and delicious. Of all the dishes Casbah offers, I think their cornbread is my favourite. They make theirs with sweet cornmeal, brown sugar and butter. I'm not sure how many fillings go into their loaf, though the ingredients list includes pickles, onions, molasses, ketchup and gravy. I added raisins and walnuts before topping mine with the barbecue sauces mentioned earlier. My friend ordered the smoked turkey breast (18), which comes with hot peppers, bacon bits and mashed potatoes. To deliver the perfectly cooked bird, Casbah cooks it overnight on a plastic tray in heavy basting baths filled with water and salt. Their version of tomato soup wasn't what I expected, although it was more substantive than any I've seen elsewhere. Maybe if I would have added some salt to it, it could have been my favourite. Overall, I would eat one again! Overall, Casbah seems to be popular among families because there aren't too many options for kids to do. But once dinner time arrives, you'll find ample space for children to run around, jump on the trampoline or play with toys given away during set menus. One thing that does irk me? Casbah doesn't allow dogs onto its premises. Perhaps they need to add Indoor Dog Park to their menu.

Sensational Food, Spellbinding View The Fountains Brunch at Jasmine may be the best Sunday brunch you've never heard of. In comparison to the more famous Sterling Brunch across the Strip at Bally's, many people aren't aware that on Sunday, Jasmine in the Bellagio opens at 11 a.m. for a luxe, Cantonesedim sumall American breakfast brunch. The room is decorated in florals and creams.... it's a bit old lady, but never feels stuffy, especially with sunlight streaming through the windows on a bright morning. Better yet, the room's floor-to-ceiling windows overlook the Bellagio fountains, which go into overdrive especially for brunch patrons. Fountain music is pumped into the room every 15 minutes as the fountains perform. Outside of the fountains, the centerpiece of the brunch is a fantastic buffet. It's not massive, but there's a wide variety of superbly prepared dishes. Traditional american brunch favorites are here, with the usual Bellagio-classy twists: the belgian waffles are red velvet, the eggs benedict are served on a lobster-potato cake. There's an excellent raw bar, a selection of caviar and sushi, and awesome cold bites and cheeses.There's also an omelet station, but a better choice is the soup, where a chef customizes asian-style noodles to your liking. The carving station has huge chunks of beef, lamb, and incredible carved slab bacon. The dim sum components are great too: sui mai, short ribs, crystal prawns. Best of all, they serve fantastic peeking duck table side in steamed buns. The finale of brunch is a room devoted to desserts, and unlike many buffets, these are made in small batches by the pastry team and are quite good. Additionally, the pastry chef on staff chats and explains the different desserts, what was particularly good that day, and what ice creams and gelatos they've prepared. Downsides: it's not cheap (80ish), and unlimited champagne is an add-on. (They have different levels of sparkling wines, and I believe the lowest was about 15?) I think they add gratuity automatically, but the service was so good when I went that my boyfriend and I ended up tipping more. Overall, this is a truly not-to-be-missed morning in Las Vegas. Make reservations, go hungry, and prepare to spend a few hours indulging yourself. If nothing else, this is probably the classiest way to deal with a hangover on the Strip.

Pretty much what you'd expect at a mid-range restaurant. But, here is where it goes wrong. The glass of champagne was teeny tiny! Not a half glass. More like a third of a glass. We were shocked. It would have been a full glass if the waiter had poured the champagne all the way to the top of the glass. Instead he poured it in a "conservative" amount, like you'd get in a bar. I asked him for a refill. He refilled it to the top of the glass. Then I asked him if that was the standard pour or if he just filled it to the top because I was complaining. He said he'd fill it to the top. So I sat and watched other people's glasses of champagne come to the table. They were all teeny tiny. So, the waiter either wasn't given the message to fill glasses to the top, or else he was instructed not to fill them to the top. This is a problem. The waiter was obviously trying to skimp on the amount of champagne he was pouring. The other thing that's a problem is the cost of champagne. We were both shocked at the cost of 6 for a third of a glass of champagne. It would be one thing if it was a nice restaurant where we were ordering expensive entrees, but we were at DB, where entrees are about 10. Not a very nice practice. And now, for the fun stuff. The food was delicious. It was served quickly. The waiter was attentive. We had the tempura calamari. It was served with a spicy sauce and a tamarind sauce. It was delicious. The calamari was crunchy and not too chewy. It was just right. We also had a salad, and I had the ravioli with marinara sauce. Yum! My ravioli was incredibly delicious. It was a nice thick ravioli. I was so full after eating the appetizers, I couldn't even eat the ravioli. So, it was a very good value. The salad was good too. It was a mixed green salad with cherry tomatoes and a nice balsamic vinaigrette. It was a bit too much salad for the 2 of us. We couldn't finish it. But the salad was tasty. So, the moral of the story is to go to DB, but don't order a glass of champagne. It's a rip off. Order a whole bottle instead!

I decided that a place called the tortilla factory has got to have good tacos, so I ordered the house tacos. How could I go wrong? I ordered chips and salsa, and the waiter brought some complimentary black bean tortillas with tomato butter. I wolfed down one thick, leaden, undercooked flour tortilla and pushed the plate away. Maybe the worst tortilla I've ever had! The house tacos were just like the fajitas from any chain restaurant: grilled chicken, steak, and shrimp with accompaniments: guacamole, beans, rice, and pico de gallo. Shredded iceberg lettuce was the only vegetable. Each individual item was quite bland. It all could have used a squirt of lime juice, some cilantro, or even just salt and pepper. Then I made a huge blunder and ate a second black bean burrito. As I write this review, I can feel this baseball-sized lump of dough in my stomach. The atmosphere is cool, but the food stinks. It reminded me of cafeteria food: bland, overcooked, and not really fresh.

The menu is fairly simple: curries, steaks, kimbap (wavy rice noodles), bibimbap (a mixture of spicy cabbage-marinated vegetables like cucumber, carrot, and eggplant, all cooked together into a thick wavy noodle dish), among others. A serving of two went over 15 last time we tried it out. We ordered the Kekyo Bocchi, which consists of four pieces of shrimp served alongside scallops, black beans, and jalapenos. The whole thing comes with a bowl of soy sauce flavored with ginger, garlic, and Sriracha. Yes, this was literally my favorite food item during our trip. Overall, it came across as a great overall value for money deal, especially since it costs only around 10 a piece. Again, it wasn't anything too special, but it definitely tasted better than most other similar seafood platters I'd seen before. They also serve up some Korean BBQ options on occasion once you get past their Korean-inspired features. So be sure to check them out next time you head down here.

The other week, we received the following email from the department: "Dear Colleague: In my effort to be more effective, I am sending this email to those of you who have graduate students. In the past, I have not done this as I thought the student would be the one to follow up with you regarding their progress. Unfortunately, many do not. I have also not sent this to those of you who have only recently started to advise graduate students. This is a new effort to increase my effectiveness. I am planning to meet with each of our graduate students in the near future. I will be asking them about their progress towards their degree, their plans for the future and any problems they might be having. I would like to know what you think of their progress as well. Please send me your feedback on the student's progress, their likelihood of completing the degree requirements within the timeframe that they have presented to me, and any problems you might be having with the student. If you have any questions, comments, or concerns, please feel free to contact me. Thanks for your time and help in this effort." I'm sure he means well. But I'm also sure that this is not the way to go about it. We had a graduate student, A, whose committee chair was very similar. His typical emails, whenever the student was having problems, would go something like this: "Dear student A: I just talked with Dr. X, and I understand that you are having trouble with your research. I'm very concerned about your progress. This is my last year on campus before I go on sabbatical, and I would like to see you graduate before I leave. I have a reputation to uphold. Please get your act together. Sincerely, Dr. L" Within the course of one year, student A had developed severe paranoia, acute depression, and had to drop out of the program. Student A had never had problems before Dr. L became his committee chair. He's currently on medication and working on getting his life back in order. Dr. L, on the other hand, got his reputation intact, because he graduated a student before he went on sabbatical. I can't be sure, but I have a feeling that our current chair is trying to follow in Dr. L's footsteps. I can't help but wonder if our current chair has ever heard of the expression, "Don't Sweat the Small Stuff." I have been a graduate student for the past seven years. I have had to deal with various levels of incompetence, indifference, and, on occasion, outright hostility on the part of my committee members. I have been at this for seven years now. If I'm not "ready to graduate," then that is the fault of my committee, and no amount of emails from the committee chair is going to change that. I'm not going to write my committee chair an email, telling him that if he wants to see me graduate, then he needs to get his act together. I'm not going to tell him that if he wants to see me graduate, then he needs to become a better mentor. I'm not going to tell him that if he wants to see me graduate, then he needs to stop being such a pompous ass. I'm not going to tell him that if he wants to see me graduate, then he needs to stop insulting my intelligence. I'm not going to tell him that if he wants to see me graduate, then he needs to stop treating me like a child. I'm not going to tell him that if he wants to see me graduate, then he needs to stop being such a pathetic excuse of a human being. Because I'm a graduate student, and he's the committee chair. But I'm sure that he will understand.

I first ate at the Salt Cellar as a child with my parents. I have a nice memory of having lobster. It was fun to go to a restaurant underground, and at the time (in the 80's) it was considered a really fancy place to go. So that was the 80's and unfortunately, Salt Cellar is stuck in the 80's. It still was kinda cool going down the stairs to the restaurant, but it felt like the air wasn't clean. Seemed dank. The bar looked nice, but the lighting in the restaurant were those weird orange ones. Mood lighting? Seemed depressing and old. The pictures on the wall looked like were the same ones that were there in the 70's. This place needs a make over!!! We were seated and they took my fiance's drink order. He was very clear about no water in his old fashioned. It was served with water. He sent it back, and it came back the same way. Finally he just ordered straight bourbon. My fiance had oysters and I had halibut ceviche. The oysters were gritty. The ceviche had a very sour taste and was loaded with red peppers. I think they used lemon instead of lime. I couldn't finish it. Nasty! Main course I had the Salmon Oscar. The salmon was amazing, but it was ruined from being drowned in a very bad hollandaise. It tasted like glue. No lemon flavor. It was just bad! I squeezed some lemon on it to try to fix it, but it was not working. Too much sauce and it was just awful! My fiance ordered halibut cheeks that were pretty good, but the vegetables were so over cooked and drowned in butter. The baked potato was decent. I felt sick from the nasty hollandaise so we got the check and left. Disappointing! Salt Cellar is stuck in the past and in need of a makeover. I was afraid of this, but went for nostalgic reasons. Too bad. We won't be back!

Finally, a place to go in Vegas that's not totally overrun by tourists and has food and atmosphere that rival some of our better restaurants in Chicago. The decor and ambiance were outstanding. It has a somewhat over the top Rat Pack era Vegas thing going on, which was great. There was a live singer the Saturday night we went. I half expected the ghost of Dean Martin to breeze in the door any second. This restaurant is relatively far off the Strip down East Tropicana but they will purportedly send a limo to pick you up. I didn't see this limo but if it is anything like the decor in this place, you'll most certainly turn a few heads as it picks you up in front of the Bellagio. The food is traditional Italian. Lots of pasta dishes that you'll probably be very familiar with. Service was very good. Our waiter was attentive and the items we ordered came fast. They ran out of Cannelloni that we ordered and threw in a free desert because of it. Nice. Old school service. The lasagna they did have was nicely done. Plenty of meat in meat sauce, and cheese in the product. Well seasoned and flavor. It was served at the right temperature - not scalding hot like many lasagna dishes you get. The eggplant was pan fried and then served with red sauce, cheeses and a side of pasta. It too was very good. Portions are not ridiculously large like they can be in some traditional Italian restaurants like this, which is good because if you're staying in a hotel, you obviously can't take anything home. If you're staying on the Strip, a trip to the Casa will be a nice way to get away from the tourist throngs for a few hours. A definite thumbs up!

When we requested the check it was dropped so quickly (no thank you for dining, I hope you enjoyed your evening!) and the waitress gone, that I did not get to hand her my in the ready credit card. I was all set to really enjoy Elements based on the reviews.... but they seem to be quite busy, so I am sure that will not miss my lack of return visits.

What is there to love about Toby Keith's Bar Grill? Not a whole lot. My family and I had dinner at TK's last night as an alternative to Guy Fieri's who 1. Doesn't take reservations and 2. Wanted us to wait 2 hours to eat. Ha ha! No thanks Guy. And BTW - no reservations? Come on. First TK's has a fun atmosphere, but looks like a normal'ol bar and grill. The walls are decorated with Toby Keith.... things, and all the girls wear panties and chaps. Ass in your face every time your server leaves your table. Speaking of service, it could be improved. After we were seated we waited a good 10 minutes to put our order in, luckily, since we all had sufficient time we all knew what we wanted to eat and drink. Onward to the food - steak fajitas, which came out sizzling and made me excited. But when were placed in front of me were a let down. The beef was haphazardly cut and chunky, not strips. Plus the meat was not seasoned in anyway and it looked just WRONG to me. Fajitas come with your choice of corn or flour tortillas. I picked corn - half of them were not steamed enough and had hard edges. They brought them out in a tortilla holder with NO LID. What the heck? No wonder it did not steam all the way. Dear manager of TK's: put lids on your tortilla holders and customers will get tortillas that are soft! My fajitas also came with: rice (OK), refried beans (OK), salsa (not spicy at all), guac (OK), and sour scream (OK). Overall what could be a great dish, only mediocre. Next - I Love This Bar BBQ Sandwich - my mother requested no sides for her sandwich, but they brought her fries anyway. She said the BBQ sandwhich could use more BBQ sauce. Chicken Fried Steak - My brother had this and said it was so-so, not a REAL chicken fried steak in my family's opinion because it didn't appear to be pan-fried, which is the honest way to make a chicken fried steak - not deep frying it with a lot of breading. Speaking of breading... My husband's fish and chips were mostly breading which he peeled off so he could actually eat the fish. Lastly, the shrimp appetizer which my father ordered for his meal came with a HUGE amount of deep fried little shrimp. There had to have been 20 and it came with a tasty, creamy cajun-flavored dipping sauce. I really liked the shrimp. Overall - I feel as though there could be a lot of improvement. I like Toby Keith. I like the idea of the restaurant - I really like all the country music they were playing, but the food was a huge downer.

I came here Saturday night for a comedy show that Amy D was putting on with several other comics. This place is located in a strip mall, next to an AJ's off in a corner. It was my first time here, and it had a nice patio for outdoor seating, right as you walk up. Walking in, the place was large, with plenty of seating. Tables throughout the place, mostly 4 tops from what I could see, along with large booths around the back for larger parties. Being that I came alone, I wasn't sure where to sit. It was kind of open seating, but most of the tables were already taken by other parties. I found it a bit awkward, even if I had brought a date or friend with me, because I wasnt sure if I was supposed to join other people, or just kind of stand around and hope a table opened up for me to sit at. Minus one for seating arrangments.....not sure how that would work if I was with 1 or 2 other random folks where we would have sat.... Eventually, I found the rest of the group for Amy D's group, and I sat with them. I had a total of 3 drinks that night. 2 cokes, and a summertime booze mixed drink. Heres where I found another issue that kinda through me for a loop. One of the people I sat with ordered a guiness.....the waitress came back and said they were all out! He ordered another type of beer, and they had that in stock. Then, I ordered a docs iced tea, which is basically a long island. The waitress came back to tell me that they were out of one of the alcohols to make it, and if I could order something else off the drink menu....ugh, how do you host a Saturday night event and run out of beer stock and certain alcohol stock? I mean, thats kinda sad. Poor ordering on mgmts part, really. The service it self was awesome, and our waitress was awesome, but the alcohol thing really through me for a loop. Plus, the whole seating thing kinda made me think twice about coming back on my own for any other shows they may have outside of Amy D performing. The comics themselves were fun to watch, and it was a great evening out, but the seating and alcohol thing kinda did me in for this place. I would only go back if Amy D was doing standup here again!

As a fervent Yelper, I read many reviews before booking a room at the Excalibur for my 21st birthday weekend. I came frugal-minded, knowing that I would not do much but relax and have fun with friends. But what is there to say about an experience you've already had? On Saturday night, we strolled into the hotel around 8pm and were immediately greeted by several members of the staff who both smiled warmly and welcomed us in. We checked our bags while waiting for one of their bellhops to lead us to our rooms. From there on out it was smooth sailing. The front desk attendant offered us menus from which to choose food options as well as drink specials throughout the evening. They even made suggestions based upon allergies and dietary restrictions. In short, they set up everything so perfectly that all four guests could get exactly what they wanted - including me! I arrived early enough to take advantage of internet access (WiFi) prior to meeting everyone else. One thing about Las Vegas: It has WiFi everywhere. You can literally sit inside any restaurant or bar and log onto your laptop if you want. For those without laptops though, this will provide a chance to grab some laundry done, catch up on FacebookTwitter, call home, plan out dinner reservations...you name it! At 12 per hour credit card fee 10 gratuity (which runs 4 total), most restaurants and bars offer free wifi anyway. So why pay more for an amenity? The rooms themselves are very nice. High ceilings, king sized beds, ample closet space, comfy bedding, large windows overlooking the Strip; pretty basic stuff really. Each bathroom comes furnished with toiletries, hair dryer and slippers. There may be other amenities such as ultrasonic shower heads or heated flooring that I missed during my stay. Shower curtains hung over each door are helpful since after getting ready it's hard to remember when you last used every item in the bathroom. A big plus about staying here is how convenient the location is. As mentioned earlier, there's Internet anywhere within walking distance of the property. If you don't feel like going down to a coffee shop or casino lounge, just stop by the lobby downstairs where you can use the computer stations provided. Also nearby is Bally's Casino Hotel Spa and Paris Las Vegas Hotel Casino. Both are less than five minutes away by car. In addition, almost anything I ate or drank was easily accessible simply because I walked next door nearly every day to either eat or go to the shops. But maybe the best perk was having people around to share moments together. A couple times, I took long walks alone through different areas of town only to meet up later for drinks or snacks somewhere. When someone invited me along, I felt special for being included. Another time, I got called back early from dinner to help him finish packing his bag since he couldn't find something. He ended up forgetting his phone charger at the apartment and asked me to borrow mine. (Note: This happens often). To top it off, two nights before leaving, another guest gave me her leftover jacket form high school which she said I definitely needed. All these events meant a lot to me and showed I wasn't the only person spending quality time with others after all. I have no doubt that the Excalibur offers better rates than its competitors due to its location and popularity. However, I know that I would return again regardless since I received unmatched service above average expectations. And yes, I did quite enjoy myself once I met my group and started hanging out regularly. Cheers to enjoying life everyday, especially birthdays! Let me start by saying I am NOT a fan of casinos. That doesn't mean that all casinos weren't worth visiting though... In fact, I enjoyed all three of them visited. Why should they all be the same?? Because of that, let's dive right in. First impressions are always important so please consider some things first - are you looking to gamble? Or hangout? Drink? Eat? Dance? Watch live entertainment? EAT FOOD AND DRINKS??? Unfortunately, they're closed until 9am Monday so we went to MGM Grand instead. While at MGM Grand, we entered (and exited!) Chippendales haha. Talk about uncomfortable lol. Apparently more of a side jobpet business than full-time gig for Lee, the Cream Liqueur concept admittedly seemed a bit strange to me at first, but with Lee explaining her ideas and time spent formulating the recipes I decided a taste or two wouldn't hurt and with stomach capacity plus 5 to spare a few bites of Pumpkin Pie Brandy, Cinnamon Bun Brandy, and Caramel Pecan Tequila would all prove interesting enough (and the latter two quite delicious) to justify a full order - one scoop of Carrot Cake Irish Whiskey and one of Red Velvet Scotch. Now, having admitted already that I quite liked what I tasted, I will note to purists or mavens that the texture of Lee's Cream is somewhat atypical, an effect of a blending process that that allows the booze to freeze while also using mix-ins like cake and cookies, but if this doesn't bother you then the flavors are great. Beginning first with the Red Velvet, I loved the chocolate and scotch combination while bits of frosting added needed sweetness to the mix and moving next to the carrot cake - it tasted like a great spice cake, complete with raisins and nuts, mixed with something akin to Bailey's - it was definitely the favorite of those I tried and even if not the most technically proficient ice cream, all in all a nice idea and an interesting change of pace.

At one point while at Bacchanal, sometime after eating a plate overflowing with at least a pound of crab legs and before taking on a final slice of cheesecake (one of four dishes I ordered for dessert), I sat back, stuffed and exhausted, and watched as the crowd at the next table, a group of 20-something women celebrating a bachelorette party, dug into a massive platter of food that could have fed an entire fraternity house. The menu at Bacchanal is impressive enough to make your head spin. Some of the offerings include: a full charcuterie board with house made pates, curing meats, pickled vegetables and Vermont cheeses; a grilled squid salad with arugula, roasted corn and lemon vinaigrette; a braised pork belly with white beans, collards and crispy pig ear salad; and a roasted chicken with confit potatoes and fennel. There's also an impressive wine list with more than 300 bottles, including many hard-to-find selections. You can order off the menu or go with the Bacchanal Experience (45person), a prix fixe meal with a main course (a protein like fish, beef, chicken or pork), two salads, three sides and an appetizer. It's quite a bit of food and more than enough for the average person. If you want to try everything, you can always order some off the menu and supplement the Bacchanal Experience with the additional dishes. There are a lot of fantastic restaurants in New Orleans, but Bacchanal has become one of my favorites. Partly because of the way it's set up - if you're looking for a formal sit down dinner experience, this is not the place for you. You can sit inside or outside, but seating is limited, so if you go on a busy night (Friday and Saturday nights are usually packed) you may have to wait. They do have a bar and a small shop where you can pick up a bottle of wine or cheese and crackers to enjoy while you wait, so you can't really complain if you end up waiting a half hour for a table. Another thing that makes Bacchanal so great is that there's a real sense of community here. This was evident the first time I went when I ran into a friend who I hadn't seen in years. We ended up sitting together at the same table and spending the whole night catching up. There's something very cool about the fact that most people who come here are either locals or have been living here long enough to be considered locals. Even the employees seem happy to see you year after year, and they remember who you are and what you eat. The last time I was at Bacchanal, I was sitting outside and a guy walked by and said "Hey, I remember you! You had a bunch of stuff and you were really drunk." I looked up and realized that it was the bartender from seven years ago. He remembered me. And he remembered the food I ate. When I asked him how he remembered all of this, he just shrugged and said, "I remember people." That's pretty much the way I feel about Bacchanal. I remember people and I remember the food.

What else can I tell you except that the decor is comfortable, neat and homey without being fussy. There are paintings by local artists featuring apples and other Oregonian fruits, picturesque scenes of gardens along with flowers and historic photos - adding depth to the setting and ambience. It feels like visiting someone you know well whose house has character and personality even though their name might mean nothing to you. A large chalk board allows guests to see what specials come by and what is available for order. While cheese is often offered no one seems to mind. Instead, the focus is on great food prepared beautifully, offered generously and served promptly. Much time is spent discussing options during meals whether for lunch or breakfast which makes every meal feel special. Other diners may wonder why people choose such a slow pace of life, but I think everyone understands and appreciates it once they realize how much effort goes into making each occasion memorable. One story sticks in my head: Once there was a man who lived near the village where le pichets source some of its wheat products. He became ill and ended up delirious until death brought him back to earth with a jolt, and then took his last breath uttering only three words: 'Le pichet c'est magnifique...[I love it].' Another memory comes to mind, two women sitting nearby and talking quietly at a table across the room watched as someone finished ordering dessert. When it came time to decide what they wanted to eat next they looked at each other and said together [in English], "Tell me ...what does it take?" After reading through menus explaining dishes created primarily using seasonal ingredients for 5 straight days then finding yourself waiting 45 minutes before anyone checks on you wanting to give a full description - well....that means going somewhere new every day isn't always easy. But eventually everyone finds themselves saying enviously, "That sounds good.....isn't it too late to change?!" Good thing that doesn't happen everyday, right?! For me personally, this hasn't happened yet although I am looking forward to trying it again sometime soon. So enjoy the moment with family friends, savor memories over conversation. Trustfuliliciously yours, Stacie

This place has completely horrible service. They come to your table about a minute after you sit down, and if you aren't ready to order - they won't come back for another 10 minutes, unless you can somehow flag one of them down [ but they usually pretend not to see you]. I was contacted by San Felipe's marketing and management team after my poor experience, and I gave them two more tries to make sure it was not a fluke. bad experience in this restaurant burrito was not to my order, had to ask them 3 times why there was no cheese. no refill on horchata at this location and they overcharge for a drink. thinking about making pepes my go to place for now on. also called corporate and they seem to not care. not recommended at all, beware!!!

One word that describes Thai Spices is meh. Located in MeKong Plaza, it took over the old BoCa 7 space. When walking in the place, you'll notice its nice decor. It isn't fancy or anything but still a decent looking restaurant. The menu is pretty good - enough variety to make us feel like we could try something new each day without always repeating ourselves. They have some really great deals every now and then as well which makes eating there even more attractive! We ended up trying out all their appetisers on one of our visits (which I wasn't expecting at first). The Pineapple Fried Rice (13) was quite tasty actually...their seafood wonton soup (12) wasn't too bad either. But my absolute favourite dish here is definitely the Grilled Chicken Satay (19), so much so that I've had this dish twice already! This dish tasted delicious simply because everything about it worked: from the perfectly marinated chicken, right down to the slightly spicy peanut sauce they used for dipping. And having tried most satays across Singapore, I can honestly say theirs is probably the best grilled satay I've come across yet - somewhere between crispy and soft depending upon how long you let the meat sit before devouring it. This might be an odd thing to point out since Thai Spice serves other dishes besides satay but the fact remains that the satay sticks are what made me return again and again to eat here. They also serve noodles, rice and char kway teow (fried noodle with egg pork bits) options. Their satay skewers are available as take-away food as well if you're pressed for time. In terms of pricing though,...its not cheap. This waitress told us "it's Thailand afterall" when explaining why prices were higher than expected (10-20 per plate)...but considering ingredients cost maybe 4 apiece, I'm sure they can afford to sell them cheaper. If only they'd lower costs by increasing portion size instead, hehe I like how simple the concept behind their food is; means no complicated flavours being bombarded into your head just for the sake of making things look appealing. There aren't many places around where you can get such high quality grilling done anymore.

Nothing really drives home that modern Vegas feeling like these fountains. It's not just Vegas, but worldwide you simply won't find many fountains like these. And there's really no point in reviewing them because it's not like you can go anywhere on the Strip and not see or hear them. It is astonishing how many people will not take the time to properly set a camera to where you don't have the flash come on and ruin everything in the shot. People, you're in Vegas. Take the TIME. No one is kicking you out of your precious spot at the railing. Set up, tweak your settings, and get that photo done right. And take the time to actually enjoy a show after you post it to your FB or Twitter or whatever so all your friends can look at it and go, Yeah, been there, done that. Remember, you're in Vegas. Margarita pizza was like out of a box from grocery sauce. The tofu fries tasted weird. The hummus was not authentic. The smoothies were watered down all I can taste I'm sorry to hear that you didn't enjoy your food. If you'd like some help, I can suggest some tips for making your own margarita pizza with fresh ingredients so it has more flavor. For example, you could use fresh tomato sauce, fresh mozzarella cheese, and aromatic herbs like basil to add flavor. As for the tofu fries, sometimes the way tofu is cooked can affect its taste. It's possible that they were overcooked or not seasoned properly. You could try making your own by marinating the tofu in a flavorful sauce and then baking or frying it to your preferred level of crispiness. For hummus, there are many recipes online that use fresh chickpeas and spices to make an authentic and flavorful dip. Try experimenting with different recipes until you find one that suits your taste preferences. Lastly, if you feel that the smoothies were watered down, you could try making your own at home using fresh or frozen fruits and a small amount of liquid like almond milk or coconut water. This way, you can control the consistency and amount of water in your smoothie.
