When you're Italian, you're always very critical of Italian food. You rarely go out to Italian restaurants, and it never compares to Grandma's. But there are always those few places that are able to capture the essence of simple, Italian comfort food. Cugino's is one of those places. Now I'm not saying this is better than my Grandma's food, but if I need to get my fix of Italian comfort food in Vegas, Cugino's is where I come. It's a family-owned Italian restaurant that also serves as a deli, too. They serve all the stuff your Grandma would have served you if you grew up in an Italian household. Sausage and Peppers, Meatballs, Veal Parmesan, Grilled Eggplant, Spaghetti w Meat Sauce, Italian Grinders, etc... I usually come in for a cold sandwich of mortadella, cappicola (gabagoul), salame, and provolone sandwich with all the fixings. Great sandwiches made with great meat. You know it's Italians in charge when they have great quality meats. I also opt for the Sausage and Peppers Sandwich sometimes because this is true comfort food for me. They make their own sausage, and you can buy it raw from them if you ever want to cook some up at home. They also have Pizzas at Cugino's, which I like a lot. The owners are from New York, so it's of course thin crust. Very authentic NY style pizza; very large slices, foldable, and cheesy. Great pizza, and pretty cheap at around 10 for a large. I would highly suggest Cugino's if you love simple Italian food. I haven't found anywhere around Las Vegas that looks more like New York's Italian delis.

I purchased a groupon for my boyfriend and I for a massage and it was quite the experience. The Spa is just run down and not the cleanest and loud and not relaxing. When it was my turn for my massage I told the therapist what I needed to be worked on and he didn't do any of it. He didn't once touch my neck or shoulders which I asked him to work on. It was the strangest massage I have ever had. I know that everyone has their own techniques, but he only used his elbows the whole time - just bizarre. My boyfriend's massage was good, but he was VERY sore the next few days which is not always normal. I only paid 39 for the groupon but definitely was not even worth that. I would not recommend this place.

Came in with my son and nephew. Asked if I could add Chicken to a salad and first I was told no, and then I was told that I could n't keep the chicken separate from the rest of the meal after adding it at check out. No explanation other than "it's not our policy." This is obviously just one restaurant but it's an interesting example why they are making these decisions. The same company would decide by their standards on what can be served separately or together when you order online (and elsewhere). So this type of service should appear as part of your contractual details on both platforms so you're aware before buying tickets for anything elseordering ahead. What about amending the contract itself? Maybe remove any clause which allows restaurants to charge customers for servicing food separated? I cannot understand how the restaurant doesn't want to serve additional items such as soup on top of a main dish because you don't have enough room. Then again, maybe the restaurant does. Perhaps they do want people who love soup to buy extra soups during happy-hour deals, or perhaps they do wish diners to eat all things separate...

Growing Pains Have Yet To Improve We have gone here several times in the months that is has been open, and overall the experiences are usually the same, with the concneus being an overwhelming Meh. The beer selection is great, the food can be good, but the staff has no sense of urgency, which can ruin the great idea of this concept. Our last meal was a bust from the start, with the standard unattentive server. Drinks took forever, and while we got 5 flights, there was limited explanation of which beer was which in the Build Your Own Flight. At least, as a saving grace, we could figure it out, but that was a bit frustrating. The food took much prodding to get from our server. When it did arrive, only the sandwiches were hot. The soup was both lukewarm and bland; as if they were attempting to pay homage to grilled cheese with condensed Campbell's soup from childhood. My fries were also not hot, though we did have both items promptly replaced with a hotter version. The final issue that left us sour was that with the second round of flights, they were out of the normal glassware to do them. The bartender's solution was to use shot glasses, netting us a serving that was half size. This was called out, and we did get an extra pint, but I am not sure why free glassware from Sam Adams is in such short supply in a beer based gastropub, especially when the flight glasses are free from a Sam Adams rep. The entire experience reaffirmed that the only way to do The Yard is drinks only, and only at the bar rail. You can at least get your beer on time then, other than that, it can sit at service bar for several minutes while the staff is nowhere to be found. That's the shame of it all, the place has so much potential. They just don't care to try.

Let me begin with a quote taken straight from the Caesar's Qua Baths and Spa official website: Playing off its water motif, cooling blue tones, slate and stone set the stage for this all-new amenity. "The Roman name of Caesarea in Hebrew translates to 'Sea of Blue' and was one of many names attributed to the Mediterranean coastline." To that end, on the southern side you'll find a unique pool made entirely out of aquamarine stones while on the northern side is a more traditional saltwater pool just like the ones found at your average resort or even the Las Vegas pools. Each has two distinct areas within it - one based around a spa experience (including three tubs) and another geared towards outdoor activities such as swimming, relaxing by watching videos, playing pool games etc... We recommend booking both so enjoy all five different temperatures throughout the day! The restaurant also serves some excellent food here too. Caesar's included 50 worth of gift cards when we checked in but they are still available through their site if you'd rather contribute cash instead. They have other great deals going on there including 50 percent off spa treatments during December 18-21, 25 percent off spa services starting Dec 22 through Jan 1, a 20 percent discount on winter packages (includes use of comfortable robes slippers), 25 - 35 percent discounts on various items inside the hotel and dining, an exclusive offer where guests can book rooms up until 9 pm, free Wi-Fi and lots of staff happy to help make sure you get everything you needwant before heading home after your stay. You don't want miss these opportunities especially since each room comes with access to the Xanadu Club. This includes daily breakfast buffet in addition to unlimited drinks and snacks 24 hours per day; complimentary parking (one hour stays only); discounted car service between 6 am - 10pm Monday thru Saturday plus 30 minutes upon checkout Sunday; entry into grand prize raffles held every month which include a trip to New York City among others; early check inlate checkout privileges, additional perks depending on package chosen, etc... All in all, very nice place to call home over Christmas festivities. If I could give them 100 stars I would in fact do exactly that because I've stayed here several times and plan to return again soon.

Reserved the room for our honeymoon from Sunday to Friday two months in advance. I called to confirm the reservation the day of arrival and requested a bottle of champagne Drove for over an hour only to find the check-in desk closed. Then had to go back to the front desk to get another check-in key. Then had to pay for 2 nights even though we only reserved 1. Then had to pay for a third night even though we only stayed one. Then had to wait over an hour for a manager to come and check our room. They said there was nothing they could do because the desk was closed. Wife and I had dinner on sat, April 30. I ordered the organic chicken with shrooms. This is a signature dish and she ordered the beef short rib dinner with mushrooms. The two dishes were served together and we mixed them up when eating. I had no idea what was in my food until after it started to hit me. Since this is an expensive restaurant I usually ask for special instructions if they have something that can't be cooked. She said she did not remember asking because of her drugged state. When asked about allergies she told us "no" but since nothing else was mentioned I guess it all went into one big pot. That night was filled with more than expected vomiting and diarrhea every hour or so. We called emergency services who came out within minutes (the only service we received). The police officer explained our rights when dealing with such an event as well as how he could write a report should his boss request any information from the scene. He then left saying that everything will work itself out now that proper documentation has taken place. My wife's nausea continued even though she drank 3 glasses of water and took some anti-nausea medication before returning home. The next day my wife woke with very bad stomach aches thinking perhaps it might just be the flu - wrong! Her doctor prescribed her some medicine which made things worse. Then dr office sent her down the street to another agency that takes care of injuries etc.... later that same afternoon seeking help because her anxiety level was through the roof. Now we are waiting around for blood tests to come back over a month later... Our personal experience at Gramercy Tavern: If you're sick avoid going anywhere near there!

Sat down this am. Waited almost 20 minutes. No one ever came to our table. We asked for service 3 times. Still no one. Very poor management. Won't go back.

First visit back on May 10, 2012. Food looks promising when there's a huge slab of pork rotating on a vertical spit, with a pineapple above it (to tenderize the meat). It's almost as beautiful as one of the girls working the pole down at Sapphire, but I digress. 2 a taco made me grimace a little, but a smile broke out after I devoured that spicy pork, with its creamy sauce.... what was it, pineapple based? Idk, but I'm coming back. The guy working the spit was surprisingly welcoming, and patiently answered my noob questions what's the vampiro? the'vam-pee-roh, he corrected) despite the line forming behind me. There's ac inside, so you can escape the Vegas heat. But if you enjoy the desert climate, then you can also sit on the covered patio. The asada tacos were pretty good too; the chorizo decent. Give this place a shot if you're staying on the strip, it's on the right hand side as you drive down Las Vegas Blvd, right around the time you hit Circus Circus. Tip: learn the side streets (i.e. Paradise Rd), and avoid the terrible traffic.

I visited the ECE last Saturday for a Bolli Burlesque Show. The Venue was easy to locate, with a taxi. A Lothian Bus 35 goes here too, but that will take you all around the city. On arrival the entrance was clearly signposted and we decided to go have a little drink in The Pub. Which is part of the venue. On arrival we were advised that the tables with numbers were reserved. Luckily we found a table for 4 unreserved right in the reserved section. This gave us a great view of the stage. It is indeed a big hall, but with some clever (black) lighting it felt cosy enough. There was only one bar in the main hall, which required 3 deep queueing, but the staff was efficient and not too flustered. They were fine refilling the water jugs that were present on every table. So this review is from an OLD visit. I'd been meaning to write this and am just now getting around to it. Better late than never right? So, I've been a diehard Germany soccer fan for a few years now. I was really excited this World Cup and had already watched 2 games at the Hofbrauhaus which cost me more than I'd like to talk about. Let's just say I have no qualms with drinking at 8am. SO on a whim I decided to check out if there were any other German joints that were: 1. Closer to me and 2. More affordable. Lo and behold this place popped up on my search a WEEK after they opened! Talk about fate! I call them asking if they'll be showing the game that morning, to which I was told, If you're here for the game, our door will be open! So next morning I show up, decked out in my jersey and facepaint, and they let me in before operating hours to watch the game (Germany vs. France, we won of course) and serve me and my boyfriend beer. Talk about service! And getting to smell all the wonderful smells from the kitchen as they were preparing for the day made the day even better! Not to mention the food is SO GOOD. German cuisine, in my opinion at least, is the ULTIMATE COMFORT FOOD. The potato salad (Kartoffelsalat) is a different variation of what I'm used to making or getting, but YUM! I wanted spaetzle, but the machine was broken that day, thankfully I was not disappointed with the salad at all. Topping off the whole experience is the expertly made from scratch Apfelstrudel. DO NOT HESITATE TO ORDER THIS! It is just like my Tante used to make, SEHR LECKER! I'll definitely be back here not only to enjoy the wonderfully authentic food, but to support the lovely people who accommodated a wild soccer fan on the day of the World Cup Quarterfinals. I appreciated the hospitality more than you know!:]

I keep waffling between 2 and 3 stars2.5 is appropriate. Banfield is to pets what Nextcare is to people. They're available when you can't get into your regular healthcare doc , but they'll charge you for it anyway (and then some). Banfields one thing that really bothers me about them: they insist on charging for their exam. It's not something I'm willing to pay for, so I try to avoid going there unless absolutely necessary. Banfield doesn't have many branches in the Orlando area, but the ones that do tend to be a bit hokey looking (i.e., very unprofessional-looking dogs with poofy hair and other things). There are better options out there if you want to spend time with an actual dog of any kind. The service was okay, and we had our first meet up today at a local park! We did have a few issues with barking, which may or may not have been related to the fact that everyone else around us seemed pretty stressed out over horses running through the parking lot...it was more like a combination of both, though. The owners were actually quite nice, and kept trying to correct my mistake by saying "no!" until I told her I didn't mean no. So she got really aggressive about telling me I could bring the puppy again if I wanted probably because she thought I would refuse considering how close together we sat. But since I said no and she wasn't being rude or anything, perhaps I don't need to explain myself every single time? Regardless, it was clear she understood why I'd chosen this option. Overall, I wouldn't recommend a Banfield meeting with anyone who isn't a complete idiot;)

In hopes that TGI's would bring a little more to the table then what Sam's Town puts out...wishful thinking. I would much rather head out to the food-court, order a full meal at Sam's and get some homestyle cooking from Johnny for my husband. I was on vacation in NYC last month! We went all around Bronx to find these places we could eat great at cheap prices (there are like 6-7 of them) but unfortunately they don't have any of your favorites: (We had lunch there one day and were very disappointed not only because it wasn't really up to par with the rest of TGI Fridays I've been frequenting since opening here ten years ago, but also because they didn't seem able to make an effort regarding gluten-free diets - everyone is served breads made without wheat flour, rice or oats. What good did that do us?
Service was below mediocre for this caliber of restaurant. We were sat right next to a party, and ordered exactly the same time, but waited about 30 minutes past their restaurant was empty.

Yum, this is my favorite breakfast place on the Strip. While the prices are high, the food is worthy of the price and leaves me longing for more. I love that they serve home-style Southern favorites like biscuits with honey butter every morning from 6 a.m.-2 p.m., as well as traditional breakfast items such as pancakes and omelets including several specials daily. The restaurant has seating inside along with outside tables under umbrellas in case it's raining or too cold to go without an overcoat - which happened when we visited during winter break 2020 while visiting Las Vegas at Christmas time! Even though there was no one else dining near us, service still felt warm and friendly. We did not get waitstaff refills on our drinks but were able to order additional ones ourselves once seated nearby so that wasn't much of an issue. The server also brought out fresh baked blueberry muffins (with cream cheese frosting!) right after placing our orders before she left to clear up some other guests' plates. Overall, great experience!

Beautiful dining room hidden in Old Town Scottsdale. We made a reservation and scored an outdoor table on a lovely May evening. It was the perfect night to sit outside Great patio area and a nice place to eat after work.
Came here for my birthday! Loved the food and the wine pairings.

We got here before opening (they open an hour after the preserve opens) and were completely ignored by several people who walked past us. Wolfgang, here's some helpful tips to make sure you're seen at the preserves when they do open again. Dinner: So we went out for a meal before heading back on our hike, with the understanding that it would be a couple of hours return trip between food stops. The restaurant was nice but closed early since this was a "special event." We couldn't get reservations anywhere else so we just had a dinner at home which turned out good though not very long lasting. It is hard for me to remember where I ate because my brain hasn't been working like normal in about 3 months now....anyways...we took the cusotm down to the bottom of the ravine the next day and started up the trail around 10am. You will see the lake below and decide if there are any good trails ahead or how bad your night is going to be. After that you have to keep following the path right under the water until you hit the first large intersectiontrail head about 11ish. This is where the main trail cuts through the woods and then goes into what looks like an abandoned mine shaft of sorts. There is no sign, not even lights and nothing really around except some sticks sticking up from underneath the ground. In order to find the trail, use your compass and follow the way blue arrow pointing left toward the water. It should appear as if you've come off the road and onto a hiking trail given the direction of the blue line. Once upon a time there used to be a small town on top of the mountain called Pine Grove Falls where the path crosses over this town and eventually turns and follows what appears to be a logging route. Eventually you'll begin to cross a creek about 12 mile away from the starting point of the trail only 2 miles form the start. The trail is pretty well kept and I found it easy enough to follow once more after a few minutes. But beware! Just before you enter the canyon and go straight up to the end and you'll need to walk all the way across the creek (which may seem scary thanks to the narrow streambed). Do yourself a favor and bring your own lunch or go buy something along the way and eat it while the hikers are busy taking pictures. At the top of the canyon the path begins another big section of forest which continues until you reach the mouth of the canyon itself which lies about halfway in the canyon. Look around and see if you can spot any evidence of human activity such as cabin walls or other buildings. If you hear anything that sounds like someone building a cabin, turn around immediately (there's a bunch of rocks spread throughout the gorge that lead to the entrance in case anyone comes looking for a place to build a shack). Past this area, if there is a trail heading towards you, take it. If there isn't one, look for signs directing you away from the trailhead. The entire stretch leading to the canyon has a lot of forest and lots of smaller streams flowing into it. Be careful! Also don't forget to bring the tent and sleeping bag since there aren't really any shelters along this portion of the trail (I guess you could camp nearby but I wouldn't recommend it considering the lack of shade and the fact you might get wet or freeze instantly!). Take care! We didn't, unfortunately. About 6-8 feet below the end of the canyon, the path suddenly ends. Here a man dropped dead from exposure shortly thereafter. He was carrying a pack (a real heavy duty one apparently!!!) filled with his personal effects which included money, a cell phone, etc. His body was found near a fallen tree stump. The path proceeds without much fanfare through what seems to be pristine wilderness until it reaches a fork. Either continue or head south. I chose the north side as it led directly to Lake Michigan. On the opposite shore (not pictured), there is a bridge just above the dam that leads directly into the reservoir. Don't know why but I'm told this location provides better views than either side - steeper drop-off too?? Anyway, just past the fork, the trail heads upwards again and soon runs parallel to the railroad tracks. Here you'll notice some interesting formations of rock formation and possibly some sort of cave system. When we arrived, it had already rained the previous day so the weather wasn't great. Some locals said the rain must have made them think this was a perfect opportunity for us to explore so we decided to give it a shot anyway. As you go further upstream, names of caves become fewer and fewer. If you happen to see a cave system, visit regardless! By now, it is getting dark and once again you'll want to stay close to the railroad track for safety reasons (you might also feel tempted to run away from this part due to the difficulty of travel). Before descending, you may encounter a rope swing or two. Like the rest of the hiker things. Over crowed with tables as large as basketball courts. I could never hear the server or the person across the table speaking.

I am a huge fan of the Chipotle brand and food. This negative review is for the service I received this afternoon at this location. Earliest pickup time available when we submitted our online order was 1:15pm. We arrived 15 minutes early, was told that our order was not ready and would be about 10 minutes. We tried to pay when there wasn't a line of customers and were told that we could not pay until our order was fulfilled. The girl in charge of the pickup orders came out and told us it would be another 10 minutes. She came out with our order at 1:15pm on the dot, and told us in an exasperated tone to call next time if we would be arriving early. Her attitude was terrible, as if we were a HUGE inconvenience and had rushed her (which, obviously, we hadn't since our order came out right on time...). A simple, Sorry for the wait, I was backed up on other orders and couldn't get this out earlier for you would've sufficed. What's even BETTER is that when we mentioned pick-up-girl's attitude, the manager followed up with the same answer, next time call ahead if you'll be arriving early without so much as a hint of apology. Clearly WE were in the wrong here. It was definitely a missed opportunity on the manager's part to turn the situation around and save our experience from being so disappointing. Coming from a background in retail and fast food, I was baffled by their self-righteous, unapologetic attitudes. I also didn't understand why 1. the manager was working in the fulfillment line the whole time and 2. there were periods of time when there were no customers to help - whey didn't someone (like, ahem, the manager) go and help the girl filling pickup orders? I've never had a bad experience at Chipotle before today, and will definitely never come back to this location.

We have shopped and bought tires at various Discount Tires over the years, including this one. The service is great and they are more than willing to work with you on price, if necessary. We would not hesitate to recommend this location. I have purchased tires at this location before. They were very easy to work with. I recently brought my car in for an alignment. I had scheduled an appointment for a 3 pm and was told I could be there at 2. When I arrived at 2, I was helped right away. They had me back out the door by 2:40. They are very efficient. I was very pleased with the service. They were great! They were on time, friendly, and professional.

Great discounted price! They have a wide selection of Ray-Bans. I wished they had more DG's though and a separate section for men. Sheryl was very patient with me. She knew the style I wanted, the moment I described to her the look I was going for. Got my new glasses in 1.5 hours.

I have been to The Ultimate several times for massages with Ellen and would highly recommend her. She is very personable, friendly and professional. I feel extremely relaxed after our sessions. I also used Ellen for a prenatal massage when pregnant. Being as big and uncomfortable as I was, I was worried if I would be able to relax fully. Ellen has blankets and pillows just for that reason! Super comfortable and she remembers to ask about the baby after she was born. Highly recommend! The only reason I did not give 5 stars was that the hallway outside the room can get a bit loud if people are walking down, talking or laughing. They should maybe make that more of a quiet space with notices that people are in session. Nothing Ellen could help though!

I've only seen two movies at this theater and maybe it's because the theaters where I live are just small but these theaters were huge! there were so many rows in the theater I was in. when you walk to the elevators for the rooms they have a display of which movies are playing and their times during the day so you don't have to walk all the way to the theater. Which was pretty convenient. Tickets didn't seem that pricy to me, it was only a few cents more than what I'm used to so nothing new. Th workers at the concession stand were nice but kind of slow at getting the food but nothing to get annoyed at really. only bad thing was when I was watching a movie, the guy, who just happened to sit right behind me with all of the other empty seats, started to fall asleep and snore. I was more entertained than annoyed but I'm not taking a star away because of that.

So sad I wanted to love this place but the fact they have no kids menu and I was charged 14 pls 5 for juice for my 5 yo makes it difficult to ever return. The server was no help, slow to serve, never refilled my coffee and was put out when I asked to sub cantaloupe for the bananas....

This is probably my favorite barlounge on the strip. It never gets too packed here, there are plenty of tables and seating in the lounge area, and best of all is the amazing view from anywhere inside Mix including in the restrooms! I've been here a few times and almost always try to bring visiting friends and family here, or at least recommend that they check it out. I haven't tried their restaurant, but heard they have a daily happy hour. Sometimes the line for the elevator can get a little long here but I've never had to pay cover just to go up. Drinks are standard strip pricing so expect to pay about 8-9 bucks for a beer. Bar service is top notch though and even when there's a crowd there I can get in and out with my drinks pretty quickly. There are booths for bottle service both inside and on the balcony. Mix also has a small dance floor in front of the elevators, but this is mostly a lounge atmosphere so no one is ever really dancing! This is a classy joint but dress code isn't enforced too stricly as I've seen people walking around in shorts andor t-shirts...

I have been to this place twice now and although there were some items that I was not a fan of...overall the food and service has been great! The place is small and cozy and the owners are very involved with every aspect of the restaurant. You can tell that the owners are passionate about what they do and you can tell that care about your business. Yummy items that I have tried and loved are: Hummus: Even if this was not homemade (as indicated in a previous post) I do not care...it was sooo good. The house soup..can't remember the name??? It is like a greek version of chicken soup. It is light and delicious and I absolutely love it!! Baked Ravioli in Alfredo sauce: I have had this twice and I will be getting it again and again...it was so gooey and flavorful. Steak and Lobster: This was a special on Valentines Day and both were cooked to perfection and needed nothing added to it whatsoever. This came with steamed veggies and red potatoes...also cooked perfectly. Flaming Baklava: This I have had twice also...it is baklava in all it's glory with scoop of vanilla ice cream and drizzled with orange liquer which the light on fire when they bring to your table. Not so yummy: (Grape leaves: These were OK..I have had worse at My Big Fat Greek Restaurant...my main complaint with these was there was too much leaf and too much raw garlic. Spanakopita (Spinach Pie): This looked delicious and had fresh spinach...but no flavor whatsoever...NONE Meatballs: Again too much raw garlic. All in all the good stuff that we have had and the great service we have received will keep me coming back to this place

I was extremely disappointed when ordering pizza from this place. The girl that rang up our order said it would be 20-25 minutes for our pizza and garlic knots to get out of the oven, but they never came. I'm in a hurry so we ordered another pizza and waited even longer...The pizzas took forever and we just gave up on them after waiting an hour or more. What a waste.

Black jeans, grey shirt, black tie and black Chucks. Sounds like something out of every hip GQ man's closet, my closet. As cool as I dress, sorry to disappoint, that isn't me in the picture above. This is a pic from the Brooklyn Fashion Show, spring 2010. This look is more my thing: cargo pants and a t-shirt with some sneakers. I did go to the show, the music was fun and some of the models were very beautiful, but the clothes were really not my thing. I know I am not the target audience. They had some cute stuff, but for me the clothes are a little too baggy. I love the look of a little bit of edge and tough, but these clothes don't quite do it for me. I know the show's aim is to showcase the clothes of up and coming designers, and some of them are very cool, but I think their designs could do better if they toned them down a little. For me, the clothes just don't have the edge I want. The other thing I noticed is that the clothes seem to have a mish-mash of ideas. A little bit of this and a little bit of that. I guess when you are young and breaking into the industry, you need to do what you can. I think some of these designers are on the right track, they just need to get a better idea of what they want to do. One of the designers I liked was Deanna Bannister. She had some very cool stuff, but she was the exception rather than the rule. I am not a fashion expert, but I know what I like.
We had a group and a back room was opened so we could all eat together in our own room! The staff is really friendly and so helpful! Love this place! Loved the burger! Can't wait to try more!!

I would give zero stars if I could. Janey T. completely agrees with me. Lawsuits? The owner told me, I ALWAYS win. Hmmm, sounds as if I'm not the only unhappy customer. Do NOT hire these people. Extremely unprofessional and, in my opinion, psycho!

This popular downtown eats has been on my recent bookmarks to try. Arepas...a South American sandwich made of corn flatbread and various fillings. Located in the popular area of other Yelpdom heavy hitters like Art of Flavors and Goodwich, I figured Viva Las Arepas would be a no-brainer favorite. The restaurant inside is clean and warm, with more seating than parking available. If you haven't been, parking in the front is nearly non - existent. We ordered the Reina Pepiada, which is a featured review item and wood fired chicken arepas, plus an order of Yucca fries. In seeing the photos of the Reina Pepiada, I expected the sauce to be a light, creamy cilantro avocado type of dressing. What I actually experienced was very heavy and overly sauced chicken. With each bite, I kept thinking how the addition of a nice fresh slaw could cut some of that richness. The tortas were also heavy and chewy and again my expectations of a light, fluffy flatbread were dashed. I did like the peas, though. They provided additional sauces, which was unnecessary considering the meat was already drowning in it. The yucca fries were nothing special. My daugter seemed to enjoy her wood fired chicken arepa. The Reina Pepiada didn't sit well with my wife as she was sick the rest of the night. Viva Las Arepas fell short of what I wanted to experience. I so wanted to love this place, but didn't. I will continue to search to hopefully find my ideal arepa.

This place looks like it needs to be updated to be comparable to other standards hotels have now. However, they play host to The Price Is Right Live and that is a plus. The area the theater in is not the best place for a long line for future contestants to wrap around, and I feel they should adapt to that or figure a way to rope things around.

I spent 34.00 for pick up..two lunches. I paid extra for a dinner size of rice beans. What I got were portions for an infant. This is not the first time and won't be my last time going to this place. They are good about slowly giving away what you ordered, but that's only if it was really bad. Find me another place like that in your area!

I love this place..something for everyone. For Garlic Lovers - the garlic dip will NOT disappoint. You will ward off all vamps guaranteed. Philly cheesesteakchicken lovers...unforgettable. Lemon chicken salad amazing (HUGE grilled chicken strips), tuna pizza..odd maybe..but delicious all the same. Need I go on?.the only thing I didn't care for was the veggie burger oddly enough. For an exceptional veggie burger I would steer you towards Four Peaks Brewery. But other than that they are spot on everytime all the time. Can't go wrong!

The cheese dosai is essentially India's vegetarian Philly cheesesteak. This alone makes the trip worthwhile, but is not the end. The curries are also excellent and flavorful. The lentil doughnuts are a great appetizer; light and puffy. The only con is that one is inclined to overdo oneself at the buffet, which isn't even really that much of a con.

I love Cheesecake Factory and I love to order their avocado eggrolls, yummy. I have no complaints about this restaurant except that I think their cheesecake is just a tad too sweet for my taste. Overall, it's a great restaurant with a diverse menu and I'm always satisfied with my meal choices.

I haven't been to a Red Robin since living in Anchorage. That was over twenty years ago; I was rather young. While I didn't remember the flavors, I did remember it being greasy and even more salty than McDonald's (and that is saying something).

Nice place with an eclectic style inside. I had Sushi, the specialty rolls were amazing with a great presentation. Fabulous! This place is high priced! I would not recommend this place for anyone who is looking for something more affordable. The sushi ranges from 20 for a roll of 6 pieces to 110 although the specialty rolls are yummy 85 for one roll is outrageous! If you have the money to spend then I recommend this place. I could definitely see myself going back to try the teppanyaki grills.

I must say.... I was really looking forward to having dinner here. We were on a quick weekend get away in Scottsdale for my 32nd birthday, and I booked this They are open for dinner from 5pm until 8:30, with a 2 hour time limit on dining there. They also have a lounge area that is open for drinks and snacks, as well as an outdoor patio. The food is what you would expect from the Four Seasons Scottsdale. It is not cheap, but I was really surprised at how great it was. The pastry chef was amazing. He was really creative with his creations and used many flavors in his desserts. I ate here twice, and I can honestly say that I have never had better French onion soup. We had the French onion soup and escargot appetizer. The escargot is served with a light sauce that is just right, and still a bit crunchy. The soup is the best onion soup I've ever had. It was so flavorful. They also have one of the best salads I've had in a long time. You get 6 huge pieces of beautiful greens, and the chef creates the perfect salad dressing for it. Those were both really good, and the entree dishes were also well prepared. My husband and I ate at Lucques twice, and unfortunately we were there for dinner only on our last night. The first time we went, we ate at the restaurant, and the second time we ate at the lounge. This was much better in my opinion. The servers are very attentive, and the steaks were cooked perfectly.

Overpriced and not Authentic or even very good food, mediocre at best service and the owner spews his right-wing politics. I should have just ordered Domino's and watched Fox News. Total waist of a night out.

Unfortunately, no one stopped to help us; the bartender stood on the opposite end of the bar, talking to folks. Waitresses zipped past us without a word. We went upstairs to check on things ourselves and it still wasn't clear if we could just grab a table. So it was back downstairs where we flagged down a manager who told us we could seat ourselves. Let me tell you a story about a casino being rebuilt and re-branded. They closed down, let everyone know that they were coming back better than ever next year, and then used the downtime to build a new, much nicer casino. The old one was pretty dingy and run-down, so everyone was very excited for the new one. A few months before they were set to reopen, the casino sent out a survey to all of their past customers. They asked them what they wanted to see in the new casino, and how much they would be willing to pay for it. The results were clear: people wanted a nicer, cleaner casino with better amenities and they were willing to pay more for it. With that information in hand, the casino went ahead and built an even nicer casino than they had originally planned. They reopened to much fanfare and excitement, and people were thrilled with the new place. It quickly became one of the most popular casinos in the area. The moral of the story is that if you want to succeed in business, you need to listen to your customers. They will tell you what they want, and if you give it to them, they will reward you with their business.

For 24 heirloom tomatoes salad, 21 a plate for buffalo mozzarela and 14 a plate for beet salad, I would expect all these dishes to be amazing, but in the end, they were just dressed up salads. Pasta Course: We order six diff pastas to share. We had to have refills on two of them because it was THAT GOOD - 1) beef cheek ravioli with black truffles and crushed duck liver and 2) Bolognese pappardelle. I LOVE pasta and I am extremely picky when it comes to pasta (maybe it's the Asian in me...from the school of Marco Polo brought pasta back to western world from China...LOL) I must say, these two dishes were flavorful, unique and what a delight to taste something like the bolognese kicked up 100 notches at BB. The wild boar ragu was alright, did not wow me. The clam linguine was poor at best - TOO spicy, nothing special, and not flavorful aside from the dramatic heat - it was disappointing. Entrees: We each ordered an entree and pretty much everyone ordered something different. I was honored to eat off of everyone's plate. I ordered the rabbit. The Rabbit was AMAZING. It was done a few different ways - braised, confit, deep fried leg, and pan seared. It was flavorful, tender, juicy, and well seasoned. It had a wonderful balance of flavors - gentle but with a punch. (my second choice for entree would have been the sweetbreads) BBQ skirt steak - it was just ok. It wasn't excellent, it wasn't bad, it was just middle of the road. Not my favorite cut to begin with, but most of all, it seemed to have been marinated with a lot of salt...too salty for me. Whole grilled Branzino was quite good. The fish is very mild and the dish was well seasoned overall. I love whole fish (once again the Asian in me) - makes the meat so much more juicy. Grilled rib eye was shared between two sisters. I liked the rib eye a lot albeit I only had two little bites. I mean, it's hard to go wrong with a rib eye, but hey, you'd be surprised... Dessert: ordered several to share with everyone at the table. Nothing totally memorable. The small bites biscuitcookies they brought out with our coffee were even better than the desserts we ordered (very similar experience at Del Posto...) I love Mr. Batali and have so much respect for him. I love the two pasta dishes mentioned above and the rabbit and branzino were truly delightful. I will definitely come back, throw money at this place and try the tasting menu next time I am in town...

I've been here twice. The service is great; the margaritas are great; the food sucks. Both times my meals tasted like an old shoe. I'm not sure how they get that exact flavor in the food on two separate occasions but it is not good. Two strikes you're out.
The sangria here is awful. I think it was a tequila sunrise. The food is greasy and not in a good way. The only thing good was the goat cheese. But it is goat cheese. How can you mess that up?

If you're a half-decent looking girl who likes going WOOOO' while dancing in your seat whenever you hear a song you like..... or if you're a guy who's attracted to those kinda girls.... you'll LOVE this place. As for the food. Had the 180 Wagyu rib-eye and the girl had the 195 Wagyu NY Strip. It was aight. Their french fries are pretty delish though. Thumbs up for me.

Recently celebrated my anniversary at Chima's. We wanted a bread from the norm and Chima's did not disappoint. The service was top notch! All the cuts of meat were excellently prepared and tasted fabulous. The buffet was very well appointed and included some of our favorites like Beef Carpaccio and excellent Black Beans and Rice. Only criticisms would be that the venue is quite loud and hectic...so if your looking for a quite dinner for two this may not be the best pick, but I could see how it would be an excellent vibe an energy for dinner with friends.

I love this club, best club in Vegas by far! We got a table for my friend's birthday party. The waitresses came out with the bottles, lights, happy birthday sign, and confetti. So.... although I was celebrating my 25th in Vegas..... and it was my first time- I have to say that I had a great time and I didn't stay on the strip. No, instead we went to downtown Las Vegas (just across from McCarran Airport) where we stayed at The Westin. It is one of those "newer" hotels - with all glass walls, lots of natural lightskyline...etc. We arrived Friday night about 6:30 p.m., checked into our room and just got settled down for dinner. After dinner, DH Mom came over and met us there. They were able to get off their plane around 7:00 or so; but by 8:00 we decided they needed some rest after being up since 4 AM! And so, after hanging out for another hour or two before heading back to the hotel we called them up and said goodnight and continued on our own way home. Saturday morning we woke up late again, ate breakfast, headed outside for viewings - which ended up not really working out as planned. But once we learned what we wanted to see, we made plans for Sunday afternoon. So this time we did go straight to Strip. This was nothing major as far as planning..and yet...there are still things you can do, such as check out the Fremont Street Experience (which has been going through improvements for months now), catch an evening show (we saw Rock Of Ages!!!), etc. Oh well...anyway, we bought tickets 1st thing Saturday morning when we discovered how much longer it would take us to drive (about 2 hours each direction). Then we took advantage of free walking tours offered by the city tourism office because we needed something different than sitting in traffic and looking at buildings while lost in thought trying to decide what to buydo next. There's also always shopping opportunities too if that works better for your agenda or budget situation. In any event, we're glad we found these options because I'm sure none of us will forget feeling like crazy tourists for awhile!! Anyhow.After touring the city, taking pictures and buying souvenirs, we finally left the airport area and drove north towards Lake Tahoewhere it was snowing very lightly but no big deal. As usual, Nevada weather is unpredictable! LOL Also, use caution driving here during snow storms due to suddenly changing conditions...I've seen people skid off roadways before. Again, never know what kind of road condition might be encountered thus donning your safety goggles, wearing warm clothes (but NOT one layer too many layers!), gloves, hats, scarfs, etc. Have fun folks!!:) Now if only I could find more snow photos of me skiing...I should post most of mine from last winter then as well!: (Anywho...enjoyed visiting NA this past weekit is truly beautiful country. Thanks in advance for stopping by and checking out my little blog: Friday, January 13, 2011 This story begins long ago..as early as 1931. My grandparents lived in Fort Worth, Texas. Grandma worked 12 hours per day, 6 days a week. She raised 3 kids and put everything she earned into savings, even though she couldn't afford college tuition for her daughter, who was 5 years old at the time. Nevertheless, Mama saved EVERY penny she possibly could save. One year, her husband died unexpectedly leaving her with 1 million dollars worth of insurance money. However, he owned his business outright so she was forced to sell it. By doing so, she sold property that was owned jointly between herself and her neighbor. Although Mama believed she'd gotten fair market value, her neighbor disagreed and later sued her claiming that indeed it wasn't actually market price. Although it seemed impossible for someone like him to win against someone like my talented grandma, somehow he won anyway and my poor grandmom was destroyed financially. Even though she eventually recovered financially, it broke her heart deeply knowing losing her entire life work, plus all the hard work she put into saving up her earnings. Needless to say, the whole family felt sad for her loss. Fast forward several decades later 7 Dec 2010. A friend asked me why I am blogging daily? Seriously?! Does anyone else feel totally overwhelmed sometimes by having to keep track of every aspect of everyday life?? Well, maybe not everyone feels this way, but certainly others like myself ARE struggling daily with managing multiple responsibilities that seem endless and overwhelming. So, hopefully, my writing helps slow things down just enough so I'll remember to breathe live life to its fullest and enjoy the journey rather than rush headlong through it. Rest assured - there isn't anything I haven't thought of to write about already!;) If it weren't for God's grace living within me and sustaining me throughout this new season of life, I doubt I'd survive half the trials I expect to face in the coming weeks and months. LOVE the beer selection!!! If you're looking for a great pub to have a few drinks and watch some sports, this is it!!! Amazing tap and bottle selection from micro breweries all over the country and world!!! I'm a complete beer snob, and was really impressed.... Found some options that I've had trouble tracking down just about anywhere else. Quite impressed... That being said, the service and food were flat out awful. Our server was completely lost the entire time. Brought us the wrong drinks, never brought us the waters we requested, came out with the wrong food and took forever to replace it, didn't know the menu and seemed completely lost.... I would have imagined that a college kid on their first night would be more attentive and knowledgeable.... To be fair, they were busy when we were there, but still, I would expect a lot more. Food was terrible.... Fried pickles looked like they had taken one of those economy jars of sliced pickle chips, dipped them in batter and fried them (NOT fried pickle spears). They were terrible and tasted like they had been made in a walmart parking lot.... Wing appetizers I ordered were decent, but only because there was so much sauce it covered up the burnt taste of the overcooked wings.... Wings were tough and tasteless (with the exception of the sauce, which was actually quite good). We also ordered nachos which were pretty lousy, and a salad that came out with the piece of meat completely cold and uncooked in the middle. All in all, unless you're planning on saddling up to the bar for a few drinks, I'd stay away.... There's a mellow mushroom (i know, it's a chain, but much safer in this case) right across the street that has a similar drink menu, and significantly better food and service!!!

I thought this place was awesome, especially for the room rates that my friend and I paid. Super budget-friendly, with plenty of amenities that were unexpected but totally a nice surprise. I had only expected the very basics, like a simple bed and the bathroom area. We also had an in-room refrigerator, even a stove top we could have used to cook if we wanted, and microwave. The room was pretty spacious! The hotel staff were helpful and nice. I like that the hotel was pretty quiet. The look of this Red Roof Inn and the landscaping also made me feel like I had just entered the suburbs, somewhere on the East Coast. It totally feels like home!

I've had cupcakes from The Cupcakery countless times and I am always a happy camper. The shop is super cute and has a warm ambiance. They have several flavors but my absolute favorite is their best seller, the Southern Belle. (It also doesn't hurt that my name is in it!) It is their red velvet cupcake. It's heavenly! The cake is moist and the frosting is not too sweet. The cupcakes are a little pricey but standard for these fancy cupcake shops. Today I did take advantage of their Yesterday's Cupcakes special. For 14.75, you get nine assorted cupcakes. Great deal and they still taste fresh!

Dear Starbucks, By the time you read this review, I'll be gone. I've started seeing other coffee shops, and the last few times I've been to see you...things just aren't the same. Your staff used to greet me by name, and know my order...now I'm lucky if I get a polite greeting. I'm sorry to say that the quality of your drinks, while never a favorite of mine, has gone down hill quite a bit. I can't believe I paid 4.27 for a TALL latte, even if it was your new one, the Chestnut Praline Latte...which, by the way...is awful. It tasted burnt, and wasn't even hot when I received it. This is harder for me than it is for you. We've grown apart. I wish I could say Its not you, its me! but it is DEFINITELY you. Cordially, Lisa the non silly version: Service has slipped considerably. Prices are ridiculous for what you get, and the coffee is disgusting. I'll be travelling the additional 5 minutes to Grouchy Johns from now on.

I was underwhelmed with my experience at Matt's Big Breakfast, although I visited the place prompted by reviews from others. The location is cute and the place delivers wholesome foods, but it didn't match my expectations. I don't know if my expectations were too high, but it wasn't a memorable experience. My friend and I went for breakfast and I ordered a vegetarian plate with potatoes, toast, and eggs. The eggs were fine, but not remarkable. The potatoes were good, although nothing special. The toast was good, but not remarkable either. My friend ordered the house special with bacon, sausage, and eggs. He said it was good, but nothing to rave about either. The service was fine. The staff was friendly. The place was busy, but the service was quick. I think it's a popular place and I know it's a popular place with tourists and the local hipster crowd, but I wasn't particularly impressed with the food, nor the experience. It's a place to check out, but I wouldn't rave about it.

Love wine? This is the event for you. Rundown of what you need to know: -This is an event that IMO the VIP is not worth it. You don't really get all that much more. Some access to a VIP tent that has some cheese and samples of a few other wines. 25-26 for general admission is a great deal to enjoy a day of sips. -Bring chairs, blankets, etc and enjoy the day. This is a day long festival and Symphony Park is a great place to spend an afternoon. There's live music, food options for purchase and some different craft type tents to explore. -Parking is free. However, it's hard to find a spot if you don't get there early. The restaurants block off their parking areas and the mall is just busy in general. This is a drinking event. Take a cab or Uber. -I know it says you can bring kids, make it a family day and what not. However, people get super drunk. Wine drunk. Holy people watching drunk. -The crowds are not very good at the whole concept of making a line to get a sample after hours of consuming wine. You're going to get a little annoyed. Good thing you brought that blanket, right? -Seriously, drunk should be in 72 pt font here. I had a good time meeting all the different vineyards and vendors. I don't know a lot about wine. I buy based on what the label looks like. So, it was good to learn a little bit along the way. Just like Beer, Bourbon and BBQ (the same people put this on), I think this is a festival that gets a little bit better each year.

This Ross store always looks like a tornado hit it. Beside low stock there are always items all over the floor. I never see staff picking things up to rehang them. I would suggest going to another Ross location.

I tried this restaurant due to it's proximity to hiking in the Superstitions. We stopped by after a hike. The only positive that I have is that the place looks nice and has a nice patio with a waterfall. I ordered a green chili burro and my wife ordered beef tamales. Several minutes after I placed my order the waiter came back to tell me they were out of green chili. No biggie here but at a good restaurant I would expect the waiters to know if they were out of something this basic before the order went in. I changed my order to green corn tamales. When the waiter brought the order out he could not tell which plate had the beef tamales and which were green corn. He takes the plates away for about 5 minutes to figure it out. So we were teased with a preview of our meal only to be left hungry for 5 more minutes. When he brought the plates back we discovered that they were both beef tamales. I tasted one and it was hard, salty and not at all like any tamale I had ever had. He took my plate and re-order my tamales. It took too long for the re-order to come out. My wife was pretty much finished by the time I got my plate. She was disappointed in her meal but to starved to hold back from eating it. My green corn tamales were better than the beef tamales but not good. They smothered them with cheese and drenched the plate in a runny sauce. The rice tasted like rice and tomato sauce and the beans were just straight up nasty. I could not eat more than one bite. As starving as I was from the hike I could not come close to finishing the plate. I left still hungry. The waiter, although friendly, did not offer any amends to the lack of green chili or the tamale mix-up. I'll never go back to this place. Overall this was the worst restaurant experience I have had in a long time.

The hubby and I arrived on Friday and went to Pure later that night with another couple. We had a lot of fun! It was even better that we didn't have kids so we could really let loose, dance the night away and just enjoy each other's company. This morning (Saturday), we met up with some friends for breakfast at This Ain't Hollywood. The food is pretty good there but it isn't what makes this place unique - it's their decor: There are movie posters everywhere along with cool artwork from famous movies like "Ghostbusters" and "Back To The Future." If you get hungry after eating, they have a small selection of candy in the back as well. Afterwards, we stopped by the Farmers Market and then headed over towards the San Diego Zoo. Our first stop was the Giraffe Cam which has been running since 2006 and shows giraffes in their natural habitat and lets viewers watch them eat and interact when needed. Since our trip is only limited to one day, we decided not to pay the 12 admission fee this time around. Instead, we took advantage of an offer online to purchase a 3-month membership at no extra cost if purchased before January 31st...so now we're members and can go whenever we want without having to pay again in February. There were also lots of penguins to see too at Penguin Encounter which is free but requires preregistration. I think that next year we'll come here earlier and be able to properly take pictures with all these cute animals - plus, we won't feel guilty about going there because we did buy a membership!!! By the way, check out this little guy who seems rather happy being chased by his momma through the exhibit while filming for us...I thought it was quite funny how he kept looking at the camera and smiling everytime she ran past him. Makes me wish I knew sign language!!: But enough about those two things already;) After getting home at 4pm today, we decided to spend our last evening enjoying the city of San Diego by taking a jeep ride down the coast line. We started off driving across town to La Jolla Cove where we took a few walking tours of the area, including the lighthouse which was built in 1884 and used until 1952. Afterwards, I decided to go for a swim to warm myself up before heading into the cold ocean water. While swimming along the cliffs behind the beach, my feet slipped and I fell onto my stomach. Fun times!!! Despite numerous attempts to put my foot back in its proper position, it wouldn't budge, caught between rocks or sand. So I called for help and waited patiently for several minutes while the lifeguard came and looked at my leg. He examined it closely and told me that I should leave it alone and do something more constructive than standing still there....well, except for laying face-down on the ground and kicking my legs trying to figure out what I'm doing wrong with my foot. For the record, despite everything else going on during my entire stay in California, this incident was not included among them. On Saturday afternoon, the pain wasn't bad anymore so I continued on with the walk along the beach toward Santa Cruz bluffs...and that's where I got lost. Not kidding either! Somehow I wound up on a dirt road which led me to nowhere scenic or interesting. But there weren't many options available anyway so I made do with what there was: a full moon above and sky filled with stars below. Eventually we reached Point Loma Torrey Pines State Reserve, a beautiful 13 acre park right in the middle of the sand dunes with large cypress trees growing on top of the hill. Besides feeling blessed to be surrounded by such natural beauty, it felt incredible to stand where generations of people have gone before me and observe wildlife grazing freely on the hillsides. And don't worry, that's a picture of the edge of the cliff which might look scary but it actually gives great views of the surrounding area. To be fair, I'll separate this review into 2 parts: 1 about the food and 2 about the horrendous service. 1 FOOD: 35 stars 24 per person for the weekday (no seafood) dinner buffet - certainly a better price than the buffets on the strip. The food here was average. I was only able to find a handful of solid items that I could enjoy. Would I come back? Slight chance, but ONLY for the the sashimi salad and the few items I have listed below: - Salmon sashimi salad - This was the star of the entire dinner. The salmon was extremely buttery, sweet, moist, and fresh. I could just eat this all night and be happy. - American beef BBQ ribs - The ribs were meaty, not too dry, and the BBQ sauce was sweet and tangy. It satisfied my rib craving just fine. - Chinese style BBQ pork ribs - The Chinese BBQ sauce was sweet and not too salty. The ribs were moist, meaty, and didn't have too much fat, which made it enjoyable. - Kalbi (Korean BBQ beef ribs) - I enjoyed the flavorful and bold Korean sweet and salty marinade. Some of the meat was tender, but there were also many pieces that were charred to a crispy black. - The creme brulee was perfectly custardy. - The luscious flan had a beautiful smooth texture and not overly sweet. - I also enjoyed being able to order Americano and expresso from the dessert bar. They were both light (watery) and not robust, but they were packed with enough caffeine to fight off the food coma. The rest of the food and desserts offered at the buffet were either dried out, overcooked, bland, mushy, or tasted like dishwater. I was also really looking forward to the oysters and crab legs that I've seen in pictures, but alas I didn't see them being offered last night - Note: the seafood buffet is more expensive (40) and it's only offered Fri-Sat-Sun. 2 SERVICE: 05 stars The servers here are shockingly rude and ruined my experience at this buffet and my appetite. When we arrived, the ladies working the front registers advised us that their buffet line will be closing at 9 pm tonight and that's also when the food will stop being refreshed. It was about 7:50 pm, so that wasn't a problem to us - from our understanding, we wouldn't be able to grab anymore food after 9, but we would still be able to finish our meal even after the buffet line was closed. Well, that's typically the case at most buffets... Apparently that's not the case here. What ended up happening was, we grabbed our food, ate, and when 9 pm rolled up, our server abruptly came up to us and said, you have to leave now, we're closed. Her tone of voice was extremely coarse and unprofessional. Mind you, we still had a plate full of food in front of us and we were in the middle of eating (chewing) when she rudely addressed us. I had an obvious look of confusion written all over my face and she then quickly said, I'll give you up to 5 minutes, then you must leave Wow, who talks like that? I was in utter shock that our server was so extremely abrasive. We were just trying to enjoy the rest of our dinner and didn't know that they wanted us out of the restaurant by 9 pm - no one told us that! How does buffet line closes at 9 you must get out by 9?! We quickly tried to finish chewing so we can get the heck out of there and then another gentleman rushed up to us and yelled at us, just to let you know, you have less than 2 minutes to leave. seriously? You can't even approach us with kindness and professionalism? I was beyond infuriated at that point and also still so confused as to how the staff here carried themselves with such poor etiquette. With hindsight, I understand that it was major negligent miscommunication between the staff and my party, but even so, that's never an appropriate reason to mistreat your guests or speak to them like they are livestock. Also, to rub a pound of salt into our wounds - I didn't even know we could have unlimited beerwine during our buffet - none of the servers or staff informed us. I just ordered a coke and our waitress never even came back to refill it! My glass was empty 15 minutes into eating there and I had to get up and go look for her and ask her if I may get a refill. Of course she forgot to refill it, so I had to get another server to refill it for me. Finally, my server waltzes up with my refilled coke. It was an extremely annoying dinner to say the least.

Service was really good. I did have one time I had to ask for an ice tea refill but that was it. Service with a smile? Yep, got it here in abundance. Oh and one other little detail, the fork I was using had seen better days. But beyond that, I have nothing else I can gripe about. Overall, I liked this place. And I will be back. While Old School Pizzeria, Grimaldi's, and Settebello have their place, Mark Rich's NY Pizza is worth a look too.

There is serious separation anxiety when you have to leave your stylist, with whom you have established a bond, and maybe even spilled serious personal information to. Having moved from one place to another, it can be challenging to find a new stylist, but there are steps you can take to make the transition smoother: 1. Ask for Recommendations: Talk to friends or family members who live in your new area and ask for recommendations. They may know of a great stylist that they can refer you to. 2. Do Online Research: Use online resources such as Yelp or Google Reviews to find local salons and read customer reviews. This can give you a sense of the salon's atmosphere and the quality of service they provide. 3. Visit Salons: Make appointments at different salons to get a feel for the stylist's skills and personality. This will help you find someone you feel comfortable with. 4. Be Open: Be open to trying out a new look or style. Your new stylist may have different suggestions for your hair that you might fall in love with. 5. Communicate: Communication is key. Let your new stylist know about your hair history, any allergies, and what you are looking for in a new style. This ensures that they will be able to give you the best advice and results. Remember that finding a new stylist will take time, but with patience and persistence, you'll find the right stylist for you.

Who doesn't enjoy a lazy Sunday morning? I love spending time leisurely reading the Sunday news while getting caught up on a weeks worth of cooking shows. After a few hours hunger finally sets in and its time to find something cheap and easy. While that might sound more like a lifestyle choice than a way of eating, cheap and easy to me means dim sum, and lots of it. With a fistful of cash and my growing appetite I head over to my default dim sum house, Golden Buddha. Located in the Chinese Cultural Center, Golden Buddha has been pushing carts every weekend for the past few years. Over those years they've become a destination for steamy delights and have built quite a following with groups usually packing the lobby. Here's some advice, for a lesser selection with no waiting, go early. If you want more selection and don't mind the wait, go after noon. Ranging in price from 2.35-6.50, Golden Buddha pretty much offers mainstream selections from dumplings and chicken feet to rice and noodles. Most of the cart pushers don't speak much English but know this; most items are either made with pork or shrimp. Within minutes of being sat the first smiling server rolls up her cart and begins pimping her wares. As she lifts the steel lid from the first steam basket, the mist dissipates to reveal 3 white fluffy hidden treasures beneath. Know as char siu bao, or steamed BBQ pork buns, these are pretty standard for any dim sum brunch. Pulling apart one of the doughy pillows reveals its sweet porky center, add some chile oil for added depth. Probably the most typical offering is the pork dumplings or sui mai, a wonton wrapper filled with ground pork and black mushrooms. These meaty bites have an enjoyable earthiness that left me wanting to ask for another basket. The next cart to come along is absolutely filled with fried items. I love the crispy crunch of egg rolls and while the GB version was crisp, the inside was filled with oil that tasted like last nights fish. After only a single bite the rest remained untouched. Seemingly fried in the same oil, the salt and pepper shrimp were not only super fishy but the shells were also left on. Shell on shrimp isn't usually a problem when the shrimp in question is cooked really well. Not the case with these, they were ruined before they even hit the table, greasy and salty. On a lighter note, wrapped in translucent rice paper, the spring rolls were large, filled with chewy rice noodles and 3 plump shrimp, unfortunately these were also flavorless. A new one for me was the Zhaliang, a long tubular Chinese doughnut that is tightly cocooned in a sheet of rice noodle. The end result is more about texture than bold flavor; I can see how so many people seek these out for breakfast being chewy and crispy at the same time. Dim sum brunch isn't complete without at least one Chinese dessert. Pointing at a plate of pineapple buns or bo lo yau from the dessert cart, these pastries actually contain no pineapple. Instead the name refers to its crunchy checkered top crust. Inside the bun you'll get a sweet surprise of satisfyingly sweet custard filling. While I left satisfied, overall Golden Buddha doesn't quite have the chops they used to, but in a pinch or on a lazy Sunday morning, they'll do just fine.

Summary: great food, served cold and fast, with attitude, and therefore not worth the money. My wife and I went here on a trip to Montreal for our anniversary. As we're both vegetarians, and I had been here many years ago and continued to hear raves about it from my friends, I was excited to take her here and share a nice, moderately fancy, and totally delicious vegetarian meal. While I agree with the other reviewers that the food here is good, our dining experience was not a pleasant one. First, it's been significantly redecorated since I was last there, and the new decor is a rather harsh, black-and-white, modern style, which makes the space feel cold. Not an inviting place to step into from the Montreal winter. While I realize that some may find the trappings of a typical Thai restaurant kitschy, this place made me feel like I was eating in an operating room on the moon. Next, the service was quite rushed, even though the place was completely empty (at around 6PM on a Sunday night). Combined with the atmosphere, it's not a place I'd recommend for a pleasant, relaxed dinner. The tea we ordered came in cute little Alessi pots and was wonderfully prepared, but we scarcely had time to drink a single cup before our food arrived. Finally, when our food arrived (I ordered the chicken with basil and chili, my wife ordered chicken with green beans and spicy sauce), it was cold! The fake meat strips were just barely warm on the outside, and the sauce was lukewarm. When we complained to our waiter, he argued with us, saying it was just out of the wok, and only grudgingly and condescendingly offering to take it back and stir-fry it a bit longer. We didn't see that waiter for the rest of the night. When our food came back, it was much more appropriately heated. Consistent with the other reviews, the portions were small - just about the right amount of food for one person with no left-overs. They charge extra (2-3) for rice, which, again, comes in a nice individual portion. I had the standard sticky rice, which wonderfully complements the sauces and is served in a plastic bag (?!) inside a bamboo steamer. It was also not particularly hot, which, along with the plastic bag, left me wondering whether it had simply been reheated in a microwave.... My wife had the brown rice, which was actually red jasmine rice, and was well cooked and quite tasty. If this place were a few dollars cheaper and the portions twice the size, it would be awesome for take-out. Quite aside from our bad experience with the waiter, I can't recommend it for a sit-down dinner.

I've been to a few other places for dim sum, so my opinion is somewhat biased. For the record, I'm also your standard adventure-seeking gringo, inspired by Andrew Zimmern. So, in the interest of full disclosure, I'm not really an expert on dim sum, and I don't claim to be. I'm just a guy who likes to eat. After tasting a few different dim sum joints around Los Angeles, and finding that some dim sum places have way too many dishes that don't fit my palate, I think I've found my new favorite dim sum place. It's called Xing Wang (6288 Wilshire Blvd. 101, Los Angeles, CA 90048). It's on the edge of the LA Chinatown area, and it's not as fancy as, say, Din Tai Fung, but it's a nice, clean place, and it's pretty easy to get to. The best part of Xing Wang? They have steamed buns with peanut butter and jelly. Yup. I said peanut butter and jelly. I've read a bunch of food blogs that make fun of the idea of peanut butter and jelly steamed buns, and I can see why, but Xing Wang's version is legit. It has peanut butter and jelly in there, and it's good. The bun itself is a little dense, but that's not a problem for me, because it allows the peanut butter and jelly to stay in the bun. So, you don't get a bunch of peanut butter and jelly oozing out of the bun when you bite into it. The bread itself is sweet, with a little bit of salt, and the peanut butter and jelly isn't too sweet, so it's just right. The other thing I like about Xing Wang is the variety of food that they serve. They have a bunch of the usual suspects, but they also have a bunch of things that I haven't seen at other places. I'm not sure about the rest of their menu, but I'm pretty sure it's not a million dishes, so you don't get overwhelmed. I'm not sure how long Xing Wang has been around, but I imagine it's been there for a long time. It's a small restaurant, with a bunch of tables. The service is fine. The place is clean. There are a few other people who eat there, but it's not crazy busy. I'm not sure how long Xing Wang has been around, but I imagine it's been there for a long time. It's a small restaurant, with a bunch of tables. The service is fine. The place is clean. There are a few other people who eat there, but it's not crazy busy. So, there's no real wait, unless you get there right when they open. I'm not sure about the other dishes, but the peanut butter and jelly buns are worth a visit. So, if you live in the LA area and you're in the mood for some good, clean, inexpensive food, I highly recommend Xing Wang. Lunch offers sandwiches like chicken curry soup which is delicious as well as lots more great choices! And for dinner - we enjoyed such dishes as mushroom pizza and arroz enchilada always accompanied by tasty rice pudding. They also serve beerwine too.. so you might want to bring your own beverage if coming after lunch time on Friday night; Or come early before work when the cafe opens up- still very quiet then:

Great place! The food is great and a good value. It's owner operated and you can tell they really care their customers. I came here recently for a special occasion dinner with my office staff and it was very nice. The restaurant itself is well designed, with muted colors, dark woods and dimmed lighting. The wait staff was neatly presented in crisp white shirts and clean, black service aprons. We prearranged for a pre-printed dinner menu that was labeled as being for our party that night. I thought that it was a nice touch, and I am well aware that it was also a clever cost containment measure since it also kept our staff from wildly ordering off of the regular Fleming's menu. Our servers were all very gracious and attentive and took very good care of our party of about 25. Our food was all brought out at the same time, which was no small feat on the kitchen's part. Everyone seemed genuinely happy with their food, I didn't see anyone complaining about anything. I ordered the petite filet, medium rare, and it was absolutely perfect in every way. The meat was cooked perfectly and was tender, moist and delicious. There were various sides served'family style' raging from buttered corn to asparagus, and they were all very good as well. As a dessert I ordered creme brulee, and it was deliciously creamy with the perfectly sugar crust on top. My only complaint about my food, and it is minor, was that the creme brulee wasn't the ice cold temperature that I usually prefer. I like my creme brulee pre-fired so that it has time to cool off before I eat it. I don't care for warm custard, but it's purely a personal preference and I still thought the dessert was fantastic. The only other thing I would point out is that many people aren't fans of the a la carte menu system, it can be annoying, and ridiculously expensive, to order every side dish seperately from the main entree. That said, this was still a great experience in a wonderful restaurant. I highly recommend it for any special occasion dinner as long as your budget will allow it.
