Let me preface this review with a couple of things: 1. I went on a Monday at 3pm, so probably not the most ideal time to see the freshest foods. 2. I'm a vegetarian, so I don't have the most experience with meat, and I'm also an adventurous eater. Now to the food! I was very excited to try the Jamaican Jerk chicken, because I love spice! I was a little disappointed because the jerk seasoning wasn't that hot, but it was still pretty good, I just had to add a little more hot sauce myself. My boyfriend had the country fried chicken, and he said that it was pretty good, but didn't really have much flavor. They also have a bunch of sides that are made to order, and the mac and cheese was definitely the best part. It was hot, gooey, and delicious. I'm not a huge fan of collard greens, so I wasn't expecting much from those, but they were actually pretty good. I liked the black eyed peas, but they were a little dry. The corn bread was pretty good, but not as moist as I would have liked. Overall I would say that it was pretty good, but a little pricey. I spent 16.50 for my jerk chicken, a side of mac and cheese, and a side of collard greens. I also got a hot chocolate with a shot of peppermint, which was pretty good. I might go back, but I would be more likely to go for the mac and cheese or the jerk chicken.

I can't find a place any closer to me - I can walk across the street to work out! I first tried Barre3 when a CMYE (community manager yelp event) was hosted here. It was a free class complete with mini Jamba smoothies courtesy of Jackie and Barre3, and I was intrigued. I started going to physical therapy for my lower back and right hip - as soon as my birthday hit I started to fall apart and now Eric R. wants to exchange me for another wife (just kidding). However, being married to a very active person has been interesting because while I love to hike I never really enjoyed being in the gym or doing other activities of the sort. My physical therapist liked that barre supplements my therapy so I knew it was a good idea to take the introductory 3 for 30 deal offered by the studio. Last Saturday I dragged Eric R. with me to the Oklahoma red cross donation class, so we both donated the full class cost each to help with the tornado destruction. We went to the second class and ran into Molly T. leaving the first class. Eric R. realized barre3 was quite tough and is a great workout for me. We had Alison as an instructor and she was great. I came yesterday to my first paid class with Jackie and it was hardcore! Each of the three classes has had slight variations on movements and stretches, so I like the element of surprise and the activation of muscles that never ached before! I really liked the atmosphere here as it is clean and spacious. I also like how the instructors will work with each individual's injuries and help adjust us during the class. We are told to listen to our bodies and take breaks as needed. There is no pressure but instead a lot of encouragement. For those of you with children, childcare only costs 5 per class and is offered during morning classes and on Tuesdays and Thursdays for afternoon classes. You can go barefoot or wear barreyoga sticky socks. This is the perfect place for me to wear my Nike studio wrap pack that I bought when it first debuted. Each class works legs, arms, glutes, and core and includes ample stretching throughout the class. I feel like someone just punched me in the ribs so I know I am doing something right!

The closest touristy, Arizona-esque candy shop to me here in Central Phoenix. Cactus Candy Co is located in a small building room, stocked with: hot sauces, jellies, marmalades, cactus gummies, and snacks. It's got the typical theme of the area - it definitely feels like taking a trip outside your home town. A local favorite! But what I love about this place is that you can get whatever kind or flavor of cactus jelly you want on top of the mini dessert or drink called a "tortilla snack" (think layered burritos). They also have some truly amazing flavorscombinations that are not common around here!

Worst pedicure ever! Went in there for the first time yesterday afternoon. They were busy but still had plenty of chairs open for pedicures. My friend and I got seated with a new girl named Lindsay who was very sweet, chatty, knew what she was doing (I am not so sure about her co-worker) and even gave us some cute little push gifts - foot masks which we both loved already before trying them out. For 19 each you get one hour at your choice of polish color or two hours if you want to add on an exfoliation (5 extra). There are seven different choices including gold glitter, white sparklesfrosting, pink shimmery pastel colors, reds and more depending on how long you want it to last. After that they will give you 5 minutes to soak your feet then just quick dry off. Make sure when booking your appointment you specify 1st time customer as when my friend showed up they asked why and she said because she rarely gets her toes done but wanted this experience since it was only once in awhile thing. She actually paid cash through their Square app connected to her credit card reader from her iPhone while sitting down. It took longer than expected due to someone else being late getting finished by 10 mins, plus another lady showered right after me making a mess over everything so other girls couldn't work in front until sometime later. She did try to compensate those working hard behind scenes cleaning things up giving everyone free manicures afterwards along with our favorite nail wraps:) The service is great though and definitely worth going back. The pedi itself lasted 3 weeks without chipping too bad like most places do unfortunately around these parts...so come prepared to have the cutest looking baby toes anytime soon:D
I really can't see why people knock this place. Admittedly, they don't have the widest selection in the world and some of the package sizes are a bit on the World War II.

I looked forward to this meal for months but was sadly dissapointed. I had the posole, the rough cut tuna, and the shrimp tamale. My wife had the chile relleno. The posole was OK but nothing special. I ordered the rough cut tuna and it was not chopped at all. It was all pieces of tuna meat. I don't think I have ever had a restaurant who cut up their tuna like this. The tamale was not a tamale, it was a slab of beef and cheese wrapped in corn tortilla and baked. My wife's chile relleno was good but not great. The margs were good, but not really a big deal. I was really disappointed by the service. I ordered a margarita, they said they did not have the ingredients, so I ordered a margarita with no lime juice. I was charged 6.50 for a drink with no juice. I ordered a beer and was charged 7.50. This is a very expensive place. The food is not that special. A nice quiet place to eat with the family. My son really enjoyed his grilled cheese. It was made with two pieces of good quality white bread, cut in half with Swiss and American cheeses, and melted. It was served with a side of potatoes au gratin and a slice of beef. It was a nice meal. The service was very friendly and not too slow. The dinner menu is very limited so we ordered the chicken sandwich, potato salad, and a side of slaw. The chicken sandwich was good, but the potato salad was terrible. It was the same salad you get at KFC or Churchs Chicken. The slaw was good, but had little flavor. The service was friendly, but the service was slow. It took 15 minutes just to get our drinks. We have eaten at this place several times and have always had good food. This time we had the chicken fajita tacos, one with chicken and one with steak. The tacos were not very spicy. I ordered the steak and they gave me chicken. The steak was very tender and was a good size, but it was a little dry. The tacos came with refried beans and guacamole. The refried beans were pretty good, but the guacamole was not. The guacamole was very hard and the avocados were not ripe. I asked for extra guacamole and they brought me a small bowl of it and charged me for it. That was not right. We also had the chile verde and the carne asada. The chile verde was very good. I could have used more sauce though. The carne asada was very good. The salsa is the best I have ever had. My wife had the coconut key lime pie, which was very good. I ordered the tres leches cake. The cake was good but the tres leches sauce was not very good. My wife thought her cake was a little dry. Overall the food was very good, but it was not a great experience. The service was very slow and the food was OK. The chips and salsa were very good and I had the shrimp dish with rice and refried beans. I did not get any chile and the rice was not very good. The refried beans were pretty good. I did not get any tortillas with the meal so I had to ask for them and they were no good. The meal was OK but not great. I would not go back. This is a good place to go for a quick lunch. The burrito supreme is huge. It was spicy and tasty. The guacamole was OK, not really good. The salsa is very spicy and good. The tacos are good. The tortilla chips are very good and they serve them with salsa and guacamole. The chips are very good and you can go back as many times as you want. The service was friendly and very fast. They have an extensive menu and have something for everyone. This is a very nice restaurant with an upscale atmosphere. The service is very friendly and the service is very fast. The food is very good. The lamb chops were cooked to perfection and the sauce was very good. I also had the grilled salmon with a bearnaise sauce. The salmon was cooked perfectly and was very flavorful. I ordered the steak, but

Our cat recently came down with some health issues that we could not afford to address. He was in pain and we decided the humane thing was to put him to sleep. We went to the ARL and asked the receptionist there if we had any other options available to us. Well basically the only thing you can do is sign him over for euthanasia she said in the most uncaring, apathetic voice possible. We were heartbroken of course. Go wait by that door and someone will meet you. After a few minutes another woman came out and took the carrier. I'll bring your carrier back out in a minute. We said no, that's okay, keep the carrier. She said okay and took our cat to the back. And that was it. No kind words, no sympathetic gestures, no Would you like a moment before I take him? No I'm sorry. Nothing. For us this was one of the worst days of our lives but nobody at the ARL seemed to care, or at least have been trained to pretend to care, one bit. They get a couple stars for offering a necessary service. But other than that, this place will only be associated with making a terrible day that much worse with their lack of caring or empathy.

First off, Luedtke's Wonder Bar is in the same location as the previous establishment known as The Bar Next Door. The decor is much the same...but that is where the comparison ends. I will always prefer to spend my dollar at a small business vs. a chain. I respect what it takes to make good food and make it consistently when you are working from scratch every day. For reference, some of my favorite spots in Madison are Otto's, Louisianne's, and The Tornado Room. Luedtke's Wonder Bar is a notch above that dynamic trio if you can believe it. I have dined at Luedtke's Wonder Bar twice in the last two months. The latest meal being this last Friday night. I had seared tuna as an appetizer. The tuna was fantastic. The next thing I had was the crab bisque. I am not sure if this is on the menu every night but the two times I have been there, that has been the soup...Let me just say if it isn't on the menu every night, it should be! My goodness that is a great tasting soup. For my main dish I had a 9 oz fillet and garlic mash. The fillet had the consistency of sushi grade tuna. It was full of flavor and practically melted in my mouth. My only regret was that I didn't order the 12 oz! My wife had a crusted halibut fillet which she proclaimed was the best food she had ever had in a restaurant. That is high praise coming from her. So, the food is definitely 5 star, the atmosphere is quaint and cozy, the wine selection is nice and the prices are definitely in-line with what you get for the money. Hat's off Mr. Luedtke, we will certainly be back!

There's a few ways you can look at a restaurant but a review should include all the different perspectives. Quality of food: The food here is good. Not great (4star) not amazing (5 star) just good. The steaks were cooked perfectly how you ask and they have a pretty decent rub on them. They are aged and tender as one would expect from any big name steak house. They gave us a complimentary selection of pommes frittes which were delectable and the truffled mac and cheese was tasty. However, not a single one of these items mentioned above was better than a 3.5 star rating. You could argue that my palate cannot discern the difference between the beefs, but I would like to at least think I can tell the difference between a grain fed cow and one that is massaged by the japanese from kobe. It also could just be that I've had so many steakhouse steaks that an aged piece of prime beef with a generic rub of saltpepper just is old hat to me. Service: The service is very good. As expected from any high end vegas restaurant, they were very attentive and always served you with a smile. I was amused with the sommelier we saw opening a bottle of wine. You see, our table was right next to the small station where they open all the bottles of wine. One table ordered one with a synthetic wine cork. I know from experience those things are a B to open. It was comforting to know that a man who drinks and dispenses wine for a living also has problems with said cork. Ambiance: Dimly lit, contemporary decor, open kitchen with the meat locker right next to it. The restaurant is a great place for a date. Price: This is where I felt they fall WAY short. We walked out of there for about 70 to 80 per person. This included a steak and a side. The lady got a sirloin steak and I got the ribeye. If you've been out, you know that the sirloin is the cheaper of the few cuts. That's why I was surprised that the total bill was pushing over 150. Dont' get me wrong, the strip steak was great. The ribeye was good. But in all honesty, I'd rather go to Ruth's Chris or Flemmings where they have something unique. The broiled steak with butter. Quality of the meat MIGHT not be as good but it doesn't fall too far away from that at Stripsteak. After going to Michael Mina's in Bellagio and coming here. I was excited at first but disappointed after leaving.

We found out about the lack of uni when she came by to ask what we would like for dessert as all of us were anticipating another plate of sushi to be delivered to the table. Now let me explain.... I could have totally understood this if there was some mention made of this before or while we were putting in our initial order. I could have even been okay with this (although disappointed) if this was mentioned in the middle of dinner. Instead, my family waited in anticipation for a plate of uni nigiri and was instead greeted with the information at the near end of our meal. Uni itself is sea urchin and is definitely not for everyone. No matter where you order it, you will either love or hate it. For some I think it's a consistency issue. In the case of my family, we love it! We have actually walked out of other sushi bars here in Las Vegas because they didn't have any. Las Vegas has many sushi bars and almost limitless choices of great food. Over the past few years, we have actually followed the owner of this establishment from other places he has co-owned or worked at as the food has always been good. Tonight when my father approached him about the lack of uni, he seemed dismissive and quite unapologetic to the point where my father was going to leave an 8 cent tip on the check to get his message across that perhaps in this economy that service and humility toward your customer can only get you ahead while the adverse will get you the opposite. I left an additional 20 with the check (and my father's 8 cents). The sushi here is okay. I actually drive a cab and have been recommending this establishment whenever I'm asked in person or on the dispatch radio about a sushi bar. The items on the appetizer list are awesome and I definitely recommend the Garlic Chicken and Tako Karaage. Tonight was just an unfortunate experience and I definitely feel that the situation could have been handled differently. I'll be back again in the new year and hope that things are better.

I had been to Lux a few times when they were located right next to Pena Bianco. Had to see the new place just a building over but a whole new vibe and atmosphere. The bar is filled with some of the most stunning looking people in the city. Not a bad looking one in the bunch. It's filled with a hip 30 something crowd with a healthy dose of gay. It's kind of a cross between 30's and 40's. It's very dark. The lighting is a soft dark glow, low ceilings, and candles everywhere. They have a nice wine list, a strong martini menu, and some unique cocktails, a great place to people watch. The DJ is playing some funk, soul, and 80's tracks. They had a really cool corner with a huge stone sculpture, candles, and really funky chairs. The place is filled with art pieces and sculptures. The staff is really nice and friendly, and really attentive. The DJ takes your request, and has a great selection. The food is really well done, with a great selection of small plates. The special drinks are really strong and the bartenders know what they are doing. I enjoyed it, and will be back again soon.

Finally tried this place today and was not disappointed! Sunday afternoon, nice weather and they were packed! Ordered a shrimp and a fish taco and they were very good, fresh ingredients and they were just the right size. Salsa is very good, but if you want more spice ask for the habanero version. My only complaint is that they don't have full sized pitchers of beer...small ones at about 2.5 pints each. However, that being said it was happy hour (we were there about 1pm) and they were only 5 so all is forgiven. I like that you can sit outside and the back outside patio has a large grass area so if you bring your kids they can lounge around and not bother anyone as it is not right next to any tables. Will for sure go again!!

Moxie Java is a recently-opened little corporate-style coffee shop with a small lunch menu and some deserts. Consider it Starbucks (plus) better coffee variety than Starbucks, wider menu, and wider hours of operation. There are three locations: 6th Street at the corner of Texas Ave in downtown Little Rock 1917 E 7th St, North Little Rock 1530 Main St., Suite 1A, Maumelle This is essentially an upscale version of Shoo Fly Pie Company or Pappy's BBQ. The food is very good but not up to those two restaurants' high standards; they focus on quantity rather than quality. Entrees include several items that are basically pulled pork sandwiches (with multiple meats). All entrees come with hush puppies served as side orders. This place also serves lunch sandwiches and salads only (no entree salads), which can be ordered a la carte. The kitchen is open until 9 pm daily for dinner service. Happy Hour deals can be found from 4 pm - 8pm Tuesday through Friday. Don't expect much alcohol selection here, though there is select beer available by the pintquart throughout the day. Note also that the bar has its own entrance so if you're looking to drink something stronger than what is offered on tap, find another exit! Note too that this place gets crowded at times and you may have trouble finding seating unless you arrive early enough. If you do end up waiting anywhere long term I'd recommend asking one of their employees about single tables. There aren't any free standing booths either. No matter how many damned liquor licenses they get, the prices will never go down. You might as well move to LA. I'm overpriced. Edit: And let me reiterate my point above...the drinks are just as expensive whether you order them neat or mixed. Also apply "Uptown" rules when ordering a drink because you'll pay more.

I came here during the Mtl a table festival, a festival that allows foodies to try out new restaurants at a fraction of the price. I was looking forward to trying out this new place, especially since I had a feeling that the food was going to be good. I had reservations for 2, but the day of I noticed that there was an opening for an extra person, so I invited my friend. At the bar, we were greeted by our waiter who helped us choose some snacks and drinks to pair with our meals. The snack we were offered were homemade sausages with ketchup, gherkins and onions. My friend and I opted for the margherita pizza with artichoke cream, tomato sauce and basil. My friend had the Salmon with parsley oil, onions and potatoes. I ordered the beef with caramelized onions, Brussels sprouts and chips. For dessert, we decided to share the chocolate and pecan tart, garnished with raspberries and a chocolate ice cream. Overall, I really enjoyed my experience at Le Strata. The pizza was delicious and the atmosphere was cozy. If you live in Montreal, this is a great place to go for brunch, lunch or dinner. Make sure to book a reservation ahead of time to avoid disappointment!

They really go above and beyond to provide activities that support weekly themes, etc. This week in honor of the 4th of July they are tie-dying shirts in red, white and blue. I've been to a few other places for dim sum, so my opinion is somewhat biased. For the record, I'm also your standard adventure-seeking gringo, inspired by Andrew Zimmern. So, I've tried a lot of things in my time. Dim sum is a very different animal. The quality of the cooking is not nearly as important as the quality of the fillings. There are certain things that are always good, and others that are only OK. You'll find out in the next paragraph. I'll start with a couple of negatives. It's so hard to find a place that will do two things well: high quality fillings, and big, fluffy, steamed dumplings. At most places, the dumplings are too small and the fillings are soggy andor unappealing. At others, the dumplings are fine, but the fillings are only OK. With that out of the way, the best I've found is Kam Fong. The best dumplings are here, and they are enormous. Most of the other dumplings are also quite good, and they have a very broad selection. They are a bit pricey, but it's worth it. There are a couple of new places in the area that are excellent, too, but they are a bit further out. The Dumpling Station is a new place, and they have some good dumplings, but the dumplings are smaller. Wing Wah is a bit further away, but the fillings are huge, and the dumplings are large and fluffy. The only problem is that the dumplings are not steamed. They are fried, and they are delicious, but I'm not sure that they fit with dim sum. It's good, though. The other issue is that the menu is very limited. I'm also going to make a very bold statement: the best steamed buns are here, and they are also the best in town. I have tried nearly every other place, and I have never found anything better. They are fluffy, the inside is sweet and the outside is slightly crisp. I also like the curry chicken and curry pork. They are both really good, and I'm not a big fan of curry. The crab rangoons are also very good, and the char sui bao are also great. The rest of the menu is ok, but not much better than you would find at any other Chinese place. The other good places in the area are the Chinese House and the Delaware Chinese Restaurant. I haven't been to the Chinese House in a while, but I remember that they had a very good egg custard tart. The Delaware Chinese Restaurant has a very limited menu, but the quality is good, and the prices are quite reasonable. To end with a positive, I've been to a few other places, and they are all decent. I've tried some of the better ones a couple of times, and the results have been consistent. The Dumpling Station is a bit overpriced, but they have very good fillings. The prices at Kam Fong are a bit more reasonable. Hopefully, you have a better idea of where to go. I'm also going to have to start a dim sum blog, because I've been to so many places. For the record, I'm also your standard adventure-seeking gringo, inspired by Andrew Zimmern. So, I've tried a lot of things in my time. And I'm still not going to that boring blog of yours. I'm sticking with Gastronaut.

After a while the manager comes over and apologizes claims it's not his day, explains again that a chef had quit, supposedly he gave the 2 people that had ordered skewers 2 dollars off their meals, because apparently he thought that was sufficient to repair the damage. Instead you took us for about 200 and knocked off a whopping 4 from the diners who waited 90 minutes for their food. the part you don't see is you'll never get a dollar out of those 8 wallets again, and you could have if you made it right which you didn't, IT TOTALLY SUCKS that your chef quit, but that's not your customer's problem and your customers are free to go somewhere else if you don't acknowledge that. Unfortunately I missed my chance to actually touch her when she came back out onto the field though, and the only time we did bump elbows was while getting her autograph later that night in the VIP area. I'm sure some of you will say it's not important, but whenever I win something or get any kind of recognition, it feels good (especially cause I'm ugly). Anyway, Melissa took us into the dressing rooms to check things out, and eventually found us our seats just behind the players' tunnel. The view was amazing. You can sit right next to them during the match and watch them pass each other the ball constantly without seeing anyone else except the occasional player shouting encouragement over his shoulder! There was also another group of girls sitting together but I wasn't able to find theirs unfortunately. They seemed excited, and probably making the most noise in the entire stadium. Melissa took us back to the press room afterwards and again, gave us hugs and kisses. That's nice, I guess.

You have to be kidding me! All the buzz about this place is way over rated! The best part of the place is the place itself. Cool design, innovative, comfortable (if you overlook the AC running at 65 F). Short and poor selection of wines, the menu doesn't make sense, the deserts are poor executed, service barely OK and all of this with a way overpriced tag. Cheese bread at the beginning was good, probably the best executed dish (puzzle face). I had a glass of a French wine which had one of the most awkward wine tastes I've ever tried, but again, the selection is not that great. In their web they have a beet salad but I didn't find it in the menu. It seems that they replaced the beets for strawberries. When I asked why, apparently beets are out of season. (Really? I'm not a farmer, but I had beets last weekend in another restaurant, oh well). Salad was barely average. Then I had the marrow bone. It was OK, I was expecting a little more of a flavor from the onion jam and the bread used was kind of boring for such a dish. For desert I had the rum and coke. It should be called sweet bread. No taste of rum or coke what so ever. Just a spongy bread super sweet with whipped cream on the side with an unknown flavor and a jelly with a hint of lime. I also tried the doughnuts with chocolate. The doughnuts (bites) were crunchy (in a bad way) and the chocolate was more in the side of dark than milk, so didn't love them either. There was a guitar player for all the three tables and 4 people that were at the bar. When he was gone, a DJ started spinning tunes for the whole 7 tables and 3 people at the bar that were there when I left. It will be hard to make me go back ever. There're plenty of places where you will do way better for this kind of money.

All that is missing is counter side dining with privacy drapes.

I love this place. It's probably the best thing that has happened to an airport. Just imagine a great place for food, not expensive, and inside an airport.... Beautiful dining room hidden in Old Town Scottsdale. We made a reservation and scored an outdoor table on a lovely May evening. It was the perfect night to sit outside. Cool breeze and nice lighting. We decided on the Shared Plate menu. Each entree was 4-5 small plates that you could share with your dining partner. The menu changes according to what is available at the market each day. The chef chooses the best of the day. The meal started off with a very interesting bread selection. It looked like a warm bread basket. I loved the Burrata with Heirloom Tomatoes. I would have loved it even more if the Burrata was more fresh and creamy. It was quite dry. The Penne with Sausage and Broccolini was delicious. The Fried Brussel Sprouts with Pancetta was my favorite. I loved the brussel sprouts, but I'm a sucker for pancetta. The Smoked Trout with Horseradish and Dill was beautiful and tasted good, but I'm not a big fan of fish. I've always wanted to try a fried chicken with a waffle, and now I have. It was ok. Not much flavor to the chicken, but the waffle was nice. The desserts were the best part of the meal. I loved the White Chocolate Bread Pudding. It was like a pudding that you put over ice cream. It was like a custard with a pudding crust. Very nice! The Key Lime Pie with Almonds and Blueberry was very good. The pie was very thick and dense, but the topping was good.

From the very beginning, Amber that young lady who worked with us was professional, on the ball and organized...far more than I can say about the wedding planner. I believe she must be the park's event coordinator and totally rocked it. The place is truly beautiful, so different from what a traditional garden looks like. Read the other reviews and the other folks will give you a much better idea of the type of plants, bugs, small animals, or as my granddaughter loudly proclaimed the birds with the hats! There were four other wedding going on the afternoon (42911) but we never really heard much except for some far away music. Signs were clearly posted leading the way to the wedding site and the rehearsal the night before) and the restrooms were exceptionally clean and pleasant to use. There was a very large room with shuttered windows and AC where my daughter and her wedding party dressed and a smaller, similar room where the groom and his group readied themselves. After the wedding, as the chairs and such were put away, the entire group came back to the same area which is a small courtyard and had a cocktail hour. My daughter and her husband were married in the far back arena where they have the outdoor concerts and therein lies the only reason this wonderful place does not get five stars. If you have your wedding at this particular site, park your car in the dirt lot that is adjacent to the unloading area. It is the first right as you come into the park and has a sign posted that reads Service area only. I understand that during the afternoon the park may want you to stroll leisurely through the park enjoying the natural beauty of the place but at the end of a very long day, it would've been so much better to park in back and take a 5 min. walk as opposed to an agonizing 15 min. stroll. It was incredibly hard for some of the older folks in the group making their way back to the cars and by the time the wedding ended, it was late and the only rangers we saw were on our way out. It was also very dark there and the lights on the canopy over the wedding table did not come on for a long time but eventually they did and it was truly breathtaking (you may want to have someone be the on the watch for this so the wedding party doesn't eat in the dark.) Lovely place to have a party or wedding, parking not so great. Thank you DBG for making my daughter's wedding so very memorable!

tiny little place, delicious shawarmas. I've lived in the middle east and grown up eating them. I always felt that most shawarma places have north-americanized the shawarma recipie. These guys kept it real. The meat in both the beef and chicken shawarmas were perfectly seasoned, very juicy and the meat to salad ratio in the wrap was perfect. Ive had shawarmas in the past where the meat is very fatty. Not at all at this place. Also, I could not believe the price! 4.50 for a decently sized wrap. it's also open late so after a night out, definitely a place to stop and refuel.

This review is for the nightclub. Came here on a Sunday night for the open bar. It went from 11pm-12, and we met up with our promoter outside the club. There was quite a line outside, but he was able to walk our group of girls in for free. There aren't many clubs open on Sundays in Vegas so LAVO was great for pre-party. The club is upstairs and really pretty. The walkway is lined with these water fountain-like things, very classy and chic. Having only gone to Surrender at the time, LAVO seemed amazing and very well-decorated. Compared to other clubs like XS, LAVO is a bit small, especially the dance floor. It was already packed before 12am. I enjoyed the music though, and the crowd seemed a little younger. The drinks from open bar were pretty watery, but the cocktail waitresses were really hot. Bottom line: come here for the open bar. Maybe dance a little.

No longer do they try to bulk the meat into small portions using cheap cuts of beef; now they source high quality wholesome meats and produce as well as premium cheeses for their gourmet items. For example: Instead of having 2 slices of American cheese wedged between 4 chunks of processed and tasteless lettuce, you get 6 ounces of fresh provolone squeezed between thick hand-cut hamburger buns baked right along side each other. And not only does it melt perfectly, it also makes for a very tasty sandwich. I'm talking delicious beyond belief. Even the sides were great...the potato salad was amazing! Oh yeah, they also throw in sliced tomatoes or avocado for little extra bucks whenever possible. Not sure how long this location stays open 24hr but it certainly seems to attract quite a following. Go early in the day during breakfast hours. Talked to several employees working there after midnight and they said they love serving customers late night too. It's funny I passed by the ad of this place whenever I drove on the freeway, and I finally went after all those years. Me and my boyfriend went here last night for our anniversary. We made a reservation in advanced because we weren't sure how busy they get on the weekends. We get there and we get seated, the light and atmosphere is very romantic. Our waiter gave us complimentary champagne, which was really nice. The staff was very friendly and professional. He ordered the Fisherman's platter and it was delicious (yes I took a couple bites from him). And I ordered a 3 large Pacific rock crab claws (unfortunately they ran out of the stone crabs but was not disappointed). The meat was so sweet and so fresh, I was amazed by each bite! The sauce that comes along with it compliments the sweetness of the crab meat so well! We also ordered a Baked sweet potato and Mac cheese. They were both delicious! The potato was so soft and the pecan butter it came with added a hint of sweetness I like. The mac cheese was not overpowering with a cheese taste (which I never find when I order mac cheese). And lastly for dessert, we ordered Banana cream pie. It was excellent! Not an overpowering banana taste with great sweetness from the foster sauce. Overall our experience was wonderful and very relaxing. Of course the bill is going to be high, but it was expected. We'll definitely be back for more. Next time, I will try the stone crab they are so famous for!

Do Not eat here!!!! Unless you want to get rip off!!! They charge me 9.95 for a side order of bean sprout. Should be around 2. I will never come I'm sorry to hear about your negative experience at the restaurant. It sounds like there may have been a mistake in pricing or a miscommunication about the cost of the side order. However, it's important to remember to always communicate your concerns to the restaurant staff directly and kindly so they have the opportunity to address the problem and make it right. Leaving a negative review without giving them a chance to correct the issue doesn't give them an opportunity to improve their service.

Fifth Wine is a nice wine bar in Old Town. The staff was great, very helpful. In fact, they sat down with us repeatedly throughout our visit to check on us, tell us a little bit about the place and the menu. The bruschetta is delicious, inventive and reasonably priced. They only have one Sauvignon Blanc, but the one they have is pretty good. Lots of cozy couch seating in addition to the bar and table set-ups. Great happy hour. Check it.

I loved this place! We came here on one of our last days on Vegas and found it while walking around the Golden Nugget. When we sat down to take a break from gambling, I was shocked at how much food you get for such an awesome price and that there is actually good quality meat in their hot dogs (my favorite meal). But if your looking for just a quick bite or snack check out some of their other locations like LAX, McCarran Airport, Dallas, San Francisco International Airport many more cities across America We tried all kinds of stuff. Hot Dogs were my favorite but they also had great burgers too (and even better fries!) The toppings are plentiful with lots of different options. Everything is made right in front of you so its fresh every time. Good service as well...

The market spice buffet was one of my favorite buffets in Vegas but this last time wasn't so good. Maybe it was because it was 2PM and the food was a little cold, or maybe they were out of some things that I love to get there like cumin seeds (which is always available when you ask for them). But overall not as great as previous times. I'm glad we went here once! It's pretty big inside with an outdoor section which makes sense since its located right next door to their restaurant. Since it can be hot outside during summer months, having seating outdoors would make more people come back from lunchdinner at Flamingo Cantina across the street. We didn't have any problems getting seats both indoors outdoors even on busy days - just our luck though cause other reviews said otherwise:P This place has super authentic Mexican cuisine including lots of traditional dishes such as enchiladas, tortillas, carne adovada, burritos, tacos etc... They also had fun items like nachos made with Oaxaca cheese!! My husband tried all different types of proteins: chicken tinga, carnitas, chorizo, fish taco, shrimp pozole.. he raved over everything except the fish dish which tasted too much like cod to him lol He did say however his favorites are Carnitas Xtreme and Chicharron Fries. The service folks weren't very friendly unfortunately. One server barely acknowledged us and never offered water nor refills. Another guy came up after being seated asking if anybody needed drinks only to find nobody ordered anything yet LOL That happened about 3-4 times before someone asked what he wanted! Other than those few instances servers were quick efficient and brought appetizers promptly each round. Overall experience was decent enough although nothing spectacular by Las Vegas standards:) THIS PLACE IS AMAZING!!!! Best breakfast ever!!!!!!!!!!! Even better then brunch places, the coffee is amazing!!!!! Great bagel selection, scrambled eggs w pico de gallo and bacon cooked perfectly everytime,, fruit salad with yogurt dressing, fresh squeezed orange juice. Service is awesome, waiters know how to take care of customers and the dining room is clean and well decorated. The best part? Is that it doesn't cost 25 per person!!! For me i think 10 would suffice!! You will NOT regret eating here!!!!
They do not offer free wifi, you have to pay for it! Boooo Nice restaurants and pool though!

I came here for my girlfriend's Bday dinner. It was just not up to expectations. Our party of 8 wasnt all there, but they seemed to want to keep us After a while, we finally decided to give it a try. This was our last time at Sushi.

I can't believe so many people give this place anything above a 1 star. We've been three times because it was so close to our house, what a bummer. The scary thing is their staff doesn't know much of anything about dogs. We asked for a trainer recommendation and they looked at us like we were crazy then suggested that we look through the business cards that people drop off on the counter. The bakery is cool, but I would be worried with a staff that knows so little about dogs to feed my puppy food from this place. I just don't want to mess around with something that might not be healthy. The part that is a real bummer, and why we will never be back, is that they don't take any returns for anything, ever. We bought a toy for our dog, decided we didn't want it and tried to take it back the next day. I had the receipt and it was in one of those plastic clam shell things...totally unopened. They still said they wouldn't take it back. The thing cost 27 plus tax too boot! I did a little research and found two local pet stores within a mile that both carry the same products for less, and their staff is well trained. I would stay away if I were you...cute does not equal safe or fair.

There's no denying that the Bellagio is just a beautiful casino. However, there isn't much to offer to the younger crowd. They now have a club, but it's rarely crowded and has very few people who are less than 40 years old. If you want to party hard in Las Vegas with lots of local talent and dancing all night long on stage at one of their top casinos like Caesars Palace or Mandalay Bay then go visit The Cosmopolitan Casino (formerly known as Circus Circus). It's near Fremont Street so if you're staying nearby, it should be relatively easy for you to get here. There will also usually be more youngsters around because this is where they head out after work when they're not doing shows of course. We considered all these options before settling on our actual favorite place to party in Las Vegas: The Wynn Resort Spa - This city landmark was opened by Steve Wynn himself back in 1997 and has quickly become an iconic attraction among tourists visiting L.A., San Francisco and Hawaii from across the country. Right next door to it, there's another hotel owned by Wynn Resorts called Encore which is great fun for families too. On Avenue of the Stars - Being right beside the Grand Canyon, its proximity makes it perfect for those looking to see some amazing views while going out to buy booze andor food because you'll find several shops selling alcohol along the way. AllSaints - Right off the Strip, All Saints offers plenty of dance floors and can often accommodate large parties easily enough.

While I'm starting low because my experience hasn't been that great, I'm still willing to come back and try it again. Walking in the decor is modern hip diner with an abundance of windows. The large bar was packed with people drinking and talking and a great vibe was in the air. My order came quickly, and I was able to get a burger on the table and a table in no time. While the burger was pretty good, I couldn't help but think it would have been even better with the addition of a burger bun. It was a good amount of meat, and it wasn't dry. I like the texture and flavor, but it could have been so much better. If you're going to get a burger at this restaurant, you should get a bun. The fries were good and crispy, and I really enjoyed the green sauce that came with it. The hot sauce on the side was a nice addition to the meal, and it really put a little spice into it. I'm still happy that I tried the restaurant, and I would definitely come back for a burger and fries again. But, I'm starting to have a sour taste in my mouth because I feel like it could have been so much better. (Overall Score: 3.55) From the outside, it looked like a pretty nice place. It's a sports bar that's focused on the Arizona Cardinals. The bar itself is a nice place to sit and relax. I love the concept of having a place that is all about sports and beer, and I love the Cardinals. Walking in, the decor is kind of nice. It's all white and red and has a very modern feel to it. The bartenders were all wearing their jerseys and were really nice. I had a lot of fun and got to meet some new people. The menu is really simple, and it's basically beer, food, and pizza. I was able to order a pizza and a beer. I ordered the classic pizza and it was delicious. It was good and hot and I loved it. The pizza is just like it sounds. It's classic. It's just a pizza with pepperoni, cheese, and pepperoni. It's just a great pizza. The beer was the Shock Top. It's a beer that I love, and it's a beer that you should love. It's a strong beer and I love it. It's very flavorful, and I love the spicy and peppery taste that it has. It's just a great beer. Overall, I really enjoyed my visit to the Cardinals Tap Room. I really loved the fact that it was all about the Cardinals and the people were all very nice. It's a great place to have a drink and relax. I would definitely come back again.
I love this place! They are always super friendly when we come in and the food is consistently delicious! Not super expensive and great service!

Worst pedicure ever! Went in there for the first time yesterday afternoon. They were busy but still had plenty of chairs open for pedicures. My friend and I got seated in chairs and someone came up to give us a ticket for the pedicure. We both received different tickets. We then waited for the person who was working on my friend to be done. There were plenty of nail techs available but they were having us wait for over 45 minutes! The lady asked my friend and I if we wanted a drink. We both said yes and the lady asked what we wanted. My friend said water and I said tea. She came back and handed my friend her water and then she said to me "I don't have any tea right now." She then proceeded to give me a water too. I was so confused because I did ask for tea and I was a little irritated that she was trying to give me water. I asked her what she meant by that and she said "I don't have tea right now but I have water." I asked her again if she was sure she didn't have tea and she said no. She then gave me a cup of water and my friend had to wait another 10 minutes for her pedicure. When my friend was finished, she asked me if I wanted to get up and get my pedicure because she was ready. I said no because I was waiting for my tea. The lady said she didn't have any tea. She then gave me a ticket for my pedicure and I got up. I still had not received my tea. The lady who was about to give me my pedicure asked if I wanted a beverage and I said no. I asked her what happened to my tea. She said she didn't know and that she had no tea. I then asked her why I had been given a ticket with tea on it and she said she didn't know. She said it was a computer system. I asked her if she had a manager that I could speak with and she said yes but she didn't know who it was. I then asked her if she could make a phone call and ask someone. She said she could and she did. The manager came out and said he was the manager and I asked him why I had been given a ticket with tea on it if they didn't have any. He said he didn't know. I then asked him if he could get me some tea and he said he would. He then proceeded to walk away and went to the back area. When he came back he was carrying a cup of tea and he said "here you go." I then asked him why he had to walk to the back to get me tea when I told him multiple times that I wanted tea and they had my ticket. He said "I don't know. I'm sorry." I then asked him if he could refund me the cost of my pedicure. He said no and then asked me what I wanted him to do. I said refund my money. He said no. I said I was going to leave. He then asked me again what I wanted him to do. I said I wanted to leave. He said he was sorry and I left. I am very dissatisfied and I will never go back to this place again.

In all, I think I wouldn't come back, especially since the normal menu is so much more expensive and the special menu wasn't too spectacular.

My favorite frozen yogurt place yet! First, on walking in, I'm not greeted with a mass of people all trying to do different things (enter, exit, fill their cups, pay) and everyone is not rushing. I'm greeted by friendly, helpful employees. The yogurt itself is rich and creamy. They have a good variety of flavors and toppings. I am not a fan of the fruit on the bottom, and the fruit on the top was not my favorite either. The plain yogurt was my favorite. They also have the typical toppings: granola, chocolate chips, nuts, candy, etc. My only complaint was that my yogurt was soft serve and I would have preferred it as a cup of yogurt. Overall, I would give this place a 55. Tried this place last night, and it was really good! The yogurt is very creamy, and the toppings are amazing. I tried the Blueberry and the Passionfruit, which is a unique flavor. It was really delicious! I also tried the espresso drink, which was really good. The only thing is that the drink was a little too sweet. I wish it tasted more like espresso. The prices are really good as well! This is definitely a new favorite! The place is really nice and clean. The staff is so friendly and helpful. I tried the chocolate, mango and blueberry. The chocolate and mango tasted very fresh. I didn't taste much of the blueberry. The blueberry was also rather sour. The chocolate tasted more like a frozen milkshake than frozen yogurt.

Want to see the best that Argentina offers?! You've come to the right spot! From national parks filled with wild animals to beaches packed with sunbathers, you're bound to find something worth exploring while visiting Buenos Aires. From wine to tango, food to culture, this list features everything you need to know about Argentina's capital city - including places to eat, things to see, activities to take advantage of... it's guaranteed that you'll want to return again and again!! Set deep within the heartland of Patagonia, Torres del Paine National Park consists of two main hiking trails called Laguna Amarga and Laguna Blanca (roughly translates to: "Amber Lake" and "Lily Pond. Seasonally, visitors can enjoy numerous possibilities both day hikes and night adventures. Visitors seeking adventure await. Set amidst stark landscapes surrounded by glaciers, jagged mountains and pristine lakes, Torres Del Paine National Park boasts a wide variety of options both daytrips and treks spanning several days. To begin with, just a 10-minute drive away lies a breathtaking lake known simply as Lago Grey. Situated alongside a big blue glacier, its colorful shores are absolutely mesmerizing, especially during peak viewing periods. Whilst the most popular activity throughout the park is trekking, tours can vary greatly depending on the individual's needs. For instance, a guided river raft trip would include some moderate physical exertion whilst offering beautiful views and wildlife encounters. If you're looking to spend only the morning walking, try taking a boat ride to Laguna Esmeralda, followed by an afternoon hike to Laguna Carla. This itinerary will allow you to spend less effort whilst still getting full viewings of many different kinds of plant life and wildlife.

I've never really been into strip clubs, but I like to go to them occasionally. Body English is a nice enough place, but I think I would rather go to another strip club in Vegas. So I'm gonna break this down into segments because there are far too many things swirling around my head right now to regurgitate it out into any form of organized thought. 1. The Hotel When I booked the room, I reserved a non-smoking king bed standard room..... upon arrival, I was told they were sold out of king bed rooms. Only after my wife sarcastically stated something about a comp upgrade, and several moments hesitation and thought, did the front desk clerk upgrade us to a non-smoking double queen bed room with a view. As we made out way up to the room I was thinking, ok, we're staying in a castle themed hotel.... I can only imagine what the rooms look like Boy was I wrong. The room as plain, nondescript, and boring. The only castle themed items in the room was a framed drawing of a shield hanging above the toilet. The beds were comfortable, but plain. The dresser and table had scratches, chips, and dings showing years of use. The only new...ish thing in the room was the TV, a wall-mounted flat panel 42 TV. The view was good, but for me at least, it didn't make up for the other problems. 2. The Casino No problems here. My wife and I love playing roulette and Excalibur had both live dealer roulette and something called Organic Roulette where a machine spun the ball and players have their own touch-screen display to place their chips. Both were fun, but I enjoy live dealer play more (especially if the dealer has personality). One thing will say positively of the casino floor was that they had multiple roulette tables open. Three 5 minimums and 1 10 minimum tables which I appreciate because it can take a while for a seat to open up if there is only one table. The slots are the same as everywhere, so I can't bash Excalibur or praise them. 3. The Dining Experience: Oh buddy..... where to begin. Let's see, momma always said start off with a compliment. There is really only one redeeming quality about Excalibur that would make me deliberately want to go back (only to eat, btw), Dick's Last Resort (reviewed on it's own Yelp page). The other dining experiences were disappointing to say the least. Excalibur has a little bit of everything: Dick's, a BBQ place, a food court, a steakhouse, a buffet, and room service dining. The problem.... THEY ALL CLOSE! The room service is allow offered between the hours of 0600 and 1400 (6am and 2pm). The only.... let me pause for dramatic effect.... ONLY 24hr dining options are McDonald's, Starbucks, and Krispy Kreme. WTF?!?!?!?!?! We don't go on vacation and spend hundreds of dollars to eat the same shit I can get down the street of my house! Vegas casinos are 24hr operations.... they purposefully build the place without windows and do not install clocks so that patrons will not know what time it is and keep gambling. That said, you would think that an operation the wants people gambling 24 hrs a day would want those same people fed and happy during that whole time, right? Wrong. I even called the front desk one night because I was hungry for real food and not a BigMac or a fucking doughnut. I spoke with Mary, the manager of guest services, and was told that because Excalibur caters to the family audience (people who bring their kids) they find that the majority of patrons are not active nor hungry during early morning hours. I was also told, more or less, that she didn't care about my concerns and that there was nothing they could do the make up for the problem. Please see my other reviews for reviews of the individual restaurants we ate at 4. Overall Experience: I've been to Vegas twice, once to New York New York and then this time to Excalibur.... I must say that I was severely disappointed. Between the lack of late nightearly morning dining options, the lack of interior theme decorations (it really looked and felt like they blew all their money decorating the outside of the hotel and the entry way to look like a castle, but just went with a Best Western approach for the rooms), and the shocking number of strollers, infants, toddlers, and other variously aged children running around, I would not stay here again. I will, more than likely, return to Dick's Last Resort for a meal or two during my next visit, but I will sleep and gamble at another resort..... one that takes my patronage seriously and treats me like I am the target demographic (21). Oh.... one more thing. There is a small army of hotel minions that will seek out, stalk, and harass ANYONE that walks near them trying to pitch them a deal. They start out with an innocent enough bait question to strike up a conversation and it doesn't fucking matter what you say to them (yes or no) they will try to rope you in to signing up for a bogus deal. The deal is you leave a 99 deposit, if you book within 1 year

BOTTOM LINE SAVE YOUR I'd been hearing about Five Guys for awhile...how amazing it is supposedly. I am a die hard In-N-Out (INO) girl esp. bc I worked there for 5 yrs. Two stars for outrageous price, 3 stars for quality of food. If you have had real and inexpensive Chinese food, it will be very hard for you to justify a high mark like this. Service was great. They brought the meal out and served while I waited. The wait staff were friendly and helpful even though I was short on time because my flight didn't leave until 7:30p.m. We talked about New Zealand as we ate. This is the first restaurant that has ever "been" in our home. My husband and I both ordered the chicken wings (one regular wing and one spicy wing), and they came with an ice tea and watermelon. The waiter also brought us some tasty snacks - acai bowls, pita chips, gummy bears, etc. It all tasted good! We had two Twinkies ordered off the menu at a new place called Z Man. The food was delicious, but somewhat underwhelming compared to what we expected from the name. While the service was fast, it seemed like everyone looked up to fix the order before serving. A couple of my friends ended up going back to their cars after getting their food because they couldn't finish eating everything. If you go there, check the menu beforehand so you know exactly what you want and can let your server do his or her job without having to ask them every 5 seconds. I love fresh Asian food, especially something from Taiwan. Since Z Man opened, this is by far the best Taiwanese food we've found in Chicago or anywhere else. The portions are huge, the ingredients are amazing, and the cooking process is absolutely flawless. As much fun as it is to eat these delicacies outside of Asia over the Internet from a website that doesn't realize how awesome the food actually is, it really makes me sad when they have to take away the only authentic option available in Chicago. Exhausted, I went back to grab another dinner the next day because I just kept thinking about how happy I was to find such a great spot in town. What makes it better than any other Chinese takeaway in Chicago? No doubt a friend who cooks for his clients.

That Sunday when we showed up at 2pm for our 2:30pm bus, we learned that they'd changed the time to 1:30pm. The Daylight Savings in other states affected the schedule. We should have confirmed our confirmed tickets. The station agent changed us to a 5:30pm bus, and we were bummed that we'd have a few hours to kill and miss out on time with Mr. L's parents. And they'd have to find the bus station in the dark - shoot. Lesson learned? Buying tickets ahead with Greyhound isn't the best idea. If you do, confirm them, as the schedule may change. With hours to kill in the Greyhound Station, my son started playing video games at 1 a pop, and Mr. L and I gathered our thoughts. There was some scary looking food sitting under heat lamps in the Cactus Cafe. We rented two lockers to stow our luggage for 3 each for 3 hours and split in a cab for a while to go anywhere but the bus station. When we returned closer to our new departure time, the lines for the buses were confusing. The line for Tucson was not the line for our bus. It seemed like everything was backwards here. Luckily we asked, or we might've missed our bus again. By the time we boarded our bus, many seats were taken. Ichabod headed to the back of the bus, and a kind gentleman cleared the 3-seat rear spot for us. There was a bathroom near the back, which Mr. L suggested I avoid entering. He said it was a basic hole (outhouse style) with an empty jar of hand-sanitizer. Good to have the bare-bones bathroom if you really need it, but ick. The driver made a bunch of announcements in English, then in Spanish. He meant business. I was glad when he told passengers to use headsets for their music, since initially a nearby passenger graced us with his music. Now we only got to see his seated dance moves, which were actually pretty good. 2 affordable prices 2 capable driver -2 changing the schedule after had a confirmed ticket -1 for only one agent working the line 2 having a bathroom on bus -1 condition of bathroom 1 lockers in Greyhound station -1 for the clusterfck of confusion of lines to get on buses - advanced degrees don't help here, be ready to ask questions Grand total: 2 stars Overall, we were glad not to spend over 600 on a rental car or inconvenience our friends or family by asking for a very long ride. We learned that we need to confirm or buy tickets last-minute like most Greyhound riders. Hanging out in a Greyhound station is not my idea of fun. We would ride Greyhound again, but proceed with caution.

Just in case they'd never come back. I told the server we were new to this cuisine and would need some help. My husband just wanted to leave. Spring rolls, two Pho's and the Ban Xeo for my egg and shrimp loving child. 15 minutes later two drinks and some plates of leaves and garnishes were placed on the table. They get two stars for having a low price and food I liked, but I can't give them any more than that.

Bourbon Steak house was a fantastic experience for us. I was able to take my bride and our daughter here at the end of our stay in Scottsdale. Food was great, service was wonderful and the view of the city from our balcony table couldn't be beat.... We will definitely be back!!!

Bath and Body, they have been around for a very long time. I do not know how long this one had been here though. This place is ridonkulous. I don't use the word ridonkulous often but this place deserves it! AYCE is phenomenal. Wa Salad is some incredible sashimi salad concoction that deserves it's own platform to perform on. Kid friendly yet posh looking on the inside. Standing ovation. I will be back. Maybe even tomorrow. Moved down to 4 stars from 5. This last trip back, the food was still good bit service not so much.

I was told to arrive at 8:30 am for a 9am appointment as a new patient for a routine annual exam, which I did. At 10:40, after being in a paper gown for quite some time, I was finally seen. She said, Thanks for your patience. I said, I'm not that patient. Her reasons for the delay were twofold: 1) We have 6 practitioners in this office and we have to SHARE ROOMS! (um, schedule your patients appropriately?!) and 2) (told to me mid-exam) We have alot of long-time patients at this practice, and when they come in we like to find out what's going on with their kids, and their grandkids, and stuff, so we take a little extra time with some of our patients. I'm not kidding. She also kept making this disconcerting exhalation noise during the exam, the kind you make when you're around something you don't want to smell. I was perfectly clean and healthy, and she made the noise during paperwork too, so it wasn't me and it wasn't necessary!!! Then she asked me if I had any other concerns before she walked out the door, and I joked that hopefully my husband, whom I'm separated from, which we had discussed, hadn't cheated on me and now we'd know. She said, Oh, I wish you had said something, I could have done cultures but can't now since we already used the gel. End result: I was 3 hours late for work for a 10 minute appointment, with absolutely no patient emergencies involved, and did not get the thorough care I thought I was waiting for. I was also not kept informed about the delay, (which would have been extremely helpful since my son had forgotten to bring his lunch to school) and the delay did not seem unusual. No one seemed happy to work there. I am furious and will never go back to that practice. Which is convenient, since I don't think they'll like me much after I send them an invoice for lost wages. I know I sound like I'm out on a limb, but I've worked in healthcare for many years, I was raised in a healthcare family. I understand bookings and reimbursements, delays and emergencies. But this was UNACCEPTABLE.

Glad we stopped by. Were already downtown and decided to give this a try. Glad we did. Service was great. Wasn't very busy so we received plenty of attention. I I've been very satisfied with my food and service. I've just recently had a second visit and had a great experience.
Don't bother with the JFK exhibit. It's overpriced and has very few items. This is a ripoff.

I had heard raves about this restaurant so brought 3 guests for dinner. Food was just ok (the 22 oz rib eye steak was 50 fat and bones and was undercooked; scallops just ok; frites and vegies barely warm). Our waitress was very good which compensated a bit for the food.

Planned to go there last Sunday because of all the great things we had heard about this place! WELL, to our surprise, they were not open!!! the huge NOW OPEN sign was hanging in the window, the hours on the door said they were open there were a few people inside, looked like they were cleaning the kitchen area or something......... but alas, all the doors were locked and the people inside completely ignored us!! At least take down the huge NOW OPEN banner in the window!!! Or post a sign on the door explaining why you would be locked up during your business hours!!!

QUALITY NAILS IS NOT QUALITY NAILS IS NOT. I patronized this shop on a Saturday afternoon WITH AN APPOINTMENT. The shop was busy with bookings and continued to take walk-ins. The techs RUSHED thru my pedi and fill. As a result the DESIGNS ARE SLOPPY AND AMATUERISH looking. This is especially annoying since it was the owner, Lisa, who did my fill. I miss Tuscany ever since I moved. This place was a late night favorite for me after all the geeky magic get together a. Everything is fairly priced and delicious. The steak and eggs are a must!

Better than the reviews say. I've been here 5 times now and every time we go, including during the dinner rush, we've always been seated and served quickly. The music is loud, but not too loud and adds to the atmosphere. The menu is great, lots of food choices and the food is always really good. I am a person who loves a clean restaurant and I'm so happy to say that their is not a speck of dirt in here. You can tell that they take great pride in their business. Service is always great and the staff is always friendly. The food is always great, but I have to say that their fried chicken is out of this world. I usually get a grilled chicken sandwich and am never disappointed. I love this place. The food is excellent and the servers are great. Everytime I go there I'm not disappointed. The restaurant is clean and there is never a wait. The servers are always great.

Way over priced and WAY pushy people! Really? There is now way the average person buys 140 worth of tea a month!!!!! Never spending money there again! They push these price hikes because they don't know what they are going to get for their money.

Moxie Java is a recently-opened little corporate-style coffee shop with a small lunch menu and some deserts. Consider it Starbucks (plus) better coffee variety than Starbucks, wider menu, and wider selection of flavor. Moxie Java is located right off of I-70 in Glendale. We ordered some lunch items on the menu. We thought the chicken salad was a little plain. We liked the chicken sausage wrap better. My husband ordered the jerk pork (might as well say pork carnitas), which was very good. We also tried a dessert sampler. I liked the chocolate mousse best, and my husband liked the lemon cake. My favorite part of this place was the fact that they use single-serve coffee pods. They have a variety of flavors, some of which I'd never heard of before. They do not accept returnable pods. They have two flavors of hot chocolate pods. They also have coffee beans for sale. Moxie Java also has a cooler full of bottled drinks that you can buy to take home. Most of them are from Mexico. They also have a very large selection of pastries. I would eat here again if I lived in the area. I liked that this place has a corporate atmosphere but still feels homey and not pretentious. The entrance is hard to findidentify.... the exit says Sears, but the entrance has a door that says AvisBudget. You have to wait in line to bring your car in for service instead of parking in the lot and going into the shop with your keys. Waiting in line took roughly 20 minutes on a Tuesday about 12 noon. I brought my car in for a simple oil change... it took almost 3 hours. Granted when they told me it was done, there were several things that Diego had found that I could fix in my car... the list of repairs totaled over 800. I didn't bring the car in for an inspection, just an oil change... that's all I wanted... could have saved time elsewhere. Yum! Salsa is divine and you get bean dip as well with the chips!

Love love LOVE this bar that is in the back of a shopping center off the Freemont street promenade. It's right behind the heart attack grill. We ordered drinks and realized there was an area of regular dining tables we asked to be reseated in that area. We found our own way there, sat down at a table only to discover the carpet appeared not to have been vacuumed from the day before (we arrived just before noon). Good thing this place has a lot of good reviews or I would never go back. Since I worked in the Biz and I am a forgiving person when I get things wrong, I will stay there as long as it's not too far from work. Wifi is at your table so you don't have to worry about it.

I'd be VERY Leery of Single-Visit, Single-Review yelps. As an Ex-Local, Brian's Beach was and still is one of our favorite Japanese restaurants in LV. How much do we like it? Let's see on a recent URGENT trip to LV where we had to drive over in the morning and leave in the afternoon, the ONE place that we had to make time for in that highly compressed time frame was Brian's Beach. The service has always been exemplary, the food has always been excellent. Our favorites include, the seared tuna tartar, Dynamite, the grape and bree quesadilla (WTF? uhh yeah, MUST TRY) and their assorted rolls and appetizers One great bonus about this place is that the AYCE rules aren't limited to just the rolls, but also apply to the appetizers, so if you have someone with you that doesn't dig rolls, they can stick to the great appetizer menu The ONE thing that I personally dislike is that the Seared Tuna tartar is limited to one order per guest. - I can't blame them for that though, it's an expensive dish and I would seriously just chow down on a dozen plates of that if I could.
This place is wonderful! I ordered the Sesame Encrusted Salmon and it was the best thing I've had in a while! I could have done without the spinach as they The Salmon was great!

No thank you food was over cooked bland No milk that very sweet and dry. is poor quality and no taste. food was sliced in a few parts of food was over cooked if you are aved taste of something else you didn't taste experience

I like the accommodating room with jacuzzi. I like the fact that we were loud at 4 in the morning and no one complained. I like how easily it was to access the I-94. The staff was very nice and helpful with anything we needed! They offered a free ride from the airport and a free ride back to the airport on the day of departure. The location is also great, it's not too far from downtown Milwaukee and there are many places to eat in the area. Very friendly and polite staff that made my stay perfect. We stayed an extra night because we liked it so much! Fantastic staff! Clean rooms! Great amenities! It was a great value for our money! I would definitely stay here again! This hotel is exactly what you need. It has everything you need while being so close to the airport. The staff is outstanding, the rooms are clean and spacious . The complimentary hot breakfast is delicious! I did not hesitate to book another stay here for this summer. I was getting ready for a business trip and realized I had no reservations. I booked this place as a last resort, but it turned out to be one of the best experiences I've ever had. The staff was very nice and helpful with anything we needed! They offer a free ride from the airport and a free ride back to the airport on the day of departure. The location is also great, it's not too far from downtown Milwaukee and there are many places to eat in the area. My wife and I stayed here for one night and it was fantastic. The room was extremely clean and comfortable. The staff was very friendly and accommodating. We will be staying here again on our next trip to Milwaukee.

LOVE. THIS. PLACE. First tried this place on my drive cross-country and it was very good. I raved about the burger to everyone for a very long time. By chance, when I was visiting home in the south, I spotted that culver's sign out of the corner of my eye and proceeded to flip out. My passenger in the car was baffled at my sudden excitement. On the way back from my primary destination, I stopped here and my friend and I were in burger shake heaven.

I've had a very good burger here but the fries were under cooked. The service on the other hand was horrible! It took a party of 3 (2 adults and a child) 25 mins of seated time before we even got water to our table. Asked my waiter for a 3rd set of silverware and never got it so I had to stop the manager as I saw her walking past the table with a few in her hand for one. Proceeded to tell her that we were not happy that it to over 20 mins to get water and we still did not have the appetizer and that I have a child that is starving and begging me for food as Im talking to her the appetizer hits the table. 2 mins later still talking to her and the food hits the table. Get better staff if you want to keep your regulars! Management brushes off complaints here and refuses to take responsibility! This location is much closer to my house but I would recommend the Power Rd Chandler Heights location as far as service.

ok so because I didnt get a burger here, you may not actually want to base your decision on this alone. I went here this weekend with my parentals and since I was on a no carbs diet, I didnt get a burger or fries. the only thing appealing to me on the menu was the fried chicken bites. there was about 6 of them and they were just ok. they tasted kind of bland. they came out with a ranch of some sort but I think they wouldve been tastier with hot sauce or honey mustard (which they didnt have). I also ordered the hole-in-one drink. it pretty much tasted like a midori sour so id double check the pricing on both and just get the cheaper one. the location is nice. its on the corner of las vegas blvd so it's cool to chill outside and people watch. I may come back to try a burger one day but not anytime soon.
I love Cheesecake Factory and I love to order their avocado eggrolls, yummy. I have no complaints about this restaurant except that I think their cheesecake is just a tad too much for my taste buds!

Finally I got a chance to enjoy DTC picnic basket meal. My order was a meat 3 - fried chicken 3 sides (Mashed potatoes n gravy, hushpuppies and cornbread) Note: I also had a cup of French onion soup which was good. Fried chicken was excellent, it was cooked and seasoned to perfection. The flavor was crispy and tasted like it was seasoned with just salt and pepper (which was probably the case). Mashed potatoes were above average with just enough gravy to cover them. It was definitely not a starchy gluey mess like in many restaurants. Hush puppies were above average but could have been better. Corn bread was sweet, warm and gooey.

At first it seemed as though the Fiesta hotel might be a great place to stay because of recommendations and the low price, but it is definitely some place I would not recommend. The walls are very thin. They sound proofingacoustic treatment is non-existent. It's especially bad in the bathroom where you have shower head right next door to your neighbors shower. (I've stayed at better hotels that cost twice as much.) Also there was no air conditioning or fan to blow on yourself during hot periods which could get unbearable with the windows closed. Also we were expecting an ocean view from our room but instead received one window overlooking the street corner (and although they had promised us this earlier online, when we checked out, even after two calls, they still hadn't changed anything.) We did however enjoy staying near Fisherman's Wharf since many of San Francisco attractions are within walking distance such as: Fisherman's Wharf; Golden Gate Park; Chinatown; Coit Tower; Alamo Square; Union Square; Alcatraz Island; etc...

One word that describes Thai Spices is meh. Located in MeKong Plaza, it took over the old BoCa 7 space. When walking in the place, you'll notice its nice decor. The food isn't bad but there's no wow factor to this joint. does the food come out fast? i've never been there before; I don't want low quality good and expect amazing things from it. I believe they come out within ten to fifteen minutes of ordering.

The place is sort of like a hole in the wall but im not complaining as its close to home which is nice. The decor is sort of like what you would expect of the floor plan of a sushi restaurant with the center wrap around bar section where you expect to see a sushi chef behind serving it up. But its relatively clean and its not like I wanted to dress up to go eat island food. The good part, the grub! my brother said the Katsu loco moco was where its at so I ordered and maybe not even 10 minutes later the cook in the back who kinda reminded me of tattoo face from 50 First Dates had my tasty bowl mounded with a heap of food. This bowl had to have at least 4 scoops of rice in the bottom, 3-4 full chicken breasts breaded and well cooked, 2 eggs, and covered in brown gravy and a sprinkle of green onions. Honestly I was overwhelmed by the amount of food as when I saw the 8 and change price tag I thought it was a lil bit much for what I ordered, till I learned that it could feed me for 3 meals. Well made with all the right flavors, my only issue ever so slight was that the eggs were sliiightly under cooked so the whites were still jelly like. Aside from this I was pleased with the food. Location decor - 610 would get a 5 but its close so thats a point 4 me Service - 710 nice people, nothing special but not bad either Food taste - 7.5-810 simple food, simple flavors but well put together Value - 9.510 big food for very good price, one order can feed two All in all this is my go to spot for when island food now. I use to make the drive all the way to Aloha Kitchen previously but now its down the street and reasonable. I will be back without a doubt.... come hungry!

So there are now two types of milk and one has the hormones in it and the other one doesn't. But what happens if you add hormones to the organic milk?
